News.title: Man in his 40s found dead in caravan at holiday park as 39-year-old arrested for murder
News.content:
CARAVAN 'MURDER' Man in his 40s found dead in caravan at holiday park as 39-year-old arrested for murder







Next

A MAN has been found dead in a caravan at a holiday park, as cops arrest a 39-year-old man.

Police were called to the Valley Farm Holiday Park, in Clacton-on-Sea, Essex, following reports of a man making threats at around 9.15pm on October 14.



Officers discovered a man in his 40s, from Frinton-on-Sea, injured inside a caravan and was pronounced dead at the scene.

Specialist officers will be supporting his family.



A 39-year-old man from Ingatestone was arrested on suspicion of murder and taken to hospital for treatment to an injury to his hand.

An Essex Police officer is also said to have been assaulted as they responded and the man has been further arrested on suspicion of assaulting an emergency worker.

Det Insp Tim Coyles said the police do not believe there was an ongoing risk to the wider public.

He added: “My thoughts this morning are with the family of the man who died last night.”

He continued: “We will work tirelessly to get them the answers they need about what happened.

“We have already made good progress at building a picture of what took place and, at this stage, we believe both men were known to each other.



“I believe there will be a number of people who saw or heard something last night that may be helpful to our investigation and I urge them to come forward.

“Officers will be carrying out enquiries at the site throughout today.”

News.title: Thug held over arson attack that killed 4 ‘just out of jail’ & ‘paid few hundred euro’ as lifted female ‘drove own car’
News.content:
Next

THE young criminal held over an arson attack that killed two children and their parents was recently released from prison for burglary, we can reveal.

Gardai tonight are continuing to quiz the thug and a female accomplice after arresting the pair this morning.



They are both suspected of being at the scene of the firebomb attack, on the outskirts of Waterford city at around 5am of Tuesday.

Innocent Philip English, in his 50s, wife Kim, 38, and their sons Callum, 12, and Jayden, nine, died in the horror blaze.



The couple’s daughter, 14, and six-year-old son continue to fight for their lives in hospital.

Detectives now believe the family’s electric car was struck by a petrol bomb, causing it to explode into the home, which became engulfed in flames within minutes.



Gardai suspect the arrested man, aged in his 20s, carried out the attack after being contracted by a Traveller gang.

He was released from prison in recent months after being banged up for a burglary offence.



His alleged accomplice, a woman in her 30s, is believed to have driven the yob and others to and from the scene — in her own car.

A source said: “The man arrested is suspected of being the one who threw the petrol bomb. He is known to Gardai as a ­low-level criminal, someone likely to have only been paid several ­hundred euro to carry it out.”

Another source added: “These are bottom of the chain. It’s certainly a line of inquiry that the men involved essentially took up the job for a Traveller gang.”

The pair are being held under anti-gang legislation, Section 50 of the Criminal Justice Act. They can be held for seven days.

Two other men remain suspects but have yet to be arrested.



Gardai spoke to at least one of them when they were among the targets of a series of raids on Tuesday evening.

Philip, Kim and their four kids were targeted at around 5am as they lay asleep in bed at 7 Birch Avenue, in the Birchwood estate.

The fire engulfed the home so quickly that the family all became trapped upstairs.

A joint funeral for the four ­victims will be held at Sacred Heart Church, in the Folly, Waterford, at 1pm on Monday.

A death notice said they will be “sadly missed” by their extended family.



The tragic couple’s two surviving kids were rescued by firefighters.

They are being treated at Crumlin Children’s Hospital in Dublin, with relatives saying their prospects are “not too good”.

Detectives quickly identified the arson attack suspects, with cops seizing cars and phones on the evening of the horror.

The National Bureau of Criminal Investigation is examining GPS data from the vehicles, to trace their whereabouts at various times.

Other experts are trawling through the phones, tracing messages and who the suspects were in contact with as they build their case.



Officers are also using CCTV to trace the movements of the lifted woman’s car on the day in question.

A senior source said: “These are complex investigations that take time, but it is progressing well.”

The victims had no involvement in crime but Philip’s son from a previous relationship claimed on Wednesday that the family were targeted over a €20,000 drug debt owed by ­someone known to them.

John James English, who said they were not involved in drugs and were “innocent”, added: “It’s a family, you know.

“Twenty grand worth of a debt, is that worth nearly five lives?”



He said they had been targeted for some time before the arson.

Philip’s car was burned out last month and he sat down with cops just ten days prior to the attack.

The Irish Sun understands the dad spoke at length about the background to the situation.

Kim had also expressed fears for her life to friends and family.

The quadruple murder highlights the issue surrounding drug debt intimidation, an issue Waterford city has grappled with for years.



Local Sinn Fein councillor John Hearne has had around 40 people who are living in fear for their lives approach him in recent years.

And he’s had his own car burnt out for his work helping others. Describing the violence dished out by local gangs, John said: “The very first case I had was, two women got put out of their home.

“A young fella said something and he beat up the two girls and beat up the child. And then the same crowd, they attacked that home, they threw a petrol bomb in the window and it landed on a kid.

“I’ve come across another girl, they beat her with a hammer.

“Another fella, they chopped off a few fingers on him. So it’s serious, it’s intimidation. They burnt out my own car one time.



“In another case, there was two different crowds trying to kick in a door, three different outfits going to the one house looking for money.

“The son had ripped off three different outfits and they were kicking in the door.”

He added: “The sadness about it, the amount of fear is incredible.

“I remember just going in and meeting parents and they can’t eat, they can’t talk, they can’t work, they can’t function with the fear.”

Local Sinn Fein TD David ­Cullinane, who knows the family, has told how people in Waterford were devastated by their deaths.



Speaking in the Dail today, he said: “This murderous attack showed utter contempt for human life, and anyone who planned, ordered, or carried out this attack must face the full force of the law.

“Drug-related intimidation must also be confronted head on. Other families are looking out their front doors and wondering, could their children be next?”

He called on the Government to ensure that Waterford has all the Garda resources needed for the murder investigation.

Deputy ­Cullinane added: “Will you ensure that families reporting threats have all the supports that they need, including an urgent risk assessment, a named contact and a co-ordinated protection plan, with access to safe emergency accommodation when needed?

“Will you commit to a review of how threats and requests for help are managed, and how families are supported? And will the Minister for Justice report to this House next week on the wider response to drug-related intimidation?



“Because the response to these murders cannot be outraged today and forgotten tomorrow.”

He continued: “We have to face down these criminal gangs. These are cowards, and what happened in Waterford has people’s hearts broken, and it should never, ever have happened.”

Defence Minister Helen McEntee vowed to “engage” with the Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan on whether more can be done to tackle the issue.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hundreds attended a vigil near the scene on Wednesday, where parish priest Gerry Chestnutt called on those responsible “to stand up, admit what you did and face the legal consequences”.

Gardai continue to appeal for info or any dash-cam video from around the time of the attack. They said: “Contact the incident room at Waterford Garda Station on 051 305 300, the Garda Confidential Line 1800 666 111 or any Garda station.”

News.title: Three kids among four killed in shooting at elementary school as suspect gunned down by ‘bystander’ during rampage
News.content:
Next

AT least three children and one adult have been killed after a suspected teenage gunman opened fire at an elementary school, reports say.

Several people were also injured during the horror in Oregon before a bystander neutralised the shooter, according to local media.



Hundreds of armed officers responded to the gun rampage at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend at 1pm local time.

Police sources told CBS News three children and one adult were killed, but this has not been confirmed by authorities.



Cops previously said at least two people were taken to St. Charles Medical Center.

It is unclear if those rushed to hospital were the victims that died.

It has also not been confirmed who neutralised the gunman.

Cops said they responded to the scene on Thursday afternoon within minutes of receiving reports that a shot had been fired into a car.



When officers arrived at the site, the suspect was already dead, authorities said.

Silver Rail Elementary School was placed on lockdown during the terrifying ordeal.

A reunification point was set up at Journey Church at 61303 S. Highway 97, near Goodwill and Dairy Queen, for students and their families.

Police said “hundreds” of cops swooped on the school following reports of a gunman opening fire.

Local authorities said: “The Bend Police Department is currently at Silver Rail Elementary School after a report of an active shooter.



“There is a large police presence in the area. Please avoid the area.”

About 450 children attend the school in Bend, cops said.

The situation is still being monitored, authorities added.

FBI agents are also at the scene, according to officials.

Oregon Senator Jeff Merkley wrote on X: “My team and I are closely monitoring reports of an active shooter situation at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend.



“As details continue to come out, my heart is with the Bend community and all of the students and families affected.

“No one should have to fear violence at school.”

The identity of the suspect has not been confirmed.

But police said it might have been a bystander.

Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook said: “We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy.



“We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence.

“No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing.”

Breaking news… More to follow…

News.title: Ex-Sun reporter John Scott who covered stories from M1 plane crash to Fred West and was ‘always on it’ dies aged 76
News.content:
FAREWELL, SCOTTY Ex-Sun reporter John Scott who covered stories from M1 plane crash to Fred West and was ‘always on it’ dies aged 76







Next

EX-Sun reporter John Scott has died aged 76.

He joined the paper as West Midlands correspondent in 1980 and covered the patch for us until 2005.

Some of his major stories included serial killer Fred West, the M1 plane crash and murderer Tracie Andrews.

Former Sun news editor Jamie Pyatt said: “Didn’t matter how early or how late you called Scotty, he would always be on it.





“Genuinely so easy to work with and one of his greatest skills was to be able to build friendships with those he had done stories with so he could always go back for more.

“A great reporter for The Sun. He’ll be missed.”

John spent his entire career in the Midlands, starting at the Birmingham Evening Mail.

He retired aged 70 from the Wolverhampton Express and Star.

He is survived by his wife, sons and grandsons.

News.title: Moment Brit-made sea drones blow up port of Russian Olympic city in huge explosion as Ukraine blockades Putin
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment Brit-made sea drones blow up in a Russian Olympic city’s port as part of Ukraine’s Black Sea blockade.

Extraordinary footage showed K3 Scout speedboats hurtling towards Vladimir Putin‘s forces during a combat operation last month.



The cutting-edge devices, made by Hampshire-based firm Kraken Technology, are believed to have travelled hundreds of miles before reaching their targets.

Jaw-dropping footage showed a huge fireball erupting after one of the unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) was intercepted in Sochi.



Russia‘s Nefrit supply ship docked near a pier in the port was blitzed during the mission – illustrating the strength and range of Kyiv’s state-of-the-art drones.

Ukraine said the vessel supported oil and gas operations, transported cargo and helped with subsea engineering work.



An industry source told The Times: “The successful use of drone boats to target key Russian maritime targets shows how much the nature of warfare has changed.

“The unwavering British support for our Ukrainian allies continues and you can see why it is something the whole country cares so deeply about, with events like this playing out in Europe.



“British industry is a key pillar of the fight against Russian aggression and we support collaboration towards that effort.”

K3 modular boats can be dropped off the back of a helicopter and act as a launchpad for hundreds of armed drones.

The advanced devices carry suicide drones or compact air defence systems for long distances.



They travel at speeds of 55 knots in the high seas and have a range of 650 nautical miles.

Many have drawn comparisons with the fictional jet-powered “Q-Boat” from the 1999 James Bond film The World is Not Enough.

Able to carry a 600kg payload, the vessels can remain in the water for one month and cost about £250,000 each to build.



The UK bought 20 of them as part of a £12.3million programme known as Project Beehive.

They can also be used for surveillance, training and nautical operations.

Some have been prepared for use in the Strait of Hormuz.

In August it was revealed that British-made drones were being used to strike long-range targets deep inside Russia.

UK-built UAVs were also used to destroy a Russian bridge in April.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kraken’s K3 Scout surveillance drones also made headlines earlier this year after it was revealed they were secretly sending data to China.

After finding the breach, the Ministry of Defence was forced to remove all internet connectivity from the cameras, the Telegraph reported.

News.title: Over 12,000 fake weight loss jabs worth £2m seized by cops in raid on industrial unit
News.content:
FAT JAB PHONEYS Over 12,000 fake weight loss jabs worth £2m seized by cops in raid on industrial unit







Next

MORE than 12,000 fake weight loss pens worth £2million have been seized by cops during a raid on an industrial unit.

Officers from the West Midlands Police raided the warehouse in Birmingham on October 14 in a joint operation with the Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA).



Some 12,000 fake retatrutide – or ‘reta’, as it’s known online – and tirzepatide pens were seized along with packaging for around 30,000 more products.

Tim Duffield, Head Intelligence at the MHRA’s Criminal Enforcement Unit, said: “We are tackling the organised criminal gangs whose illegal trade in unauthorised medicines puts people at risk of serious harm.



“Our officers seized around £2million worth of fake weight loss medicines from a filthy warehouse on an industrial estate.

“These products have not been assessed for safety, quality or effectiveness, and there is no guarantee of what they contain or whether they have been contaminated with harmful substances.

“Retatrutide has not been authorised for use in the UK.

“Products being sold as retatrutide outside legitimate clinical trials are being supplied illegally and could pose serious risks to public health.

“We urge people to avoid buying weight-loss medicines from unregulated sources.

“Anyone considering GLP-1 treatment should speak to a healthcare professional and only obtain medicines from a registered pharmacy against a valid prescription.”



Yesterday’s raid is the latest in a series of MHRA operations that has removed tens of thousands of doses of unauthorised GLP-1 weight loss medicines from circulation.

In May, cops made two arrests following a raid on a country estate thought to have been used to manufacture, assemble and distribute unlicensed weight loss medicines.

Around 12,000 doses were recovered, along with packaging materials and suspected pharmaceutical substances.

In February, around 2,000 doses of unauthorised weight loss medicines were seized, along with manufacturing equipment, suspected pharmaceutical ingredients, packaging and commercial vehicles.

The MHRA dismantled the first illicit weight loss medicine production facility discovered in the UK in October 2025.



It seized 5,000 unauthorised retatrutide and tirzepatide pens, thousands of empty pens and raw chemical ingredients.

News.title: When will Burnham realise TikTok clicks are no substitute for actually confronting the huge challenges the UK faces?
News.content:
Little to cheer







Next

CONTRARY to the Chancellor’s pronouncements yesterday, growth of 0.1 per cent in August is hardly a cause for celebration.

Rather, it is a grim indictment of just how sluggish our economy has become under the tax-and-spend Labour Government.



As he finalises the Budget, John Healey should be in no doubt that the one thing guaranteed to make things even worse is more crippling tax hikes.

But how else does he propose to fill a yawning £35billion funding black hole? The sensible option, of course, would be to take an axe to the welfare bill.



However, Andy Burnham has fallen at the first hurdle. To no one’s surprise, the PM has scrapped a plan to ban under-22s from claiming incapacity benefits worth £430 a month.

Like his spineless predecessor Keir Starmer, he capitulated at the first rumblings of discontent from Labour’s bleeding-heart backbench MPs.



The PM will happily discuss issues which seemed settled, such as Brexit or alternative voting systems — both of which are a million miles away from most voters’ real lives and concerns.

But on the tough decisions needed to get Britain growing, he meekly kicks the can down the road.

When will Burnham realise that generating clicks on TikTok is no substitute for actually confronting the ginormous challenges which our country faces?

Shaky defence

ON MONDAY, the PM looked the country in the eye and insisted he had only ever held one significant rendezvous with Manchester City’s football finance fiddlers.



That story has collapsed quicker than a non-league back four. As we reveal today, he in fact held at least SEVEN meetings with the shamed club’s execs.

Accused of covering up his cosy relationship with City’s uber-wealthy owners, Burnham has belatedly announced what amounts to an inquiry into himself.

A “manual trawl” of records relating to his dealings with the club will ensure “full transparency”, he says. Why didn’t he just do this in the first place?

He has scored a spectacular own goal.

Shore fire fail

ONE of Andy Burnham’s many big promises was to help Britain’s seaside towns “re-imagine themselves for the 21st century”.



Yet he handed mayors powers to impose a “tourist tax”, driving up the cost of a staycation and potentially decimating the hotel and hospitality trade in much-loved resorts.

Now he is weighing up doubling taxes on gaming machines, which could close almost 250 betting shops and casinos at the coast, triggering a jobs bloodbath.

Our struggling seaside towns want the bright new future promised by the PM — not to be crushed by taxation.

News.title: Paying feckless Brits to sit on their backsides while importing millions of migrant workers is moral insanity
News.content:
Next

IT is entirely possible that the ­people running our country for the past few decades are economically illiterate, deeply immoral and stark staring mad too.

That’s a pretty bold statement, you might think. But, worryingly, I fear that this is the only logical explanation for how we’ve got ourselves into the horrible mess we’re currently in when it comes to our ballooning benefits bill.



In a hard-hitting report published this week, The Centre for Social Justice think-tank has spelt out in vivid detail the shocking scale of our welfare dependency.

Hold on to your hats because the statistics it lays out in black and white in its State Of Dependency briefing are truly shocking.



In thousands of neighbourhoods, jobless claimants actually outnumber the workers, with many out of a job due to ill health rather than a lack of opportunities.

Seven million people now claim at least one or more state benefits for sickness or disability. That’s more than one in ten of the UK population and it’s risen by an astonishing 60 per cent since 2020.

The Government will spend more than £100billion this year on sickness and disability benefits alone.

Around 1,000 people a day are signing on for PIP (Personal Independence Payments), and one in seven new cars sold in Britain is now bought under the Motability scheme.

It is simply not remotely believable that such a huge proportion of the population is really sick or disabled enough to need state benefits instead of being able to work.

Yet this Labour government, and the Tories before them, are happily pursuing policies that have meant six million people who go out to work full-time now earn less than people claiming benefits.



A minimum-wage worker who does 40 hours per week typically earns roughly £1,880 a month after tax.

Meanwhile, a PIP claimant accessing all of their benefit entitlements can take home £2,000 a month.

Is it really any wonder that so many these days choose not to work and think that the people who do get up to go to a job every morning are mugs?



Why do a minimum-wage job when you can get paid more to sit at home playing on your Xbox or scrolling on Instagram?

And, indeed, many working people are beginning to wonder exactly that.

My generation was raised to believe in work. We were told that if you work hard, you can get on in life and also, for the able-bodied, work should be a duty.

Not only do we need to support ourselves and our families, but we need to pay taxes to support those who can’t help themselves through no fault of their own.

It’s what a civilised society does.



But what’s civilised about grafting all week to pay taxes to fund your lazy neighbour’s layabout lifestyle?

These days, many younger people regard work as an option rather than a necessity.

Yet instead of taking on the challenge of getting feckless Brits off benefits, every prime minister from Tony Blair onwards has preferred to take the “easy” option of importing millions of migrant workers to do the jobs our jobless refuse to do, mostly in hospitality, retail and social care.

As a result, a shocking four out of five new payroll jobs created in the past decade have gone to migrants.

Of the 3.7million PAYE jobs filled since 2014, only 734,000 have gone to those born in this country.



The biggest rise in migrant arrivals came in the years since 2020, with 2.1million new migrant workers, mostly from outside Europe, coming in the post-Covid “Boriswave”.

By extraordinary coincidence, at the very same time, the number of people claiming out-of-work benefits in Britain rose by 2.3million.

The sheer insanity of importing millions of people to do largely low-paid jobs while at the same time paying millions to sit at home all day is breathtaking.

Businesses may indeed want an influx of migrant workers who are willing to work for lower wages than Brits, but whatever benefit that brings to those businesses is wiped out by the wider costs borne by everyone else — from those new arrivals needing a home to live in, a school for their children, NHS care, roads to drive on, their rubbish to be collected and so on.

All of those public services cost money, and while I don’t begrudge anyone seeking a better life by moving to Britain for work, the majority of migrants arriving since 2020 don’t earn enough to pay sufficient taxes to cover the services they use.



And of course, after just five years of living here in Britain, migrants can apply for “indefinite leave to remain” — and then they are entitled to the same benefits as Brits.

Almost two million foreign nationals are now claiming either working-age benefits or the state pension in the UK, costing taxpayers £23billion last year alone.

This isn’t just economically illiterate, it’s also immoral.

Condemning millions of young Brits to a life on the dole is a disaster for our economy but it is also catastrophic for those young people left to rot on the rubbish tip of life without the purpose, self-respect and opportunity that an honest day’s work can bring.

This sorry state of affairs has been a long time in the making and both the Tories and Labour, past and present, are to blame, but we all know it’s not sustainable.



Our new Prime Minister insists he’s got the courage to take on the tough decisions that need to be made.

But we all know Andy Burnham is not going to cut welfare or limit migrant labour.

He’s far too afraid of his Labour backbench MPs to wield the stick instead of the carrot to get Britain’s youths into jobs and, if it were up to him, he’d open Britain’s borders tomorrow to every EU worker who wants to come here.

Britain cannot continue to spend, spend, spend to pay people to sit on their backsides while importing millions of migrant workers from overseas.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Even a seven-year-old could tell the PM that the numbers don’t add up, while hard-working Brits have had enough of the stark unfairness of paying more and more in tax to fund our ever-expanding welfare class.



You would have to be stark staring mad to think we can carry on like this.

News.title: 'Tech giants must face heavy fines for spreading Liam Payne death images'
News.content:
'Tech giants must face heavy fines for spreading Liam Payne death images'

The Mirror told how Liam Payne's family took on social media giants "for sake of Bear" after photographs of the singer's lifeless body were published online

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Liam Payne had barely been dead for 90 minutes before his lifeless body was being paraded across the internet for strangers to gawp at. It was a sickening violation of human dignity that piled unimaginable cruelty upon a grieving family. The publisher eventually removed the photographs, but the damage was done. The images had spread across social media. Liam’s family should never have been forced to turn to courts in Argentina to protect his young son, Bear, from one day seeing such horrific pictures of his father. Their anguish echoes that of William Chapman’s family, who this week have pleaded for footage of his horrific death in a tiger enclosure not to be shared. Facebook, Google, X and other internet giants must be held accountable for allowing such material to circulate. There can be no excuses for failing to remove these images swiftly and permanently. Those who fail must face substantial fines and tougher legal sanctions. Grieving families deserve protection, dignity and compassion, not costly legal battles against powerful corporations. Human decency must always come before profit.

‌



‌



Get the flu jab

A simple jab can make the difference between life and death, particularly for older people. With nearly 4,000 flu-related deaths in England last winter, the importance of vaccination could hardly be clearer. The encouraging news is that vaccines prevented an estimated 7,100 deaths and 104,000 hospital admissions, protecting families while easing the enormous pressure on our NHS. These are remarkable figures and a powerful reminder of what modern medicine can achieve. As temperatures fall and flu cases rise, we urge everyone eligible to get vaccinated against flu, Covid and RSV. A few minutes at your GP surgery or pharmacy could spare weeks of serious illness, or worse. Protect yourself, protect your loved ones and help protect our NHS this winter.

Article continues below

Cheers, Joe

Joe Lycett knows the value of a good local, and he's putting his money where his mouth is. By buying 500 pints, the Traitor’s star is giving struggling pubs a much-needed boost. With locals closing daily, his gesture is a reminder of what we stand to lose.

News.title: Dangerous baby pool floats that could cause infants to drown being sold online, says Which?
News.content:
Dangerous baby pool floats that could cause infants to drown being sold online, says Which?

An investigation by the consumer champion found 171 of what it described as lethal products for sale on six online marketplaces - Amazon, AliExpress, eBay, OnBuy, Shein and Vinted

View 2 Images Which? identified almost 200 baby floats which it deemed to be dangerous

Potentially dangerous baby pool floats are being sold on popular online sites including Amazon and eBay, Which? has warned.

‌



‌



An investigation by the consumer champion found 171 of what it described as lethal products for sale on six online marketplaces - Amazon, AliExpress, eBay, OnBuy, Shein and Vinted.

‌



Many of the swim floats included in the investigation had canopies designed for shade - but Which? said that canopies and overhead structures can become unstable in winds, leading to a risk of them overturning.

‌



Amazon’s own AI chatbot even recognised that one baby swim float had serious safety concerns and warned against buying it. Which? said some of products appeared to be identical or pose the same risks to those in safety alerts issued by the Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS).

There are at least 14 alerts for swim floats with canopies on the UK government’s recall site. Meanwhile, Which? said 25 products found in its investigation looked similar to one that was involved in the death of a two-year old in the US.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 2 Images Which? has urged parents to be cautious

The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) warned consumers in April to stop using Relaxing Baby Swim Floats. Which? said these floats can flip over or submerge the occupant underwater, posing a risk of drowning to infants and toddlers.

There is not currently a UK alert for the Relaxing Baby branded float. Another variation of baby floats that Which? deems to be dangerous includes ones that have inflatable rings that fasten around a baby’s neck. Which? found 33 examples of these for sale.

‌



Sue Davies, Which? Head of Consumer Protection Policy, said: "Babies’ lives are potentially at risk because online marketplaces continue to operate what we see as an irresponsible business model that allows anonymous third-party sellers to list almost anything and face no consequences.

"We’ve seen time and again that they will not do enough to prevent the sale of unsafe products unless they are forced to. The government must stand firm against Big Tech lobbying and do what is needed to keep children safe.

"It must urgently use its new powers under the Product Regulation and Metrology Act to impose a clear legal duty on online marketplaces for ensuring the safety of products sold through their third-party sellers, with tough enforcement for those that fall short."

‌

A spokesperson for Amazon said: "Nothing is more important to us than safety, particularly when it comes to babies and infants. It's why we prohibit certain products from our store and have strict proactive controls on this category, which require independent third party lab testing and certification documents.

"We've removed the products in question and are investigating how these came to be available. We continuously monitor our store and we take swift action when we're alerted of potential issues."

‌



A spokesperson for AliExpress said: “Product safety is a top priority for AliExpress. Following notification from Which?, we immediately removed the flagged listings from sale in the UK and are rolling out additional category-level safety measures for baby swimming floats. We are committed to working with UK regulators and consumer organisations to ensure a safe shopping environment.”

A spokesperson for eBay said: “We’ve removed the listings identified by Which? and carried out further checks to identify and remove similar items. We'll be using learnings from these listings will be used to improve enforcement and detection to make filters stronger going forward.

"eBay uses technology, AI-supported monitoring and specialist teams, working closely with regulators, to help prevent unsafe products from being sold. Together, these proactive measures prevent millions of potentially unsafe items from being sold each year.”

‌



A spokesperson for OnBuy said: "Product safety is a top priority for OnBuy, and our Risk Team works closely with Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) to identify and remove unsafe and non-compliant products.

"The products identified have been removed from our marketplace, and we have initiated and are overseeing a recall to ensure affected customers are contacted and offered full refunds. We have also undertaken a wider review to identify and remove similar products. We continue to strengthen our product safety controls, including the adoption of new technology designed to identify and block potentially non-compliant products as they are created.

A spokesperson for Shein said: "We take product safety extremely seriously and are committed to providing a safe and reliable shopping experience for all our customers. As soon as we were informed of the findings, we initiated our established product safety protocols and immediately removed the products identified from sale as a precaution while we investigate. We have also initiated a site-wide review of similar products.

Article continues below

"All sellers on SHEIN Marketplace are required to comply with applicable laws and regulations, as well as our product safety standards. We have robust measures in place to prevent non-compliant products from being listed on our platform, and continuously strengthen these safeguards."

A spokesperson for Vinted said: “Under our Catalogue Rules, items prohibited by law or regulation are not allowed to be sold on Vinted. We take action as soon as we become aware of potentially prohibited listings, whether through our own detection tools or through reports from members.

"If a listing or a member’s behaviour goes against our rules, we take action. Depending on the case, this may include removing listings or suspending accounts. We care about the safety of our members, and are constantly working on our processes and policies to respond to emerging safety risks."

News.title: Bus crashes into train on French side of Channel Tunnel with 19 casualties
News.content:
Emergency services racing to the scene of the crash in France

Nineteen people have been injured after a train and bus collided on a loading platform near the entrance to the Channel Tunnel in Pas-de-Calais, France

Bus crashes into train on French side of Channel Tunnel with 19 casualties

A bus has crashed into a freight train on the French side of the Channel Tunnel.

French authorities said 19 people were injured in the crash, which took place at the Eurotunnel site in Pas-de-Calais. The coach driver is among those injured.

No deaths have been reported and no lives are in danger, officials said. The French emergency medical service (SAMU), a mobile intensive care unit (SMUR) helicopter, and the fire and rescue service (SDIS) are at the scene.

The last two Eurostar trains running between Paris and London today were cancelled because of engineering works, not the collision, according to Eurostar. Services are expected to run as normal tomorrow.

News.title: Muliple children killed after shooter opens fire at Oregon elementary school
News.content:
Muliple children killed after shooter opens fire at Oregon elementary school

The suspected shooter has been shot and killed, according to police. Multiple victims have been confirmed and children are among the victims.

View Image Children are among the victims after a shooter opened fire at an elementary school in the US (Image: Google Maps)

Children are among the victims after a shooter opened fire at an elementary school in the US.

‌



‌



The incident on Thursday, October 15, occurred at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon - a city of around 100,000 people. At least three children and one adult have lost their lives in the incident, CBS News reports.

‌



Police have confirmed multiple victims in the incident, with at least two people having been taken to a local hospital. Their condition is unknown.

‌



Silver Rail ⁠Elementary School serves grades kindergarten to fifth, with pupils aged around five to 11-years-old. It has ⁠about 450 students and 40 staff members, said Sheila Miller, communications manager for the Bend Police Department.

Police received a call about a man shooting into a car shortly before 1pm local time. About a minute later, multiple 911 calls came in saying that person had entered the school and started shooting, police said in a statement.

Police arrived within minutes and quickly reported that the shooter was dead. It is not clear who shot and killed the suspect, but Miller said it "may have been a bystander."

‌



CBS News reports that the shooter was believed to be a teenager who was killed by a Samaritan.

The school was placed in lockdown and residents asked to avoid the area.

Police were evacuating classrooms and said there would be a large law enforcement presence at the school.

‌



FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency's local office was on scene and assisting local law enforcement.

"We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy," Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook.

"We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence.

Article continues below

"No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing.

"Our immediate priorities are caring for our students and staff and assisting law enforcement and emergency responders."

News.title: Katie Price's ex-husband thought she was 'coaching' girl, 13, he allegedly raped
News.content:
Katie Price's ex-husband thought she was 'coaching' girl, 13, he allegedly raped

Kieran Hayler, whom Katie Price married in 2013 and divorced in 2021, is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault on the teenager

View 4 Images Kieran Hayler arrives at Lewes Crown Court (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Kieran Hayler has told jurors he thought his ex-wife Katie Price was “coaching” a 13-year-old girl he is accused of raping, after discovering messages she sent to the alleged victim. Hayler, 39, took pictures of messages on Ms Price’s phone when they were together in which she talks to the girl about Hayler fancying her, adding: “I will make you a little star.” Hayler is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault on the teenager in West Sussex in 2016. Giving evidence on Thursday, Hayler denied the allegations and said: “I believe they’ve been fabricated.” He told the trial that “trust had gone on both sides” of his marriage with Ms Price by mid-2013, and he admitted affairs with three other women during their relationship.

‌



‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 4 Images Katie Price, pictured arriving at court, was married to Hayler for eight years (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

‌



He told jurors “I am attracted to older women” and that all his significant relationships had been with older women. Hayler said Ms Price was also unfaithful during their relationship. He found messages she sent to the complainant in 2017 when he was looking for evidence of her having an affair with someone else, the court heard. He told jurors Ms Price had been accusing him of being attracted to 15 to 20 other people, adding: “I thought she would be using she thought I fancied other people to warrant having this affair.” Asked by his defence barrister Arlette Piercy why he took pictures of the messages between Ms Price and the complainant, he replied: “Because she made out that I fancied (the complainant). I thought, ‘This is a bit weird’.” He said he accessed her phone the same way she had accessed his, by using his fingerprint. Asked about what this showed, he said: “The relationship is breaking down.”

View 4 Images Hayler is accused of three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Article continues below

The court previously heard that Ms Price messaged the teenager saying she had heard that Hayler and the girl had kissed and he had “tried it on” with her, adding later: “I will make you a little star.” Asked in cross-examination by Ms Piercy about her use of the phrase “little star”, Ms Price said: “That’s a figure of speech.” On Thursday, Hayler said: “Everyone can interpret it how they want, it’s very pushy. It’s a very strange comment to make. I thought she was coaching her into (saying) something she shouldn’t. I didn’t send them anywhere, I took a picture on my phone.” He told the court he found the picture of the messages “recently” after taking his phones out of storage when moving home. He then sent them to his solicitor. Also on Thursday, Hayler pleaded not guilty to four alternative counts of sexual activity with a child after the close of the prosecution case. The four lesser charges were added to the indictment so the jury could consider them as alternatives to the three rape counts and one of sexual assault.

View 4 Images Ms Price gave evidence earlier this week (Image: Jim Bennett/PA Wire)

Judge Mark van der Zwart told the jury the “really important difference” between the charges was that the alternative counts have no reference to the “absence of consent”. The judge said: “It remains a matter entirely for you to decide if prosecution have made you sure any sexual activity took place between the complainant and the defendant Mr Hayler. “No suggestion whatsoever from myself you should find any particular verdict of the facts. The position of the parties remains unchanged.” He said the prosecution alleges the complainant was raped, while the defendant will maintain nothing sexual happened between them. If convicted, the offence of rape carries a maximum sentence of life imprisonment while sexual assault is up to 10 years. Sexual activity with a child has a maximum sentence of 14 years. Hayler denies all the charges and suggested his ex-wife had “launched a campaign” against him when their marriage ended and the allegations form part of this, the court has heard. He was married to Ms Price at the time of the allegations, before the couple’s relationship broke down in 2018 and they divorced in 2021. The complainant first contacted the NSPCC in 2021 over the allegations, and the charity referred her to the police. The alleged victim is not part of Hayler or Ms Price’s extended families. Hayler will continue giving evidence in the trial on Friday.

News.title: Yorkshire Wildlife Park to reopen after tiger attack as animal 'safe and well'
News.content:
Yorkshire Wildlife Park will reopen on Friday after former child actor William Chapman, 24, was killed when he jumped into the tiger enclosure last weekend

Yorkshire Wildlife Park to reopen after tiger attack as animal 'safe and well'

Yorkshire Wildlife Park has confirmed it is set to reopen following the deadly tiger attack last weekend.

William Chapman, 24, was mauled to death by a tiger called Altai after climbing into its enclosure. An inquest opening today heard Mr Chapman died from "multiple traumatic injuries", and his family had "expressed a number of concerns in relation to his contact with mental health services leading up to his death". Mr Chapman had been diagnosed with schizophrenia and suffered previous bouts of psychosis, but was living independently.

In an update this afternoon, Yorkshire Wildlife Park said it would reopen on Friday. It also confirmed again that Altai was "safe and well" and will not be euthanised.

"Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies remain with the family, friends and loved ones of William Chapman," the park added.

Mr Chapman filmed his last moments as he approached Altai, and posted it online. The inquest opening heard how he had scaled two fences to enter the pen.

Mr Chapman's devastated family, who were not at the inquest opening, have said he was "bright, warm, and engaging".

News.title: Manchester stabbing: Woman found 'murdered' after 'screams and crash' is named
News.content:
Alisha Samuels, 26, has been named as the victim

Alisha Samuels, 26, was found with 'serious injuries consistent with a stabbing' after police were called to Dorking Avenue, Manchester, at 2am - a man has been arrested on suspicion of murder

The young woman who was found dead in a Manchester suburb this morning, after neighbours heard screams and a car crash, has been named.

Alisha Samuels, 26, was found "with serious injuries consistent with a stabbing" following reports of a disturbance at around 2am today on Dorking Avenue in Newton Heath, Greater Manchester Police said.

A 25-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder. A 61-year-old man and a 38-year-old woman have been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. All three remain in custody.

Multiple witnesses told Manchester Evening News they heard a commotion before someone tried to drive away from the scene, with at least one vehicle caught up in a crash. One resident said a driver 'tried to smash into a police van' on Briscoe Lane.

News.title: 'Excess chlorine incident' at Dublin hotel as 10 children and one adult hospitalised
News.content:
'Excess chlorine incident' at Dublin hotel as 10 children and one adult hospitalised

The Dalata hotel group confirmed 10 children and one adult were taken to hospital after 'an excess chlorine incident' at the Clayton Hotel in Liffey Valley, Dublin

View 2 Images Emergency crews outside the Clayton Hotel in Dublin (Image: Dublin Live)

Ten children and one adult have been taken to hospital after excess chlorine leaked into a swimming pool at a hotel in Dublin.

‌



‌



The Dalata hotel group confirmed that "an excess chlorine incident" took place at the pool inside the Clayton Hotel in Liffey Valley.

‌



As many as 23 people were medically assessed after complaining of feeling unwell, with 10 children and one adult then hospitalised for assessment.

‌



An investigation into the circumstances which led to the incident is underway. The Dublin Fire Brigade set up a decontamination zone at the scene, Dublin Live reports.

"Today at 15:35, 15 October 2026, an excess chlorine incident occurred within the swimming pool at Clayton Hotel Liffey Valley," the Dalata group said.

‌



View 2 Images 11 people were taken to hospital (Image: Dublin Live)

"In accordance with Dalata Hotel Group emergency security procedures, emergency services were immediately notified and responded to the incident.

News.title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says
News.content:
Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.

It says when this is not "clinically appropriate" then alternative arrangements should be made and the dignity and safety of all patients should be maintained.

The guidance also says staff facilities should be used by people based on their biological sex, while trusts should ensure enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, such as single-occupancy toilets, are offered.

Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.

That meant that a trans woman â a biological male who identifies as a woman â could have chosen to be on a women's ward, or a trans man â a biological female who identifies as a man â could have opted for a men's ward.

That guidance was withdrawn following the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 that under equality law the term "sex" means biological sex and "woman" refers to a biological woman.

The judgment said for a space or service to be single sex it should only allow those of the same biological sex to use it.

Also under the new guidance issued on Thursday, NHSE emphasised that in order to avoid discriminating against trans people they should be offered gender neutral spaces.

But the guidance also says decisions may have to be made on a case-by-case basis and must ensure clinical needs are met.

It also makes clear that there are circumstances where clinical need is the overriding priority, including on emergency units and urgent care settings.

In addition to the patient document of the guidance, NHSE has published advice for trusts on how to organise changing rooms, toilets and other single-sex facilities for staff.

Again, it says they should be used by people based on their biological sex, not their gender identity.

The document encourages NHS trusts in England to carry out an audit to ensure they are offering enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, for instance, gender neutral or single occupancy toilets.

Pressures on hospitals mean many have already struggled to keep wards single sex.

NHSE data shows that the number of breaches of the previous mixed-sex accommodation guidance has been growing every year since 2021- where members of the opposite sex were placed on a single-sex ward.

The most recent figure for August 2026 shows there were 5,520 breaches, compared to 3,853 in June 2025.

Sex-based rights charity Sex Matters has welcomed the guidance as a "momentous shift back to reality", but is concerned about how it will be applied.

"NHS patient data is a mess, with potentially thousands of trans-identifying people recorded as the opposite sex," CEO Maya Forstater said.

Trans rights organisations TransActual and Trans+ Solidarity Alliance have said they are concerned NHS staff will be unclear on how to safely look after trans patients.

"This guidance will not survive contact with reality in resource-strapped hospitals and will create unworkable operational challenges," they said.

The NHS has been at the centre of a number of high-profile arguments over the interpretation of equality law and workplace regulations.

In January 2026, Darlington Memorial Hospital was found to have violated the dignity of a group of nurses who complained about a transgender colleague - a biological male who identified as a woman - being allowed to use the female changing rooms. The nurses were told they should change somewhere else if they objected.

The tribunal concluded that the trust had indirectly discriminated against them.

The nurses are currently seeking Â£400,000 from the NHS to cover their legal costs.

One of the nurses who brought the action, Bethany Hutchison, who is now president of the Darlington Nurses Union, says they welcome the "clear and necessary guidance" from NHSE, but the test will be whether trusts follow it.

"The Darlington nurses should never have had to take their own employer to court to secure privacy, dignity and lawful single-sex facilities," she said.

"Enforcement cannot continue to depend on the courage and personal sacrifice of individual nurses."

In Scotland, another employment tribunal found, in December 2025, that a nurse, Sandie Peggie, had been harassed by NHS Fife over its interpretation of rules on single sex spaces.

Peggie had complained about a doctor, who was a trans woman, using the female changing rooms.

She was suspended after raising concerns. The tribunal dismissed her other claims of discrimination and victimisation.

An appeal is under way and expected to reach the courts next year.

News.title: Russell Brand accuser says he turned 'monster-like' before alleged rape
News.content:
Under cross-examination Brand's barrister, Ian Winter KC put it to the complainant that when she first met Brand she welcomed his attention.

"I welcomed his company, not what followed," the woman replied.

He then suggested that she fell under his spell and that she wanted to spend more time with him.

The woman replied: "That's incorrect. I did not fall under his spell and I did not find him attractive. "

Asked by the defence why she agreed to go back to the hotel room with Brand, she responded: "I'm telling you... I thought he was a gay man, very softly spoken, very effeminate.

"I felt safe â I felt sexually safe with him. He was very intelligent and that appealed to me, not in a sexual sense. "

The woman became tearful a number of times while giving her evidence from the witness box.

At one point the judge told the witness to "take a moment, catch your breath", after she became emotional.

Brand's barrister later challenged the complainant about why she did not run back into the bathroom or leave the room when she realised Brand had removed some of his clothes.

She replied: "What was I supposed to do? Hide in bathroom? Walk out the room? Walk past him? I had no phone, no reception, no idea where I was. Run into the night with him following me?"

Referring to photographs she had taken of Brand, she said: "I took those photographs, he told me to take them, he was showing off, he was prancing around... I was scared... I couldn't fight him.

"I blame myself for allowing him back into my room," the woman said.

She was also challenged by the defence barrister about why she didn't report her allegation about Brand to the police in Bournemouth.

She said: "I didn't report it as I didn't want anyone to know. I didn't think anyone would believe me."

The woman told the jury that after she says she was raped by Brand she blamed herself "in that moment".

"I hate that I blamed myself, I shouldn't have to blame myself."

She also told jurors: "I regret to this day the error in judgment thinking this man would not rape me.

News.title: Why Harry and Meghan's UK relaunch felt so much like a royal engagement
News.content:
There was something so very familiar about today.

The first time the Duke and Duchess of Sussex visited Nottingham together in 2017 they were plain old Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. They'd just announced they were getting married and it was in the East Midlands that an American actress would be hard launched as a working member of the Royal Family.

You could view today as the UK-relaunch of Meghan.

She'd not done anything like the day of events in Nottingham for several years on British soil. Those close to her told me she wasn't nervous about how people would react to her and she wanted to get out there.

This was definitely not a royal engagement.

But the thing is, it felt like one in so many ways.

There was planned choreography for each event.

Harry and Meghan visited charities and met volunteers.

There was a shared media pool working together to distribute the best video and images.

There were crowds and walkabouts.

Buckingham Palace has made it very clear that they view the Duke and Duchess of Sussex as private citizens. Whatever they do is their own business - but it certainly won't have royal status attached.

There was no pomp and ceremony today. No line up of dignitaries. No obvious police presence.

It was still a reminder of what Harry and Meghan have to offer.

News.title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits
News.content:
Senior banking executives have told the BBC they expect the sector to be "on the menu" when the chancellor announces his Budget in two weeks' time.

John Healey has described the banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, yet has refused to rule out a raid on the sector.

The biggest four banks collectively made around Â£15bn profit in the first six months of this year, leading to calls from trade unions and others for additional taxes.

However, the banking sector trade body, UK Finance, warned that "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode".

The UK's biggest banks and building societies currently pay a surcharge of 3% on top of the baseline 25% rate of corporation tax, plus a levy on the assets held on their balance sheets.

The sector contributed nearly Â£40bn to the Treasury last year, if income tax on employees is factored in.

The bank levy generated Â£1.4bn last year and the surcharge a further Â£1.2bn.

There are a number of ways the chancellor could extract more money from the sector.

The 3% surcharge was reduced from 8% under Rishi Sunak, at the same time as he raised corporation tax from 19% to 25%. Returning the surcharge to its previous level could raise around Â£2bn a year.

The bank levy currently charges 0.1% on outstanding short-term loans and 0.05% on longer-dated loans, although mortgages are excluded from the calculation.

In the past banks have successfully argued that higher taxes would risk making the UK uncompetitive with other jurisdictions and would reduce their ability to lend, and therefore be anti-growth.

In truth, banks were pleasantly surprised they were not hit at the last Budget, given the large profits they have been making in recent years. Rising interest rates have expanded the margin between the rate at which they lend to customers and the rate they pay savers.

There is another option that has been discussed with Treasury officials. Currently banks can use losses from the past to offset against profits - thereby reducing their tax bill in any given year. Lloyds in particular has been a beneficiary of this policy, as large losses from the financial crisis have been used to lower tax bills ever since.

Some analysts and bank executives have pushed the idea of a moratorium on this practice for a few years, which would yield an estimated extra Â£1bn per year for the Treasury. That would provide a windfall while being "a lot more bearable", in the words of one bank executive.

It would also spare foreign banks from an additional hit, including JP Morgan, whose chief executive Jamie Dimon has warned that the UK already has one of the highest tax burdens on banks in the world. He warned that adding further sector-specific taxes could discourage investment and damage competitiveness.

However, industry leaders say any form of tax rise that hits UK banks and exempts foreign banks' operations in the UK would be hard to square with the government's push to back British business.

Whatever form it takes, banks believe the chancellor now has much more of an appetite to take a larger slice of their pie.

News.title: Watch: Swimmer's emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM
News.content:
Swimmer Archie Goodburn has been successful in his efforts to improve brain cancer care for patients as the UK government announce new measures.

The Scottish athlete, who was diagnosed with three inoperable brain tumours two years ago, met Prime Minister Andy Burnham after making an emotional plea on BBC Breakfast for more investment to be put into brain cancer research.

After the meeting, Burnham announced a new national brain cancer clinical lead and promised a review of brain cancer progress and action to get patients treatment sooner.

Goodburn, 25, thanked the prime minister and said all three of his requests have been "promised to some extent" but "fleshing out" needs to be done on the details.

The prime minister described the swimmer an "inspiration to us all" and said he was "delighted" to welcome him to Downing Street.

News.title: London housing project wins top architecture award
News.content:
Williamson told the BBC that until he went to study architecture he lived in a council estate in the East Midlands, "and every time I go back there all the council houses have been sold off, they're in private hands.

"Which in a way can be a good thing - we're in a homeowning democracy - but the sad thing is they haven't been replaced.

"Every time I go back - without getting too emotional - I think 'where would we have lived?'

"So to me that's why this particular project was important. I think a lot of people from that sort of background live in terrible accommodaiton - temporary accommodation which isn't safe or secure.

"These houses are fantastic and they're part of a mixed scheme so it's got a fantastic feel to it.

"For me it was a very inspirational, emotional, part of the process."

Duggan, who was brought up in south-west London, said the scheme "challenged conventional suburban housing layouts centred on roads, private gardens and clearly defined front and back spaces".

Winding paths and planting weave between the blocks, connecting them and linking shared outdoor spaces.

She said she wanted it to be a public space people felt they could belong to.

"Housing needs to be progressive. People who live in the building have access to green space, allotments."

The site fronts onto Lion Green Road, with low-rise green belt housing set on higher ground to the south and traditional suburban streets to the north.

News.title: Former DUP leader Donaldson sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sex abuse
News.content:
Jeffrey Donaldson has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for a series of child sex offences, including one count of rape.

The former DUP leader stood with his hands clasped in front of him in the dock of Newry Crown Court as his sentence was handed down.

Judge Paul Ramsey said Donaldson's crimes, which took place between 1985 and 2008, had led to a "catastrophic descent into disgrace".

He was sentenced to 11 years for his crimes against Victim B and four years for offences against Victim A.

The 63-year-old, who was convicted in June, is seeking to appeal his convictions.

Both sentences will run consecutively.

But Donaldson will spend only half his 15-year sentence behind bars.

Because the offences were committed before the Criminal Justice (Northern Ireland) Order 2008 came into effect, he qualifies for 50% remission.

Should his attempt to appeal his convictions fail, it means he will be released from prison at the end of 2033.

The remainder of his sentence will be under supervision in the community on licence.

News.title: Man killed by tiger climbed two fences before suffering multiple injuries, inquest hears
News.content:
Brookes told the hearing: "He was approached by the tiger and the ensuing physical contact between the tiger and Mr Chapman led to him sustaining multiple traumatic injuries which rapidly led to his death."

Park staff secured the tiger and paramedics attended but confirmed his death at the scene.

The senior coroner said her office was awaiting a more substantial report as to the extent of his injuries.

South Yorkshire Police provided a number of witness statements from the public and staff who were at the wildlife park at the time, the hearing was told.

Mundy instructed staff to contact Yorkshire Wildlife Park to ask them to keep any relevant CCTV and inform the coroner of any previous visits by Chapman to the park.

After opening the inquest, which Chapman's family chose not to attend, on Thursday morning, Mundy adjourned proceedings until 18 March 2027.

Speaking after the hearing, a neighbour of Chapman told the BBC he was "very polite and well-spoken" and a "lovely man".

Josh, 24, who lived in the same building as Chapman, said: "He'd always have a laugh and a joke. He was quite well kept, he'd look after himself physically. He loved his F1, he'd talk for hours about his F1 if he could."

Discussing the online comments and speculation in the aftermath of the incident, he said: "People didn't know him. If you don't know him, don't make a comment."

News.title: Severe drought declared in parts of southern England
News.content:
South East Water's operations director Douglas Whitfield said standpipes remained part of the company's drought plan but were unlikely to be needed.

Whitfield said a wet winter had been forecast but timings were not clear and the firm was making any adjustments it could to protect supplies.

Whitfield said South East Water, which supplies more than two million customers, said 92 repair crews were out across Sussex and Kent tackling leaks to minimise loss from the network.

In an email sent to customers South East Water said it was optimising water pressure across the county and had more than doubled the number of teams tackling leaks in the region, increasing from seven to 16.

It said the number of leaks in the affected area had fallen from 181 to 97 and that more than 1,300 leaks had been repaired since 1 April.

Wessex Water, which supplies customers from Wimbleball, introduced its first hosepipe ban in 50 years in August and said the restrictions would remain in place for the foreseeable future.

The water company said it had increased leak repairs, moved water into the area from more resilient sources and adjusted water pressure in some communities to conserve supplies and urged customers to continue using water carefully.

Will Willoughby, director of water supply at Wessex Water, said: "We saw record levels of demand through the network - and it sustained above the 400 million litres a day for 48 days, which is far and away the toughest year that we've seen in terms of that height in demand."

He said customer impact "should be none" but encouraged customers to continue to be mindful about water usage.

Paul Tompkins, deputy president of The National Farmers' Union (NFU) said it had been a "torrid year for farmers", where the conditions proved "very difficult" to harvest crops, provide water for livestock, and a "potential dry winter could have implications for next year's crops".

News.title: Farage defends Reform's vetting after councillors filmed making racist comments
News.content:
On a different day in the ITV broadcast, Feeney is joined by two other Reform candidates, Jamie Campbell and Chris Whelan, who discuss speculation of a mosque being built in the local area.

"There's got to be a way of stopping them - like, go and buy some pork chops; we'll bury it in the ground," Campbell is heard saying in the film.

Whelan says "we'll take pictures of it", prompting Feeney to add: "I was gonna say, 'Unfortunately, this is a pig cemetery, mate'."

Discussing a female Reform candidate from Birmingham, Feeney is heard saying, "I didn't know where to look", before Whelan adds: "I'd have been sniffing that seat as soon as she got up."

The BBC has tried to contact Feeney for a response. ITV has reported that on Monday evening he had "mutually agreed" to resign from Reform UK, citing "personal reasons" and would be continuing as an independent councillor.

The BBC has contacted Campbell and Whelan, who has resigned as a councillor, for a response.

A Reform UK Solihull spokesman condemned Feeney and Whelan's "misogynistic and offensive comments" and confirmed they were no longer Reform councillors.

The spokesman said Campbell's comment "was a joke in poor taste but with no malicious intent", adding: "It's something that he deeply regrets, and the party will not be taking any further action."

Elsewhere in the film, Dean Miller, a councillor in the south London borough of Bromley, is shown campaigning for Reform in the Makerfield by-election.

"We've been ethnically cleansed out of London because you never used to get any blacks over in Bromley," he tells an ITV undercover reporter. "And now, you know, Bromley's like massive Nigerian communities there."

Miller says he is "not racist", before later adding: "The Muslim thing, that is going to be that thing that takes over everything and then everyone just has one religion. Because, apparently, King Charles is a [expletive] Muslim... I think that's [expletive] traitorous."

ITV reported that Miller would now sit as an independent councillor having resigned from Reform and had told them in a statement that he was heavily medicated due to a chronic pain condition when he made the comments.

The BBC has contacted him for comment.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Reform should take "immediate and firm action against those who've been revealed to be making these abhorrent comments".

He added: "There is no place for any form of racism, antisemitism, discrimination in British politics, and we all should be relentless in repeating that and taking the firmest possible action."

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "We should be asking why there's so many stories like this of people in Reform who are making these appalling comments."

Asked about one of the individuals being a former Tory councillor, she said: "It's not my problem anymore."

Badenoch added: "I don't want people like that in the Conservative Party. I'm glad they have gone."

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said: "This is chilling. I feel for anyone watching this tonight who is frightened to see such racism and hatred festering in their community."

A Green Party spokesman said: "Vilifying migrants and Muslims is Reform's main focus, and these racist comments reflect party policy."

News.title: Fifty arrests in crime probe after fatal A66 crash
News.content:
A total of 50 people have now been arrested as part of a wider police operation against organised crime following a fatal crash.

The arrests have been made after the head-on smash on the A66 on Teesside which killed seven people, including two police officers.

Ten of the 50 arrested are alleged to be linked to the Volvo reportedly involved in driving into two properties in the early hours of 22 August, police said.

Det Ch Sup Helen Barker of Cleveland Police, said: "Over the last two months, we have identified 50 people who we believe are associated within criminal networks that seek to cause serious violence and harm within the community through the supply of drugs."

The force said shotguns, hand guns, machetes and ammunition had also been seized, as well as Â£60,000 worth of class A and B drugs and more than Â£30,000 in cash.

Barker said: "Our pursuit of this criminality will continue, and I want to take this opportunity to thank the community for their support and patience but also for the information that we keep receiving.

"I want to encourage you to keep on reporting behaviour that is related to drugs or organised crime - no matter how small - and be assured we will act."

News.title: Mother of Henry Nowak killer could be deported
News.content:
The mother of murderer Vickrum Digwa could be in line for deportation from the UK, the Home Office has signalled.

Kiran Kaur, 53, was jailed for three years in July for removing the knife used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill student Henry Nowak from the crime scene.

However Kaur, who spent several months on remand, could serve less than half of her sentence and be freed around the anniversary of Mr Nowak's death under the Government's early release scheme, ITV News reported., external

The Home Office and Ministry of Justice declined to comment on individual cases, but said: "We will always seek to deport foreign criminals at the first opportunity."

Kaur, who is an Indian national, could be eligible for the government's deportation scheme.

She is also appealing against her sentence, with a hearing scheduled at the Court of Appeal on 5 November.

Kaur's son Digwa was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years on 1 June for the murder of the 18-year-old student, after falsely claiming Mr Nowak had racially abused him in Southampton on 3 December.

Some 5,000 prisoners are scheduled to be released in stages over the next year, down from 6,000 after ministers intervened to exempt rapists and the most serious child sex offenders.

Ministers say the expanded early release scheme is needed to prevent the justice system from collapsing, after a summer when the issue dominated news headlines.

Some 650 criminals were this week released from prisons around the country under the scheme, less than two weeks after 700 were set free early.

The Home Office said: "Our thoughts remain with the family and friends of Henry Nowak, whose life was cruelly cut short in a horrific act of violence."

News.title: King Charles praises Welsh 'sense of belonging' as he opens Senedd
News.content:
King Charles III has praised Welsh people's "sense of belonging", as he and Queen Camilla officially opened the Senedd's seventh term.

The visit marked the King's first official meeting with First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth following the election victory of Plaid Cymru - a party rooted in a strong republican tradition.

In his speech to the Senedd, with most of its 96 members in attendance, including opposition parties Reform, Labour and the Tories, the King also expressed concern for the impact of climate change on the Welsh countryside.

About 30 protesters by the steps of the Senedd were vocal throughout the royal visit, and one was arrested on suspicion of breaching the Public Order Act.

Chants of "not my King" and "down, down, down with the crown" could be heard from protesters during the visit.

Wales' national poet did not take part in the ceremony as had been planned, after Senedd officials rejected the poem she had written for the event and cancelled her performance.

The King used his visit to the Senedd to say he would return to Wales next week to visit Aberfan - scene of the 1966 coal tip disaster and meet a survivor who had been pulled from the rubble aged six.

A 21-gun salute in Cardiff Bay marked the King's arrival in the city, and Plaid leader ap Iorwerth greeted the King on the Senedd steps, together with Presiding Officer Huw Irranca-Davies and Labour Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock, who represented the UK government.

News.title: Tributes paid to crew of fishing boat missing off Lewis
News.content:
Isles MP Torcuil Crichton said Craigie's devastated family were now planning his funeral, and the islands would miss the "sparkle" of his wit and charm.

Crichton told BBC Radio Scotland's Drivetime programme: "These men were part of their own community as well as the fishing community of the islands.

"I last came across Douglas Craigie at the Western Isles Fisherman Association Conference last year in Uist, which will no longer sparkle with his wit and charm this year.

"Today would have been his 50th birthday and his family are devastated planning a funeral instead of a party."

Crichton said Murray is a well-respected member of the community of Ness in the north of Lewis, and is one of the Men of Ness who harvest young gannet known as guga.

The MP said Morrison, who is also a guga hunter, is the "kind of young person we try to encourage to go to sea to keep on this age old tradition of fishing".

News.title: Taxi driver given fake cash drove customer to police
News.content:
A man was arrested after a taxi driver who was given fake cash drove the suspect straight to a police station.

Nottinghamshire Police said the driver picked up the suspect from Nottingham Road at 23:30 BST on Tuesday.

When the customer continued to change his route, the taxi driver asked how he would be paying, which is when he was handed a counterfeit Â£20 note, the force added.

After questioning the customer and being given further fake notes, the driver took him straight to Radford Road police station.

The force said officers also carried out a search of a man's address, where they discovered a "Rambo knife" under his mattress.

It added no further counterfeit cash was recovered, but a cannabis cultivation kit was seized from the address.

A 23-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of using counterfeit currency and possessing an offensive weapon in a private place.

News.title: Another man admits raping woman drugged by husband over 20 years
News.content:
Another man has pleaded guilty to raping a woman who was drugged and abused by her husband without her knowledge for over 20 years.

Graham Brougham, 74, is the oldest of 13 men who were charged with sexual offences against the victim after being allegedly invited into her home, in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, to abuse her by her husband.

The husband, in his sixties, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife - including rape - and has given a witness statement detailing "what he says happened".

Brougham, from Northwich, was told by a judge at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court that he "should be under no illusion his sentence will be custody and a long time in custody."

The victim, who held hands with a family member, watched on from the public gallery as Brougham answered "guilty" in the dock to a charge of raping her in September 2024.

News.title: Four killed and shooter dead after gunman opens fire at Oregon elementary school
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in
