Five people, including three children and the suspect, are dead following a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday afternoon.

Officers were alerted around 1 p.m. local time after receiving a 12:59 p.m. report of a shooter firing into a car outside the facility, according to police. Emergency crews brought the injured to a local hospital. Within a minute of the initial call, law enforcement received multiple 911 reports of an active shooter inside the building.

Bend Police arrived at the scene by 1:02 p.m. — just two minutes after being notified that officers needed to respond to a critical scene — and the shooter was down seconds later. Officials noted that the gunman may have been shot by a bystander, though the suspect’s identity, total victim count and specific weapon used remain under investigation.

The incident prompted an immediate lockdown of the school while police vehicles, fire trucks and ambulances swarmed the grounds. Authorities are working on safely evacuating roughly 40 staff members and 450 children enrolled at Silver Rail Elementary to a designated reunification point at Journey Church.

“As you can imagine, the process of getting all of those people safely out of the building and down to Journey Church is a real challenge,” police told reporters during a news conference, asking for patience while officers thoroughly clear each section of the school. A large crowd of parents and community members gathered outside as the search and evacuation continued.

open image in gallery Following a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary, authorities are working to safely transport roughly 450 students and 40 staff members to a designated reunification site at Journey Church in Bend, Oregon ( Reuters )

In a statement, Steven Cook, the superintendent of Bend-La Pine Schools, offered his condolences to the community.

“We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy,” Cook said. “We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence. No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing. Our immediate priorities are caring for our students and staff and assisting law enforcement and emergency responders.”

Federal authorities are also aiding local police with the response. FBI Director Kash Patel stated on social media that the bureau’s Portland field office is on the scene to support the investigation, adding that the agency “will make every resource they need available.”

open image in gallery The incident prompted an immediate lockdown of the school while police vehicles, fire trucks and ambulances swarmed the grounds ( Reuters )

Oregon Governor Tina Kotek similarly said she was “closely monitoring the situation at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend,” expressing gratitude for the first responders on site and promising further updates as more information becomes available.

The Bend Police Department is serving as the lead agency on the investigation.

This is a developing story. More to come...

News.title: New law could see children taught how to stop ‘life-threatening bleeding’ after stabbings and car crashes
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Schoolchildren could be taught how to treat severe bleeding following stabbings or car crashes if a proposed new law successfully passes through Parliament.

Under the legislation, pupils would be taught how to recognise "life-threatening bleeding" and administer emergency treatment, alongside learning how to effectively respond during a crisis.

The Emergency and Life-Saving Skills (Schools) Bill is scheduled to be debated in Parliament on Friday, but will need government support to pass.

The Bill, put forward by Conservative MP Neil Shastri-Hurst (Solihull West and Shirley), aims to expand upon the life-saving skills currently taught in schools, which already include CPR.

Mr Shastri-Hurst is a former British Army major who also previously served as an honorary consultant trauma co-ordinator at Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Birmingham.

He said: “It’s about stop the bleed training. In a similar way that we have created a critical mass of individuals who know how to do CPR when somebody has a cardiac arrest, and that is in one way, shape or form embedded in the curriculum. Kids leave school knowing that.

“If we can train a critical mass in terms of how to recognise catastrophic bleeding and how to deal with it, that is going to save a huge number of lives, because the average time for, even in an emergency, an ambulance to come is about eight-and-a-half minutes. But you can bleed out in four.”

He added: “I would see people coming into a major trauma centre at the QE in Birmingham, one of the regional trauma centres that we have in this country, in the most acute extremis and if some of those individuals had intervention at the scene prior to an ambulance arriving and that paramedic or pre-hospital care being delivered, it is entirely foreseeable that some of those individuals who didn’t survive, may have survived.

open image in gallery Life-saving skills such as CPR is already being taught in schools ( Getty/iStock )

“It would have given them a fighting chance.

“This is literally one of those scenarios where minutes matter.”

The Conservative MP said the charity Citizen Aid had already trained 1,000 children in a school in a single day between him and a couple of volunteers.

Citizen Aid was founded by consultant trauma surgeon Sir Keith Porter and Major General Tim Hodgetts, the former surgeon general for the armed forces.

Mr Shastri-Hurst said the skills could be applied in the aftermath of a range of incidents, from a car crash to a sporting injury or terror attack.

He said the key thing to do in the immediate aftermath if there is serious bleeding would be to apply pressure to stem it.

If that does not work, make a tourniquet with anything appropriate, from a belt to a tie, to a shoelace, and twist it to build enough tension to stop blood flow.

Mr Shastri-Hurst said: “It’s giving people the confidence not just to know what to do, but have the confidence to put that into action.

“It’s a low-tech set of training, you can do most of it with a drainpipe, a bit of foam and, as I say, a tie or a bandage or a handkerchief and a spoon.

“You can do the basic training on stop the bleed in about 10-15 minutes. They then go and explain it to their families, and all of a sudden you are building up a critical mass of individuals who know how to do it.”

He added: “It’s around building up our national resilience, and part of that national resilience is having a society that knows how to respond in an emergency.”

News.title: These types of extreme pornography will be banned from November
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Pornography that depicts strangulation and incest will be banned from early November, the government has announced.

The content will be outlawed from November 6 after cross-party pressure about the negative impact on women and girls led ministers to announce the new laws earlier this year.

It means pornography which depicts strangulation or suffocation, sex between people who are related or pretending to be related, or when somebody is pretending to be a child under 16, will be illegal.

Justice minister Alex Davies-Jones said: “This government has a commitment to halve violence against women and girls in a decade. For many people, it is still easy to access harmful pornography online.

“From November 6, it will be illegal to possess or publish pornography showing strangulation or suffocation, sexual activity between certain relatives, or adults roleplaying as children under 16.

“This isn’t about criminalising harmless sexual preferences. But porn can shape what people think a healthy relationship looks like, especially young people.

“Content that normalises, or even glorifies, violence against women is dangerous and can blur the line with what is acceptable in real life.”

Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin made the recommendations in her review into pornography regulation which reported in 2025.

She said the news came “not a moment too soon”, after previously saying strangulation in porn had become “totally normalised”.

Lady Bertin’s report found pornography which shows women being choked can have “devastating” real-world consequences.

Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin ‘not a moment too soon’ ( House of Lords )

It highlighted “disturbing” role-play, including incest and adults portraying children. Both will be banned.

A study by the Institute for Addressing Strangulation in 2024 found more than a third of 16 to 34-year-old adults had reported being strangled or choked at least once during consensual sex.

A survey by the same group last year found 43% of 16 to 17-year-olds, who are sexually active, said they had been subjected to it.

In her report, published in February 2025, the Conservative peer said there had been a “total absence of government scrutiny” of the pornography industry.

Lady Bertin previously said that strangulation had “gone into the bloodstream” of society and it should be “wiped out of the culture”.

Non-fatal strangulation is already an offence in its own right, but it is not illegal to show it online.

She said: “It is very good news these offences will come into force, and not a moment too soon.

“This change in law alongside better enforcement and stronger regulation will send the unequivocal signal not only to the companies that host and facilitate porn but also to wider society that extreme and violent content that encourages real-life harm is not acceptable.”

Ms Davies-Jones said: “Young people especially deserve better examples of what healthy relationships look like. Real intimacy is built on respect and trust, not abuse.

“If you’ve got this material, delete it. If you’re sharing it, stop.

“It’s not as harmless as you may think, and after 6 November it is criminal.”

News.title: Older Brits warned ‘not to be complacent’ and get flu jab after thousands of deaths last winter
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Older people are being urged to receive flu vaccinations after modelling indicated nearly 4,000 deaths in England were caused by flu during last winter.

Age UK called on older people to "not get complacent" and ensure they get all the vaccinations they are eligible for.

Figures from the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) annual report indicate excess deaths from flu reached 3,798 last winter.

Caroline Abrahams, charity director at Age UK, said: “Nearly 4,000 deaths linked to flu in a single winter is a stark reminder that these seasonal viruses should never be dismissed as just a bad cold, particularly in later life.

“The latest evidence shows that vaccination prevented thousands of hospital admissions last winter and helped reduce the pressure on NHS services at one of the busiest times of the year.

“If you are offered a flu, Covid-19 or RSV vaccination this autumn and winter, we strongly encourage you to take up the opportunity.”

The report also found that England’s vaccination rollout prevented an estimated 104,000 hospital admissions along with 7,100 deaths.

This occurred even though overall vaccine efficacy among adults dropped from the previous winter down to between 21% and 34%.

Among children, who often transmit flu to older groups and can fall severely ill, vaccine effectiveness was recorded at 51% to 68%.

open image in gallery Ask your GP if you are eligible for any vaccinations (Alamy/PA)

UKHSA data also showed the RSV vaccine was about 82% effective at preventing hospitalisations for adults aged 75 to 79.

RSV is a common respiratory virus causing typically mild, cold-like symptoms, though it can ultimately prove fatal to older people.

Although flu cases are currently low, hospital admissions in September have been higher than in the same period over the last four years, according to the UKHSA’s first weekly winter respiratory virus surveillance report.

Ms Abrahams added: “These vaccines can reduce your risk of becoming seriously ill and help you stay well, independent and active throughout the colder months.

“Many older people are already facing challenges this winter, including concerns about energy costs, keeping warm and managing existing health conditions.

“Having the vaccinations you are entitled to is one practical step you can take to protect your health.

“I would also encourage friends and family members to check that older relatives know which vaccinations they are eligible for and help them to arrange appointments if needed.”

Commenting on the UKHSA data, Andrew McCracken, director of External Affairs at Asthma + Lung UK, said the sooner people can get your flu jab, the better.

“The flu season has started and the sooner you get your vaccine, the sooner you will be protected. That’s especially true for older people with chronic lung conditions, who are particularly vulnerable,” he said.

“Catching flu doesn’t just mean a few days in bed. If you live with an existing lung condition, flu can trigger life-threatening flare ups leading to emergency hospitalisation.

“The latest evidence shows that people living with chronic lung conditions are seven times more likely to die from flu.

“Everyone with a chronic respiratory condition in England is now eligible for a free flu jab and taking it up as soon as possible is the best way to keep yourself safe and well.”

Separate UKHSA figures published on Thursday suggest flu is currently circulating at low levels, having previously shown signs of an early rise in infections.

Hospital admissions for flu in England currently stand at 1.9 per 100,000 people, unchanged from a week ago and roughly the same rate as this point in 2025.

Flu levels last year went on to peak at the start of December, which was earlier than usual.

Dr Jamie Lopez-Bernal of the UKHSA said the agency would be “closely tracking” all the major respiratory viruses throughout the winter, including both flu and Covid-19, to “spot trends early and keep the public informed”.

He added: “While currently these virus levels are low, we can’t easily predict what may happen over the coming weeks and vaccination remains our best defence.

“If eligible, book your free NHS flu, Covid-19 or RSV vaccine or ensure your child receives their easy and painless nose spray flu vaccine as soon as possible, before viruses start circulating more widely this winter.”

Health minister Dame Diana Johnson said: “During the winter months, dangerous viruses spread more easily, posing an increased risk to older people and those with existing health conditions, who are more vulnerable.

“I am proud to support Age UK’s campaign and encourage everyone who has not yet come forward to book life-saving vaccinations against flu, Covid-19 and RSV as soon as possible.”

Dr Amanda Doyle from NHS England said that more than seven million people have already had their flu vaccine, adding: “If you’re eligible for a free NHS flu vaccination, including if you’re pregnant or have a young child who is offered the vaccine, please do come forward as soon as possible to help protect yourself and those around you.”

News.title: Who was the gunman who opened fire at Oregon elementary school leaving four dead?
News.content:

A gunman is dead after opening fire at an Oregon elementary school on October 15.

Police rushed to Silver Rail Elementary School around 1 p.m. after receiving reports of an “active shooter.”

Law enforcement arrived within two minutes, officials said. The shooter was dead shortly after police got to the Bend, Oregon, school. A department spokeswoman said a bystander may have shot the suspect - but that detail still needed to be confirmed.

Four people were killed in the shooting, and the gunman was shot at the scene. Police have said that children are among the victims.

As police continue to investigate the shooting, here is everything we know about the suspected gunman:

open image in gallery A shooter is dead after opening fire at a school in Bend, Oregon. Police have not released the suspect’s name ( Reuters )

Who was the suspected gunman?

Police have not released any details about the shooter, including the person’s name. The shooter was killed at the scene soon after the gunfire began.

What was the motive?

Authorities have not detailed a motive and say the shooting remains under investigation.

How many victims were there?

Four people were killed in addition to the gunman.Police have said that children are among the victims.

open image in gallery Four people were killed in addition to the shooter at Silver Rail Elementary School ( Reuters )

Where did the shooting happen?

The shooting happened at Silver Rail Elementary School, which is along SE Stone Creek Lane in Bend, Oregon. The school serves about 450 students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

Bend is in central Oregon and about a three-hour drive from Portland. The city has a population of nearly 100,000 people. It is the county seat for Deschutes County.

How have elected officials responded to the shooting?

Several officials have spoken out after the shooting.

“We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy,” Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook. “We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence. No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing. Our immediate priorities are caring for our students and staff and assisting law enforcement and emergency responders.”

FBI Director Kash Patel stated: “FBI Portland is on the scene and assisting our local partners in the investigation regarding an earlier shooting at a local school. We will make every resource they need available.”

News.title: BBC licence fee to be extended with ‘YouTube tax’ to force more to pay
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The government is set to unveil plans to extend the BBC licence fee to online streaming services in what is unofficially being dubbed a “YouTube tax”.

A white paper on the BBC charter renewal will be published before Christmas and will include proposals on how to overhaul the current funding model to increase revenue and reflect how audiences consume content.

A senior Whitehall source told The Independent the plan is to expand the licence fee to streaming platforms to prevent people dodging it by logging on to the internet via their phones, tablets or computers.

open image in gallery The BBC is currently negotiating its charter renewal ( Reuters )

Currently, anyone who uses a television to watch content must pay the licence fee even if they do not watch the BBC. They also pay for live television on any platform but not playback or delayed television except on BBC iPlayer. Under the proposed changes it would be expanded to cover all other online providers, such as Netflix, Amazon, Disney+, YouTube, which are currently exempt and all streaming content.

It is understood any new cash raised under the plan will need to be spent on reviving local journalism and tackling misinformation, which has fuelled the rise of parties such as Reform UK.

The Whitehall source explained that the move was “because people are able to use them to avoid paying currently”. They added: “It’s not fair that people are essentially able to watch television content but avoid the licence fee.”

The source said there had been a “hold-up” with the charter renewal talks under the previous administration. “But now we have had a change of prime minister, we are able to press ahead with the plan to expand it to streaming platforms”, they added.

The new arrangements have been dubbed the YouTube tax because the site is by far the biggest online video platform in the UK, with around 55 million users with 79 per cent penetration in the British market.

The proposal would be a means of helping tackle the crisis facing the BBC amid fears that millions of people will stop paying the licence fee, which is currently £180 a year, but free for people aged 75 and older who receive pension credit, and 50 per cent discounted for the visually impaired.

open image in gallery Culture secretary Lisa Nandy’s department is leading the talks with the BBC ( PA )

It comes as the BBC has announced that it will launch its news channel on YouTube.

It also follows the BBC director-general Matt Brittin’s comment that he wants BBC News to be on streaming sites such as Netflix in a bid to reform how the broadcaster’s content is consumed and paid for.

Mr Brittin previously said the corporation was being “held back” by its TV licence fee, which was “no longer fit for purpose”, and suggested it could be replaced by a household levy.

Speaking on the BBC One’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg, he emphasised the need to modernise the current funding model to ensure it is fair and reflects how audiences consume content.

He said: “What we need to look at is the current model. You pay the licence fee if you watch live TV or you’re on iPlayer.

“I’d like to see reform that allows us to be where audiences are. I think BBC content should be on Netflix, on YouTube, on TikTok, on Spotify, and Instagram, and everywhere where audiences are.

“Particularly news, actually, which I think is part of disinfecting misinformation. It’s our job to be everywhere.”

The most recent figures revealed that around 539,000 fewer TV licences were in force in the year to 31 March 2026. There has been a drop of around two million over the past five years.

The BBC has been facing spending cuts with question marks over flagship programmes such as Newsnight, which recently cut 10 per cent of its staff. Despite collecting around £3.8bn to £3.9bn from the licence fee, the BBC recorded an operating deficit of £121m for 2025/26.

It is estimated that an extra 3 to 4 million households will have to pay the licence fee if it is extended to streaming services.

However, the Whitehall source warned the increased revenue from the levy would not be able to fill gaps in its spending.

“The money needs to be used to help support local journalism and counter a lot of the conspiracy theories and fake news which we have seen help parties like Reform getting elected in different parts of the country,” they said.

A BBC spokesperson said: “We have consistently argued that the current funding model is outdated and needs reform. We will continue to engage with government to secure a new charter that provides sustainable, sufficient and universal funding so the BBC can deliver for audiences for generations to come.”

The royal charter is being renegotiated by culture secretary Lisa Nandy’s Department of Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) and sets out the arrangements for the governance of the BBC, including how it is funded.

The charter has to be renewed every 10 years and the current one is set to end in December 2027.

A DCMS spokesperson said: “The BBC must be funded by a model that is sustainable and fair to all those that are paying it.

“Through Charter Review, we are looking at a range of options, including how the licence fee could be reformed, but no final decisions have been made.”

Reform UK is facing a fresh crisis after a new undercover sting shows Nigel Farage appearing to let off a mayoral candidate accused of racism.

Secretly filmed footage showed Mr Farage telling his director of communications, Ed Sumner, that the party’s mayor candidate for Hampshire and the Solent, Chris Parry, must apologise to David Lammy for a social media post in which he said the then-deputy prime minister should “go home to the Caribbean”.

The footage cuts to Mr Sumner saying to Mr Farage “you’re protecting him”, before the party leader says: “It’s showing a bit of... bit of sorrow. Look, ‘I’m sorry’ is probably a good thing to hear. Just take the f***ing deal.”

In the social post in January regarding speculation that the government could be considering talks about reparations for slavery, Mr Parry had wrote: “Lammy must go home to the Caribbean where his loyalty lies.”

At the time, Labour described the remarks as “racist and grossly offensive”. Mr Parry later apologised “for any distress or offence” caused.

The footage, part of a documentary by ITV Exposure to be screened on Sunday night, captured the conversation between Mr Farage and Mr Sumner following a press conference where the party leader said Mr Parry should apologise.

open image in gallery Secretly filmed footage shows the Reform UK leader’s Director of Communications accusing Mr Farage of “protecting” the party’s mayoral candidate for Hampshire and the Solent, Chris Parry. ( ITV )

The footage showed Mr Farage saying Mr Parry “must apologise to Lammy”, before Mr Sumner tells him they had written him a text that he’s “not too happy with”.

Mr Farage said: “No, I'm sure, but he must do it and move on…Tell him that from me.”

When the Reform UK leader left, Mr Sumner said: “He's lucky, if it was up to me, I'd have kicked him out f***ing months ago.”

Mr Parry was later suspended after he appeared to liken a Jewish neighbourhood watch group to “Islamists on horseback” following an arson attack on Jewish community ambulances.

Mr Sumner told ITV News: “Nothing in the excerpts [of filming] discloses any wrongdoing, criminal activity or breaches of Reform UK policy by me… I do not endorse extremism or bigotry, or any concealment of extremism and bigotry”.

open image in gallery Mr Parry was widely condemned after he urged then-deputy prime minister David Lammy to “go home to the Caribbean” ( Reform UK )

Labour has condemned the footage as “shocking and deeply disturbing”, and told Mr Farage he needs to “urgently explain why he allegedly stood by [Mr Parry]..... instead of kicking him out of his party”.

“These latest shocking and deeply disturbing revelations go right to the top of Reform UK, Nigel Farage needs to wake up and realise the buck stops with him,” Labour party chair Bridget Phillipson said.

“Time and again Farage has had every opportunity to demonstrate leadership and get Reform’s house in order and every single time he has failed.

“In Reform’s own words: they’re defending the indefensible. They are completely unfit for office.”

Other revelations, which come a day after the same investigation secretly filmed councillors calling Muslims “parasites” and describing Black children as “animals”, include Reform MP Sarah Pochin saying senior party officials “just exclude you if you are a woman”.

Speaking at a time she was the party’s only female member of parliament, Ms Pochin said in response to being told a new female press officer was starting work: “Oh thank f*** for that. God! We so need women press officers… They are so f***ing chauvinistic.

open image in gallery Reform MP Sarah Pochin said senior party officials “just exclude you if you are a woman” ( ITV )

“I go out on all the shows and go ‘Oh no, it’s lovely, oh they’re all so welcoming’. Sh**... they just exclude you if you’re a woman...

“It’s really tough being a girl with all of this alpha male sh** going on.”

A Reform UK spokesperson said Ms Pochin had raised concerns about her experience, and “those concerns were taken seriously”.

“Reform has come a long way as a party. We’ve grown enormously in a short space of time, and we’ve been working to address issues as they arise,” they said.

An undercover reporter was also told to delete their social media account if they were considering running to be a Reform UK councillor.

In a vetting interview with the chair of a local Reform branch in Chester, Ian Frost, the reporter told him he had posted on social media in support of Tommy Robinson.

Mr Frost replied: “Anything where you've got, things, Tommy Robinson or anything like that, okay, I would delete the account and I'd start again.”

Reform UK said it is “extremely concerned” that ITV and Hardcash Productions have “used extreme methods of deception”.

“There is no room for racism in Reform UK,” they said. “We always respect due process of investigations and whilst these are ongoing it would not be appropriate to comment on individual cases.”

The Independent approached Ms Pochin for comment.

News.title: Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Economy slows before Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
The Chancellor said banks are too often seen as “distant financial institutions”, in a sign he will not raise taxes on the industry in the Budget.

John Healey has faced pressure to impose a windfall tax on bank profits to help rebuild an expected decline in his wiggle room in the public finances.

John Healey said: “My observations on the banks are just that people too often see them as a big distant financial institutions when they are hardwired into the economic fabric of this country and our future prospects.

“That said, you know I’ve got decisions to take in the Budget, and I will. I’ll set those out in two weeks’ time.

“And my special responsibility as Chancellor is to protect the resilience of the British economy for the future. That the resilience that the IMF has reported on this week by upgrading our growth figures in the UK this week, that the welcome monthly growth figures published this morning reinforce, and importantly, alongside that, the IMF reports said that Britain stands out for our deficit reduction plans, and will have his forecast actually a reflection not just on forecast plans but performance over the last couple of years. You know, a consolidation plan in place and underway.

“I’ve said from day one and week one, and I’ve had Andy Burnham in lockstep alongside me, I will meet those fiscal rules in full.

“That will be part of the Budget that I set out in two weeks’ time, and I think the IMF report reinforces that that is not just a not just a reinforcing the strength of Britain’s position, but something that they say they want to see other countries doing as well.”

News.title: Ukrainian Vampire drones drop food on town besieged by Russian army
News.content:
On Ukraine’s front lines, drones are the deadliest weapons in Kyiv’s arsenal, hunting Russian soldiers one by one with chilling precision.

But across the Dnipro River, the same machines have been given a very different mission: keeping trapped civilians from dying of starvation.

Since March, Ukrainian drones have been flying food and medicine into occupied Oleshky, on the river’s left bank, where residents are surviving on grass and weeds.

The town is less than three miles from Kherson, a city battered by Russian drones and shelling.

Since December, Oleshky has been under an effective blockade. Its roads are mined and shops have closed, with no food arriving by road since late May. Humanitarian agencies are blocked from entering, and the health system has all but collapsed.

Only around 2,000 of its 24,000 pre-war residents remain. For them, the drones are now their only lifeline.

“With the onset of winter, the situation is only getting worse,” said Elvina Osmanova of the Kherson regional military administration. “Food supplies are running out. People are facing a life-threatening choice: risk their lives trying to find food outside the city or remain without food.”

News.title: Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle
News.content:
When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

News.title: Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six
News.content:
Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Second Ebola case confirmed in Kenya
News.content:
Kenya has recorded its second-ever case of Ebola after a relative of a patient who died last week tested positive for the virus, officials have said.

A 39-year-old man fell ill on Tuesday and has since been confirmed to be infected with Ebola, according to Kenyan health authorities.

The patient, who is now isolated, is a family member of Kenya’s first-ever Ebola case, who died in a hospital in Nairobi last Monday.

The index case, a 40-year old businessman, had travelled to Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the deadly outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has so far killed more than 4,300 people.

Kenyan authorities have identified 128 of his contacts and have successfully tracked down 113 of them, who are having their temperatures checked daily for a period of three weeks, the country’s Director-General for Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said in a statement.

“There is no evidence of spread in the wider community,” the statement, issued on Wednesday, added.

However, questions remain over whether more cases will crop up in the coming weeks.

News.title: I tried Apple’s new smart home hub – the brand faithful will love it
News.content:
HomeView can control smart lights, heating, security cameras and video doorbells via touch or voice, but devices must support Matter – the cross-brand smart home standard. That means you aren’t confined to Apple-approved gadgets, but you are still limited – Ring video doorbells, for example, aren’t Matter-compatible, so they won’t work with HomeView, which could be a deal-breaker for even the biggest Apple fan.

But for anyone put off by the complexity of setting up a smart home, Apple is trying to simplify things. It has partnered with LG on Home Collection – a range of devices, including security cameras and a video doorbell – that connect with a single tap, just as AirPods do with an iPhone. They won’t be available until later in the year, but they could mark a major step towards making smart home set-up less complicated.

My early verdict

HomeView is built for the Apple faithful: set-up requires an iPhone or iPad, personalised AI features need a recent Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, and some apps work only when your phone is nearby. In a household split between iPhone and Android, Android users will get a much thinner experience, and Apple’s own services come first at every turn.

Still, HomeView is the most polished smart display I have seen. Face recognition makes it both a great shared and personalised device; the sound quality is excellent; and Siri AI is finally worth talking to, especially when it can draw on your personal context. I’ll need to live with it for a few weeks before giving a final verdict, but so far it’s a beautifully designed device I’d be happy to invite into my home.

News.title: Ed Miliband calls for ‘new deal on debt’ as developing countries face spiralling borrowing costs
News.content:
Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has called for a “new deal on debt” as spiralling borrowing costs force developing countries to spend more on interest payments than on education or health.

In a speech in Bangkok on Wednesday, Mr Miliband warned that the global financial system is failing emerging markets, and promised to use the UK’s diplomatic heft to push for urgent reform.

He said: “The short-term repayments are crippling, and while many are not defaulting on their payments they are being forced, if you like, to default on the lives and prospects of future generations.

“So we need a new deal on debt, a deal that supports countries to repay over longer time horizons and, crucially, refinancing with better rates to give developing countries precious fiscal space.”

Although public debt is not inherently problematic, servicing costs are at a 25-year-high – squeezing government coffers just as conflict, climate change and a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño push food and fuel prices ever higher.

Emerging economies in particular have little headroom: according to the Rockefeller Foundation, average interest payments now exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing nations, while UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) analysis found 3.7 billion people live in countries where debt servicing costs exceed spending on health or education.

At the same time, overseas development aid (ODA) spending from wealthy countries has plummeted – hitting social, infrastructure and humanitarian projects, and disaster response.

The mounting global debt pile has dominated discussions in Bangkok this week, where some 15,000 people have descended for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings.

This included the first meeting of the newly formed Borrowers’ Platform on Monday. A group of finance ministers and central bank governors from some 30 countries, it was formed to exchange ideas about how to deal with debt burdens – and how to avoid pitfalls.

Sports.title: Rutter scores twice as Brighton win big and go top in Conference League
Sports.content:
Georginio Rutter scored twice and set up one as Brighton thrashed Kauno Zalgris 4-0 to get their Conference League campaign off to a winning start.

Brighton were dominant from the first whistle to the last against the Lithuanian Cup winners and took the lead through Rutter, but only after a VAR check. The ball had initially been deemed to have gone out of play before Ibrahim Osman's cut-back to the Frenchman, but the goal was awarded after review.

Image: Brighton and Hove Albion's Jack Hinshelwood (second right) is embraced by his team-mates

Rutter then turned provider as Brighton doubled their lead on the stroke of half-time when Hinshelwood - returning to the side for the first time since the Premier League opening weekend - slotted into the corner.

The third came after a lung-bursting run from Malick Yalcouye, who played Osman through to cross for Rutter to turn into the net with ease.

Matt O'Riley made it four with a header as he scored his first Brighton goal since August 2025. The Australia international should have got his second with another header late on, but was denied by an excellent save from Tomas Svedkauskas.

Image: Kauno Zalgiris' Yukiyoshi Karashima (left) and Brighton and Hove Albion's Costinha battle for the ball

It is now five straight wins in all competitions for Fabian Hurzeler's side who host rivals Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

'Convincing win for Hurzeler's side'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Sophie Evans:

"A convincing win for Fabian Hurzeler's side as they kick off the club's second chapter in Europe in style. The fans around the stadium are already confident of a strong run in this competition, chanting 'we're going to go to Istanbul'.

"The Brighton boss joined his team in applauding this evening's home support. He said that their energy would be crucial in making the Amex a fortress for the opposition this season.

"It's five wins in a row in all competitions for the Seagulls. They were already the favourites to win the Conference League and their dominant performance this evening will only drive that narrative."

Key moments from the Amex Stadium...

3: CLOSE! Costinha heads over from six yards out! Excellent early opportunity for Brighton.

14: SAVE! Gross shoots from the free-kick, but his effort is tipped over by the goalkeeper!

32: CLOSE! Dunk whips a shot at goal from distance that goes just over and lands on the roof of the net!

35: SAVE! Gross with an excellent delivery from the right for Hinshelwood who heads into the ground forcing the goalkeeper to make an acrobatic one-handed save.

43: GOAL! Rutter opens the scoring after turning in Osman's cross. The goal is awarded after a VAR check.

45+1: GOAL! Rutter turns provider and crosses for Hinshelwood who produces a tidy finish across the goalkeeper to double Brighton's lead.

49: SAVE! Gross picks out De Cuyper with a lovely ball, the substitute crosses on the volley for Hinshelwood whose header is tipped over.

53: GOAL! Rutter scores his second of the night after a quality ball from Yalcouye to Osman who cuts back for the Dutchman to apply the finish.

67: GOAL! O'Riley heads across the goalkeeper and into the net to make it 4-0 to the home side.

79: SAVE! Costinha with a header at the back post. Well saved by the goalkeeper!

82: SAVE! O'Riley's bullet-header is saved brilliantly by the Kauno Zilgris goalkeeper.

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Serbian tennis player handed 24-year ban for match-fixing
Sports.content:
A Serbian tennis player has been handed a massive 24-year ban for match-fixing.

Stefan Milicevic led a "corrupt network" of match-fixing between 2022 and 2024, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), with the 29-year-old shown to have fixed six matches - five of which he played in - and attempted to with six more.

Milicevic, whose highest ATP ranking was 1338, did not engage or co-operate with the investigation, according to the ITIA, and was also fined 70,000 US dollars (£52,800).

The ITIA's statement on Thursday said: "Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network during the same period, resulting in a number of other players fixing matches."

Milicevic's suspension will officially come to an end on October 8, 2050, by which time he would be 53 years old.

The ITIA added: "While suspended, Milicevic is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association."

Sports.title: LIV Golf accuses DP World Tour of interference in bankruptcy process
Sports.content:
LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of interference in its bankruptcy proceedings at a hearing in which Bryson DeChambeau and others were released from their contracts.

The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch next year with new money from BC Partners Capital after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support having ploughed in $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.

But in order to do that it has had to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and, as a result, it has had to cancel the contracts of the existing players so they can be re-signed on new terms to LIV 2.0.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking to the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Rory McIlroy says LIV Golf was 'half a good idea, executed poorly', and admits he felt the breakaway series 'wasn't good' for the game

However, the DP World Tour confirmed this week it was taking a harder line than previously and any player committing to LIV 2.0 would be ineligible for its membership and therefore also ruled out of Ryder Cup contention.

It has been seen in many quarters as an attempt to deliver the final blow to LIV's fading hopes of survival and, according to reports in the US media, its attorney Robert Fitzgerald told the US Bankruptcy Court in New York: "We're continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we're quite concerned by it frankly.

"The timing in particular strikes us as a clear attempt to interfere with our process, with our players and potentially our reorganisation writ large."

Guy Kinnings, CEO of the DP World Tour, said in a statement on Monday: "Players need to make a choice. As we have said for many years, we have rules and regulations which are there to protect our Tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our Tour."

Also at the US Bankruptcy Court hearing in New York, Judge Michael B Kaplan also approved a motion to reject the current contracts of 19 golfers after LIV stated they "do not reflect the contemplated compensation structure under LIV 2.0".

Image: Bryson DeChambeau is technically without a contract currently due to LIV's application for Chapter 11 bankruptcy

It means the likes of DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Bubba Watson and Lee Westwood are free to pursue other options should they wish.

Jon Rahm's release, confirmed at the hearing, has seen him give up all claims against LIV's bankruptcy estate, reported to be up to $150m (£113m).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Inci Mehmet explains why Jon Rahm is to quit LIV Golf after deeming the terms offered for the proposed relaunch of the breakaway series 'unacceptable'

LIV has given up nearly all rights to use Rahm's name, image, likeness, trademarks and branding going forward, while Rahm has retained control of his LIV team Legion XIII's intellectual property and trademarks.

The next hearing in LIV's bankruptcy case is scheduled for October 20, with a deadline for player commitments agreed between LIV and BC Partners set for October 25.

Sports.title: Martinez apologises for outburst after Wilcox talks
Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology for his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Spain, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad and said he expected more from "upstairs" after he singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.

Sky Sports News understands Martinez met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, on Thursday. Head coach Michael Carrick was also present at the meeting.

In a statement released on Thursday night, the defender said: "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager.

"It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

The club now consider the matter closed as they prepare for Leeds on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

On Wednesday, Martinez issued a statement to clarify his outburst, but did not apologise.

Where does this leave Man Utd?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan brings the latest update on the situation around Manchester United and Lisandro Martinez

Sky Sports News' reporter Dan Khan:

"In pre-season, the players all spoke about how close this group has been since Carrick was appointed.

"This will now really be tested. At least one player confronted Martinez after his comments.

"On balance, I spoke to Harry Maguire and others this season, who have talked about the need to bring in as many players as possible.

"Where this leaves the changing room? We'll have to find out. But for Carrick, this is the last thing he needed.

"Now they have to face another distraction as the pressure mounts on the head coach."

'No internal pressure on Wilcox'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Dave Reed updates fans on which Manchester United players will be out of contract in the summer

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

Manchester United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Sky Sports News has been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Sports.title: Blood clot rules Eagles QB Hurts out of Panthers game
Sports.content:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out of their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday due to a blood clot in his calf.

The Eagles said in a statement on Thursday that Hurts was injured in their Week Four defeat to the Los Angeles Rams on October 4 when he took a boot to his calf area, which led to the discovery of the clot.

The Super Bowl 59 MVP practised on Friday last week, before the team left for London to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

In the meantime, Philadelphia are set to turn to backup QB Tanner McKee against the Panthers.

The Eagles have already dealt with numerous injuries this season, but hope that running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and No 1 wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) can return on Sunday.

Sports.title: Garcia set to face Lopez next after emphatic Benn win
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is set to face Teofimo Lopez in his next fight after his emphatic victory over Conor Benn last month.

Garcia defended his WBC welterweight title with a second-round stoppage of British contender Benn in Las Vegas and is now holding talks for a fight against Lopez, Sky Sports News understands.

Fellow American Lopez also holds a world title in the same division after he sealed a majority decision win over Rolando Romero to claim the WBA belt in August.

Image: Teofimo Lopez became a world champion again after a win over Rolando Romero

Lopez has been ordered to defend his WBA title against Lancashire fighter Jack Catterall, but is pressing ahead with a fight against Garcia instead.

Benn is yet to confirm his next move after the second loss of his professional career against Garcia.

His long-term trainer Tony Sims has confirmed that Benn will never fight again at welterweight.

The 30-year-old announced on social media that he will spend some time away of the ring, although he continues to be linked with a trilogy fight against Chris Eubank Jr.

Sports.title: Martínez apologises to Manchester United’s director of football Wilcox after outburst
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martínez has apologised for claiming that Jason Wilcox, Manchester United’s director of football, failed to strengthen sufficiently in the summer window after discussions with the manager, Michael Carrick, and club hierarchy on Thursday.

While any disciplinary action taken against him will not be made public by the club, it is thought that Martínez has been fined.

The defender’s apology came on Thursday evening after the 28-year-old failed to offer one when issuing an initial statement on Wednesday regarding his outburst following Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League loss at Atlético Madrid.

He posted on Instagram: “Today I met with the club’s leadership and the manager. It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

The apology is a considerable climbdown. After the Atlético defeat, Martínez was scathing of Wilcox and his recruitment in the last window.

He said: “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Wilcox]. As players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.”

Martínez claimed that Carrick had not been backed sufficiently. “I don’t think so. He does his best. You can’t keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas?” he said.

While it is understood Martínez’s apology was his decision alone, United spent £155m in the market – all on midfielders, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, and Carlos Baleba, despite Wilcox targeting a left-back.
