The wider squad agrees with Martínez’s stance regarding recruitment and has been left frustrated following a poor start to the season, with Carrick under considerable pressure.

A return of six points from six league games is United’s poorest since 1986 and Carrick’s side have already been eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Brighton.

Sports.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
Sports.content:
An impossible dream realised in the Vitality staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors had pushed hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s injury-time penalty extended the celebrations.

Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.”

Bournemouth’s new head coach has described the chaos of English football, midfield areas that can resemble a rolling maul but he has pledged to learn and adapt. “I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation,” Rose said. “If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it’s hard to beat us. That’s what we should take into the next game.”

Missing Junior Kroupi so far this season, and lately Alex Scott are regrettable problems within a small squad. Selling Scott for £80m in January, as has been speculated, speaks to the financial balancing act clubs such as Bournemouth must perform to progress. Following the 5-1 loss to Chelsea, Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Sunderland was prioritised in team selection though the second-half introduction of key men, including Rayan, proved decisive. “Everyone deserves to play and it’s good for us for the busy weeks to have a competitive squad,” said Rose, who revealed Smith had given a speech to his teammates following Stamford Bridge. “That’s my captain.”

View image in fullscreen Rayan doubles Bournemouth’s lead six minutes after coming off the bench. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Smith supplied the first proper chance. Marcus Tavernier, cutting inside, shanked that wide before a Ben Gannon-Doak cross from the byline saw Rodríguez misjudge the flight. The summer signing, raw at 22, finds decent positions only for touch to betray him. His penalty, following an inadvertent handball from Jon Gorenc Stankovic, his first goal, should help his confidence.

Graz, fourth in this season’s Österreichische Bundesliga, hardly exuded ambition, a defensive trio often morphing into a shell-like five. Amid such squeezed space, following a corner, Bournemouth had the ball in the net, for what seemed an own-goal though it had struck Bafode Diakité’s arm. Tavernier struck the outside of a post, before Graz at last began to advance. The away contingent celebrated a penalty but Belmin Beganovic was yellow-carded for simulation. Fabio Ingolitsch, the Graz coach, a Rose protége, spoke to his own team’s realities by saying: “Bournemouth is the team with the biggest market value in the Europa League.”

Another Smith cross supplied Evanilson’s goal, a header full of neck muscle looping off the angle for a first European goal celebrated in Boscombe. “Many more to come from him,” said Smith of the perpetual motion No 9. Graz fans sang whatever the game state, that being the continental way, but there became more to encourage them beyond the break. Simon Seidl’s shot whistled wide, Jürgen Heil struck a post before Jacob-Peter Hödl forced a remarkable reflex save from Dorde Petrovic for the rebound. The spectre of Premier League travails, where positive play has been unrewarded, loomed as Graz interchanges became crisper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The 70th minute triple introduction of Rayan, Justin Kluivert and Ryan Christie proved Rose’s successful attempt to both lock down midfield and increase his team’s attacking threat.

Rayan, a decent finisher when coming inside, snatched the contest from Austrian reach. Daniil Khudyakov, Graz’s Russian goalkeeper, first flapped at a corner and then got only a weak hand to the Brazilian’s drive through the proverbial forest of legs. Bournemouth’s European homecoming had been coupled with the victory the occasion had demanded.

Sports.title: Noah Sadiki stunner earns Sunderland dramatic late win against Torreense
Sports.content:
Three minutes into stoppage time Noah Sadiki hurdled a set of advertising hoardings, sprinted across a running track and hurled himself towards the ecstatic Sunderland fans.

Just as those supporters’ long-awaited party in Portugal had looked in peril of falling a little flat, the Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder capitalised on excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka to half-volley an eye-catching first goal for Régis Le Bris’s side.

It ensured a largely unconvincing Sunderland came from behind to secure a second straight Europa League win and their relief was evident as every outfield player followed Sadiki in vaulting those hoardings to join the celebrations.

“It was a difficult game,” said Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, with considerable understatement. “Torreense are a good team.”

With their home ground too small to accommodate European football, Leiria’s stadium stood in. It proved quite some substitute. An arena overlooked by a 12th-century castle constructed to defend this attractive medieval town against reconquest by the Moors created an imposing backdrop to Sunderland’s first competitive trip to the continent for 53 years.

Back in 1973 they were second division FA Cup holders. Torreense know the feeling. Having provoked widespread shock by beating Sporting to win the Portuguese Cup last spring, Luís Tralhão’s second-tier side relish their underdog status.

After winning at Lillestrøm last month, Torreense aimed to keep the surprises coming and duly left a heavily rotated Sunderland trailing at the break. Le Bris had left, among others, Xhaka, Le Fée and Nordi Mukiele on the bench ahead of Sunday’s vital Premier League trip to Bournemouth. This reshuffle permitted Luke O’Nien, a survivor from League One days, to captain Sunderland at a ground transformed into a sea of red and white. Although only 4,000 official tickets were allocated to the visitors more were readily available locally and estimates suggested the formal allocation had doubled.

As the sun dropped and the temperature fell from a high of 28C those fans watched a disjointed first half on Sunderland’s part. It seemed telling that the normally fairly impassive Le Bris looked distinctly, and unusually, irritated and frustrated at times.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland supporters enjoy their club’s first competitive trip to the continent for 53 years. Photograph: Ana Brigida/AP

Granted his humour was hardly helped by the referee’s penchant for detecting phantom Sunderland fouls but ominously Malick Fofana, a £30m summer signing from Lyon, struggled wide on the left. Ditto Nilson Angulo on the right wing.

Torreense, 15th in Portugal’s second tier might not have been threatening Robin Roefs’s goal but they succeeded in blocking and clearing pretty much everything that came their way. Indeed Tralhão’s defence looked almost as well fortified as that ancient castle towering over them.

Admittedly, midway through the first half Timur Tutierov, Sunderland’s centre-forward, thought he had headed the opener but that effort was disallowed due to shirt pulling on Omar Alderete’s part.

Then, with the interval fast approaching, Le Bris adopted hand-on-hips mode as Torreense reminded everyone precisely why they have built such a giantkilling reputation by scoring with their first shot.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It came from centre-back Volnei Feltes. With Sunderland losing concentration and standing off, he was permitted to advance unopposed before cutting in on his right foot and sending a sublime 20-yard curler into the top corner.

Although Angulo forced Lucas Paes into a fine save he, like Fofana, was soon replaced as Le Bris made a quadruple substitution involving the introduction of Le Fée, Xhaka, Mukiele and Reinildo.

This infusion of quality left Torreense a little groggy and the midfielder Jules Ahoka –a highly impressive 20-year-old £8.5m summer buy from Royal Antwerp – was able to equalise by heading his first goal for Sunderland courtesy of Mukiele’s deft dink.

View image in fullscreen Jules Ahoka scores Sunderland’s first goal against Torreense. Photograph: Luis Loureiro/Shutterstock

When the lively Tutierov went down in the box, the referee immediately pointed to the spot. However, a linesman’s flag indicated an offside so it seemed there would be no penalty. Or at least not until the video assistant referee intervened – lengthily; the eventual conclusion was no offside, no foul and no penalty.

No matter; when Le Fée dinked a gorgeous ball into the box and Xhaka played it into Sadiki’s path, the scorer waited for it to drop across him before applying the expert finishing touch on the half-volley.

Sports.title: Europa League: Lyon take down Crystal Palace as Benfica overwhelm Celtic
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage endured a frustrating return to Lyon in the Europa League as his Crystal Palace side lost 3-2 to his former employers at the Groupama Stadium.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half without a shot on target for the visitors. Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the Ligue 1 side’s two-goal advantage. The Palace substitute Daichi Kamada pulled one back with nine minutes remaining in a better second half for Palace, who could not find an equaliser.

Days after beating his predecessor, the Nottingham Forest manager, Oliver Glasner, at Selhurst Park in the Premier League on Sunday, Sage found himself returning to the home of the club he managed for 14 months.

Ismaïla Sarr, who claimed the Conference League golden boot last season, was in the Crystal Palace starting lineup for the first time this season.

Celtic found a clinical Benfica side too much to handle during a 4-1 defeat in Lisbon. The Colombia striker Jhon Durán scored for the hosts with a penalty after just five minutes having been fouled by Dane Murray and completed his double in the 35th minute, after the defender Alexander Bah had doubled Benfica’s lead earlier in the half.

Martin O’Neill’s side were cut apart at times but could have scored themselves on a couple of occasions before the break. The visitors eventually reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute through a brave header from Camilo Durán – who had joined up with the squad late after remaining in Glasgow for the birth of his second child – but they could not close the gap any further before the substitute Vangelis Pavlidis fired in a fourth for the home side with two minutes remaining.

Quick Guide Conference League roundup Show Georginio Rutter got Brighton’s campaign off to a flying start and sent a message to his manager, Fabian Hürzeler. Rutter has lost his place to Charalampos Kostoulas and was making his first start since the opening day of the season against the Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris. The French forward responded by scoring twice and creating another as Brighton cruised to a 4-0 victory at the Amex Stadium, with Jack Hinshelwood and Matt O’Riley also on target. Hearts suffered a frustrating start to their campaign as Nordsjælland scored a late equaliser to secure a 1-1 draw in an entertaining encounter at Tynecastle. The home side went ahead through Oisin McEntee’s close-range finish in the 33rd minute and had several chances to add to their lead. But they lost their way in the closing quarter of the match and Nordsjælland, fourth in the Danish Superliga, claimed a point through a deflected strike from Nicklas Røjkjær. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Randal Kolo Muani scored a stoppage-time header to give Juventus a 2-1 win at Celta Vigo which leaves them top of the standings. Hugo Álvarez had put the home side in front early on before Nick Woltemade equalised on the hour and Kolo Muani then nodded in from close range during the second minute of added time.

Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at RB Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick by the Italian teenager Alphadjo Cissè. Milan’s record signing Gonçalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the shine off the win for Ruben Amorim’s side.

View image in fullscreen Milan’s Alphadjo Cissè points to the crowd after scoring the opener in a 4-0 win at RB Salzburg. Photograph: Martin Divíšek/EPA

Bayer Leverkusen put themselves top of the standings after the early kick-offs as they followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan. The Czech striker Patrik Schick was on target twice from the penalty spot in the first half, either side of a Malik Tillman goal, to ensure the points were wrapped up for Carles Martínez’s side before the interval. Ibrahim Maza added a late fourth.

Real Sociedad followed up their opening defeat at home to Bournemouth with a 1-1 draw at Union Saint-Gilloise.

Sports.title: Alex Scott quits Disney+ role as Women’s Champions League presenter
Sports.content:
Alex Scott, the former Football Focus host, has left her role as a presenter of the Women’s Champions League coverage on Disney+.

It is understood it was Scott’s decision to walk away and focus on other projects, including her new show, One More Word WSL, with her fellow former England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams.

Scott had fronted the streaming platform’s coverage of the elite women’s European club competition since it obtained the rights in 2025. However, Disney’s production levels were criticised after the opening round following a series of technical problems. These included an unscheduled advert break that interrupted the second half of Arsenal’s 1-0 win over HB Køge for more than three minutes.

A spokesperson for Disney+ told the Guardian: “We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the Uefa Women’s Champions League on Disney+. Her passion for the women’s game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success.”

Scott, a former England and Arsenal defender and former contestant on the BBC’s Strictly Come Dancing and ITV’s I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!, has also presented major sports shows for the BBC, including coverage of the 2020 Olympics. Scott’s representatives said: “Alex is grateful for the opportunities she has had to work with the team at Disney+ and hopes that they continue to work together in the future.”

Scott presented the BBC’s Football Focus show for five seasons before its closure this year. At the start of this season’s Women’s Super League campaign she launched One More Word through her own production company, First Cap Productions, and has previously explained that show was createdin response to the BBC cancelling its weekly WSL highlights show.

Scott, who turned 42 on Wednesday, told the Observer, this month: “I feel like there’s always an excuse about women’s football shows not working because of the viewership or needing to save money. Whereas I think if they are done right, they can work, if things are given a fresh idea or a fresh format, they can work.”

In the same interview, discussing some of the criticism aimed at Disney’s Women’s Champions League coverage this term, Scott said: “Ultimately, do I agree with all the decisions that were made? Absolutely not. Did I try and advise? Yes, but I can only do so much.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“But nobody sees the conversations, the fights I have behind the scenes. But I can hold my head up and know that I’ve always tried my best for the greater good of women’s sport.”

Sources have told the Guardian the presenter’s relationship with Disney remains positive. Disney, whose coverage is produced by ESPN, secured an exclusive five-year deal to broadcast the Women’s Champions League across European broadcast territories in 2025. It is understood its presenting team will continue to include Shebahn Aherne, Nedum Onuoha and Lianne Sanderson. The lineup includes commentators such as Vicki Sparks and Jacqui Oatley. The competition resumes on 28 October.

Sports.title: Apologetic Infantino ‘not fit’ to lead Fifa, claim European FA heads after meeting
Sports.content:
European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, with the heads of the English and German football associations questioning his fitness to govern after a three-and-a-half-hour council meeting.

Infantino began the long-awaited gathering of Fifa’s 37-strong executive board by apologising for failing to consult them over his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan but failed to provide answers to dozens of questions posed by the European FAs on a range of subjects including the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, Donald Trump’s Fifa peace prize and the Folarin Balogun affair, when the USA striker’s World Cup suspension was overturned after lobbying from the US president.

Infantino’s apology was followed by a 30-minute presentation on FFE from two American lawyers, who described the $20bn (£15.1bn) valuation and proposed sale of a 20% stake to Thrive Capital as a good deal for Fifa. At the insistence of some attenders, the lawyers were asked to leave the meeting after they had presented. When questioned, one of them confirmed he had been commissioned and paid by Fifa to produce a review of FFE.

Quick Guide How do I 

“The main objective for Gianni was to survive this meeting and nothing more,” one council member told the Guardian.

Council members succeeded in deferring, until they receive more information on Balogun, a Fifa proposal to amend its disciplinary regulations by removing the scope for players shown a straight red card to have it rescinded. Infantino pledged to provide that information by their next meeting in Doha on 16 December, after nominations close on 18 November for March’s presidential election.

The issue of whether the Fifa peace prize will be revived this year or Trump left as a standalone winner has been referred to Fifa’s social responsibility committee, and the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, has been appointed to chair a new committee examining governance reform. But otherwise the meeting broke up without tangible answers, to the frustration of the English FA’s chair, Debbie Hewitt.

“We didn’t get answers to anything that we had specifically requested,” Hewitt said. “I think the man [Infantino] has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions, he’s not fit to be Fifa president. That was what was shared in the meeting.”

The German FA’s president, Bernd Neuendorf, went further by calling for wholesale reforms of Fifa’s administration, which he hopes will fall within the purview of Sheikh Salman’s governance committee.

“The whole administration has to be reformed and the whole governance has to be reformed,” Neuendorf said. “But I’m pretty clear here that this is not possible with Gianni as the responsible person at Fifa. So we need a complete restart, I think, a political restart of persons who represent Fifa.

“Yes he apologised, but I didn’t have the feeling that this apology was because of the FFE project in total. My impression was it was just because it wasn’t brought forward to the council and no one was involved.”

Neuendorf also said he was “very confident” that an alternative candidate would be found to stand against Infantino, a view shared by senior figures at Uefa, who expect a late declaration to limit the amount of time for Fifa to scupper the nomination.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The respective presidents of the three continental confederations who have called for Infantino to go – Aleksander Ceferin of Uefa, Victor Montagliani of Concacaf and Sheikh Salman – have ruled themselves out and suggestions that high-profile figures such as Arsène Wenger or Michele Kang could put themselves forward have been dismissed.

A proposal to distribute $3.5bn (£2.6bn) from Fifa’s financial reserves, which would involve each national association receiving $25m over the next four-year cycle, was approved by council.

Montagliani is also understood to have been critical of Infantino, but Fifa’s president received strong support from council members from Asia and Africa.

“I am certain that Gianni Infantino is the right president,” Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritania Football Federation said. “The majority want Gianni Infantino to stay. After finally withdrawing this proposal, president Gianni Infantino apologised to the members of the executive committee. This was followed by a responsible debate, during which this issue was more or less shelved.

“In the interests of football, the executive committee is looking ahead and seeking solutions, by focusing on the good aspects that football has to offer and trying to move forward.”

Sports.title: Vinícius claims he is targeted by referees and says flair players need protection
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior is not happy with how he is being treated by referees and wants more protection for talented players such as himself, Lamine Yamal and Julián Álvarez.

Vinícius spoke out after Real Madrid’s 4-3 come-from-behind win at Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday. The Brazil forward also acknowledged he was going through a slump, but said he had “no doubt” he would regain his best form soon.

The match against Roma came hours after he was handed a four-game suspension in the Spanish league after being sent off for pulling the hair of an opponent and for protesting against the referee. “I don’t recall any other player receiving a four-match suspension,” he said. “I tried to move the player in front of me out of the way, and I ended up getting caught in his hair.

“That was it – a red card – which is why I was so surprised. I didn’t say a single offensive word to the referee that would warrant a four-match ban. But when it comes to Vini, it’s all too easy. The opposing team will always say it’s justified, and the press will say the same. I understand that. I’m here to keep evolving and improving, because I know where I’ve come from and what I’m capable of achieving.

View image in fullscreen Vinícius Júnior leaves the pitch after his red card against Villarreal. Photograph: Alejandro Martinez Velez/Reuters

“It’s understandable for the opposing fans to jeer me, because my job is to score goals against their team, but I don’t get the referees. I’ve seen the stats: I’ve been on the receiving end of 500 fouls, yet that has only resulted in five red cards. In the end, the yellow cards always seem to go to Vini, to the attacking players. We need to protect the players who bring something different to the game, like Lamine at Barcelona or Julián at Atleti. Defenders are allowed to foul me the entire match but in the end it’s me who gets the card.”

José Mourinho complained about the timing of the announcement of the suspension. “Do you think it’s normal for a player from a Spanish team, preparing for an important match that’s also crucial for Spanish football, to find out about his four-match suspension just two hours before kickoff?” Madrid’s manager said. “We were on the bus about to arrive at the stadium when we found out … they’ve started doing things without any shame.”

Vinícius, who hasn’t scored for Madrid since August, was replaced in the 59th minute of Madrid’s victory before the team rallied from 3-1 down. “I’m working to get back to my best as soon as possible,” Vinícius said. “I know I’m not at my peak right now, but I’ve been through worse, and even when people have doubted me, I’ve always stood up for this club. That’s why I signed a six-year contract extension. The good run of form will return, and the goals will come back, too. I’m certain of that. I have no doubt. I’m here to help the team.”

The 26-year-old downplayed his frustration after Mourinho substituted him. “It’s natural for me to get upset when I’m substituted because I always want to play every single match,” he said. “I’m well aware of my current form and how I’m playing. I’m here to help the team, and sometimes you have to come off so that other players can get on and change the dynamic.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Mourinho and I have a great relationship. He’s always straight with me. Of course I got a little annoyed when I came off today, but that’s normal. In the end he was right, the team improved, and that’s what matters most.” Vinícius was replaced by Endrick, who scored an 85th-minute equaliser before Antonio Rüdiger gave Madrid the win in the 90th.

Among the games Vinícius will miss because of his suspension is the clásico at Barcelona on 25 October.

Sports.title: Southgate ‘hardly watches’ football and does not envisage Premier League return
Sports.content:
Gareth Southgate has all but ruled out a return to Premier League management and revealed he “didn’t even enjoy the wins” for more than a couple of minutes towards the end of his time in charge of England.

Southgate, who has moved away from football since stepping down as the manager of the England men’s team after defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final, said he had not attended a game since watching his boyhood club Crystal Palace beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final last year.

The 56-year-old’s only taste of club management came when he spent almost three-and-a-half years at Middlesbrough after replacing Steve McClaren in 2006. Southgate was unable to keep Middlesbrough in the Premier League in 2009 and he indicated during an appearance on the Amol Rajan Connection podcast that he had no interest in seeking a return to top-flight management.

Quick Guide How do I 

“I don’t see a scenario where I do that,” he said. “Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying … at the very least for a period, the wins keep you going. By the end, I didn’t even enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes. So, I’ve hardly watched football.

“I went to the FA Cup final to see my team, Crystal Palace, win their first trophy. I’ve not been to a football ground since. So my sort of desire to be involved in football has changed.”

Southgate managed England for almost eight years and came close to ending their hunt for a first men’s trophy since the 1966 World Cup. But he has sought different opportunities since leaving the role. He has launched a podcast and fronted a BBC documentary this year in which he travelled across the UK to understand the challenges facing young men and boys.

“I’ve loved the last 18 months of my life,” Southgate said. “I’ve had 37 years where my sense of self depended on did I win or lose on Saturday. And actually I’ve loved having different experiences.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I’ve met politicians, I’ve met people in the media industry, I have learned about leadership in all sorts of areas, I’ve travelled around the world learning things. I’ve just enjoyed playing a different film in my life.”

Sports.title: English-born striker playing in ninth tier earns international call-up under ex-World Cup captain
Sports.content:
Mohammed Mahe Khan has earned a call-up to the senior Bangladesh squad for November's South Asian Championships.

That is despite the fact that he is just 18 and is playing in the ninth tier of English football.

2 Dooley took charge of Bangladesh in May and won his debut match against San Marino Credit: Getty

The striker currently plays for Moulton in the South Premier Division, and he has been in great form.

Khan has nine goals in just seven games so far this season to earn his call-up.

And the man who has called him up is an American who captained the USMNT at the 1998 World Cup.

81-cap US international Thomas Dooley was born in Germany due to his father serving in the United States Army.

As a result, he spent the majority of his career in Germany in the Bundesliga.

And he is taking a big gamble on Khan, with the squad having to be selected before any training camp can take place.

He said: “We are going to take a young player, Mahe Khan. We will have a look at him in camp.

"However, we have to announce the final 28-man squad before the camp begins, so we won’t have the opportunity to assess him during training before making the decision.

“Selecting him now is almost like leaving it to chance.

"We believe he might be able to do the job we need. That’s the situation at the moment.”

South Asian Championship 2026

The South Asian Championship is the primary competition for countries that are part of the South Asian Football Federation.

Bangladesh are the hosts this year, with the tournament kicking off on Thursday, November 5 and coming to an end on Tuesday, November 17.

It is contested between six sides, with every game being played at the national stadium in Dhaka.

This will be the 15th edition of the tournament, with India being the most successful team.

They have won it nine times and are the highest-ranked team on the FIFA list.

Bangladesh won it once in 2003 and will be looking to claim it once more on home soil.

2 This stadium is most used to seeing cricket being played in it, but it will be very different for two weeks

The six teams are divided into three groups, with two teams from each making the semi-finals.

The winner of Group A faces the runner-up in Group B and vice-versa, with the victors in those clashes meeting in the final.

Dooley's career

Dooley played the majority of his games for Kaiserslautern and won the Bundesliga with them and Homburg, but his form did get him a move to a couple of Germany's biggest clubs.

In 1994, Bayer Leverkusen came calling before he headed to Schalke and then to the USA with Columbus Crew and Metro Stars.

On the international stage, he made 81 senior appearances for the US and appeared at two World Cups.

In 1994, he played every minute, and in 1998, he was the captain for the US before receiving a testimonial match in February 1999 and going down as one of the first proper men's US footballers to make an impact in Europe.

Sports.title: ‘They have my number’ – Troy Deeney makes passionate Watford plea amid more manager turmoil
Sports.content:
Troy Deeney has offered his services to Watford on an advisory basis as they face the prospect of another managerial change.

The Hornets sit 22nd in the Championship with only two wins from ten following their 5-1 thrashing by Cardiff City on Tuesday night.

3 Dionisi joined Watford in June, but has overseen just two league wins and faces an uncertain future at the club Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that head coach Alessio Dionisi will remain in charge for their home clash against Charlton Athletic on Saturday.

Furthermore, the Watford owners have acknowledged their hastiness with managerial changes and believe Dionisi is owed more time.

Since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012, they have had 24 different managers on the touchline, including caretakers.

Watford were a Premier League club as recently as 2022 but look set for a lengthy absence from the top flight as things stand.

But Deeney, a club legend who scored 140 goals in all competitions from 2010 to 2021, wants to help change their current trajectory.

Deeney puts himself out there for Watford

When asked on talkSPORT if he would be willing to go back, he said: "I've been asked this question a lot, and I've not really given the true answer because I thought it makes it about myself. But, they've always had my number for the last five years.

"Even when I was angry, even when I was frustrated at the way that we parted. I thought after 13 years of service, given a very successful period of time, they least they could do was tell me at the start of the window, 'You're not for us', shake hands and let me go.

"Not with three days left to go, 'Oh, by the way, we want you out; here's a payoff'. I thought I deserved a little bit more credit than that.

"I nearly went back in 2021; they said... 'You're a bit too old for us, we're going younger', so they signed Jake Livermore, who's two years younger than me.

"'We need characters, but we want to make a pathway for the young players to come through', so they signed Moussa Sissoko, Tom Ince. So, again, that's a personal thing, whatever. But if they ever need me, I'm a phone call away."

3 Deeney, who scored a record 47 Premier League goals for Watford, wants to help his former club amid a bleak period Credit: Getty Images

Deeney then sent a message to the owners when he added: "They don't (call), and do you know why they don't? Because I'll tell them the truth, and the truth is you've lost who you are.

"When you came in... I want this bit to be very clear as well: they gave us an unbelievable saving grace; they saved Watford not too long ago.

"Watford only had three stands, if you remember, when we had the (2012/13) play-off moment, the Leicester moment. There was only three stands, they put another stand in, they've spent loads of money, they've had successful times, I don't want that to be lost.

"But over the last five to six years, you've lost your way, and you've not acknowledged that you've lost your way.

"That's why it keeps going this way, and people like myself, Luther Blissett, John Barnes, Tommy Mooney, whoever you want to get involved, get somebody in who genuinely cares about the club, doesn't need the money.

"I don't need their money, I just want to see it done right for the next generation, that's all."

3 Deeney recognised the positives of the Watford ownership, but believes the club are on a downward spiral Credit: Getty

Deeney then spoke on what he thinks Watford need to do in order to save themselves from further misery.

"First, acknowledgement as to where you are," he explained. "If you look at all of the communications coming out from the club, they're talking about play-offs - you're getting spanked 5-1 by Cardiff, it should have been 9-1, by the way.

"Acknowledgement of where you are, acknowledgement that you've lost your identity, your way, shape. Survive, first and foremost, and then actually start spending some money.

"Everybody in that room and myself love Michail Antonio - he hasn't been playing the last couple of years since his tragic accident (car crash in December 2024), for a reason.

"But he's at Watford; Watford took him on - what does that say about their recruitment? Respectfully to Michail, and it's not about Michail; it's a lot deeper than that. But you're trying to stay up this year with Michail Antonio helping the ship; that doesn't work.

"The other piece to it, when I look back... I've spoken to a few of the lads, so they won't mind me saying it, but lads that weren't even able to play when we were there are now running the show.

"So either one of two things happened - they've got exponentially better over five years, or the level has gone really low. I'll let you decide."

Sports.title: Premier League cult hero now an Uber driver in surprise career change after retirement
Sports.content:
Premier League cult hero now an Uber driver in surprise career change after retirement

Former Premier League star Hugo Porfirio has swapped beating full-backs to beating red lights in a new career as an Uber driver.

Porfirio spent the 1996/97 season on loan at West Ham and made 23 appearances for the Irons.



2 Porfirio managed to win three senior caps for Portugal Credit: Getty

He managed four goals while at the Boleyn Ground before heading back to Sporting Lisbon.

He was back in England a couple of years later with Nottingham Forest.

That proved to be a far less successful spell than his one at West Ham.



Porfirio made nine appearances for the Hammers and scored a single goal.

His goals while playing for the Irons included strikes against Chelsea and Blackburn Rovers.



And in the cup, strikes came in games versus Forest and Wrexham.

His one solitary goal for Forest was in a match against Sheffield Wednesday.

On the international stage, the winger shared the pitch with Luis Figo and Vitor Baia.



He ended his playing days with Al-Nassr well before they became Cristiano Ronaldo's home in 2008.

And after briefly being a scout for Sporting, he has been spotted as an Uber driver in Portugal.

2 Porfirio is the perfect example of how different a footballer's life can turn out after retirement Credit: Getty

Porfirio now working as Uber driver

Portuguese influencer Andre Ramalho publicly unmasked the 53-year-old in a viral video.



“We had a ten-minute walk to make, but we were late and tired, so decided to call an Uber.

“We were amazed by the guy driving the car. How could he be doing something so ordinary?

“This is the fella who played at Euro 96, and played alongside Rui Costa, Luis Figo and Vitor Baia.

“He is the coolest guy of all time, and a great bloke as well.

'He drove very well'

“He also drove very well. Footballers aren’t usually known as good drivers!”



And his daughter, Madalena, also paid tribute to him, with Ramalho’s post received thousands of likes on Instagram.

She said: “My father is a machine.”

The Lisbon-born star has been totally missing from the public spotlight since leaving his scouting role with Sporting in 2013.

Sports.title: Sunderland set European record no other English club have managed after dramatic win
Sports.content:
Sunderland set European record no other English club have managed after dramatic win

Sunderland have made English football history in Europe thanks to a dramatic 2-1 comeback victory against Torreense.

Noah Sadiki scored with a brilliant volley during second-half stoppage time to maintain their 100 per cent record in the Europa League.



2 Sadiki's late goal saw Sunderland come from behind to beat Torreense in stoppage time and make history Credit: Getty

Portuguese side Torreense led on 37 minutes when Volnei Feltes scored via a stunning long-range strike at Estadio Dr. Magalhaes Pessoa.

However, Jules Ahoka headed in for Sunderland midway through the second half before Sadiki became their last-minute hero.

Sunderland reach new heights with late win

The Black Cats have now won five of their total six fixtures in major European competitions.



This is the fewest number of games by any English club to reach five such victories.

Four of these fixtures came during the 1973/74 Cup Winners' Cup, in which they won three and lost one.



In this season's Europa League, they beat AZ Alkmaar 1-0 at the Stadium of Light on the first matchday.

West Ham United, Ipswich Town and Queens Park Rangers held the previous record with seven matches.



Sunderland are also the first English side since Wolves at Besiktas in October 2019 to score an away winner past the 90th minute.

They sit in the top eight of the Europa League league phase with the victories over Torreense and over AZ Alkmaar.

Should they remain in these spots after their eight matches, they will advance straight into the knockout stages.

2 Sunderland are the quickest English side in history to reach five wins in European competitions Credit: Getty



Sunderland qualified for the Europa League by finishing seventh in the Premier League last season.

They have been tipped to go all the way, which could make them the seventh English side to win the tournament.

Only Aston Villa, Chelsea, Ipswich, Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham have won Europe's second-tier competition.

Sunderland travel to Lech Poznan next week before back-to-back home matches against Dinamo Zagreb and Jagiellonia Bialystok.



Regis Le Bree's side then face seven-time Champions League winners AC Milan at San Siro.

Anderlecht and Levski Sofia are their final two opponents in January.

Sports.title: Liverpool star suffers setback as Andoni Iraola addresses ‘bad’ injury
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has revealed that Giovanni Leoni's comeback from an ACL injury is taking longer than anticipated.

The Italian suffered the injury on his Reds debut last year in the Carabao Cup against Southampton at Anfield.

4 Liverpool are not rushing Leoni back, who is yet to get his career at Anfield underway

He has now been out of action for over a year, and unfortunately for the Italian youth international, there is no return in sight.

Speaking ahead of the Reds taking on Brentford in the Premier League this weekend, Iraola shared an update on Leoni.

Leoni injury update

He said: “It’s taking more time than we wanted. The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.

“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.

“He has to be very confident, the rehab process has to be very careful with him and we want to make sure once he comes to the team, he stays there in a good place.

“It’s true that we’ve had, not a setback, but a little bit of a delay, if you want.

“The plan now is he starts in the next break. It’s not that far but it’s a little bit later than we expected, yes.”

Leoni joined Liverpool as an 18-year-old from Parma, and despite his tender age, he was seen as an immediate option in the first team.

Arne Slot handed him his debut in that game against Southampton, and he lasted 81 minutes before he was stretchered off the pitch.

4 The concerning thing for Iraola is that there is no timescale for Leoni's return Credit: Getty

4 Leoni is back in individual training but has been delayed in his bid to join the rest of his team Credit: Getty

Injury woes

Leoni is just one of several long-term injuries at Anfield.

Conor Bradley has been struggling with a serious knee injury, with Iraola revealing last month that he is not close to training with the team.

Hugo Ekitike is also on the sidelines with a serious Achilles problem that will likely keep him out of action until the new year.

There are then injuries to Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo as well, with the duo still major doubts for the weekend.

And Dominik Szoboszlai is also on the treatment table following a hamstring issue sustained over the international break.

4 With Gakpo and Isak out, Liverpool are short in the attacking areas of the pitch Credit: Getty

Defensive instability

Liverpool might have scored six in midweek, but they also shipped three to LASK.

That came mere days after they lost 3-0 to Manchester City, with Iraola none too happy with the defending on show from his side.

He said: "[That's] probably the reason why the manager shouldn't change both centre-backs, but we were already winning 4-0 and you have to think about the next game and saving the legs of the players.

"We didn't defend properly at the end of the game."

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez issues second statement confirming talks with Man United hierarchy after outburst
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez has confirmed positive talks with the Manchester United hierarchy following his damning rant on Tuesday night.

The centre-back took aim at sporting director Jason Wilcox and the board for a lack of investment during the summer transfer window.



2 Martinez has claimed that he and United have put his outburst behind them in another statement Credit: Getty

Martinez fumed just minutes after United lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, which extended their winless run to five.

He doubled down on his anger with a statement on Wednesday, in which he said: "My words reflect how I feel."

However, in a separate message on social media, he revealed that he and senior personnel at United have spoken about his outburst.



Martinez statement

"Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager. It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.



"Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that.

"I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve out shared ambition: bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve.



"With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together."

talkSPORT understands that Martinez has been fined by the club.

It's also understood that the defender decided to publicly apologise, and everyone now considers the matter to be closed.

2 Martinez has been fined by United for his outburst, but all parties consider matters to be closed Credit: Getty

As talkSPORT reported, other senior players at United share the same frustrations with the hierarchy.



There is a sense that Wilcox missed the chance to build on the strong second half of last season as key areas of the pitch that needed to be strengthened were overlooked for three new midfield additions.

The timing of Martinez's rant has been questioned given their poor form, and club legend Wayne Rooney claimed he was 'disrespectful'.

Head coach Michael Carrick was already under pressure at the full-time whistle in Madrid earlier this week.

United next face rivals Leeds United away from home on Sunday as they eye just their second Premier League win this season.



Whether or not Carrick will name Martinez in his starting XI at Elland Road remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard open to huge Championship job as current manager under increasing pressure
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard open to huge Championship job as current manager under increasing pressure

Phil Parkinson’s role as Wrexham manager is under increasing pressure, talkSPORT understands.

Parkinson has an excellent relationship with the ownership group, several of whom would prefer not to make a change.



3 Parkinson is a Wrexham legend no matter what happens Credit: Getty

Yet results are forcing the club to consider a new manager, with new sporting director Steve Nickson involved.

TalkSPORT understands Steven Gerrard, who hasn't managed since leaving Al-Ettifaq in January 2025, is open to the role should a vacancy arise.

Scott Parker is another name expected to be considered.

Parkinson will take charge of Saturday’s game against Preston with Wrexham currently 17th in the table.



Parkinson asked for an immediate response from his players after a 2-1 defeat at home to West Bromwich Albion in midweek.

Kieffer Moore opened the scoring before Isaac Price and Aune Heggebo sealed the win for the visitors.



And after the game, he said: "When you've lost a game at home it's time to batten down the hatches and come out strong as a group, and that's what we're going to do at the weekend.

"I'm sure we'll take criticism for the defeat. That's inevitable and we totally accept that.



"But there's a lot of resilience at that training ground and we're going to show it in the build-up to Preston.

"When you lose in that manner, it's obviously harder, isn't it? Because the lads could feel it, the game was there for us.

"No-one's going to feel sorry for us in football. We've got to find a solution, look at the game and see which areas can we do better."

It has been Wrexham's inability to win games this year that has cost them.



The Welsh side have played ten, won only two, drawn five and lost three in the league.

3 Gerrard has managed three professional teams, but a chance in the Championship could await

Gerrard's credentials

The Liverpool legend's first managerial role was Rangers.

He joined in the summer of 2018 and was there until November 2021 as Aston Villa came calling.

In his time at Ibrox, the Gers won the SPFL title and went unbeaten for the whole season.



That saw some have the chance to qualify for the Champions League, which they failed to do.

Instead, they went into the Europa League, where they made the final but not under Gerrard.

That was because Villa saw him as the man to lead a brave new team in the Premier League.

He spent big money on Diego Carlos, Lucas Digne and Philippe Coutinho only for things not to go so well.



His first year saw Villa finish in 14th place after picking up 35 points from 27 games before he was sacked midway through the following year.

Gerrard made it to 11 league games with just two wins and Villa in danger of going down, so he was replaced by Unai Emery.

3 Parker is looking for work after being sacked by Burnley Credit: AFP

From there, he made a left-field move to Saudi Arabia to take charge of Al-Ettifaq.



More big-name players arrived in Jordan Henderson and Georginio Wijnaldum.

What followed was a sixth-place finish in his one full season before leaving in January 2025.

At the time of his departure, Al-Ettifaq were in 12th place, and he hasn't managed since.

Instead, Gerrard has become a regular on TNT Sports as a pundit.

Sports.title: Alex Scott quits job months after Football Focus cancelled
Sports.content:
Alex Scott has left her role as Women's Champions League presenter on Disney+.

The former England international, who won 140 Lionesses caps, was announced as part of their line-up in September 2025.

2 Scott has left her role as a presenter for the Women's Champions League a year after taking it Credit: Getty

However, as per The Guardian, Scott has made the decision to vacate the role.

"We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the Uefa Women's Champions League on Disney+," a Disney+ spokesperson told the outlet.

"Her passion for the women's game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success."

Scott's representatives added: "Alex is grateful for the opportunities she has had to work with the team at Disney+ and hopes that they continue to work together in the future."

What will Scott work on next?

Formerly of Arsenal Women, Scott is said to be shifting focus onto separate projects, such as her newly-launched One More Word WSL.

Alongside other ex-England stars in Anita Asante and Fara Williams, the show discusses news from the Women's Super League.

One More Word was launched by First Cap Productions Limited, where Scott is listed as a director on the Companies House website.

Since starting her media career after professional football, the 42-year-old has been best-known for presenting Football Focus.

It was announced in May 2021 that she would succeed Dan Walker, who had fronted the Saturday lunchtime football show for 12 years.

However, the BBC confirmed in April that Football Focus, which first aired in 1974, would not run beyond the 2025/26 season.

2 Scott presented Football Focus for five years before the BBC ended the show earlier this year Credit: Getty

Scott briefly mentioned the decision to end the programme during her opening words on the first episode back since the news broke.

talkSPORT's Martin Keown was a long-term pundit on Football Focus and called it 'an iconic programme'.

He also claimed that Scott was doing an 'exceptional job' as presenter and that its conclusion did not reflect on her.

Scott won five Women's Premier League titles with Arsenal, and then a sixth after it became the Women's Super League in 2010.

She also won the Women's Champions League and was awarded an OBE in 2017 for her 'outstanding contribution to Women's Football'.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Mikel Merino admits he's 'fortunate to be alive' after 'an angel' saved him during Borussia Dortmund bus bombing
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Mikel Merino admits he's 'fortunate to be alive' after 'an angel' saved him during Borussia Dortmund bus bombing

Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino has admitted he is 'fortunate to be alive' after 'an angel' prevented him from being injured in the 2017 Borussia Dortmund bus bombing.

The football world was shaken when the German side were victims of an attack by Sergej Wenergold, which saw three pipe bombs detonated near the bus when it was on its way to a Champions League match.

Dortmund defender Marc Bartra was left hospitalised with a wrist injury following the attack, while a police officer was also treated for injuries and unable to return to work.

Merino, meanwhile, escaped unscathed – but that may not necessarily have been the case.

'I think I have an angel on my shoulder,' Merino, who was 20 at the time, told The Players' Tribune. 'I'm actually fortunate to be alive at all.

He added: 'There was a deafening noise, and then I remember the bus nearly tipping over. I looked behind me and saw blood on the floor. Smoke, screams. I remember being at the hospital later that night, waiting for Marc Bartra, who had his wrist badly cut up.

Arsenal's Mikel Merino has said he is 'fortunate to be alive' after being onboard Dortmund's team bus during a bombing

The Dortmund bus was targeted in 2017 when on its way to a Champions League quarter-final

'The next day, someone told me that a huge piece of shrapnel was lodged in the headrest of the seat next to Marc. My usual seat. That day, the seat was empty.

'My legs were feeling a bit tight, and the seats in the front reclined. So I sat up there instead, and it may have saved my life. So yeah, I just have this belief that things happen for a reason.'

The pipe bombs were hidden in hedges by the side of the road and detonated at around 7.15pm local time. Dortmund were on the way to their stadium to face Monaco in the Champions League quarter-finals.

The bombs were filled with metal pins and had a reach of around 100 meters.

After a lengthy investigation, Wenergold, then 29, was charged with 28 counts of attempted murder for the attack. He was sentenced to 14 years in prison.

He said during the trial that he did not intend to kill any of the players but make money by betting on a fall in Borussia Dortmund's stock market price.

The match against Monaco was postponed but played the following day - a decision led to some heavy criticism of UEFA.

England coach Thomas Tuchel was manager of Dortmund at the time and after the match branded the decision to play the game 'absurd'.

'We were informed by text message that UEFA was making this decision,' he added. 'A decision made in Switzerland that concerns us directly. We will not forget it. It is a very bad feeling.

'There is a feeling of helplessness. What we think has not interested anyone. We weren't asked about playing the game.

'Everyone has their own way of reacting to events. The players had the choice not to play, but no-one chose this option.'

Sports.title: Louis van Gaal insists Man City's scandal contributed to 'all the consequences and suffering' that followed his Man United exit - as ex-boss believes 'for sure' his reign would've ended better
Sports.content:
Louis van Gaal has blamed Manchester City's financial doping for the 'suffering' that he endured in his torrid 2016 Man United exit. The Dutch manager was given his marching orders on the heels of the 2015-16 season, which saw the Red Devils narrowly miss out on a place in the following term's Champions League. Both Man City and Man United wrapped up with 66 points, but the Cityzens, playing their final season under Manuel Pellegrini had the superior goal difference which secured their spot at Europe's top table. Van Gaal was despatched despite ending the season having won the FA Cup, and in correspondence with the Athletic, stressed that he believed that failing to qualify for the European top flight had prompted the club's Glazer ownership group to swing the axe. 'For me, at the time, that (missing out on the Champions League in 2016) was probably the deciding factor in my dismissal from Manchester United and all the consequences and suffering this entailed,' he stated. The former Barcelona boss added that 'for sure', things might have been different if he had been playing in a fair competition. Louis van Gaal admitted that he believes his time at Man United might have ended differently if not for Man City's financial manipulation The former manager was dismissed at the end of the 2015-16 season after missing out on a spot in the Champions League, despite finishing level on points with City Van Gaal subsequently took a hiatus from management, which he described at the time as being a 'sabbatical'. He only returned to the dugout in 2021, when he was appointed as head coach of the Dutch national team. Van Gaal's tenure at Old Trafford fell during the period between 2009 and 2018 that Man City have been found guilty of artificially inflating revenue made through sponsorship. City were found to have used 'sham' contracts and agreements to cook their books by around £900million over a nine-year period, claiming a commercial income of £949.94m of which only £119.25m had come from sponsors. The Premier League said the panel found City arranged ‘sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on ‘sham’ agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs’. Deals with a number of sponsors were part of ‘a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees’, the statement added, saying that ‘the remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club’. The result was that the club had ‘filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators’. Man City have doubled down on their innocence and appealed the verdict, with the club underscoring that they are in possession of 'irrefutable evidence' which will clear their name. For Van Gaal, he admitted that there was little he could do as he 'cannot turn back history now.' 'Not even the English Football Association can (do that),' he added. But the 75-year-old is not alone in wondering what might have been had Man City not been able to inflate their revenue and in turn, invest in some of the players fundamental to their multi-year successes. Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard admitted that he wanted the club to 'suffer' after 'stealing memories', with the Reds icon going without a Premier League medal during their era of dominance. Liverpool came second to Man City when they claimed the title in 2013-14, and although Gerrard was circumspect last week as he discussed Man City's potential punishment, he ultimately called for the club to be sanctioned heavily. 'I think I have come to terms with that I have never won the Premier League, that I was short in that department in terms of winning it,' Gerrard said last week. 'I have come to terms with the incident that happened to me at the back end of that season and I have heard a lot of City players, a lot of City fans, and celebrity fans say "you can't take those moments away from us". 'What about the memories they have taken away from not just possibly me, and the team that I played in but over that period of time, nine, ten years? 'Spurs fans, United fans, Everton fans, teams at the bottom, teams in the cups? City, ex-players, current players, and City owners, everyone connected with City have got to think about the memories they have stolen away from everyone else. 'Multi-year punishments, that would be my opinion,' he added when asked what was deserved. 'I'm not saying that's the right opinion, but that's just how I feel sitting here in this chair. 'I think putting them down to the Championship is not fair on the EFL. I don't think it's enough, because they'll bounce back. You look at that team yesterday. Can you imagine that in the Championship? With all due respect, it's not fair on the teams playing against City week in, week out. It's not fair on the potential team that could be the third team to come up. 'I think it needs to be a transfer ban. I think it needs to be points over a period of time. And make them suffer like they've made everyone else suffer for the nine, ten years that they've done it for. That would be my opinion. But there needs to be an example set.'

Sports.title: Man United outcast Andre Onana concedes directly from a corner - after Mo Salah stunner had put their Trabzonspor side in control of Conference League clash
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana conceded a goal directly from a corner in the Conference League on Thursday night. The 30-year-old, who is still contracted to United but on loan at Turkish side Trabzonspor, was playing in his side's European game against Kuopion Palloseura of Finland. His side started well, with former Southampton forward Paul Onuachu putting them ahead in the third minute of the game as Thomas Reis's side looked to start the competition on a positive note. Then, in the 44th minute, Liverpool legend Mohamed Salah, who moved to Turkey in the summer after leaving the Reds, made it 2-0 with a fine finish to pick up his eighth goal of the season in ten games. The forward ran onto a blocked shot that was bouncing in the box, and finished high with the inside of his left foot to seemingly put the game beyond the hosts. Franculino Dju then made it three just after the break, but veteran Petteri Pennanen got his side back into it with the help of Onana's error. André Onana is unable to keep it out as KuPS score directly from a corner 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/91Wv44oSzt — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 15, 2026 Manchester United's Andre Onana conceded a goal directly from a corner on Thursday night Onana found himself on the floor in his goal after failing to keep the ball out The midfielder put in a corner minutes after his side went 3-0 down, and Onana jumped but was unable to keep the effort out of the goal. The Manchester United loanee lay on the floor as his team-mates walked away, and had to gather himself for the rest of the game. He would concede again just before full-time, with the game ending 4-2. United fans rushed to social media to give their verdicts, with one fan writing on X: 'Do not miss this man, no matter how bad we are.' Another wrote: 'Nice to see he is still an absolute liability.' A third added: 'One of the worst goalkeepers I have seen.' Onana is rebuilding his career out in Turkey after a calamitous spell at United – who he joined in 2023 – which resulted in him losing his place and, eventually, being loaned out. His wages are not being covered by the Red Devils, and it is expected he will leave permanently either this summer or when his contract expires in 2028. Mo Salah with a BEAUTIFUL finish to double Trabzonspor’s lead ✨ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nF15dy6wcI — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 15, 2026 It has been a mixed season for Trabzonspor so far, having been knocked out of the Europa League in the play-offs and thus dropping into the Conference League. Trabzonspor are currently fifth in the league table after seven games, having won four of their matches so far. Onana has formed an unlikely friendship with Salah, who has been an instant hit with the club's fans.
