Sports.title: Cherries on top! Bournemouth make European history as Sunderland score last-gasp winner and Brighton enjoy easy win... but Crystal Palace fall to defeat in five-goal thriller against Lyon
Sports.content:
Cherries on top! Bournemouth make European history as Sunderland score last-gasp winner and Brighton enjoy easy win... but Crystal Palace fall to defeat in five-goal thriller against Lyon

This was a night for Bournemouth to look back as much as it was to look forward.

A night to reflect on how far they’ve come, from navigating a 17-point deduction that put their Football League status at risk in 2008 to playing – and winning – their first ever European home game, thanks to a sublime treble from Evanilson, Rayan and Alvaro Rodriguez, who added the cherry on top with a late penalty.

There was a special tifo behind one goal to mark the historic night, with a record crowd of 12,010 packed in to witness it.

It was Adam Smith, who has been with Bournemouth since 2010 when they played in League One, leading them out as club captain.

Here was owner Bill Foley, seeing his vision to get Bournemouth into Europe, a target he ambitiously but explicitly set back in December 2022, occurring a year ahead of his five-year target.

But when Smith’s cross in from the right was expertly flicked up into the air by Evanilson, looping over Sturm Graz goalkeeper Daniil Khudyakov, it was a moment for Bournemouth to look forward, too.

Tournament favourites before they beat Real Sociedad in San Sebastian last time out and back-to-back European wins has done little to rubbish that label. Bournemouth have had to take the long way to the top but now they are here, they are showing just how much of a punch they pack.

Evanilson scored Bournemouth's first European goal at home in their 3-0 win over Sturm Graz

Bournemouth fans celebrated the club's journey pre-match, with the club now among the leading contenders to win the Europa League

Boss Marco Rose, who made five changes for this one, described the weekend’s 5-1 drubbing at the hands of Chelsea as a ‘good slap’.

Bournemouth were ruthlessly dismantled in south-west London. But to paraphrase the iconic ‘Tubthumping’, a song by British band Chumbawamba, when you get knocked down, you get up again, and that’s exactly what Rose’s side did.

It was a suffocating first half for a Sturm Graz side that started with a back five before pivoting to a back four at the interval.

Bournemouth had 10 efforts on goal to the visitors’ zero, with Ben Gannon-Doak and Evanilson a constant threat down the Bournemouth right.

Good sides ride their luck at times, too, and Bournemouth are no different. Sturm Graz wanted a penalty just before half-time when Belmin Beganovic was clumsily felled by Smith, only for the referee to adjudge Beganovic to have dived.

In a much improved second half, Graz struck the post when Jurgen Heil was picked out in the area.

But when you’ve battled back from the brink of minus-seventeen in League Two, and all the perils that come with trying to gatecrash the Premier League elite from a starting base in the fourth tier, adversity in Europe is light work.

Second halves have been an issue that have pockmarked Rose’s tenure on the south coast so far, coming into this one having led in six out of eight, only going on to win two of them. It was an irritation away to Sociedad, and here was proof that Rose and his players are learning lessons on the fly.

Marco Rose wants his side to take their performance against Sturm Graz into the Premier League

Justin Kluivert, Rayan and Ryan Christie all formed part of the cavalry sent on by Rose in a bid to settle the game and allow the party atmosphere to kick into another gear and that roll of the dice paid off with 15 minutes to go.

Khudyakov dealt poorly with a Bournemouth corner and after dropping it in his six-yard box, Rayan smashed in as Rose threw both arms into the air in celebration.

Rose is already looking ahead to how they can now secure their first league win of the season - starting on Sunday, when Sunderland visit the Vitality.

'Performance-wise, clean sheet, attitude, effort - a deserved win and now we have to continue, have to get consistent in these things and Sunderland is the next challenge,' said Rose.

'I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation. The squad is working, everyone is keen to play, everyone deserves to play and its good for us for the busy weeks to have a competitive squad.

'If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it's hard to beat us. That's what we should take into the next game.'

For all the fireworks, tifos, light shows, and noise that lit up the night sky, here was proof of just how far Bournemouth have come… and how much further this ascending group can go with Champions League football in their sights.

Torreense 1-2 Sunderland: Sadiki scores last-gasp winner

By Michael Pavitt

Regis Le Bris was forced to call on the cavalry to rescue his side as Sunderland came from behind to win their first European away match in 53 years in stoppage time against Portuguese second division side Torreense.

Noah Sadiki struck in the dying minutes prompting wild celebrations from the near 4,000 travelling supporters, who had earlier seen summer signing Jules Ahoka cancel out a spectacular opener from Torreense defender Volnei Feltes.

The winner owed much to the creativity of Enzo Le Fee and Granit Xhaka as the pair, who began the night on the bench, underlined their importance to the Black Cats.

Having watched their team-mates struggle to break down Torreense, Le Fee produced a delightful dinked pass into the penalty area to find Xhaka, with the Swiss flicking the ball first time into the path of Sadiki to score his first goal for the club.

‘When Granit touched it I heard him scream shoot and I didn’t think twice,' Sadiki said. 'I just hoped it was going in and the keeper wouldn’t save it. I’m really happy. It was a beautiful moment.’

Le Bris had taken the understandable risk by deciding to make seven changes for the fixture against arguably their weakest Europa League opponents, with Torreense currently lying 15th in the Portuguese second tier.

Noah Sadiki scored a stoppage time winner as Sunderland beat Portuguese side Torreense

Sunderland were forced to fight back following a stunning opener from Volnei Feltes

With just four points in the Premier League and five matches left to play this month, this was the match to give an opportunity to fringe members of the squad.

Torreense, though, have proved they are more than capable of springing a surprise. Their journey to the Europa League is one to rival Sunderland’s own having stunned Sporting Lisbon in last year’s Portuguese Cup final to qualify.

Their opening goal proved just as unexpected as that triumph.

Feltes was well inside his own half when he received possession and opted to embark on a forward run. After driving towards the Sunderland box, the Brazilian defender chopped between the challenges of Malick Fofana and Nilson Angulo and curled magnificently into the top corner.

Whatever happens to the minnows, they will come away with one of the best goals of this year’s competition.

Sunderland were forced to be patient when trying to break down their opponents, who dropped deep in the second half.

Le Bris turned to his bench moments after Nilson Angulo saw a header superbly kept out by goalkeeper Lucas Paes, with Omar Alderete failing to convert the follow-up.

His quadruple change of Xhaka, Le Fee, Reinildo and Nordi Mukiele proved crucial. The latter's cross for Ahoka to equalise with a header while Xhaka and Le Fee were central to Sadiki's winner.

'Winning this game just at the end is really special,' Le Bris said. 'It’s important for the club and the fans – they were fantastic once again.

'We are growing and we need experiences and I think the team showed the belief until the end which is really important for us. We showed again we have this mindset.'

Lyon 3-2 Crystal Palace – Eagles defence struggles again

By James Sharpe

Now Pierre Sage knows how Oliver Glasner feels. He knows how it feels to return to your old stomping ground, one where you achieved great things, and come away with nothing.

Just as Glasner took his new Nottingham Forest side back to Selhurst Park at the weekend and lost, so too did Sage as Crystal Palace endured a frustrating night in Lyon where he once helped save the French side from relegation.

In truth, a night like this has been coming. Palace cannot keep defending like this, be so open and unorganised, and expect to win matches. Sooner or later, you leave yourself with too much of a hill to climb.

It took Forest just three minutes to open the scoring at the weekend and Lyon needed only seven minutes and 31 seconds here. As always, it was all too easy.

A bog-standard corner into a crowded six-yard box and, despite the hordes of black Palace shirts, the ball still dropped to Lyon captain Corentin Tolisso.

Only this time, Lyon didn’t miss the rest of the chances that came their way like Forest did. On the stroke of half-time the hosts cut through Palace with simple passes and Keito Nakamura squared for Ernest Nuamah, who darted ahead of the defenders to finish. Tyrick Mitchell, for all his goalscoring exploits this season, made little effort to track his run.

It was this leakiness that caused a few shudders in the Palace boardroom, letting in 11 goals in their opening four matches, and sparked rumblings that Sage could be the first Premier League managerial casualty of the season.

Pierre Sage saw his Crystal Palace side fall to a 3-2 defeat against his former club Lyon

Ernest Nuamah was among the scores as Lyon capitalised on poor Crystal Palace defending

If there is a saving grace to which Palace can cling, it’s that when they do get it right under Sage, they do look menacing. There was little of that in a dreadful first half but, after the break, they clicked into gear. They are just, as yet, unable to find the balance.

Having wantaway forward Ismaila Sarr back in the line-up always helps with his directness in the final third.

And when you have the precision of Adam Wharton in your midfield, you will always stand a chance. It was his delightful first-time through ball to Yeremy Pino after a fine short corner routine that helped fire Palace back into the game.

The introduction of Daichi Kamada swung momentum further Palace’s way. He was bundled over inside the box but Palace’s furious protests fell on deaf ears. He had a shot from close range saved and, eventually, found the net after some chaos inside the box.

The only problem was that, by then, Lyon had already added a third courtesy of Pavel Sulc’s cheeky backheel flick.

Palace kept pushing as Chris Richards saw a late header from a corner saved but, ultimately, in vain. This time, it wasn’t enough. This time, they didn’t get away with it. This time, they gave themselves too much to do.

'I’m really frustrated about the result but really frustrated with the way of playing in the first half,' Sage said.

'Our game started at half-time and it was too late.

'We play too quickly sometimes with the idea to play out the back quickly in transition but we are not a team like this, we have only one or two players able to run and make the difference with the speed.

'That’s why we have to move with the ball, travel with the ball, and we did that in the second half.'

Brighton 4-0 Kauno Zalgiris – Seagulls cruise in Conference League

By Kieran Gill

It must be up there with the finest feelings in football – the relief that washes over when your team finally finds a way through that dastardly low block in front of them.

For Brighton, that arrived just before half-time. There was no blaming Kauno Zalgiris for their tactical approach. Hardly anyone other than Fabian Hurzeler, who was perhaps being polite when listing the Lithuanian side’s attributes before kick-off, gave them a hope in hell of escaping their first-ever fixture in the main stage of a European competition without losing.

Once Georginio Rutter found that first goal after 41 minutes, this turned into a much more enjoyable evening at the Amex Stadium. Even more so when Jack Hinshelwood, back from his ankle injury and appearing for the first time since August, added a second before the break.

With that, the floodgates opened, Brighton started their Conference League campaign in style, and truthfully, this competition should sit high on Hurzeler’s priorities this term.

Georginio Rutter scored the opening goal as Brighton overcame Lithuanian side Kauno Zalgiris

While we often praise Brighton for the way in which they work – including in the talents they find that the richer clubs then seek to steal – all that is missing is the silverware to complement it all.

Despite being brilliantly run, they have never won a major trophy in their history, and the Conference League is an opportunity to correct that. Other English clubs such as West Ham and Brighton’s rivals Crystal Palace have used it well. To sides such as Kauno Zalgiris, these are giants they are competing with, opponents competing on an entirely alien level to their own.

While Hurzeler had explained why Kauno Zalgiris would be confident – he warned us they were the champions of Lithuania and that they had won the Lithuanian Cup at the weekend – Brighton are in a happy place, too. This made it five successive victories for them in all competitions.

They are third in the Premier League behind only Manchester City and Arsenal, and into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup after winning away at Manchester United – a club now linked with liking Hurzeler in case they move on from Michael Carrick.

With that, we had an inkling as to how this game would go. Brighton would attack, and Kauno Zalgiris would defend, and the opening 30 minutes was all about blocks. From Anton Tolordava, from Nosa Iyobosa Edokpolor, from any Kauno Zalgiris player with a body for throwing at the ball.

But then arrived the breakthrough. It was a nice finish from Rutter despite the on-field officials thinking the ball had gone behind for a goal-kick in the build-up. It had not, and VAR overruled to award Brighton their opener. Hinshelwood added a second before the break before Rutter grabbed the third goal and Matt O’Riley the fourth.

‘We want to keep improving every game,' said Hinshelwood. 'What’s happened in the past has gone now. We want to look forward to the future.’

It was a good way to warm up for Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, though Brighton may be reminded by the Amex’s away end which side have won a trophy of late. Hurzeler should be embracing this European competition as a way to give his supporters a season to cherish.

Sports.title: Jon Rahm leaves £75.5MILLION on the table to walk away from LIV as bankrupt tour lets go of one of its biggest stars in major blow
Sports.content:
Jon Rahm leaves £75.5MILLION on the table to walk away from LIV as bankrupt tour lets go of one of its biggest stars in major blow

Jon Rahm has left a staggering multi-million-pound sum on the table after walking away from rebel tour LIV Golf following Saudi Arabia's exodus from the sport.

The Spanish star deemed the terms of the LIV 2.0 to be 'unacceptable', after Saudi's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced that it would stop funding the tour at the end of the 2026 season.

The tour plans to rebuild with new backers BC Partners, a private equity group, but Rahm will not be part of the cohort playing in 2027 after coming to a 'consensual separation agreement' with LIV.

Rahm and LIV have reached a deal to release all of his monetary and economic claims against the league, with Rahm previously the organisation's largest unsecured creditor owed £5.7m of his contract after LIV filed for bankruptcy last month.

But in walking away, Rahm has also foregone the remainder of his contract, which adds up to a staggering £75.5m ($100m).

In exchange for doing so, the 31-year-old is believed to receive rights to his name, image and likeness in return.

Jon Rahm has walked away from the £75.5m outstanding from his lucrative contract with LIV

This will mean the return of his nickname 'Rahmbo' used on the tour, and his 'Legion XIII' team name, which he played under on the LIV tour.

Confirmation of Rahm's deal with LIV will come on November 5, when it will be judged by US Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey Judge Michael B Kaplan.

Rahm has won the past three seasons of the tour after being tempted to join the Saudi-backed rebels by a mammoth contract agreed at a reported £258m ($350m) - to be paid out over multiple years.

While LIV 2.0 will hope that many of their big-name stars stay and continue to play for the second coming of the tour, their filing for bankruptcy in New Jersey opened the door for stars like Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton to wrap up their time on the tour.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month that while Bryson DeChambeau's deal expired at the end of the 2026 season, he is expected to recommit in return for equity in the league.

The rebel golf circuit, which launched in 2022 with the financial backing of the PIF, paid nine-figure bonuses to lure top players like Brooks Koepka, Dustin Johnson, DeChambeau and Rahm away from the PGA Tour.

Further temptations including lucrative prize money, with some tournaments offering up to $20million in funds.

But it all began to fall apart earlier this year with PIF's withdrawal, prompting a number of events to be cancelled in 2026.

Sports.title: Following decades of US domination, British heavyweight boxing is on top - after Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley and Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua, there are Brit-bashes galore waiting to be made, writes JEFF POWELL MBE
Sports.content:
In the small hours of May 16, 1955 my father woke me in the darkness, lit a candle in the scullery, plugged in his old crystal radio set and told me to listen to a world heavyweight title fight taking place in San Francisco.

Don Cockell of Balham, south London, was challenging Rocky Marciano of Brockton, Massachusetts, for the world heavyweight championship. Most of the sound which came whistling through the static was that of Marciano’s eight-ounce gloves thudding into Cockell’s head and body.

Marciano kept knocking down Cockell, who kept getting up. Until the ninth round, when Rocky nailed him to the canvas for good with a booming right which seemingly connected while he was on his knees.

When the BBC radio commentator put that question to the champ, Marciano replied: ‘Britain can be proud of her boy Don Cockell.’

Jack Powell, whose toughness had carried him through the landings and trenches of the Second World War as well as countless fights inside and outside the ring, slammed his fist on the kitchen table and said: ‘As if keeping beating us ain’t enough, they have to bloody patronise us.’

I was 13. Not until I was 50 – and Marciano had long since become the only heavyweight champ to retire undefeated – would Lennox Lewis end our century-long wait for a successor to Bob Fitzsimmons.

Lennox Lewis (pictured) ended Great Britain's wait for a successor to Bob Fitzsimmons as the United States dominated the heavyweight scene

American stars such as George Foreman (left) and Muhammad Ali (right) dominated the previous era

That eternity was flooded with such revered Americans as Jack Johnson, Jack Dempsey, Joe Louis, Floyd Patterson, Sonny Liston, Muhammad Ali, Joe Frazier, George Foreman, Mike Tyson, Larry Holmes and Evander Holyfield.

The golden age of heavyweight boxing gave us the Fight of the Century and the Thrilla in Manila – both between Ali and Frazier – the Rumble in the Jungle with Ali and Foreman, the Upset of the Century by Buster Douglas over Tyson, Dempsey v Gene Tunney, Louis v both Max Schmeling and Jersey Joe Walcott and Ali’s slaying of the Liston monster. That was the time when the Star Spangled Banner flew over America’s mocking of ‘Britain’s Horizontal Heavyweights.’

Henry Cooper remained perpendicular against The Greatest of them all but there was scant recognition over the water of how he knocked Ali down and almost out with the left hook renowned as ‘Enery’s ‘Ammer’ in the first of two stadium fights he lost to his propensity to suffer cuts.

So, oh, how we gloated when we watched Riddick Bowe dump his WBC belt in a London dustbin rather than fight Lewis, who was thereby elevated to his first title by decree. Rejoiced when Lennox validated his title by beating Oliver McCall in September 1995. Acclaimed Lenny the Lion when he became our only three-time world heavyweight champion.

We breathed a huge sigh of relief when Frank Bruno beat McCall at an emotional Wembley, finally to become world champion. Just as we fretted for him when he genuflected umpteen times on his way to the Las Vegas ring for a second crushing by Tyson and the loss of his crown.

Even so, British heavyweight boxing was transitioning from famine to feast. The US can boast 53 champions all time in the prize-ring’s marquee division. All the way back to the immortal John L Sullivan in the late 1880s. But the UK has accelerated from one active heavyweight champion in 2003 – Lewis when he bloodied and defeated Vitali Kliltschko – to a running total of 11 today if you delete the asterisks against Michael Bent, Herbie Hide and Henry Akinwande who wore the WBO belt before that organisation was fully recognised.

David Haye built on the Lewis legacy when he bamboozled Russia’s 7ft giant Nikolai Valuev and thereby emulated Holyfield’s feat of an undisputed cruiserweight king becoming world heavyweight champion.

The Russo-Ukraine brothers Klitschko broke the US domination but then both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua followed that Lewis victory over Vitali by vanquishing Wladimir.

British heavyweight boxing was transitioning from famine to feast, which has included the likes of Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua (right)

Britannia’s Rule was stunningly interrupted by Oleksandr Usyk’s revival of the Kyiv Conspiracy with two dazzling victories apiece over the Gypsy King and AJ, followed by another double over their heir apparent Daniel Dubois.

Oleksandr The Great’s abrupt relinquishing of all the belts opened the gateway to an immediate UK renaissance. One in which it is not Americans but Brits fighting each other for the glittering prizes.

This Saturday at the O2, Dubois and the amazingly reconstructed white-collar boxer Fabio Wardley reprise their blood and thunder war for the now-respected WBO title. This time with Dynamite Daniel as the champion.

The winner is likely to go on to meet in the not-too-distant future whoever prevails in the over-long awaited settlement between Fury and Joshua - which, belatedly though it comes in December, is so full of fascination that it has sold ticket at prices higher than the gross national product of some third-world countries.

By then Moses Itauma should have recovered from the drastic loss of stamina – and a blown IBF title shot against Croatia’s Filip Hrgovic – to resume leadership of the next generation. German WBC champion Agit Kabayel will soon be in all those crosshairs.

With all the above except Joshua in Frank Warren’s stable there are more Brit-bashes galore waiting to be made. With only one big guy of promise, Jared Anderson, to be seen on the western horizon.

And to think Americans used to belittle their last heavyweight champion of note Deontay Wilder as ‘just a puncher’.

The biggest puncher since Iron Mike, as it happens. How they must be wishing over there that Fury had not ended the Bronze Bomber’s five-year run of knockouts in the murderous final act of their epic trilogy.

Daniel Dubois (left) and Fabio Wardley (right) will face off this weekend with more Brit-bashes galore waiting to be made

Throughout America’s glorious boxing history the world heavyweight champion was the symbol of their national manhood. Today they lay no claim to any of the alphabelts.

There are extraneous factors at work. The majority of strapping young American athletes - be they graduating from college or seeking ways out of the projects - are taking to basketball, their version of football and baseball, rather than take a headbashing in the ring on the off-chance of making their fortunes.

US boxing is down to pinning its hopes on a brash young Mexican-American welterweight Ryan Garcia - on the back of his destruction of a humiliated Conor Benn. All while the Blue Riband of the ring is hoisted this side of the pond.

Not so Yankee-Doodle-Dandy now, gentlemen.

Sports.title: England captain Harry Kane agrees new contract to stay at Bayern Munich until 2029
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has agreed a new contract that will tie him to German champions Bayern Munich until 2029.

The England captain is in the form of his life, netting 50 goals so far this calendar year, and he is currently the front-runner to win the Ballon d'Or.

Having taken his country to the World Cup semi-final, clubs such as Barcelona were monitoring his situation, with the forward keen to sort his future following the summer tournament.

That has now been done, and it's bad news for Europe's other top sides, with Kane verbally agreeing a new three-year contract.

The Bundesliga side are now said to be drawing up the paperwork to make the new deal official. Kane will be 36 when the contract expires.

Kane and Bayern had both said there was 'no rush' to sort his future before the summer, with the forward saying in May: 'It's not the time to talk about that now, but there's no panic. We wanted to hold conversations until the end of the season and we've got a World Cup still to play.

Harry Kane has verbally agreed a new contract at Bayern Munich that will keep him at the club until 2029

Kane and his wife Kate (left) has settled into life in Germany since moving there three years ago

'But everyone knows how much I enjoy it here. That situation is calm.'

His initial deal had run until the end of this season after he signed a four-year deal after moving to Bayern for £100million from Tottenham in 2023.

The striker believed to be on around £400,000-a-week in Germany. There is no indication on if he will receive a pay rise with his new deal.

He and his young family have settled into life in the country, with Kane and his wife, Kate, often seen taking part in community activities such as Oktoberfest celebrations.

The couple and their four children moved to the county from north London three years ago and it seems they will not be heading home any time soon.

The forward continues to break records for both club and country, too, having equalled Peter Shilton's England cap record over the recent international break with his 125th appearance – a number he will almost certainly take to 126 next month.

At Bayern, meanwhile, he became the fastest-ever player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals (in 98 games) and scored the most goals in a player's first 50 appearances in the league (55).

He has won the Bundesliga twice while with the club, as well as the German Cup and two German Super Cups.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez says SORRY! Argentine apologises for angry interview calling out Man United's hierarchy - as he concedes his words 'did not help' after showdown talks with bosses
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez says SORRY! Argentine apologises for angry interview calling out Man United's hierarchy - as he concedes his words 'did not help' after showdown talks with bosses

Lisandro Martinez on Thursday night apologised for his withering takedown of Manchester United’s hierarchy after ‘positive’ clear-the-air talks with director of football Jason Wilcox and other key figures.

A fuming Martinez publicly criticised Wilcox and United’s top executives after defeat to Atletico Madrid for not backing manager Michael Carrick in the summer transfer window and for not fronting up to criticism after a miserable start to the campaign.

Martinez looked to clarify his remarks with a statement on Instagram on Wednesday – the squad’s allocated day off following the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid – before releasing a fresh statement after talks with Wilcox and the board.

He is also understood to have accepted a fine.

‘It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after the game,’ Martinez said.

‘Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

‘The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.’

Lisandro Martinez has released another statement after meeting with Man United chiefs

While Martinez has for the first time apologised for the timing of his remarks, made just moments after the match concluded in Spain on Tuesday, it is not clear whether he apologised privately for the nature of his blistering critique, particularly of Wilcox.

Club sources stressed that Martinez alone made the decision to apologise publicly for his comments. The matter, in the eyes of United’s hierarchy, is seen as closed.

‘Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that,’ he added in his latest statement.

‘I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition: bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve.

‘With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together.’

Carrick, who was also present in Thursday’s crunch meeting at Carrington, is going to need Martinez on Sunday when United travel to Elland Road to face Leeds United, not least with Noussair Mazraoui, Patrick Dorgu and Luke Shaw all already sidelined at the back.

Martinez’s long-term future is more uncertain, however. He is out of contract at the end of June, although United can extend it by another year.

If there is no resolution in the coming weeks, Martinez is free to negotiate with clubs outside of England for a pre-contract agreement.

United are unlikely to let a 28-year-old World Cup winner leave as a free agent five years after his £57million move from Ajax, but could trigger the extension so they can demand a transfer fee for him.

Sports.title: Louis van Gaal claims Man City antics influenced 'deciding factor' in Man Utd sacking
Sports.content:
Louis van Gaal claims Man City antics influenced 'deciding factor' in Man Utd sacking

Louis van Gaal was sacked by Manchester United in 2016 having missed out on the Champions League - with Manchester City topping them during a period where they were breaching financial rules

View 2 Images Louis van Gaal lasted two years before being sacked by Man Utd (Image: PA)

Louis van Gaal has bemoaned Manchester City's cheating scandal with his Manchester United sacking coming after he narrowly missed out on the Champions League - with their neighbours the ones to pip them to fourth spot.

‌



‌



The Dutchman lasted two years at Old Trafford, but a fifth place finish in 2016 proved to be the final straw and he was shown the door with Jose Mourinho replacing him.

‌



Van Gaal's final game was the FA Cup final, where he claimed victory over Crystal Palace, but 24 hours later he received his marching orders, owing to a poor league campaign that saw United capitulate from December, finishing outside the top four on goal difference.

‌



It was City who edged them and Van Gaal believes that their league position was the "the deciding factor" in him losing his job - and that frustration has only furthered after the Etihad outfit were found guilty of 114 financial breaches from 2009 to 2018.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Van Gaal told the Athletic: “For me, at the time, that (missing out on the Champions League in 2016) was probably the deciding factor in my dismissal from Manchester United and all the consequences and suffering this entailed.”

City's guilty verdict came after years of investigating, and has already been appealed by those on the blue half of Manchester, but Van Gaal claims irrespective of what happens next “I cannot turn back history now. Not even the English Football Association can (do that).”

Van Gaal saw his United team claim four points in the games against City in the 2015/16 season - drawing at Old Trafford before they secured a statement win at the Etihad with a young Marcus Rashford scoring the only goal of the game.

‌



View 2 Images Man City beat Man Utd into fourth place in 2016

Despite Van Gaal's frustration United can only have themselves to blame with fourth spot within their grasp going into the final weeks of the season. They had control of their own destiny but they lost at West Ham in the penultimate game of the campaign and that gave City the breathing room they needed.

Van Gaal left United having won 54 of his 103 games, giving him a 52 percent win rate. He was the second manager to take charge in Manchester after Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, replacing David Moyes in the aftermath of the World Cup in 2014. He finished fourth in his first season, but couldn't repeat that feat.

Sports.title: Man Utd ROCK BOTTOM in Europe as five-year transfer splurge completely exposed
Sports.content:
Man Utd ROCK BOTTOM in Europe as five-year transfer splurge completely exposed

Lisandro Martinez's post-match interview comments have brought further scrutiny on Manchester United's transfer business

View 2 Images Man United's squad value has plummeted highlighting their diminishing power in Europe. (Image: PA)

Manchester United have come under the spotlight after one of their key players took aim at the recruitment in the wake of their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Sporting director Jason Wilcox was targeted as Lisandro Martinez hit out at the recruitment.

‌



‌



His angry reaction to their first defeat in the Champions League, and a third in the last five, comes with the club in their latest plight, with Michael Carrick already under pressure. They were busy in the summer as they moved to replenish the midfield following the departure of Casemiro.

‌



However, a recent report from Football Observatory has found that United's squad value has plummeted by a staggering £342million - the steepest drop of any club across Europe.

‌



Harry Kane verbally agrees Bayern Munich deal - but fails to get desired contract length READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez makes Man Utd apology after meeting with Michael Carrick and club chiefs READ MORE :

The 28-year-old has since apologised for words but they have split opinion amongst supporters. While some back the sentiment behind his message, others have speculated whether there was an alternative agenda at play.

One thing is certain, Manchester United remain a considerable distance from the lofty standards they achieved during Sir Alex Ferguson's reign at the club and have not secured the Premier League title since 2012.

Managers have arrived and departed, as have players. Yet there's particular focus on the club's recent recruitment strategy, having ended up 15th in the 2024/25 campaign before Michael Carrick steered them to a top-four placing last season.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Martinez believes that the current United squad is not equipped for Champions League football and anticipates more from the club during the latest summer transfer window.

United splashed out £191.7million on new players over the summer, despite the club announcing they had allocated £155m to secure four signings, Karl Darlow, Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos. While there was a concerted push to bolster the midfield, supporters had been hoping to see a new left-back and striker arrive at the club.

‌



It proved to be a frustrating summer, and a recent study examining the club's transfer activity since 2022 only serves to highlight just how sharply the club's fortunes have declined.

Ironically, Martinez himself joined in 2022, and over the past five years, United's squad value has fallen dramatically despite a strategy of targeting younger players with significant potential since Sir Jim Ratcliffe took charge nearly three years ago.

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez spoke plainly about Manchester United's situation (Image: @primevideosport)

‌



The report has found that the Red Devils are the only club to suffer a greater fall in player value was Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Hilal, whose squad depreciated by £424.6m, according to the same report.

The decline is comfortably the most severe of any English club, with Tottenham Hotspur - who have also endured a turbulent period - the nearest to United, registering a depreciation of £99.8m.

The findings make for grim reading when set against Manchester City's squad value, which has actually grown by £378m over the same period.

‌



The figures will only lend weight to Martinez's argument that recruitment has fallen well short of the required standard in recent years. That said, it is worth noting that the responsibility cannot fall entirely on Wilcox's shoulders, given that he only took up the role of technical director in 2024.

The analysis covers the period from 2022 to the present day, meaning Wilcox and the recruitment department can only be held responsible for the last two years.

In 2022, United splashed out heavily on Casemiro, Antony and Martinez. While Casemiro ultimately won supporters round, the Brazilian represented a costly investment at £70m for a player who was then 30, and his fellow countryman Antony proved to be a hugely expensive failure, commanding £86m.

‌



Martinez, who arrived for £56.7m and is now valued at an estimated £38m, remains the sole player from that transfer window still at the club. The subsequent summer saw Mason Mount, Rasmus Hojlund and Andre Onana all brought in for substantial fees, and they have since struggled, with their valuations dropping well below the sums paid.

Hojlund has departed the club on a permanent basis for nearly half what United forked out, while Onana is away on loan, and Mount's worth has nosedived following persistent injury problems and disappointing displays.

Other significant acquisitions in recent seasons who have failed to hit form and are now valued considerably less than when they arrived at the club include Joshua Zirkzee, Manuel Ugarte and Leny Yoro.

Article continues below

United's £200m spending spree on fresh attacking talent last summer proved largely successful, with only doubts surrounding Benjamin Sesko, though there were encouraging indicators as the Reds secured third place under Michael Carrick. Nevertheless, there is widespread agreement that the recruitment team erred this summer, having failed to land several priority midfield targets including Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Elliot Anderson.

Instead, United splashed out £155m on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, with all three failing to deliver thus far. Reports emerged last week suggesting that, behind closed doors, United bosses acknowledged they had misjudged the summer transfer window and regretted not bringing in a new left back, with injury-prone Luke Shaw their sole senior option in that position.

United's campaign has begun disastrously, and Martinez's furious interview outburst has done the club no favours whatsoever. While United are backing Wilcox despite some within the squad sharing the view that their summer recruitment fell short, the CIES study has laid bare their wasteful spending in recent years.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte 'tells Man Utd bosses' he would be keen to replace Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Antonio Conte 'tells Man Utd bosses' he would be keen to replace Michael Carrick

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is under mounting pressure and Antonio Conte, currently out of a job, would be keen to replace him if a change was made

View 2 Images Antonio Conte is a man looking for a job (Image: 2024 Soccrates Images B.V.)

Antonio Conte has made it known to Manchester United bosses that he would be keen on the job if they did decide to axe Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



The Premier League season is only six games old but, after their worst start to a season in 40 years, there is major pressure on the Red Devils. Carrick was handed the reigns permanently in the summer after an impressive interim spell, but has found things tougher going this term.

‌



He's presided over just one win in six games and already been dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton, who came back from 2-0 down to win at Old Trafford.

‌



Carrick's CV was flagged as a concern by some onlookers, but United chose to give him the job regardless, and he's now feeling the heat. Conte is a man out of a job having left Napoli in the summer.

The Italian, whilst enduring relatively brief stints in his previous jobs, is a known winner and has delivered league titles at Napoli, Inter Milan and Chelsea over the past decade.

TalkSport understands his representatives have made it clear to those calling the shots in Manchester that he would be open to the role if they did part with their current boss.

Conte left Napoli in the summer after two years, finishing second to Inter Milan last term after winning the Scudetto in his debut season. His success with Chelsea is well documented, winning the title in his first season before claiming the FA Cup the following year, beating Manchester United in the final.

‌



Conte's job hint

The Italian, who also had a brief period in charge at Tottenham, made it known recently that in his next job he wanted to restore a fallen giant - a category that United would fall into. They are without a league title since Sir Alex Ferguson left in 2013 and have failed to challenge in the 13 years since.

View 2 Images The heat on Michael Carrick has ramped up after the loss at Atletico Madrid, which was followed by Lisandro Martinez's outburst

They are no longer even Champions League regulars but Conte spoke about a desire to make a powerhouse name a winning outfit when he spoke about his next challenge.

Article continues below

He recently told the Athletic: "If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself - a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories - you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back, if it isn't there today, to fight for those goals.

"There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history. I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more. Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete."

Sports.title: Andy Burnham issues new statement and orders 'manual trawl' to uncover Man City documents
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham issues new statement and orders 'manual trawl' to uncover Man City documents

Andy Burnham continues to face scrutiny over his dealings with Manchester City during his time in office as mayor

View 2 Images Andy Burnham says he has asked for a 'manual trawl' of data relating to his dealings with Man City. (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham says he has asked for a 'manual trawl' of records relating to contact with Manchester City. The Prime Minister continues to face questions over his relations with the Premier League club during his time as mayor in Greater Manchester.

‌



City have appealed the decision by the independent commission which found them guilty of over 100 breaches of Premier League financial regulations. Uncertainty surrounds the future of Enzo Maresca's side, with the list of sanctions ranging from points deductions to relegations out of the top-flight, and potentially the English Football League (EFL).

This week, declarations of Burnham's contact with City were released but it emerged that records of two dinners with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak were deleted. During his time as mayor, he declared dinners valued at a total of £1,000 for hospitality.

The Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) mentioned an informal meeting in the stands in 2019 and a formal meeting at the UK Government's Global Investment Summit in 2021 but two dinners were not specified. The Prime Minister has now said that he has asked the GMCA to go through the records with a fine-tooth comb.

He said: "It was included in the statement, it referenced meetings and hospitality at Manchester City when I was there as a guest. It did mention it, it was not prepared by me, it was prepared by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, so it was comprehensive.

"I've asked them to do a more manual trawl because I want everything possible to be out there. There is no question about that full transparency."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

City's ongoing legal battle with the Premier League has sent shockwaves within not just the footballing world but the wider community too. With the potential threat of political interference, Independent Football Regulator David Kogan has warned the PM that he will resign if the government step in.

He said: "Let me be really, really clear about this. You'll be aware that the original legislation brought in by the Conservative Government had in it a reference which we have to take some regard of some British trade relationships. That was removed from the legislation.

"Actually this was specifically discussed when it was going through Parliament so we are absolutely bound by one thing and that one thing is regulating football and regulating football clubs.

View 2 Images Prime Minister Andy Burnham with Manchester City Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. (Image: PA Wire)

"Considerations beyond that are beyond our view and are not going to be part of any decision that we make about any outcome of any club that we regulate.

"Our independence is absolute and my independence personally is absolute. I made it very clear last year that if have any form of Government interference on the way we operate is going to result in me resigning from this role and I stand by that completely.

"I should say, to be crystal clear, we've come under absolutely no political pressure on this or any other topic and I don't expect to in the future. Ministers know full well that we are going to act completely independently."

Sports.title: Entrepreneur who found route to racehorse ownership from ‘ChatGPT’ buys 23 horses
Sports.content:
Entrepreneur who found route to racehorse ownership from ‘ChatGPT’ buys 23 horses

Romy Sia, founder of an organic food retailer in the Philippines, has been on a spending spree since April and has even bought a house in Epsom

View 2 Images Romy Sia: bitten by the horseracing bug (Image: Tattersalls)

A Philippine entrepreneur has been bitten by the racing bug after researching the sport on ChatGPT.

‌



‌



Romy Sia founded an organic food retailer Healthy Options in his home country in 1995 and has developed it into a business which now operates throughout Asia.

‌



He had no involvement in horse racing until earlier this year since when he has been buying horses to race in Britain and Australia. He started spending earlier in the summer and during October has splashed out on more yearlings at the elite Tattersalls October Sale in Newmarket, making acquisitions at both Book 1 and Book 2 auctions.

‌



Aidan O’Brien expects Champions Day upturn from Constitution River and Gstaad READ MORE :

Sia, speaking to Tattersalls, said: “I’ve always been interested in horse racing but never knew anyone who could bring me to Ascot or Epsom and so I started asking ChatGPT back in April and it’s just like falling into a rabbit hole.

“Every time I asked a question, I got an answer. Finally I discovered I could own horses through syndication, just buying a small share and from there I didn’t stop.”

‌



He continued: “Now I have 23 horses, 12 in Australia and 11 here but I just bought four in this sale alone. I bought three at Book 1 with partners, 50 percent some of them or 37½ others. I’ve been very busy.

View 2 Images George Scott: will train for Romy Sia (Image: Martin Dokoupil/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

“It’s amazing. It’s out of this world. I’ve always thought why haven’t I done this before. Everything is thanks to the good people I have met.”

Article continues below

One of his earliest purchases, a yearling filly secured for Sia in Ireland in July, is to be trained by Jamie Insole while others will be shared among several different trainers.

Sia, who attended the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe earlier this month, said: “The ones we bought last week and this week, one will go to George Scott, one to Karl Burke. Yesterday we bought one for Andrew Balding and I’ve also got a share in one with Roger Varian.

“I plan to buy some more at Tattersalls and hopefully win races in Royal Ascot and Epsom, because I bought a house in Epsom just to be near the horse racing.”

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes 'deserves respect' after 'carrying history of Man Utd on his shoulders'
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes 'deserves respect' after 'carrying history of Man Utd on his shoulders'

Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes has been defended by former player Ander Herrara, who has hit out at the criticism levelled at the Portuguese playmaker

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has not been at his best this term as Man Utd struggle for form (Image: Getty Images)

Ander Herrera has told the critics to stop hammering Bruno Fernandes and show the Manchester United captain more respect. Fernandes has faced some flak following a mediocre start to the new season.

‌



‌



The midfielder has been nowhere near his best, with United winning just two of their opening nine games in all competitions.

‌



But former United star Herrera has leapt to the defence of Fernandes - and insisted he deserves huge gratitude for carrying the team on his back in recent seasons.

‌



Appearing on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast, Herrera said: "For me, he's a leader. He has had Manchester United on his back a lot of years, a lot of seasons. Sometimes playing, I'm not going to say alone, but carrying the history of the club on his shoulders.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"In difficult times he was there, always putting his face there, asking for the ball, scoring goals, assisting. After defeats, going to the media to talk. I have huge respect for him, for what he has done for the club. And he could have left the club and he's still there, putting his face in difficult moments and he deserves credit. A lot of credit. How can Bruno be the problem? He has been a solution a lot of times."

Michael Carrick is feeling the heat, following a woeful run of six games without a win. But Herrera remains convinced Carrick is the right man for the job - and will bring success back to the fallen giants.

He said: "We have to give him time because, as I told you before, the Premier League that I found was not the same Premier League that you found. And Michael, when he got in charge, the Premier League now is not top four, top five. It's almost top eight.

‌



View 2 Images Ander Herrera insists Michael Carrick is the right man to lead the club (Image: Getty)

"So I think we have to give time to the coaches, to the managers, to build something, to create something. And I think Carrick is the man. I want him to be the man, but I also believe he is the man to bring trophies to the club. I don't know if he will win the Premier League in two or three years, but he is going to be there. He's going to be competing. I'm sure of that."

Herrera spent five years at United, winning four trophies, including the FA Cup and he was left heartbroken when United bosses failed to give him a new and improved deal. Instead, the club wrote him a letter informing him of a 12 month extension, which left him so fuming he decided to join Paris Saint Germain.

‌



Herrera added: "After my third season, when I won the 'Player of the Year' award, I expected the club to come to me. I said to my agent, 'whatever they offer is going to be OK. I'm going to sign because I want to stay at United. I'm so happy.

"They didn't come, so I started to feel sad. And I remember what killed me is when they sent me that letter saying we are going to renew automatically your fifth season at the club. They didn't even call me to say, 'Ander, we want you to stay'. They sent me a letter. When I received that letter I thought, 'I'm done'. My heart was already a little bit broken."

Sports.title: Man City misdemeanours will not impact on football's integrity - only the Premier League's
Sports.content:
Right, a confession. I’m not spectacularly bothered by Manchester City’s cheating. Of course, in a professional capacity, I’m obliged to find it outrageous, abhorrent even.

In a professional capacity, I’m compelled to portray the proprietors of the club as pariahs and be sickened by the sight of its current stars carrying on with life as normal.

Personally, though, I’m not dramatically fussed. That’s the truth. Their years of impropriety had no significant impact on my club - if it had, my feelings would certainly be different - and I quite enjoyed watching their brand of football. That’s the truth.

Like anyone who values fairness in sport, I deplore and condemn City’s deception but I haven’t lost a wink of sleep over it. Of course, they should be punished severely. I hope they are. What they did was fundamentally wrong. If the punishment includes removing all the honours won during the period when the offences took place, then fine.

‌



They probably won’t have the appetite for it, but the Premier League should be scrutinising City’s accounts from the most recent eight years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

City absolutely deserve all that is coming to them. But the bottom line is that a competition that has prided itself on its financial might has been undermined by one of its mightiest financial institutions breaking its financial rules. There is an irony in there somewhere.

‌



Who do we feel sorry for in this saga? The players and fans of the clubs who might have won the league had it not been for City’s fiscal chicanery. Obviously. But it doesn’t necessarily work that way. And there is no way I’m dabbing away tears for John W Henry and the owners of Liverpool, or the Glazer family and the owners of Manchester United.

We should all be outraged, the argument goes, because City’s scandalous behaviour has threatened the integrity of the game. Only it hasn’t. It has threatened the integrity of the Premier League. That is different. And for some, the Premier League is becoming hard to love. Take the champions, for instance.

Arsenal have always been a club that is easy to like. Great traditions. Do things the right way. Now, they have told staff that 60 jobs could be under threat at a time when the fanfare over Mikel Arteta’s new £20million-a-year contract has barely died down. Explain it how you like, that is a dreadful look.

View 2 Images Arsenal's recent redundancy announcement has not painted them in a good light (Image: Getty Images)

‌



So, when supporters of clubs outside the Premier League are asked about Manchester City’s misdemeanours, there is often little more than a shrug. The EFL is great, the non-league scene is great. There are wonderful storylines throughout the pyramid - and none of them involve VAR.

Last season, just under 24 million supporters went to an EFL match. And that figure will be matched or bettered this season, that is for sure.

The Premier League is also sensationally popular, there is no denying that. But the demographic status of the match-going Premier League fan is probably changing. Outside the Premier League, support comes overwhelmingly from local communities.

Sure, the State of the Game report from the Independent Regulator - published this week - paints a picture of a pyramid that is in dire financial trouble, with so many clubs on the brink of disaster. But that has always been the case. From my viewpoint, the love of the game has never been stronger on these shores.

‌



And Manchester City’s grave misdemeanours will not change that. Of course, there will be ramifications in the Premier League. But the game will go on and will be enjoyed up and down the land, regardless.
