Sports.title: Frank Warren Rates Dubois Wardley Rematch Even
Sports.content:
Frank Warren still views Daniel Dubois against Fabio Wardley as a 50-50 fight heading into Saturday night at the O2 Arena in London. Even though Dubois won their violent clash in May, Wardley dropped him in the first and third rounds, proving his power can alter the course of the bout instantly.

Dubois weathered that storm to secure the stoppage, yet those early visits to the canvas give Wardley massive confidence that he can flip the script. The real challenge for Wardley will be finishing the job if he gets Dubois in trouble again.

“I just feel that either of them can win. I think it’s still an even-money fight,” Warren told talkSPORT. “Daniel will go as favorite because he’s probably … got more experience as amateur as well as pro.”

Surviving clean bombs once does not guarantee Dubois can take them a second time. At the same time, reckless aggression could cost either man dearly.

“You’ve got to remember he called for this rematch,” Warren said of Wardley. “It was a brutal fight in May, and here we are now, and it’s on, and he believes that he can win it.”

Warren believes victory hinges on establishing the jab instead of hunting for wild knockout blows right away. For Dubois, a sharp jab keeps Wardley on the outside and stops him from landing cold early.

“For me, the key to this fight is getting behind the jab,” Warren said. “Not looking to lead with big punches, to actually go out and try and … jab and then let your shots go.”

Both heavyweights know what to expect after their first battle. The winner will be the man who made the right adjustments and capitalizes on them first. Neither fighter is built to play it safe, which is why Warren expects another explosive finish before the final bell sounds. Dubois proved his resilience, Wardley proved his firepower, and both step into the ring knowing one clean shot can end it.

When promoters preach boxing fundamentals and patience for a high-profile rematch, they are usually trying to protect their fighters from another grueling brawl. The problem is that fans are paying for fireworks, not a tactical chess match.

“They know each other’s strengths and weaknesses,” Warren said. “It’s who’s learned from the last fight and who can exploit what he’s learned.”

If Dubois and Wardley actually listen to Warren and spend 36 minutes trading cautious jabs from ring center, public reaction will be brutal. Paying premium pay-per-view prices on DAZN just to watch two sluggers neutralize each other behind the lead hand is the exact opposite of what made their May fight thrilling.

“I don’t think the fight’s going to go the distance, whatever happens.”

The thin undercard makes that risk even worse. Here, there is zero safety net. If the headliner devolves into a safety-first sparring session, the whole broadcast will disappoint, and the backlash from paying customers will land squarely on Warren.

Sports.title: Ermal Hadribeaj Taunts Sebastian Fundora Ahead Of Upset Bid
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora gave Ermal Hadribeaj an icy glare during Thursday’s final presser at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Tension spiked when Hadribeaj aimed an imaginary sniper rifle directly at the champion’s chin.

Fundora kept his cool. The towering titlist didn’t swat the hand away. He didn’t shove the challenger. He simply stared him down, leaving the theatrics entirely to the Albanian contender.

Many boxing fans dismiss Saturday’s DAZN broadcast as a total mismatch. They might be forgetting history. Brian Mendoza knocked Fundora out cold in 2023. Erickson Lubin battered him. Tim Tszyu landed heavy leather on him. Those past fights prove the champion absorbs massive punishment when his defense gets sloppy.

The height gap between the two southpaws is ridiculous. DAZN’s faceoff clip showed the eight-inch difference clearly. Hadribeaj stands five feet ten inches tall, forcing him to point his fake rifle skyward toward Fundora’s 6’6″ stature.

Landing real leather will prove vastly tougher than gesturing on stage. Hadribeaj has to slip past huge reaching punches. He must escape clean counters. Closing distance against the champion is tricky because Fundora actually loves trading in tight phone booths.

That exact habit offers Hadribeaj his clearest path toward an upset. Fundora constantly surrenders his height by planting his feet inside. Shorter opponents suddenly find themselves in prime position to connect clean shots.

Mendoza exploited that flaw with a brutal left hook. Hadribeaj hasn’t demonstrated that kind of world class power against elite fighters yet. Still, writing off the challenger ignores the defensive gaps Fundora regularly presents.

The champion stayed composed on stage. Bringing that same discipline into Saturday night keeps the challenger outside, preventing Hadribeaj from getting the messy close-quarters brawl he desperately craves.

Hadribeaj’s taunting is unlikely to get Fundora to fight with reckless anger. Fundora has been through heated build-ups before, taken real damage in wars with Lubin and Tszyu, and generally keeps an even temper outside the ring. At the presser, he watched the sniper pantomime without flinching or retaliating.

The interesting part is that Hadribeaj probably does not even need to make Fundora angry to get the fight he wants. Fundora naturally surrenders his eight-inch height advantage without any emotional prompting. His default setting is to march forward, plant his feet, and throw uppercuts and hooks in a phone booth.

He gives up range as a matter of style, not because his temper got the better of him. That was how Mendoza caught him, and that was how Tszyu landed punishing overhand rights before the cut changed the dynamic.

Hadribeaj’s hurdle is what happens when he actually gets inside. Fundora is lethal in close quarters, throwing sharp uppercuts that chew fighters up as they try to stay under his reach. If Hadribeaj spends energy looking for one theatrical, loaded-up counter shot against a guy who throws heavy volume in the pocket, he risks getting overwhelmed by the sheer number of punches coming back at him.

Sports.title: Devin Haney-Shakur Stevenson Purse Clash Could Sink Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson finally agreed on 145 pounds, but dividing the revenue could scuttle their bout before either man steps into the ring.

Talks have reached a critical point, putting the targeted November 28 date in Atlanta in real jeopardy. Settling on a catchweight gave both camps a clear target. Splitting the revenue creates a deeper rift because it hinges entirely on personal market valuation.

Haney’s November 28 date allows almost no room for further haggling. Just over six weeks remain on the calendar, meaning both boxers require signed contracts right now to launch proper training camps. Every day squandered bickering over percentages pushes that target closer to collapse.

Haney has every right to challenge an even split. He already proved his drawing power as a headline attraction. Agreeing to parity would concede commercial ground that his team believes Shakur has yet to earn.

Backing from Turki Alalshikh changes the financial landscape. Deep financial support guarantees a massive overall purse, but funding a guarantee is not the same as generating revenue through paying customers. Haney’s side will almost certainly demand terms that honor that distinction.

“A potential fight between Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson is facing obstacles,” Mike Coppinger reported, adding that negotiations were “reaching a critical stage to keep this fight alive.

Coppinger did not reveal the figures being discussed, but if Shakur wants an equal or larger share, that could be where the talks are getting stuck.

Haney holds the cards here. Devin has options, commercial value, and a willing audience. Shakur cannot afford another inactive stretch where he sits around polishing belts while the division moves on without him. If he lets his ego dictate both the scale and the purse split, Haney will simply walk, leaving Shakur with an empty calendar and nobody to blame but himself.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia-Teofimo Lopez Talks Advance For Early 2027
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are moving closer to a welterweight title fight in the first quarter of 2027, according to Mike Coppinger.

The January-through-March target gives Ryan a major payday to pursue without squeezing in another appearance in December. No firm date or venue was included in the update, and the fight has yet to be announced.

“Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are now in advanced talks to fight in the first quarter of 2027, sources tell. Expect this welterweight title fight to happen next. And it’s a big one,” said Coppinger on X. “I believe the Garcia-Teo fight will happen regardless of the WBA’s ruling here. Catterall could end up being elevated.”

Teofimo’s WBA mandatory obligation to Jack Catterall remains unresolved, but that doesn’t have to stop the Ryan fight. The WBA belt isn’t needed to sell this matchup. Ryan’s WBC championship would still be available, and the appeal comes largely from putting these two recognizable names together.

The belt’s greater value to Teofimo could be at the negotiating table. Arriving as a fellow champion gives him another argument when discussing his share of the money. Relinquishing it would remove that bargaining point.

However, if Ryan, his promoters, and the financial backers are willing to offer Teofimo comparable money without the WBA title, keeping it becomes harder to justify. He could surrender the belt, remove the mandatory obligation, and proceed directly toward the bigger payday.

Facing Catterall first would introduce a risk that negotiations alone cannot remove. Teofimo could lose, suffer an injury, or come through a difficult fight needing more recovery time. Any of those outcomes could affect the timing or financial terms of a Ryan matchup.

Catterall has publicly opposed stepping aside. The WBA ordered the fight and gave the camps until October 22 to reach an agreement, leaving Teofimo with a decision if the organization insists on enforcing its mandatory.

That makes the financial terms of the Ryan negotiations especially interesting. If the offer depends heavily on Teofimo bringing his championship, he has a reason to seek permission to bypass Catterall. If the money is essentially the same either way, relinquishing offers a straightforward route.

The WBA can determine what Teofimo must do to retain its belt. Whether that belt is worth keeping could ultimately come down to how much Ryan’s side is willing to pay him without it.

Sports.title: Agility Drills Cannot Mask Canelo Alvarez’s Fading Gas Tank
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is putting his feet through plenty of work ahead of Christian Mbilli, but a movement-heavy approach could leave him short of energy before their October 31 fight reaches its toughest rounds.

Alvarez trying to reinvent himself as a nimble mover at age 36 looks like a recipe for disaster. The math simply does not add up when looking at his gas tank and output history.

Against Terence Crawford, Canelo was barely working, averaging just 28 punches a round while trying to plant his feet, load up on single power shots, and conserve energy. Even with that rock-bottom volume and virtually zero ring traversal, he was visibly gassing by round six. His body has shown clear signs of mileage for several fights now, and stamina has always been his primary limitation whenever opponents force him to work at a sustained clip.

Now his camp is circulating clips of him running agility ladders, doing cone drills, and practicing lateral movement to stay off the ropes against Christian Mbilli. While it makes for good social media optics, applying that in a real fight is completely detached from reality. Moving your feet constantly under pressure takes far more conditioning than standing your ground and picking spots.

The work doesn’t stop for Canelo! 💯 🎥: @Canelo 🎟️ Buy #CaneloMbilli NOW at https://t.co/yxybEeoyF5 | Oct 31 | Mexico vs The World | Live on DAZN | @RingMagazine https://t.co/zDOn7OR9xH — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 15, 2026

Mbilli is a pure volume puncher who thrives on throwing 70 to 80 punches a round, pressing forward with reckless abandon. If Canelo’s tactical adjustment is to skip around the ring, make short escapes, and play keep-away, he is volunteering to burn the exact energy reserve he does not have. Avoiding shots on the move still costs cardio, and Mbilli will not politely hit pause between drills to let him recover.

Canelo has never been an elusive ring mechanic. He built his career on upper-body slips, tight high-guard defense, and brutal counter-punching off a solid base. The only way he beats a swarmer like Mbilli is by doing what he has always done best: planting both feet and landing shots hard enough to break Mbilli’s spirit and stop the forward march. If he spends the first four rounds burning his legs on lateral movement, Mbilli is going to drown him in volume before the second half of the fight even gets started.

That script is practically already written. If Canelo gasses out trying to play Willie Pep at 36 and drops the belt to Mbilli, the post-fight press conference will be a masterclass in deflection.

Fighters with that level of clout rarely say, “I cooked up a terrible game plan in camp, convinced myself I could turn the clock back eight years, and completely misjudged my own gas tank.” Instead, the narrative instantly shifts into passive corporate speak. It becomes “we made tactical adjustments that didn’t materialize on the night,” or Eddy Reynoso will quietly take the heat to protect the brand, talking about camp fatigue or lingering elbow issues that allegedly flared up in the dressing room.

The irony is that Canelo’s entire late career identity has been built on stubborn pride. He genuinely believes his ring IQ can outsmart the physiological clock. Attempting to dance and pivot away from an engine like Mbilli is purely an ego-driven attempt to prove he still possesses the agility of his prime 154- and 160-pound runs.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Puts Rematch Pressure on Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley believes Daniel Dubois faces the greater pressure in their rematch, with the champion needing to repeat his victory against a challenger who believes he has corrected the mistakes that cost him their first fight.

Dubois recovered from two early knockdowns to win. Wardley admits he became overconfident after that success, giving the champion an opportunity to recover. If Wardley avoids those mistakes, Dubois could face a different task this time.

“I think that for me, like again, it’s something Daniel’s gone through, but now he’s got three losses on his record,” Wardley told Fight Wire. “Two of those to Oleksandr Usyk, so you chalk them up a bit differently.”

Wardley argues that another defeat would put Dubois in a difficult position, while he views his own first loss as something he can repair.

“It just frees me up. It’s okay, we had a loss. Things didn’t go too great. Not the end of the world,” he said.

The pressure on Dubois goes beyond the number of defeats. He needs to demonstrate that his previous victory was repeatable, rather than a result that depended on Wardley getting careless after putting him down twice.

Wardley believes he has identified how he let that opportunity slip. Better decisions could leave Dubois with fewer chances to recover, although maintaining pressure without wasting energy or walking into punches will require more than determination.

“There’s a few adjustments to be made, a few things we need to capitalize on better, and then the fight’s ours,” Wardley said.

Dubois proved he could beat Wardley that night. Whether he can handle a more disciplined version remains unanswered. Wardley still has to deliver those improvements under fire, but the champion cannot assume the same openings will appear again.

Wardley also questioned Dubois’s conflicting comments about his punching power, suggesting some of his opponent’s remarks sound rehearsed.

“Especially when the camera comes out, some of the lines you can very much tell are forced, or they’ve at least been told to him to put in there,” he said.

The verbal sparring adds to Wardley’s portrayal of himself as the more relaxed fighter. Dubois’s harder task is showing that he has answers for the changes Wardley brings into the ring.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Calls Sebastian Fundora A Cheat Code
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga can’t understand how Sebastian Fundora fits into the 154-pound division. Looking at a workout photo of the WBC champion, he compared Fundora to a video game character and suggested he should be making his money in the NBA.

Fundora’s long legs and arms dominate the picture. Berlanga fights two divisions above him at super middleweight, yet even he sounds taken aback by the sight of someone that tall competing at light middleweight.

How do they allow him to box at 154lb he’s a cheat code character from GTA WTF 🤣🤣🤣 listen he would have been a 200 million dollar NBA player. This is unacceptable he looks like a building https://t.co/AYW3y9aSuM — Edgar Berlanga Jr (@EdgarBerlangaJr) October 15, 2026

Berlanga isn’t the first fighter to reach for a video game comparison. After Fundora stopped Erickson Lubin in April 2022, Terence Crawford called him “a cheat code,” comparing him to a created Fight Night boxer with the height turned up in a smaller weight class.

It’s an understandable reaction. Finding sparring partners who can prepare an opponent for Fundora is difficult enough. Then comes the task of getting past those long arms and landing on a head that sits well above the usual target.

The odd thing is that Fundora often gives opponents a chance by coming to them. He likes fighting up close, throwing short punches rather than spending every round keeping shorter men at the end of his jab. They don’t always have to chase him to get their shots off.

That makes him entertaining, even if Berlanga thinks his dimensions look unfair. Fundora can make 154. The men across from him have to figure out the rest.

His WBC title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj this Saturday is a harder sell. Hadribeaj is the mandatory challenger, but most fans know little about him. They’re waiting to see Fundora against the bigger names in a division with plenty to offer.

Hadribeaj gets his chance to make himself known once the fight starts. Until then, Fundora’s unusual frame is likely to draw more conversation than the matchup itself.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Faces Long Wait For Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Liam Paro booking another defense puts more distance between him and Ryan Garcia, though Garcia’s alternative choices present a far bigger hurdle. Matchups with Teofimo Lopez or Devin Haney carry massive commercial appeal, which could strand Paro well past his ideal timeline.

“We’re not going to sit on the sideline,” Paro told Fox Sports Australia.

Staying active is the smartest move Paro can make. Continuing to take bouts keeps him sharp instead of burning months chasing an opponent who sees little urgency to fight him.

Teofimo gives Garcia an established American audience. A return bout with Haney carries built-in personal drama. Paro holds a world championship belt, yet hardware alone might not outweigh the bigger paydays Garcia could chase instead.

The calendar for Ryan creates another headache. If Garcia sits out until May, that single appearance eats up the first half of 2027. Another high-profile date could easily swallow the remaining months, leaving Paro on the outside looking in despite handling his business in the ring.

Teofimo’s mandatory duty against Jack Catterall adds some problems, but it will not kill a potential Garcia meeting. The WBA might grant Teofimo an exception so he can keep the strap. Teofimo could also surrender the belt outright to lock down the more lucrative bout.

That situation does not assure Teofimo gets the nod. Still, Paro cannot count on sanctioning body politics to eliminate a popular name from contention.

Title dynamics bring further chaos. If Garcia meets Teofimo first, Paro must hope Garcia wins so the WBC unification prize remains intact. A Garcia loss instantly ruins that scenario before Paro ever secures a signed contract.

Paro holds the power to defend his title and keep his phone line open. He cannot dictate Garcia’s opponent, dictate fight results, or force Garcia to pursue undisputed status.

Taking another bout makes complete sense. Chasing Garcia is worth the ambition, but Paro must build an active calendar that keeps rolling even if Garcia never calls. Paro landing that fight in 2027 makes zero sense from Ryan’s financial perspective.

Ryan operates purely on box office scale. A return match with Devin Haney already has massive public heat, personal grudge, and built-in history that sells pay-per-view buys effortlessly. A fight with Teofimo Lopez brings two huge American fanbases together for an absolute blockbuster. Those two events generate monster gates. Paro simply cannot generate that kind of revenue in the United States.

On top of the financial gap, Paro presents a terrible risk profile for Ryan. Paro is a tough southpaw with an awkward style who makes life miserable inside the ring. Taking on that kind of stylistic headache for a fraction of the money Ryan can make elsewhere is bad business. Fighters in Ryan’s tax bracket do not volunteer for difficult nights unless huge checks back it up.

Then you have the calendar reality. Ryan is not fighting four times a year. If he takes a marquee date in the spring, that eats up the first half of 2027. A massive fall date takes care of the rest. Between Teofimo, Haney, or other lucrative names floating around, 2027 fills up instantly.

Paro holding a title belt does not move the needle for Ryan either. Ryan transcended the need for sanctioning body belts long ago because his name alone drives the promotion.

Ghana News.title: MTN Ghana trains civil society organisations on artificial intelligence
Ghana News.content:
Telecom giant MTN Ghana has organised a one-day Artificial Intelligence (AI) workshop for Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) at its Head Office in Accra, as part of efforts to deepen understanding of AI and its impact on society.

The event was attended by over 100 participants is an annual programm introduced as part of the company’s commitment to develop human resources in Ghana.

Delivering the opening address, the Acting Senior Manager for Corporate Communications at MTN Ghana, Efua Falconer, said AI is transforming every aspect of life, and no stakeholder should be left behind. "AI, transformation. It is indeed transforming everything around us. And we cannot leave you behind," she said.

We've had these conversations in secondary schools, in the communities, in the markets, with our media, our regulators, across all the different stakeholders that we work with. And today is your turn," she added.

Ms Falconer said the workshop brought together seasoned AI professionals to build the capacity of participants through practical and interactive sessions. She urged participants to be attentive, engage fully, and follow the practical demonstrations on their laptops.

Our message here today is very simple. It's an interesting conversation. You will learn a lot if you are attentive. Please make sure you ask questions; there's a lot of practical work. Engage, take your laptop and just follow along," she said.

She explained that while government regulates and companies like MTN build the infrastructure powering the AI journey, civil society plays a critical role as the voice of the vulnerable.

You are the mouthpiece of the vulnerable, the youth, the market woman who doesn't know a lot about data, the school children who are using data. You are the people who speak for the vulnerable in society. So we cannot leave you out of this conversation," she stressed.

Ms Falconer said MTN was confident participants would take the knowledge acquired beyond the walls of the training room and apply it in their various spheres of influence.

"If we don't, we are going to be left behind. You give the kids today a mobile phone, and the kind of things they are able to do within a short period; you at 40, 50, you can't do it. So please, they are leaving us behind. So we have to catch up.

And the youth, this is your time," she told participants.

Speaking on behalf of the Chief Corporate Services and Sustainability Officer, Madam Adwoa Afriyie Wiafe, the Senior Manager for Regulatory and Government Affairs at MTN Ghana, Samuel Bartels, challenged CSOs to make their knowledge visible online.

He said CSOs do advocacy, interventions, and community work and know communities better than anyone, yet their rich knowledge is missing from the digital space that powers AI.

Do you know that a lot of the things that concern Africans are not online? If you call an AI tool for some information, it may not give you that perspective, because some of the things are still hiding in the Balme Library, and AI doesn't travel to the Balme Library at the University of Ghana," he said. According to him, AI can only work with what has been codified and put online, and currently only about 2% of the data used to train Large Language Models (LLMs) is from Africa.

Quoting a book titled Best Story Wins, Mr Bartels said only those who tell their story win.

He warned that if CSO research and project reports remain as hardbound documents locked in cupboards at their secretariats, AI systems will never learn from them. "So, in terms of storytelling, we are falling behind in this AI revolution because our information is just not available to train an AI model. So, the AI model will still tell stories that paint poverty, conflict and disease about us, because they don't have the alternative story," he said. He lamented that much of the content Africans now produce online is for entertainment rather than for reflection and knowledge sharing.

Unfortunately, a lot of the content we develop now is just for people to laugh, and not necessarily for people to think or reflect.

So, in the storytelling game, Ghana and Africa will lose out because our stories are not out there," he noted.

Mr Bartels said as technology emerges, two questions arise: what can the technology do, and what should we do with the technology? He said while the workshop would address what AI can do, CSOs must help answer what should be done with it, given their closeness to communities.

This is why it was important to have this conversation with you. It's important that we also listen to your perspective. What you hear in the communities, we at MTN may never hear.

What we may miss, you see," he said. Facilitating the first technical session, Data Scientist at MTN Ghana, Elie Tetteh Wayoe, said AI has become an opportunity for everyone and must be leveraged responsibly to serve society. "There is a new area that is coming.

It's making life easier. But for it to have impact, it must be used in the right way," he said. Mr Wayoe said MTN's vision is to ensure AI is made accessible and scalable for everyone, not just as a business tool, but as a force for good that is deployed responsibly.

Presenting on the topic "MTN and AI, focusing on responsible innovation for social and systemic impact," he said AI is not here to take people's jobs, but to augment human efforts. "If you don't make use of it, then you are the one who is behind. We don't expect AI to take everyone's place; it helps augment us to become better," he said.

He outlined MTN's AI strategy, which focuses on value creation and building a foundation for practical use cases, with emphasis on responsible adoption. According to him, for AI to be adopted responsibly, there must be guardrails, governance, trust principles, and human accountability. "You have to be accountable for what you do, for ensuring things will be done in the right manner. There has to be trust.

Without governance, responsible adoption is impossible," he said.

He added that the training would also explore practical examples of how AI can be applied in the daily activities and advocacy work of CSOs to enhance efficiency and deepen their social impact.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod FX framework aims to make dollar supply predictable – Acheampong
Ghana News.content:
Economist and political risk specialist Dr Theo Acheampong says GoldBod’s foreign exchange framework aims to make dollar supply more predictable, while the Bank of Ghana retains its role in tackling excessive exchange rate volatility.

The Finance Ministry’s Technical Advisor said transparency and advance planning were central to the arrangement.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, he explained that the framework should help the market anticipate foreign exchange needs and plan supply.

“What you want is a clear and transparent process that you know in advance how much, let's say, FX you need next week, next month, and then you can predict and provide that FX which is available.”

His comments followed a question from host George Wiafe about whether GoldBod’s involvement had the Finance Minister’s backing. The host also raised concerns about a possible overlap with the central bank’s responsibilities.

Dr Acheampong said the framework was already being implemented and that GoldBod had made its details public.

“GoldBod has communicated this very clearly to the market. The information is out there on their website.”

GoldBod announced its new Spot FX Sales and Intermediation Framework on October 5. It provides for dollar sales to authorised commercial banks, ordinarily on Tuesdays and Thursdays, through the GoFX platform.

Where demand exceeds available dollars, banks receive proportional allocations. The programme operates under the Bank of Ghana's regulatory oversight, with the central bank granted real-time access to the platform and to transaction reports after each sale.

GoldBod subsequently reported a maiden sale of approximately $125 million to commercial banks. The sale took place on October 6 under the new arrangement.

Dr Acheampong stressed that the central bank remained responsible for responding to sharp movements in the exchange rate.

“Remember that as part of the FX framework, the central bank would step in if they see excessive volatility within the exchange rate. That is the function of a central bank.”

He said instability in the cedi would require the Bank of Ghana to act.

“So if you see the cedi being wobbly and being all over the place, what is a central bank to do? It's meant to do its job.”

Ghana News.title: How does a Ghanaian team make it to the BAL?
Ghana News.content:
First, what is the BAL, and why does it matter?

The Basketball Africa League (BAL) is Africa’s premier men’s club basketball competition. A partnership between NBA Africa and FIBA, basketball’s international governing body, the league brings clubs from across the continent together to compete for the continental title.

For players, it offers the chance to compete professionally in Africa and showcase their talent to an international audience. For clubs, it creates opportunities to build a following, attract partners and strengthen the organisation behind the team.

The league is also exploring permanent franchises, with the aim of encouraging longer-term investment in teams, facilities and player development.

For Ghana, a place in the BAL would mean more than continental representation. It would put a Ghanaian club alongside some of Africa’s strongest teams, expose local talent to a wider audience and give young players a visible example of where their talent could take them. It could also strengthen the case for greater investment in basketball infrastructure, player development and the commercial growth of the sport.

Domestic success opens the door to continental competition, but Ghana does not have an automatic place in the BAL. Its route runs through the Road to BAL, the qualifying competition organised by FIBA Africa. Spintex Knights, three-time Greater Accra Basketball League champions, have represented Ghana in successive campaigns after winning the domestic league.

There are two main stages to navigate: the initial group phase and the Elite 16. For the upcoming campaign, those qualifiers take place in October and November 2026, with qualification for the 2027 BAL season at stake.

The Road to Qualification

Spintex Knights’ journey begins in Tripoli, Libya, from 21–25 October 2026.

The club has been drawn in West Division Group B alongside Energie Basketball Club of Benin, AS Douanes of Burkina Faso, NPA Pythons of Liberia and Red Flames of Sierra Leone.

The task is to finish in the top two to secure a place in the West Division Elite 16.

Before the club can think about the BAL itself, it must earn the right to keep going.

The Elite 16 is the final qualifying stage, split between the West and East Divisions. Its field includes teams advancing from the opening groups, alongside clubs granted direct entry or wildcard places.

The West Division tournament is scheduled for 10–15 November in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire. The top two finishers in the division secure BAL qualification.

In the previous two campaigns, the West Division format required teams to finish in the top two of their Elite 16 group and then win a semifinal. That semifinal victory secured qualification, with both finalists earning BAL places before playing for the division title.

Two Campaigns, One Goal

In 2024, on their first Road to BAL attempt, Spintex Knights became the first Ghanaian club to reach the Elite 16.

In 2025, the club returned and went further, reaching the West Division semifinals in Praia, Cape Verde. A 93–82 defeat to Jeunesse Club d’Abidjan ended the campaign, with JCA Kings securing the BAL place Spintex Knights had been fighting for.

The two campaigns demonstrated that a Ghanaian club could compete beyond the country’s borders. The next step is to convert that progress into qualification for the continent’s premier club competition.

But progress on the court requires resources off it.

The $200,000 Question

For Spintex Knights, the upcoming campaign requires approximately US$200,000 to support its continental ambitions. International travel, accommodation, transportation, training and preparation, player welfare, equipment and tournament-related logistics all contribute to the cost of competing at this level.

For a club representing Ghana on the continental stage, securing these resources is a major undertaking. It requires more than the commitment of players and technical staff. Corporate sponsorship, strategic partnerships, institutional backing and community support all have a role to play in making the campaign possible.

The investment also carries implications beyond the club itself. Competing at this level can give Ghanaian players greater exposure, provide valuable experience against some of the continent’s strongest teams and create a stronger platform for local talent to attract opportunities. A successful campaign could help build interest in the domestic game, encourage investment in basketball development and give younger players a clearer pathway towards elite competition.

However, these opportunities depend on Ghanaian clubs being able to participate and compete. When the financial demands of international basketball become a barrier, the consequences can extend beyond a single campaign. Players may lose valuable opportunities for exposure and development, while the country risks missing opportunities to grow its profile and strengthen its place in African basketball.

What Is at Stake for Ghanaian Basketball?

Spintex Knights return to the Road to BAL with lessons from two campaigns and a clear objective: to secure Ghana’s first appearance in the Basketball Africa League.

The club has already shown that it can progress through the qualifying stages. The challenge now is to assemble the resources required to take the next step.

The question is about what Ghanaian basketball stands to gain when a local club reaches the continental stage, and what could be lost if financial constraints prevent that opportunity from being pursued.

What happens to the ambitions of Ghanaian players if the pathway to continental competition exists, but the resources to pursue it do not? What does it mean for the future of the domestic game if Ghanaian clubs can earn their place on the court but struggle to finance the journey?

These are questions that extend beyond Spintex Knights. They speak to the kind of basketball future Ghana wants to build, the opportunities available to its players and the investment required to make those opportunities sustainable.

The journey to the BAL begins on the court, but getting there requires a collective effort off it. For Spintex Knights, the task is to compete for qualification. For potential sponsors, partners, and supporters, the opportunity is to help Ghanaian basketball take a step it has yet to achieve.

Ghana has the talent. The challenge is to give that talent the resources and platform to compete.

Visit ascent.spintexknights.com to learn more and support the journey.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s investment climate presents opportunities for industrial growth and job creation.
Ghana News.content:
Roshan Buddhagamage

Ghana’s investment climate is favourable for industries such as mining and construction to thrive, but sustained growth in these sectors will require investment in technical skills and job creation.

The Country Manager of Senok West Africa Ltd, Roshan Buddhagamage, says the expansion of industrial activity presents opportunities for businesses to invest in machinery and develop the local workforce needed to support the sectors.

Speaking at the official launch of the company’s authorised distribution of JCB construction machinery in Ghana, Mr Buddhagamage said the country’s mining and construction industries were contributing to economic growth.

According to him, investments in these sectors must also support the development of local technical expertise to ensure Ghanaians can participate in the opportunities created by expanding industrial activity.

“Ghana is actually growing. The economy of Ghana is growing because of these industries,” he said.

Mr Buddhagamage explained that the company’s approach would go beyond selling machinery to training mechanics and equipment operators.

He said JCB had trained more than 5,000 technicians across East Africa, adding that developing a technically competent workforce would be important to supporting the growth of Ghana’s mining and construction industries.

The skills development focus, he said, would help prepare local workers to operate and maintain heavy machinery as industrial activity expands.

The Deputy Managing Director for East Africa at JCB India Limited, Rupesh Nagar, says the company is looking beyond machinery sales to building the technical capacity needed to support Ghana’s growing industrial sectors.

Speaking at the official launch of the latest JCB machinery range, Mr Nagar said the country’s expanding mining and construction industries were contributing to economic growth and creating a need for a technically competent workforce.

“Ghana is developing as we speak. If you see the industry that we are present in, whether it is the mining industry or the construction industry, Ghana is actually growing. The economy of Ghana is growing because of these industries,” he said.

He explained that JCB’s approach would involve training local mechanics and equipment operators to ensure the country has the expertise required to operate and maintain heavy machinery.

“What we are providing assurance through JCB is we are not here to sell machines only. We are here for capability building of the industry,” he said.

“Our endeavour in Ghana is: how do we train the mechanics, how do we train the operators, to ensure that a few years down the line, you have manpower which is competent, technically trained to operate the machines,” he said.

He said building a technically skilled workforce would be important to the development of Ghana’s industries and the broader economy.

Ghana News.title: ‘I paid thousands to a company for jobs that never came’
Ghana News.content:
Apurv Patel said he paid Synetal Solutions £3,600 and claimed he was verbally promised a guaranteed sponsored job

A company has been accused of promising jobs in the healthcare sector which never materialised, leaving people thousands of pounds out of pocket.

Registered in 2025, Synetal Solutions Ltd says it offers career-focused training programmes in the healthcare and IT sectors.

But the BBC has spoken to a number of people who claim they were promised training and support to secure sponsored healthcare jobs that were never made available for them to apply for.

London Citizens Advice says it has seen an increase in recruitment-related scams since the government stopped overseas recruitment for care workers. The charity described the firm's practices as "unethical".

Synetal Solutions says it "takes these concerns seriously and disputes the broad allegation that its services or candidate outcomes are fictitious".

'Miserable'

Apurv Patel, who has been in the UK on a Skilled Worker visa since 2023, said he paid Synetal Solutions £3,600 across February and March for healthcare training after he and a friend were verbally promised guaranteed sponsored jobs.

Eight months later he has received no job offers, interviews or meaningful employment support, he said.

"I'm frustrated. I paid money, I wasted my time. I did whatever they wanted without any result," he said.

"It's had a miserable effect on my family and finances."

Patel said he did receive some training but described it as poor quality and ultimately "worthless".

Having previously worked for two years as a healthcare assistant, he said he became concerned when a trainer was unable to answer routine questions about care work.

"She didn't give us any answers and we realised she didn't have any experience of healthcare," he said.

The company disputes claims that training was ineffective.

He also alleged communication with the company deteriorated after he made his second payment, with responses sometimes taking several days.

Patel has since complained to his bank and sought help from Citizens Advice.

The BBC has seen emails from the company advertising a "three-month recruitment programme" offering "training and placement with sponsorship" for £5,500.

Home Office guidance states agencies may charge for services such as training or CV-writing assistance, but cannot charge fees solely for finding, or attempting to find, employment.

Responding to questions about its marketing, Synetal Solutions said: "We acknowledge the 'guarantee' wording in the emails supplied and recognise that contractual terms alone do not resolve concerns about those assurances."

As part of its programme, Synetal Solutions created accounts for trainees on iHasco, a health and social care training platform.

The BBC contacted iHasco, which confirmed the company was a customer. However, it said its terms did not permit customers to resell its training content to individuals who were not employees.

The company said it was reviewing Synetal Solutions' account and would take appropriate action if necessary.

Synetal Solutions said it had acted in accordance with its agreement with iHasco.

The Care Quality Commission said there was no single qualification that automatically qualified someone to work as a care worker. Instead, providers are responsible for ensuring employees are appropriately trained and competent for their roles.

The BBC also contacted a number of healthcare organisations whose logos appeared on Synetal Solutions' website as examples of employers where graduates had worked.

Those organisations that responded said they had no links to the company. Some also said they had not authorised the use of their branding, and some said they would not accept certificates provided through the company's training.

Daniel Blake says the way Synetal Solutions has operated is unethical

Daniel Blake, director of London Citizens Advice, described the company's approach as "exploitative".

"The promises that were made are impossible promises," he said. "They are targeting people with vulnerable immigration status.

"This company is asking for large sums of money upfront without any reputable standards, without any reputable evidence of success, and yet when it goes wrong they are refusing to take any responsibility.

"For us, it seems a very unethical way of conducting business."

He added that no reputable recruitment agency would guarantee a successful outcome without first assessing a candidate and matching them to a suitable role, and urged anybody asked to pay large sums upfront to seek independent advice.

"If it seems too good to be true, it probably is," he said.

The company's website stated: "Synetal Solutions provides the right support, guidance, and guaranteed job placement to help you succeed."

But since the BBC contacted Synetal Solutions mentions of job guarantees were removed from the website.

Its social media channels also promoted healthcare as "one of the most reliable paths" for people seeking visa-sponsored work in the UK.

The website previously promised applicants a job - but this has since been removed

Sarah and Rahul, whose names we have changed, said they paid £3,000 to Synetal Solutions while seeking sponsored employment before the expiry of their student visas.

Rahul, a former dentist in India, could remain in the UK on a graduate visa for longer, but Sarah's immigration status was close to expiring.

To pay the fee, the couple said they borrowed money from a family friend and took out a loan.

Rahul said he was shocked by the quality of the training.

"The mentor didn't know anything about healthcare," he said.

The couple said they were also shown the names of established healthcare providers, including Bupa, as examples of potential employers. Bupa told the BBC it had no connection with the company.

Synetal Solutions says some of their candidates "told us they had secured employment with Bupa" and the reference was "not intended to suggest a formal partnership with Bupa".

It says it had not verified those outcomes and "cannot attribute the recruitment decisions to our training".

Rahul said he secured one or two interviews, but prospective employers rejected the certificates he had received through the programme.

The couple said Synetal Solutions had since stopped responding to their messages.

"We're desperate," Sarah said. "We don't see any other way out."

Amisha - not her real name - says her certificates were rejected as invalid by one company she had an interview with

Amisha, whose name has also been changed, said she signed up with Synetal after being told that both a placement and visa sponsorship were guaranteed.

Her student visa is due to expire soon.

She said the training consisted of three sessions lasting around 90 minutes each.

After paying an initial instalment of £1,800, she became reluctant to make a second payment because she felt she had received little in return. She said the company warned her that her contract would be cancelled if she failed to pay, prompting her to transfer a further £1,800.

"I was waiting for interviews for two or three months. They were ignoring me," she said.

According to Amisha, the company applied for only a handful of vacancies advertised on job-search website Indeed. She eventually secured an interview for a healthcare assistant role, but said the employer told her the certificates she had received were not recognised.

A screenshot of a supposed testimonial from Synetal Solutions' website with content that does not appear to make sense

The BBC also identified what appeared to be at least a couple of stock photographs or AI-generated images used as testimonials on the company's website.

The company said it had not authenticated the two reviews identified, and removed them after we contacted them.

Teni Shahiean, an immigration lawyer at OTS Solicitors, said the promises being made to individuals facing visa deadlines were "particularly concerning"

Teni Shahiean, an immigration lawyer at OTS Solicitors, said it was "particularly concerning" where individuals facing visa deadlines were being asked to make substantial payments on the understanding that jobs, sponsorship or immigration outcomes were seemingly guaranteed.

She urged caution, adding that a job offer alone does not guarantee someone will be able to remain in the UK.

"The outcome can depend on the role, the sponsor, the individual meeting the relevant immigration requirements and, ultimately, any decision by the Home Office," she said.

'Go to the police'

Blake told the BBC: "If it seems good to be true, it probably is. If you are considering handing over money upfront then seek advice."

He said that "if people have given money and haven't received the service that they were entitled to they should seek redress".

"First of all, make a complaint directly to the company, then to Trading Standards.

"If people feel a criminal offence has happened, we would encourage and support them to go to the police."

A government spokesperson said: "We know how much distress scammers cause to their victims, which is why we will do everything in our power to protect hardworking families and vulnerable customers.

"Our reforms have provided Companies House with new and improved powers to prevent companies from acting unlawfully and to query, remove and share suspicious information."

Synetal Solutions said: "We provide training and employment assistance and maintain supporting records. Recruitment, sponsorship and visa decisions depend on employers and the Home Office."

The company said it had records of genuine candidates who had secured jobs and sponsorship through its services.

Ghana News.title: SSNIT intensifies informal sector enrolment drive with Techiman float
Ghana News.content:
The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has intensified its drive to bring informal sector workers onto the pension scheme, with a vibrant sensitization float through the principal streets of Techiman in the Bono East Region.

The exercise, a precursor to the launch of SSNIT's Customer Service Week, formed part of the Trust's Self-Employed Enrolment Drive (SEED) campaign, which seeks to provide a reliable source of income and financial independence for workers during retirement or periods of inactivity.

The float was designed to raise awareness about the importance of social security and to extend pension coverage to self-employed individuals and informal sector workers, offering them a safety net and social protection.

Speaking during the exercise, Alex Appiah, SSNIT Area Manager in charge of the Bono, Bono East and Ahafo regions, underscored the significance of taking the campaign to the doorstep of workers who are often too busy to visit SSNIT offices.

"We are targeting the people who are unable to visit our offices due to their busy schedules," he said.

Mr. Appiah stressed that joining SSNIT remains one of the surest ways for informal sector workers to guarantee their future, describing the Trust's product offering as unique.

"It is important to join SSNIT because they are unique in terms of the products they offer, which have to do with monthly payments until death," he explained.

The SEED campaign is SSNIT's flagship initiative aimed at extending pension coverage to the country's large informal sector, which includes traders, artisans, farmers, transport operators and other self-employed professionals.

Under the scheme, contributors enjoy:

· Lifetime monthly pension payments after retirement

· Financial independence during old age

· Social protection during periods of inactivity

· A reliable income for beneficiaries in the event of death

The Techiman float saw SSNIT staff engage traders, commuters and residents, explaining the benefits of the scheme and how self-employed persons can enroll.

The exercise forms part of a broader push by the Trust to demystify pensions and make social security accessible to every Ghanaian worker, regardless of whether they earn a formal salary or not.

Ghana News.title: Ghana seeks long-term mining investments that benefit local communities – Armah-Kofi Buah
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has reaffirmed Ghana’s readiness to partner with Guangdong Shengmai Tech Co. Ltd. to explore investment opportunities in the country’s mineral sector.

Speaking during a meeting with a delegation from the Chinese company, Mr Buah said Ghana was interested in investors who looked beyond short-term profits and demonstrated a commitment to developing the communities in which they operated.

He also emphasised the importance of responsible mining practices, urging investors to prioritise environmental protection and the restoration of degraded mining areas.

Mr Buah said Ghana expected mining companies to adopt sustainable practices that protect the environment while improving livelihoods in mining communities.

The delegation, led by Tang Zhong Chun, expressed the company’s interest in expanding its operations into Ghana, citing the country’s rich mineral resources, peaceful environment and investment potential.

Mr Tang highlighted the use of modern electromagnetic technology for mineral exploration, saying it could significantly reduce the time and resources required for exploration while promoting environmental sustainability and value addition.

He said the company was willing to work with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources and other relevant agencies to identify opportunities where its expertise could support the development of Ghana’s mineral sector.

Mr Tang also outlined the company’s long-term plans to establish a gold refinery and introduce a gold branding initiative in Ghana.

Ghana News.title: GHATOF demands compensation for 85 businesses affected by La Pleasure Beach demolition
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Tourism Federation (GHATOF) has demanded compensation for 85 businesses affected by the demolition at La Pleasure Beach, warning that about 4,000 jobs, largely held by women, have been put at risk.

The federation also called for the displaced traders to be given the first right of refusal in any redevelopment of the beachfront, questioning why businesses with operating permits were demolished without proper notice.

At a meeting with the affected traders on Wednesday, October 15, GHATOF said many of the businesses had operated at the beach for decades, contributing to the local economy through taxes, tourism levies and other statutory payments.

The federation is seeking accountability from the relevant district assemblies and public institutions that issued operating permits to some of the affected businesses.

GHATOF President Seth Ocran said the federation would pursue compensation for the traders and advocate for their inclusion in any future redevelopment plans.

He warned that the treatment of businesses that had obtained official permits could undermine investor confidence in Ghana's tourism sector.

The demolition has particularly affected women engaged in food vending, general trading and the sale of arts and crafts.

Some traders say they have lost their main sources of income, along with equipment and other investments made in preparation for the December festive season, one of the busiest periods for tourism-related businesses.

The federation argues that the impact extends beyond the loss of business structures, threatening livelihoods and employment opportunities linked to the beachfront economy.

GHATOF is therefore calling for the concerns of the displaced traders to be addressed as authorities consider the future of the site.

The demand for a first right of refusal is intended to allow the affected businesses to return if commercial activities resume after redevelopment.

The dispute has also raised questions about the protection afforded to businesses operating under permits issued by public institutions and the obligations of authorities when such businesses are displaced.

GHATOF said it will continue pressing for compensation and meaningful engagement with the affected traders over the future of La Pleasure Beach.

The federation maintains that the treatment of the businesses will have implications not only for the displaced traders but also for confidence in Ghana's tourism investment environment.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
