World.title: Israel halts commercial goods from entering Gaza; Hamas denies tax claims
World.content:
The halt to commercial shipments, including fruit and winter clothing, cuts off a key source of critical supplies.

Israeli authorities say no commercial goods have entered Gaza for two days, citing what they claim is a tax dispute between local merchants and Hamas.

COGAT, or the Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories, the Israeli military body that “oversees humanitarian affairs” in Gaza, announced the halt on Wednesday.

COGAT claimed that local merchants “made the decision in response to a 10,000 shekel ($3,220) fee imposed by Hamas on each truck entering Gaza” as well as a demand for 30 percent of all sales in Gaza to be carried out in cash.

This decision is expected to impact a crucial source of food and goods for the 2.1 million people in the Strip, who are completely reliant on Israel’s border crossings in a territory that is still suffering from famine.

Gaza’s government media office refuted the claims on Thursday and condemned the “blatant disinformation campaign and false statement”.

The media office instead said it was an attempt “to hold the government apparatus in Gaza responsible for the disruption of truck entry” and that the fee was a voluntary payment to a fund providing aid for those in need, such as widows and orphans.

It also said that cash payments were encouraged due to what it described as an acute cash shortage in the war-torn territory, but were never a mandatory requirement.

An already dire humanitarian crisis

The halt to commercial shipments, including fruit and winter clothing, cuts off a key source of food and other critical supplies as fears mount ahead of the encroaching winter.



Aid groups generally bring in staples such as flour, while merchants import more perishable foods like fruits and meat, according to data released earlier this year by COGAT.

The suspension is raising fears about affordability, with humanitarian workers saying a combination of aid and a robust commercial market is needed to keep prices under control.

“The humanitarian sector on its own cannot meet the needs of all the people,” said Shaina Low, a spokesperson for the Norwegian Refugee Council. “The markets need to be functioning.”

Local merchants step in

The head of Gaza’s private truckers union, Nahed Sheheiber, denied the Israeli narrative, saying: “The Israeli coordinator is claiming that Gaza’s merchants are responsible, but the truth is that the Israelis are the ones who imposed the restrictions.”

Following COGAT’s announcement, Sheheiber’s union met with Gaza’s Ministry of Economy to express concern and say Israel was citing fees levied by the ministry as a pretext to cut off commercial goods.

A global hunger monitor in July warned that more than two-thirds of people in Gaza could face acute hunger by the year-end.

Israel is obliged under a US-mediated agreement to allow a minimum of 600 trucks carrying humanitarian aid to enter Gaza each day.

Diplomats say that far fewer than 600 trucks normally enter Gaza each day. Sheheiber said the figure was closer to 300, with two-thirds carrying commercial goods.

World.title: Man United’s Martinez apologises for outburst after talks with Carrick
World.content:
Lisandro Martinez meets with his Manchester Untied manager Michael Carrick before apologizing for criticism of the club.

Share Man United’s Martinez apologises for outburst after talks with Carrick on social media

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for criticising the club’s hierarchy following their Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, after holding talks with manager Michael Carrick and senior officials.

Martinez met Carrick and club executives after training, two days after saying the club needed greater investment to help the team compete at the highest level following Tuesday’s 2-0 loss.

“Today I met with the club’s leadership and the manager,” Martinez said in an Instagram post, in his second statement since the interview.

“It was a very positive conversation where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game.”

A club source said that any internal disciplinary action would remain private, adding that it had been Martinez’s decision to apologise publicly and that all parties considered the matter closed.

British media, including the BBC, reported that United fined the defender over the outburst.

Martinez acknowledged that his frustration following the defeat had got the better of him and apologised for choosing the wrong moment to air his feelings.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity,” he said.

“The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

The Argentina international had singled out director of football Jason Wilcox in the post-game interview, saying United needed more signings to compete with their rivals and build a squad capable of challenging in Europe.



Martinez said his comments had not reflected the unity required at Old Trafford and stressed his belief that everyone at the club was working towards the same goal.

“Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that,” he said.

“I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition, bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve.”

Martinez finished his statement by drawing a line under the episode.

“With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together.”

United are 13th in the Premier League after six games in their worst start in 40 years. They travel to seventh-placed Leeds United on Sunday.

World.title: Trump administration sues California over noncitizens on voter rolls
World.content:
Lawsuit comes weeks before midterm elections and follows debunked claims of noncitizens voting in various states.

The administration of United States President Donald Trump has sued the state of California after the state missed a deadline to review a list of registered noncitizen voters sent to officials.

In the lawsuit, filed on Thursday in a US District Court in California, Department of Justice (DOJ) officials asked the court to prevent the state from counting mail-in ballots from voters on a list shared with the state that it said contained 20,000 noncitizens. The agency said it had attempted to “work collaboratively” with California to identify noncitizens registered to vote in the state, but “California made no serious effort to do so”.

The move follows a 48-hour deadline the DOJ gave California in letters sent to officials in several counties in the state on Tuesday, threatening further action if they did not review lists of allegedly ineligible voters the agency said it had shared.

California Secretary of State Shirley Weber, the top state official tasked with administering elections, responded to the letters, saying in a three-page letter that she wanted to “set the record straight” on events that transpired since July. The senior California official maintains that the administration is demanding “unprecedented measures that threaten thousands of Californians’ right to vote, based on unverifiable information or methodology that you still fail to explain or provide”.

Weber said she was informed that the lists provided to local officials include the names of roughly 20,000 individuals. Weber said no list was ever sent to her office. The department previously said it suspected “thousands” of registered voters of being noncitizens, and a lawsuit filed earlier Thursday by the Justice Department put the number at “tens of thousands”.



“Despite failing to send the list of alleged non-citizens to my office, you demand that we request transmittal of the list, review and confirm the citizenship status of each of the approximately 20,000 individuals on the list on the eve of an election and within a mere 48 hours,” she wrote. “This is an emergency of the DOJ’s creation.”

In a statement on Wednesday, election officials in Los Angeles County, one of the county offices that received the ultimatum from the DOJ, pointed out the threat was issued just 21 days before midterm elections. The county statement said it had received a thumb drive with the letter and a handwritten note with what appeared to be a password, but it would not attempt to access the drive because “we do not consider the device a secure medium”.

The county office said maintaining accurate voter lists was “a fundamental responsibility for our office” and that state laws clearly require that removing individuals be “based on verifiable information”.

Trump has repeatedly levelled the false claim that large numbers of noncitizens, who are legally not eligible to vote in federal elections, are casting ballots in Democratic-led states, including in California. State officials, including in California, have said the number of such voters is negligible and that the scale of the problem does not warrant intervention just weeks before elections, scheduled for November 3.

California Governor Gavin Newsom has sharply rebuked the DOJ lawsuit against his state, calling it a “sad, desperate attempt by” Trump to “suppress California voters just three weeks before Election Day”.

“Courts have made clear the federal government has no role in running state elections,” Newsom said in a statement. “We will defend free and fair elections in the Golden State and call out every authoritarian attempt to undermine our democracy.”

Trump has long falsely claimed that noncitizen voting cost him the 2020 election, blaming it on Democrats, despite the issue being a very rare occurrence.

Courts have pushed back on Trump

Earlier this month, a federal judge in Florida ruled that a federal law criminalising voting by noncitizens was unconstitutional, delivering a major setback for Trump administration efforts to pursue such cases against individuals.

The court ruled that, under the US Constitution, only individual states have the authority to set voter qualifications, and that each one had already criminalised such voting by anyone who was not a citizen. Thus, it was up to the state to prosecute such individuals. The DOJ has at least 45 such cases pending nationwide, where the accused could now raise the same objection brought up in the Florida ruling.



Another federal judge ruled this month that the DOJ unlawfully sought state voter rolls for cross-checking them against a controversial federal immigration database to identify ineligible voters. The Trump administration has often touted the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) database, but numerous reports have found it inaccurate and capable of flagging citizens as noncitizens. Forcing states to use such a database would be unconstitutional, the judge said.

In September, the US Supreme Court rejected a Trump administration effort to restrict mail-in ballots for the November 3 elections, which Trump argued were especially susceptible to misuse by noncitizens because states were failing to verify who was sending them.

Two dozen states, led by Democrats, filed lawsuits against the Trump administration over attempts to limit mail-in voting, including an executive order directing federal agencies such as the US Postal Service not to handle mail-in ballots without verifying the eligibility of those casting them.

According to the Election Assistance Commission, a bipartisan government agency, around 30 percent of all ballots cast in the 2024 elections were sent by mail. Mail-in ballots are even more widely used in many western states such as California.

World.title: ICE tactics spark debate before pivotal US midterm elections
World.content:
Polls have found that Trump’s hardline immigration enforcement effort has divided voters before the 2026 midterm race.

US midterms 2026: Is ICE still a Republican strength? | This Is America

United States President Donald Trump’s mandate for aggressive immigration enforcement has fractured public support in advance of next month’s critical midterm elections.

In the lead-up to the November 3 vote, Fox News released a poll that found 53 percent of registered voters felt the immigration crackdown had “gone too far”.

That rate was even higher among demographics that may be key to the Republican Party’s prospects in November.

The poll, conducted in September, found that 60 percent of independent voters agreed with the idea that Trump’s immigration efforts have overreached. Two-thirds of Hispanic participants also agreed with the campaign having “gone too far”.

Experts say the political debate about immigration in the US has shifted since the last major election in 2024. At the time, the focus was largely on border security. But increasingly, attention has fallen on how enforcement operations are being conducted.

Cynthia Penaloza is among those questioning the Trump administration’s tactics.

In August, her sister, 23-year-old Joceline Penaloza Magana, was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Houston, Texas, during a traffic stop. Joceline remains in custody to this day.

“We’re always afraid. We’re uncertain of what’s going to happen, if she’s going to be sent back to Mexico, if we’re ever going to be together again or how this is going to change our lives forever,” Cynthia told Al Jazeera correspondent Phil Lavelle.

She rejects Trump’s assertion that his administration’s immigration enforcement operations have targeted “the worst of the worst”.



Joceline, according to the Penaloza family, was an honour roll student who does not have a criminal record. She was brought to the US as a young child, about five years old.

“She’s always been a good girl,” Cynthia told Lavelle.

A focus on ‘criminals’

Still, the Trump administration has tied its campaign of mass deportation to efforts to control crime.

In a statement earlier this year, the Department of Homeland Security, which oversees immigration enforcement, credited Trump’s policies with having “unleashed ICE to target the worst of the worst criminal illegal aliens, including pedophiles, murderers, gang members, terrorists, and rapists”.

Immigration arrests have been on the rise under Trump. In September, ICE announced it had tallied two consecutive months with more than 50,000 immigration arrests, beating a record set in June, when 43,900 people were detained.

Homeland Security has argued that approximately 70 percent of its immigration detainees are criminals, if pending charges are factored in.

But critics have questioned that statistic, given that the legal system in the US gives suspects the presumption of innocence until they are proven guilty in a court of law.

In other words, many of the accused could be acquitted or see their charges dropped. A large portion of those with criminal charges may also be accused of non-violent crimes.

Analysts have found that a majority of people currently in immigration custody are not considered criminals under the law. According to the Deportation Data Project, which analyses government data sets, some 70 percent of those held in ICE detention have no criminal record.

The Trump administration has nevertheless pushed to increase detentions.

“We need more. We need more arrests, and we need more deportations,” Tom Homan, the White House “border czar”, said in an interview in July.

Pushback on the campaign trail

The aggressive arrest tactics may have repercussions on the Republican campaign for the midterms, though.

Republicans are hoping to defend their majorities in both chambers of Congress, as well as in key state and local elections.

Trump made significant gains in the 2024 elections with Hispanic voters. During his re-election bid, he received nearly 48 percent support among Latinos, according to an exit poll from the Pew Research Center — up 12 percentage points from the 2020 election.



But Pew found that his gains may be eroding. Among the Hispanic voters who supported him in 2024, his approval rating has steadily declined, from a high of 93 percent at the start of 2025 to a low of 57 percent as of last week.

Some Republicans running in the midterm election, including Congress member Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida, have even openly criticised the president’s hardline immigration policies.

“Mr President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far,” Salazar said in an  campaign launched in September. She cited the large number of immigrants who were arrested without a criminal record.

Other Republicans, however, blame previous presidencies for creating the conflict over immigration enforcement.

“A mess was created, and now cleaning it up is dirty business,” Jeremy Price, a Republican in Texas, told Al Jazeera. “You’re having to find people, arrest them against their will and remove them from the country because they don’t want to leave.”

Democrats, meanwhile, hope to convert that outrage over immigration enforcement tactics into votes, come November.

“I would hope they’d abolish ICE,” Richard Gonzales, the chair of the Hidalgo County Democratic Party in Texas, said in an interview with Al Jazeera’s Lavelle.

“I mean, in my perspective, I think that they’ve, the agency has just lost its identity, and there’s no way to rehabilitate that.”

World.title: Robots dance the ‘Macarena’ at Japan tech expo
World.content:
NewsFeed Robots dance the ‘Macarena’ at Japan tech expo

Humanoid robots were seen performing the “Macarena” and skateboarding as tech innovators from around the world are showcasing their latest breakthroughs at the annual CEATEC technology exhibition in Chiba, Japan.

World.title: At least 7 crew members missing after drone attacks on ships in Black Sea
World.content:
At least 7 crew members missing after drone attacks on ships in Black Sea

NewsFeed At least 7 crew members missing after drone attacks on ships in Black Sea

Emergency teams are searching for 7 missing crew after two chemical tankers were attacked in the Black Sea. Fires broke out on the ships after they were hit by suspected Russian drones.

World.title: Bus hits train stopped on French side of  Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
World.content:
A bus has hit a stationary freight train near the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel, injuring the driver and 18 passengers, the French authorities say.

The bus, which was carrying lorry drivers due to take a shuttle rail service, struck the train at the loading platform of the tunnel in Coquelles, near Calais.

Two people were severely injured and evacuated by helicopter though no one's life appeared to be in danger, a local official said.

Local sub-prefect Agathe Cury said that freight traffic and Eurostar passenger traffic through the tunnel had not been disrupted by the incident, which occurred at 19:27 (17:27 GMT), apart from a brief stoppage to allow the injured to be evacuated.

World.title: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has called off plans to livestream the execution of former US army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan by firing squad.

Trump had previously said he approved of showing the death of the Fort Hood attacker, while Vice-President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would happen and said he would not watch it.

Trump's decision to cancel the livestream came after widespread criticism in the US and globally. On Thursday, he said that "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die".

"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan," Trump said.

"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," the president added in the post on Truth Social.

Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US military personnel and injured 32 others at a military base in Texas in 2009. His execution by firing squad will be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

Trump said the families of the victims can still view the execution in person if they wish.

"They deserve to witness JUSTICE!" he said.

After the Pentagon announced last week that it would execute Hasan on 3 December 2026 by firing squad and livestream the event, a cascade of criticism quickly followed from human rights groups and many others. The United Nations called the plans "abhorrent".

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two nations carried them out publicly. According to Amnesty International, 11 public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025 and another six in Afghanistan.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth defended his decision to air Hasan's execution online, saying that "people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things".

World.title: Russia accuses Ukraine of attacking oil refinery after Zelensky says strikes to resume
World.content:
The Kremlin said Kyiv had "attempted a large-scale attack" on a refinery south of Moscow early on Thursday.

According to Russia's defence ministry, four missiles and dozens of drones were intercepted and the falling debris caused a fire at the site in Ryazan.

Zelensky said dozens of Ukrainian cities had come under Russian attack in the past day.

He previously said he would agree to the "energy ceasefire" announced by US President Donald Trump on Sunday if Moscow also abided by it.

But he accused Russia of ignoring the proposed deal within hours of it being announced, with strikes leaving hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power. The Kremlin never said it had agreed to the deal.

Zelensky agreed that he felt betrayed by the US when asked by Piers Morgan on Wednesday night, after Washington appeared to withdraw key elements of its support.

European leaders have rallied around the Ukrainian president. Italy's Defence Minister Guido Crosetto told the BBC that the US restricting its intelligence-sharing with Kyiv would be a "complete mistake".

"Because it is a fundamental form of support. This means denying a country any chance of defending itself."

He added: "Peace will be achieved when Putin will be convinced that there is a stalemate... that he cannot advance anymore. But if he sees a weakness on the Ukrainian front, if the United States takes its resources away, then Putin will think he can win, and so he will continue the war."

Zelensky met Nato chief Mark Rutte as a two-day summit of European leaders began in Brussels on Thursday. The head of the military alliance said they had discussed "the importance of implementing an energy ceasefire as well as Nato allies' continuous support for Ukraine".

Zelensky told the FT that Ukrainian officials had been told by US counterparts that "if you will not stop [the strikes], we will block intelligence".

Ukraine's military relies on US early-warning alerts of incoming Russian aerial attacks to mount air defences, limiting successful strikes, while Starlink internet links are used throughout its war effort to guide drones and protect its skies.

There were suggestions a technical glitch was to blame for the sudden Starlink restrictions on Tuesday evening, but owner Elon Musk appeared to deny this and suggested it was the Trump administration's doing.

"It was not a technical problem, it was the will," Zelensky told the FT.

Trump has denied halting intelligence-sharing. Starlink's sister service Starshield is provided to Ukraine under a US defence department contract. The BBC has approached the US authorities for comment.

World.title: Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
World.content:
Venezuela's former leader NicolÃ¡s Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, appeared in court on Thursday to plead not guilty to new charges of conspiracy to commit torture.

The US government initially accused Maduro of narco-terrorism, drug trafficking and weapons-related offenses, before adding new charges against him and Flores last week.

Maduro and Flores were captured in January during a US military raid, after which they were taken to New York, where they remain in jail.

The couple has pleaded not guilty to the allegations and both have argued to have the case thrown out on the grounds that they qualify for sovereign immunity. Their trial is scheduled for June 2027.

In a new indictment last week, government prosecutors alleged Maduro and Flores "created and maintained a violent system of repression" that saw "thousands of Venezuelans" killed, harassed, and tortured.

Nicolas Maduro denied the new charges brought against him by the US government, telling a court on Thursday he denied the "false accusations and false testimony against me."

"I reject this document entirely," Maduro said in Spanish through a translator.

Judge Alvin Hellerstein interrupted Maduro, and declared the court would enter a plea of not guilty for Maduro.

"I am completely innocent. I am not guilty," Flores said through a translator.

Maduro and Flores wore beige jail uniforms and both appear to have lost weight during their detention in Brooklyn.

The alleged torture methods included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture", the indictment states.

The US also accused Maduro of authorising the use of torture "against specific individuals" and alleges US citizens were tortured under this system.

Prosecutors already have accused Maduro, his wife and son, and their accomplices of engaging in a cocaine-trafficking conspiracy and partnering with cartels designated as terrorist groups.

Maduro previously called such charges a tool to further "imperial" plans for getting access to Venezuela's rich oil reserves.

He and his wife's lawyers have argued that Maduro is the leader of a sovereign country and therefore immune from prosecution. They contend the US taking him by force is illegal.

Flores unsuccessfully petitioned a judge to allow her to be released on bond while she awaited trial, arguing she had heart problems and other health issues while detained at the notorious Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn.

World.title: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
World.content:
At least 33 pupils and a teacher have been killed after a school roof collapsed in the north-western Pakistani city of Peshawar, according to hospital officials.

More than a dozen others are injured, with some in a critical condition.

Emergency services were called to the private Al-Khair school in Dir Colony at 08:48 (03:48 GMT) on Thursday after lessons had begun, rescue official Bilal Faizi told the BBC.

The roof of an upper-floor classroom had collapsed, he said, causing ceilings below to cave in and trap children beneath the debris.

Announcing the arrest of the school's owner, police chief Mian Saeed promised a thorough inquiry into "whether there were any violations of building codes".

Warning: This article contains distressing details

An English teacher from a nearby school said he immediately rushed to the site with other local residents when they heard sirens and the sound of ambulances.

Together, they pulled more than 20 children from the rubble, he said.

"I personally pulled out six children with my own hands. Most of them were alive and talking. But later it was found that they had passed away."

"There was a lot of blood," he said. "One child said he was in a lot of pain. His tongue had dried up in his mouth, [and he was] asking for water."

Sohail, another local resident, said he and others tried to remove children from under the rubble "using shovels".

World.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills two, minister says
World.content:
The Houthis have been launching missiles and drones at airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the strikes on the territory that they control in western Yemen, including the capital Sanaa.

On Saturday, a Houthi missile strike killed 13 people at Riyadh's international airport, which was the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.

Saudi Arabia's deputy foreign minister accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis to escalate their conflict with the kingdom.

"Iran continues to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN Security Council resolutions," Rayed Krimly told reporters, according to AFP news agency.

"We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," he added.

There was no immediate response from Iran's government. However, it has previously denied supplying weapons to the Houthis and said it only supports them politically.

Iran's foreign minister has also said it is ready to provide "any assistance necessary to facilitate the start of talks" between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran.

Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes.

At least 1,282 people have been killed and 5,890 injured in the fighting in Yemen since 6 August, according to the government's health ministry.

The UN says another 201,000 people have been displaced and that there has been an alarming surge in suspected cholera cases.

World.title: Was Neanderthal life violent? This wound suggests lethal fighting was more common
World.content:
A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been struck through the chest by a sharpened wooden spear, archaeologists say.

They say a 15mm hole found in a shoulder blade in a cave in Iraqi Kurdistan could be the earliest evidence of lethal violence involving such a weapon.

From the angle of the wound and other evidence, the researchers believe the spear entered the individual's chest and passed through the body - probably damaging a lung and major blood vessels - and exited through the left shoulder blade to leave a near-perfect hole.

The research is the latest in emerging evidence that suggests Neanderthal societies experienced more violence than previously thought.

Neanderthals were a separate species of humans that went extinct around 40,000 years ago. They lived across a large expanse of Europe and western and central Asia, and sometimes overlapped with our species, Homo sapiens.

The wounded Neanderthal's remains were found in a cave in Iraqi Kurdistan. As well as the left shoulder blade, the individual's right hand, three ribs and some teeth were also found.

A hole in the shoulder blade may be the earliest evidence of "lethal interpersonal violence" from a wooden spear, according to Dr Emma Pomeroy, study lead author from Cambridge's Department of Archaeology.

"The fatal strike may have been an intended heart shot," she told BBC News.

World.title: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
World.content:
Seven of 12 crew members are missing after a drone attack left a chemical tanker ablaze off Romania's coast on Thursday morning, naval authorities say.

The San Marino-flagged Wine Trader was 13 nautical miles (24km) east of the mouth of the River Danube at Sulina, when it reported blasts and a fire.

Romanian President NicuÈor Dan confirmed that the Wine Trader and another chemical tanker in the area, the Yara J, had both been struck by drones - the Yara J on Wednesday.

The Wine Trader was empty of cargo at the time.

Moscow said two cargo ships with military cargo heading to Ukraine's Odesa port had been hit. It did not name the vessels.

Overnight, a swarm of Russian drones was detected not far from the scene, near Ukraine's Snake Island.

The west coast of the Black Sea has recently seen a spate of drone attacks.

On Tuesday, two merchant ships were struck by drones further south along the coast of Bulgaria, Romania's neighbour, and one of the vessels sank, leaving 11 crew members missing.

Bulgaria said it suspected Russia was behind that attack, summoning the country's envoy.

A search and rescue operation for the missing members of the Wine Trader continues, Romania's authorities have said. Two Black Hawk helicopters and two rescue boats have been deployed.

The Romanian interior ministry has released a video showing one of the helicopters hovering above the vessel.

The priority is now to reach the four crew members confirmed to be alive, while ensuring the safety of rescue teams with very high waves reported in the area.

The Wine Trader tanker, which was sailing from Tunisia to Romania, reported several explosions on board at about 07:00 (05:00 GMT).

Romanian media cited crews on nearby ships as saying the Wine Trader had been hit by two drones.

The leaders of Romania and Bulgaria are due to discuss shortly whether Article 4 of the Nato treaty should be invoked.

This allows any member of the military alliance to request consultations with its allies if it believes its territorial integrity or security is threatened.

The Romanian president said: "We want to have all the information about what happened, but there will be a response from the Romanian state."

Dan is due to meet Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte in Brussels alongside Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev to discuss growing security threats in the Black Sea region.

The Romanian president said discussions would focus on operational requirements, including additional equipment to protect shipping in the area.

Ukraine has directly blamed Russia for earlier attacks on civilian vessels in the western side of the Black Sea - a key route for Ukrainian exports and imports.

On Tuesday, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen spoke of the Black Sea becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable".

Russia's military has recently intensified its strikes on vessels in the area, as part of its war against Ukraine.

A fire broke out on the Comoros-flagged Yara J late on Wednesday after being struck by a drone, but its crew - who are all reportedly safe - were able to douse the flames themselves.

Last week, another two ships were struck off Bulgaria, and on the same day Ukraine hit an oil tanker in the Russian Black Sea port of Sochi.

Moscow says it is targeting ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports.

Kyiv and its European allies say merchant vessels carrying grain and other civilian cargo are being attacked.

Both Russia and Ukraine are major grain-exporting countries and Turkey has called on both countries to halt attacks in the Black Sea.

Moscow has repeatedly rejected calls by the US and Europe for a naval ceasefire in the Black Sea, blaming Ukraine for attacking Russian merchant ships in the area.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

World.title: One in four children under five stunted in Akwa Ibom, survey shows
World.content:
Nearly one in four children under five in Akwa Ibom State is stunted, highlighting the scale of chronic malnutrition confronting the state as the government moves to coordinate nutrition interventions across its 31 local government areas.

The 2023–2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) puts the prevalence of stunting in Akwa Ibom at 24.1 per cent, confirming figures cited by the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF). Nationally, 40 per cent of children under five are stunted, according to the survey.

Stunting occurs when children are too short for their age because of chronic undernutrition. It can impair physical growth and brain development, undermine learning and affect productivity in adulthood.

The figures were highlighted on Tuesday during the inauguration of Local Government Committees on Food and Nutrition across Akwa Ibom’s 31 local government areas.

The Akwa Ibom State Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning organised the event in Uyo in collaboration with UNICEF.

UNICEF’s nutrition specialist, Oluniyi Oyedokun, said the state’s stunting burden required coordinated action to address the factors responsible for childhood malnutrition.

He explained that stunting is linked to inadequate nutrition, particularly during the first 1,000 days of a child’s life, from conception to the second birthday.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The period is critical for physical growth and brain development. Prolonged nutritional deprivation during this stage can have lasting consequences for children’s health and development.

Mr Oyedokun warned that stunted children face an increased risk of impaired cognitive development, poor school performance, frequent illnesses and reduced productivity in adulthood.

He said establishing nutrition committees in all 31 local government areas was intended to bring interventions closer to communities and strengthen implementation of the National Policy on Food and Nutrition.

He called for collaboration among the health, agriculture, education, water and sanitation sectors, noting that tackling malnutrition requires action beyond the health sector.

The Akwa Ibom State Government said the committees would coordinate, monitor and implement nutrition interventions in their respective local government areas.

The Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Nsikan Nkan, said the inauguration of the 217-member committees aligned with Governor Umo Eno’s ARISE Agenda, which prioritises human capital development and a healthy, productive population.

The committees are expected to improve coordination among relevant government agencies and other stakeholders in addressing food insecurity and malnutrition at the grassroots.

World.title: Senate probes death of ex-SUG president in Enugu NYSC camp
World.content:
The Nigerian Senate has ordered an investigation into the death of a member of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), Etimbuk Daniel, at the NYSC camp in Enugu State.

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that Mr Daniel died while undergoing his compulsory three-week orientation course at the NYSC.

The deceased corps member was the immediate past president of the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of the Akwa Ibom State University. He hailed from Akwa Ibom State, South-South Nigeria.

Investigation

Anietie Ekong, a media aide to the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, announced the Senate’s decision to investigate the NYSC member’s death in a statement posted on Facebook on Thursday.

The media aide said the Senate resolved to investigate Mr Daniel’s death following a motion of urgent public importance moved by Akwa Ibom North-East Senator Aniekan Bassey, calling for a review of medical services in NYSC camps nationwide.

He said the upper chamber resolved that the investigation would be carried out by the Senate Committees on Police Affairs, Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, Ethics, Code of Conduct and Public Petitions, as well as Youth Development and Health.

Mr Ekong said the committees would carry out the probe in conjunction with the Nigeria Police Force and the State Security Service.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the Senate would also investigate the state of health infrastructure in NYSC camps across the country.

He said the Senators noted with concern the sudden, untimely death of the NYSC member, describing him as a vibrant, patriotic young Nigerian and a shining light in his community who had only set out to serve the country.

The media aide said the lawmakers equally expressed concern over reports that Mr Daniel died from complications arising from a “minor” headache after allegedly experiencing a delay in obtaining timely and adequate medical attention at the camp clinic.

He said the Senate further expressed worry that the incident was not isolated, but highlighted a recurring pattern of systemic negligence, poor medical infrastructure, and absence of qualified emergency personnel and rapid referral protocols across NYSC camps.

World.title: 2027: On election day, APC will realise they’ve made very serious mistakes – Kwankwaso
World.content:
The 2027 vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has tackled 31 Nigerian governors for backing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid instead of working in their states.

Mr Kwankwaso, a former governor of Kano State, spoke on Channels TV’s Politics Today on Thursday night.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that at least 31 governors have publicly endorsed the 2027 re-election bid of Mr Tinubu of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Some of the governors – such as Osun State’s Ademola Adeleke and Anambra’s Charles Soludo – are not members of the APC.

Speaking on the Channels TV show, Mr Kwankwaso argued that both the governors and Mr Tinubu were teaming up ahead of the 2027 general elections because they lacked confidence in winning re-elections on their own.

“I think a lot of mistakes were being made by the governors to the extent that they themselves believe that they are not competent enough to win elections on their own.

“Therefore, they had to lean towards the president. And I believe the president also believes that he can’t do it himself. He has to lean towards the governors,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘APC and governors are worried about NDC, Peter Obi’s popularity’

Mr Kwankwaso boasted that the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, is very popular in Southern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 elections.

He also argued that the NDC had gained a strong presence in northern Nigeria and that the party now has a “formidable team” given that many Nigerians seeking to solve the country’s problems are with the party.

The former governor believes the NDC’s popularity has become a concern for the governors backing Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid.

“I believe that there is no governor who is not concerned about the popularity of our candidate, the ticket itself, and of course our party.

“So I personally believe that the governors don’t understand the dynamics now. But I believe that on election day, they will realise that the APC has made very serious mistakes over the years,” he said.

‘Hardship and insecurity will make Tinubu and the APC fail’

Mr Kwankwaso argued that Mr Tinubu and the APC’s popularity have diminished due to growing hardship and insecurity across the country.

“The issue of security, especially in northern Nigeria. The issue of poverty, everybody is very much aware of it.

“You can see that the major issues in this country are not being addressed,” he said.

Continuing, the politician said: “People are in a very difficult situation today. Many of them have left their villages and towns and have been away for many years now.

READ ALSO: Mbah speaks on shootings at NDC secretariat

“But I can tell you, outside here, and even here in Abuja, people are very angry. And people are looking for a way out.”

The NDC vice-presidential candidate then expressed concern that the ruling APC might rig the 2027 election.

“Normally, as politicians, if they (APC) realise that they are not popular and that they are not being loved by their people, the tendency is for them to start thinking of ways and manners (to rig the elections).

“And we have heard many of them, especially the people around them, that as usual, they are boasting that even if they get 1,000, they will write the result for themselves,” he said.

World.title: Will a Nobel solve the world’s Trump problem? The president thinks so, By Azu Ishiekwene
World.content:
US President Donald Trump doesn’t just think a Nobel will solve the world’s Trump-inflicted problems. He believes it. He has said, quite clearly, that he deserves a Nobel Peace Prize for his extraordinary labour of peace, especially in his second term.

He claims he has ended eight wars, from the Israel-Hamas War to the Israel-Iran War, the India-Pakistan War, the Thailand-Cambodia War, and the DR Congo-Rwanda War.

Can you think of anyone who has, in his words, saved millions of lives and done so much for world peace and security in the last nearly two years? And each settled war, for Trump, is the equivalent of one Nobel – eight prizes in all, yet he has been denied even one!

He’s not the only important person who thinks he has done what Napoleon could not do, and yet remains largely despised. In a meeting at the White House in January, the Venezuelan opposition leader, Marina Corina Machado, presented Trump with her 2025 Nobel Peace Prize gold medal, to right the wrong of the Nobel Committee.

Proxy Medal Not Enough

Yet, the proxy medal has not appeased Trump. From his reaction when the Committee announced the 2026 winners in Oslo last week, the President is dying to get the real thing. That prize appears to be worth more than the combined value of Cuba, Greenland, the Strait of Hormuz, and the rash of trade tariffs.

He used bad words for the Nobel Committee, describing it as “forever discredited” and calling the members “a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilisation.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Trump also launched an attack on the prize winner, Navi Pillay, calling her a “mystery person nobody has ever heard of.”

Solicitation As Strategy

Solicitation is a rare thing in the history of the Nobel. But what Trump cannot undo does not exist. In the cases of Leo Tolstoy and Albert Einstein, there were repeated third-party nominations, never a demand for the prize from the nominees or the nominators. The nomination of Adolf Hitler by a Swedish parliamentarian in 1939 was clearly a parody, and the nomination was quickly withdrawn.

This is why the 2026 Nobel Prize for Peace will go down in the records as one of a kind. Not just the laureate but the committee, the domicile country and the International Criminal Court are all in hot water because of the outrage of a sore loser.

President Trump has updated his list of “disgraced countries,” once an exclusively African collection, to include Norway, perhaps making it a list to be proud of.

Who Nominated Trump?

Who nominated Trump for a Nobel Peace Prize? The Nobel Committee reportedly keeps lists of nominees and nominators confidential. It neither confirms nor denies claims during the period. Last year, US Republican House of Representatives member for Florida, Anna Paulina Luna, publicly announced that she nominated the President for his self-acclaimed role in brokering the Israel-Hamas ceasefire.

Yet, the Trump-engineered ceasefire in Gaza has turned out to be a bloody campaign under a white banner. More than a year since the ceasefire came into effect on 10 October, 2025, international monitoring groups and independent news analyses note that Israel has conducted daily air and drone strikes – attacking the territory on roughly 325 out of the first 361 days of the “ceasefire.”

According to data from the Gaza Ministry of Health and UN Humanitarian reports, at least 1,493 Palestinians, including women and children, have been killed. Also, about 5,299 people have been wounded during the ceasefire. While Trump covets the peace prize, Israel continues to breach the ceasefire without consequence.

Bombings, shootings, restrictions, encroachment by Israeli settlers, expropriation, theft of livestock and farm produce, and blockade of access to food and medicines in Gaza continue under the full glare of the peacemaker, Trump.

If that’s the ceasefire for which even Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is also reported to have nominated Trump for a peace prize, then they left the Nobel Committee no chance other than simply to create a new Prize for War.

MAGA Delusions

The trouble remains that the US, under a MAGA-shared delusion, railroaded a demagogue to the White House, and must imagine that their hysteria would press the world, including the Nobel Committee, to bestow a laurel on a gangster hero.

The dilemma of Trump and his supporters was captured in the press conference on Iran, where the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, laid out the Middle East conflict in stark, anachronistic rhetoric. It’s a tragedy that the Trump White House is wantonly destroying the world order of peace and security and damaging institutions that the US was at the forefront of building after World War II – institutions that have served the US and the world well, despite their shortcomings.

The Nobel Committee recognised Pillay for “pressing states and national leaders to comply with the rule of law,” a subject in which the Trump administration has set one of the worst precedents ever. Pillay, a worthy recipient of the peace prize, had variously chaired investigations into serious human rights violations in places like Myanmar, Rwanda and Gaza – the last one an active crime scene where Trump’s policies have enabled travesties.

L’État, C’est Moi.

Trump didn’t stop at attacking the Committee. Being the state and the grandmaster rolled into one like Louis XIV of France, he has got the US to impose sanctions on the ICC; sanctions that are as doomed as his adventures in the Strait of Hormuz.

The indictment of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and the likely future indictment of Trump for war crimes in Gaza and Iran, respectively, by the ICC, must be upsetting for Trump, who wishes to “obliterate” every suspicion with a grand Nobel.

As he did to undermine the UN – instituting a Board of Peace filled with carefully chosen billionaire oil sheikhs – Trump might well be considering a parallel award in the class of the Nobel Prize, even if the sole objective is to award such a prize to Donald Trump. That’s how much the President craves recognition to evade accountability.

Midterm Blues? Perhaps

Unfortunately, the world is stuck with these hallucinations for the remainder of Trump’s term – which seems like an eternity. The flicker of hope that the mid-term elections might produce a Democratic majority in the US Congress is tenuous. Demagogues like Trump seldom leave events to chance. The Capitol Hill invasion in January 2021 was a clear indicator that, when push comes to shove, institutional guardrails are the first casualties.

If Trump could park the world into Mar-a-Lago, or cram the seas and oceans into Trump Tower, he would have them like sausages. He would rename the Earth “Trump Island” and crown himself His Imperial Majesty and the owner of Planet Earth.

His Footprint Speaks

Meanwhile, from Europe to the Middle East, and from Asia to Africa and North America, the world is reeling from the blows of the rash policies of this Nobel-Laureate-Wannabe, and paying the price in supply chain disruptions, rising inflation, geopolitical tensions, and worsening global misery.

It’s a joke that the current White House should think the President worthy of a peace prize, even a fake one. What does it take to call this insanity by its name?

Azu Ishiekwene is Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book,Writing for Media and Monetising It.

World.title: Anambra ‌‌demands more benefits from oil, gas sector
World.content:
Law Mefor, Anambra Commissioner for Information and value reformation, urged the federal government to ensure the state fully benefits from the nation’s oil and gas-related programmes and initiatives.

He said it was unfortunate that as an oil-producing state, Anambra was yet to be fully integrated into the nation’s oil and gas master plan.

The commissioner said this in Awka on Thursday while declaring open a one-day workshop on Nigerian Content capacity building for media stakeholders.

The event was organised by the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB).

Mr Mefor commended the organisers for bringing the workshop to Anambra.

He said Nigeria has the human capacity to manage its oil and gas resources effectively.

Speaking earlier, the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, Felix Ogbe, said the workshop was part of the federal government’s inclusivity drive for the industry.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ogbe, represented by Omomehin Ajimijaye, director of planning, research and statistics, urged the media to properly educate communities on the importance of participating in the board’s initiatives.

The General Manager, Corporate Communications, NCDMB, Obinna Ezeobi, urged the media to raise awareness about opportunities in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.

He also urged them to hold industry operators accountable, particularly regarding compliance with local content requirements.

Mr Ezeobi advocated for better reporting on Nigerian content issues to enable more locals and businesses in Anambra to participate actively in the oil and gas value chain.

He said the media has a critical role in advancing the implementation of the Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act.

He said they can do this by informing the public about industry opportunities, explaining government interventions and monitoring compliance with relevant laws.

He urged journalists to use their positions as agenda-setters and gatekeepers to draw attention to issues affecting the industry and highlight opportunities for Nigerian businesses and professionals.

He further urged them to ensure that oil and gas operators met their local content obligations.

According to him, the workshop was designed to deepen journalists’ understanding of the Nigerian content framework.

He said it was also meant to improve the quality of their reportage and strengthen collaboration between the board and media organisations in Anambra.

He described Anambra as an important location for the engagement, noting that the state is recognised as an oil-producing state and ranks as the second-highest oil producer in the South-east.

(NAN)

World.title: Eno reveals lawmaker leaking Akwa Ibom Assembly’s secrets to him
World.content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor Umo Eno said the Leader of the State House of Assembly, Otobong Bob, has been leaking information to him whenever state lawmakers plot a “coup” against him.

Mr Eno disclosed this on Friday during a constituency briefing organised by Mr Bob, who represents Nsit Ubium State Constituency, the governor’s own local government area.

“Sometimes he’ll come to me in the night and whisper to me. Most times when they’re planning a coup. He’ll come to me and tell me we should dissolve this coup before it crystallises,” the governor said of the young lawmaker, whose father, Effiong Bob, a former senator, is a top politician in the state.

As Mr Eno spoke, Mr Bob, standing, gestured toward the deputy speaker, KufreAbasi Edidem, prompting both lawmakers to smile. The governor was also captured smiling as he made the remarks.

Mr Eno, however, did not explain the nature of the “coups” or identify the lawmakers involved.

The governor described Mr Bob, a lawyer, as his “son” and the “stabiliser of the assembly”, praising his role in managing internal political disagreements.

Mr Eno also described members of the current assembly as the most “enjoyed” since Akwa Ibom State was created, insisting that official records supported his claim.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Let me say without any contradiction that this House of Assembly, as far as I know, has enjoyed more than any assembly since the creation of this state. I stand to be challenged. The figures are clear; the documentation is clear. But they are very good people. All of them are my friends,” he said.

Bob pledges support for Eno’s re-election

In his remarks at the event, Mr Bob thanked Governor Eno for his support for the legislature and pledged the support of Nsit Ubium people for his re-election bid in 2027.

“This is an opportunity for me to tell the people of Nsit Ubium what I have been doing with the mandate they entrusted to me at the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly. It is also an opportunity to demonstrate practical representation,” he said.

“I thank Your Excellency for the support you have shown to the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly.

“I want to assure you of the support of the people of Nsit Ubium as you seek re-election in 2027. We will support all our candidates, from the Presidency to the House of Assembly, in the 2027 general elections.”

The lawmaker gifted several items, including cars, minibuses, generators, hair dryers, motorcycles, and sewing machines, to his constituents at the event.

Political background

Mr Bob, a lawyer serving his second term in the assembly, was elected on the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) platform for his first two terms before defecting to the All Progressives Congress (APC) alongside Mr Eno.

He has secured the APC ticket to contest for a third term in the 2027 elections.

His father, an ally of the governor, leads the Akwa Ibom North-East Senatorial District.

Mr Eno’s remarks highlight the close relationship between his administration and the assembly leader as political alignments take shape ahead of the 2027 elections.

Mr Bob did not respond to PREMIUM TIMES’ call and a text message seeking his response to the governor’s remarks at the time of filing this report.

World.title: Reps demand enforcement of 18-year minimum marriage age
World.content:
As part of renewed efforts to curb child marriage and protect the rights of girls across Nigeria, the House of Representatives on Thursday called for the enforcement of the Child Rights Act, 2003, which sets 18 years as the minimum age for marriage.

The House made the call during plenary after adopting a motion titled, ‘End Child Marriage and Invest in the Girl Child,’ sponsored by the Chairman of the House Committee on Women Affairs and Social Development, Kafilat Ogbara.

The House considered the motion in commemoration of the International Day of the Girl Child, observed annually on 11 October.

Leading the debate, Ms Ogbara said effective enforcement of the Child Rights Act and its domestication across all states was necessary to ensure that children enjoyed equal protection regardless of where they lived or their socioeconomic circumstances.

She described child marriage as a major human rights, public health, educational and socioeconomic challenge, particularly for girls in vulnerable communities.

According to her, early marriage deprives girls of their childhood and limits their access to education, healthcare and economic opportunities while exposing them to other forms of vulnerability.

“Child marriage remains a significant human rights, public health, educational, and socioeconomic challenge in Nigeria, disproportionately affecting girls in vulnerable communities and undermining their ability to enjoy childhood, complete their education, and participate fully in national development,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Ogbara said girls forced into marriage at an early age faced heightened risks of early pregnancy, maternal and newborn complications, gender-based violence and poverty.

She said the consequences could affect their health, education, economic independence and ability to contribute to national development.

The lawmaker said ending child marriage was also consistent with Nigeria’s obligations under international human rights instruments, including the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women and the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child.

She said the agreements required governments to protect children from harmful practices, exploitation and discrimination while safeguarding their fundamental rights.

Ms Ogbara said tackling child marriage required coordinated action by federal and state governments, local councils, traditional and religious leaders, parents, communities, development partners and other relevant actors.

“The theme, ‘End Child Marriage and Invest in the Girl Child,’ calls for urgent and coordinated action to protect girls from harmful practices, uphold their fundamental rights, and provide them with the education, healthcare, skills, and opportunities necessary to reach their full potential,” she said.

The House subsequently urged the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs to work with the Ministries of Education, Health and Social Welfare, Justice and relevant agencies to strengthen programmes aimed at preventing child marriage and protecting girls at risk.

It also called for greater coordination among government institutions and other stakeholders to tackle the social and economic factors that push girls into early marriage, while improving their access to education, healthcare and other essential services.

For stronger legislative oversight, the House mandated its committees on Women Affairs and Social Development, Education, Health, Human Rights and Justice to engage relevant ministries, departments and agencies, civil society organisations and development partners.

The committees are to assess existing interventions, identify gaps in implementation and recommend legislative and budgetary measures needed to end child marriage and increase investment in girls.

They are expected to report their findings and recommendations to the House within four weeks.

The House also reaffirmed the National Assembly’s responsibility to strengthen legislation, formulate policies, and provide budgetary support to protect children and promote the welfare and development of Nigerian girls.

World.title: Odinkalu makes inaccurate claim over Tinubu’s APC campaign council appearance; Presidency reacts
World.content:
The Presidency has rejected a claim by human rights lawyer and activist Chidi Odinkalu that President Bola Tinubu was not physically present at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on Wednesday.

Mr Odinkalu alleged that Mr Tinubu’s appearance and speech at the event were pre-recorded, even though political leaders attended the programme and local and international media covered it.

The activist made the claim in an early Thursday post on X, attaching a video of Mr Tinubu speaking at the inauguration.

“It does not require close study of this clip to understand that this was a pre-recorded address. @officialABAT was not at this venue in person,” he wrote.

He added that the transitions in the video were “un-natural,” while describing the camera work as “a production” and the event as “an orchestration.”

“The parties to the crime are many. Let them produce the clip of his promenade & a wide angle,” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the APC inaugurated its Presidential Campaign Council on Wednesday at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja as the party commenced preparations for the 2027 presidential election.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

This newspaper can independently confirm that Mr Tinubu was physically present at the inauguration, contrary to Mr Odinkalu’s claim.

Presidency reacts

In response to the post, Bayo Onanuga, the President’s special adviser on Information and Strategy, accused Mr Odinkalu of letting partisan politics influence his judgement.

“You’ve let partisanship cloud your vision and judgement. You are now a member of the internet mob, eager to disregard the truth and push false narratives online. You should be ashamed of this post,” Mr Onanuga wrote.

Also rejecting the claim, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, described it as an “outrageous claim.”

Mr Keyamo said the allegation reminded him of a conspiracy theory during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari that claimed Mr Buhari had died while receiving medical treatment in London and had been replaced by a body double known as Jubril from Sudan.

“We thought we had seen and heard the worst nonsense from certain characters during the Buhari era when there was a conspiracy theory claiming that former Nigerian President, Muhammadu Buhari died during medical treatment in London in 2017 and was replaced by a cloned body double or lookalike called Jubril from Sudan,” he said.

“Now, some educated fellow (supposedly) comes up with an outrageous claim that the President’s appearance and speech yesterday at the launch of the APC Campaign Council were pre-recorded.

“Meanwhile, both the local and international Press physically covered the event LIVE.

“I really don’t know whether to laugh or to cry.”

Mr Keyamo further accused opposition figures of exhibiting signs of “mental distress,” a comment likely to intensify the political dispute over the claim.

Reactions from X

Several users on X also criticised Mr Odinkalu, questioning why he would allege the President was absent despite media coverage of the event.

One user, @gbengagiwa_tt, said Mr Odinkalu should seek help, arguing that the activist could have confirmed the president’s presence through media organisations that covered the event.

“He has many avenues to confirm the authenticity of the physical appearance of President Tinubu at yesterday’s event, especially from his friend Rufai Oseni @ruffydfire, whose television station, @ARISEtv, covered the event live, yet he chose to take this embarrassing route, despite calling himself a Professor,” the user said.

Another user, @cmpoba, urged Mr Odinkalu to delete the post, asking how Mr Tinubu could have been absent when other attendees interacted with him.

“If President @officialABAT wasn’t there, who did Prof Soludo @CCSoludo, the Anambra State Governor, shake hands with? Everything is not propaganda,” the user said.

Similarly, @oluomokolade linked Mr Odinkalu’s claim to the earlier conspiracy theories surrounding Mr Buhari’s absence from public events during his administration.

“A group of people groomed with a culture of conspiracy-driven lies and hatred claimed it was Jibrin of Sudan that was in Aso Rock instead of PMB,” the user said.

“That group has started with their mischief again. It’s very pathetic, the extent of hate in them.”

Mr Odinkalu’s claim and the subsequent reactions have renewed debate on social media over the use of unverified allegations in political discourse ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: No plan to increase electricity tariffs – FG insists
World.content:
Tegbe

The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said on Thursday that the Federal Government (FG) had no plan to increase electricity tariffs.

Tegbe said this in Ibadan while flagging off the 17.7MW hybrid solar mini-grid project, with a 17.74MW Battery Energy Storage System for communities in Oyo State.

The minister described reports of a planned tariff hike circulating on social media as misinformation and urged Nigerians to disregard it.

“I want to say this clearly and without ambiguity: there is no plan to increase electricity tariffs.

“What we are planning is a power sector that works round the clock,” he said.

He said the FG’s commitment to regular power supply starts with having three Energy Zones: the Lagos-Ogun corridor, Abuja-Kaduna-Kano corridor, and the Benin-Enugu-Port Harcourt corridor.

He explained that the 17.7MW project would serve communities across Akinyele, Ido, Ibadan North, Egbeda and Lagelu Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Oyo State.

According to him, the interconnected mini-grid would improve supply to homes and businesses, reduce dependence on generators and create better conditions for investment and jobs in the beneficiary communities.

Tegbe commended President Bola Tinubu for his leadership under the Renewed Hope Agenda and appreciated the Olubadan of Ibadanland for his support.

He also thanked the Rural Electrification Agency (REA), Paras Energy, the World Bank, Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC) and the Oyo State Government for their contributions.

He said the FG plans to build and improve the national grid across the eastern, western and central corridors to ensure stability and extend the 24/7 power vision to every part of Nigeria.

Mr Deolu Ijose, the Managing Director (MD)/Chief Executive Officer (CEO), IBEDC, said the new mini-grid project would provide electricity to 22,597 customers across five communities.

Ijose said the project, developed by Paras Energy and Natural Resources Development Limited, would provide 17.7MWp solar PV generation with battery storage to Bola, Jiboye, Molade-Adelubi, Ogo-Oluwa, and Sooko-Elega clusters.

According to him, IBEDC’s existing distribution infrastructure will be used to integrate and deliver electricity generated by Paras Energy.

He said that this model would show how DisCos and private developers could collaborate to improve access.

Ijose added that the project builds on IBEDC’s previous innovative interventions such as the Mokoloki Mini-Grid in Ogun and the recently commissioned Oke-Oyi mini-grid in Kwara.

He then urged the host communities to protect the infrastructure.

The MD/CEO of REA, Abba Abubakar-Aliyu, said the project details are: 1.8 megawatts in Bola, Akinyele LGA and 3.5 megawatts in Jiboye, Ido LGA.

Others are 6.9 megawatts in Molade, Ibadan North LGA; 3.6 megawatts in Ogo Oluwa, Egbeda LGA, and 1.9 megawatts in Sooko, Lagelu LGA.

Earlier, the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, lauded the minister for including rural and underserved communities in various power reform projects.

He urged the Oyo State Government to speed up work and complete its ongoing hybrid power project before 2027 for residents to start enjoying regular power supply.

Earlier, Gov. Seyi Makinde, represented by the state Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Prof. Dahud Shangodoyin, said the government would continue to pursue practical electricity interventions across the state.

He noted that the state government’s Hybrid Independent Power Project, meant to serve the state’s secretariat and other strategic public facilities, has a plant capacity of 11 MW.

He recalled that the 5 MW phase was commissioned in 2024.

“Our wide agenda includes solar power for public facilities, rural electrification, mini-grids, as well as private sector-led generation and distribution.

“Therefore, no single technology can meet every need,” said Makinde.

He charged the developer and implementing institutions to maintain clear construction and commissioning mindsets, and comply with applicable licenses and technical standards. (NAN)

World.title: Military has nothing to do with politics, Mai Salati case not political – Buni insists
World.content:
By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman

Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has rejected suggestions that the arrest of politician Alhaji Wakiil Goni Mama, popularly known as Mai Salati, was politically motivated, insisting that the military has nothing to do with politics.

Buni spoke on Thursday during the swearing-in of commissioners and chairmen of the 17 local government areas in Damaturu, where he disclosed that he had directed the chairman of Geidam Local Government Area to follow up on the case with military authorities and community elders.

The governor’s remarks come amid allegations in some quarters that he was behind Mai Salati’s arrest and had used the military to target the politician over political differences.

Dismissing the insinuations, Buni said he has no history of opposition bullying, insisting that threatening political opponents was inconsistent with his principles.

“I reached out to the Geidam chairman, instructed him to follow up on the case with the military commander and other elders on the case and report back to me,” the governor said.

“It is not in my principle to threaten opposition,” he added.

Buni also maintained that the military should not be drawn into partisan political disputes, insisting that Mai Salati’s case was not political.

It could be recalled that troops of the Nigerian Army’s Operation Hadin Kai reportedly arrested Mai Salati in early October over allegations of providing logistics support to suspected members of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), a faction of the Boko Haram insurgency operating in the North-East.

Reports published by TheCable and other media organisations on October 8 and 9 said the arrest followed an alleged attempt by the politician to bribe soldiers to secure the release of suspects arrested in Kanamma, Yobe State, over suspected terrorist logistics activities.

According to the reports, the suspects were being processed for further investigation when Mai Salati allegedly intervened to secure their release by offering money to military personnel.

The soldiers reportedly rejected the alleged inducement and arrested him instead, with security sources saying he and other suspects were subsequently moved from Damaturu to Maiduguri for further investigation.

The arrest generated political controversy, with reports highlighting speculation that it might be connected to Mai Salati’s reported defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Security sources cited in the initial reports rejected the suggestion that the operation was politically motivated, maintaining that it concerned allegations of terrorism-related logistics and an attempt to interfere with the detention of suspects.

World.title: Breaking: Multiple victims as gunman opens fire at elementary school in US
World.content:
A shooting has left “multiple victims” at an elementary school in the northwestern US state of Oregon, police said Thursday, adding that the shooter is dead.

“We don’t have confirmation yet who shot the suspect. It may have been a bystander. At this time, we have multiple victims,” said Sheila Miller, a spokesperson at the Bend Police Department, in a press conference.

The Bend-La Pine School District said in a statement on social media that the Silver Rail Elementary School was under lockdown.

An updated post later said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.

Miller said that officers were alerted to respond to a critical scene at 1:00 pm local time, and that police were on the scene approximately two minutes later.

“Seconds later, we received word over the radio that the suspect in this incident was down,” she said.

Miller said medics had taken at least two people to a local hospital, adding that “we do not know their status.”

The school is more than 100 miles (160 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

The United States, where firearms are readily available, is a frequent scene of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.

The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.

There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the United States so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.

AFP

World.title: Omission of NDC candidates: INEC should fix this promptly – Dickson
World.content:
Dickson

By Henry Umoru

Following the omission of some of its gubernatorial candidates ahead of the 2027 elections by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Seriake Dickson, said the party has taken adequate steps to address the cases of those whose names were not published by INEC a few days ago.

He urged INEC to urgently remedy the apparent omission, saying that affected candidates registered with the party before the statutory 21-day period required by law.

In a statement on his Facebook page on Thursday night, the former Bayelsa State governor said, “Our candidates and supporters are assured that the party has been working diligently and has taken adequate steps to address the cases of those whose names were not published by INEC a few days ago.

“All affected candidates registered with the party before the statutory 21-day period required by law.

“We urge INEC to remedy this apparent omission promptly. From the Presidential election to the State Houses of Assembly, the NDC has fielded qualified candidates who emerged through a rigorous and painstaking screening process. We are confident that INEC will correct this omission without delay.”

The Senator representing Bayelsa West in the present 10th Senate added, “In the meantime, consultations, town hall meetings, mobilisation, and campaigns should continue unabated in all states and constituencies.

“We will continue to fight without giving up until we are victorious. NDC all the way.”

World.title: Meta unveils new ‘open’ AI model to rival Chinese competition
World.content:
Meta

Meta on Thursday launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers.

Muse Spark Open “is the most capable US open-weight model to date,” Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang wrote on X.

Unlike with so-called closed models — such as Anthropic’s Claude or OpenAI’s ChatGPT — developers can download the parameters, or weights, of an open-weight model and then customize it.

Chinese developers have emerged as dominant players in the open-weight market for AI models over the past couple of years.

Alibaba’s Qwen, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Z.ai’s GLM models have been considered open-weight frontrunners globally, but Meta claims its new open model now competes on a similar level.

“Built for coding and agentic work,” Muse Spark Open “excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning,” Meta said in a blogpost, adding that “strong safeguards” have been integrated into the new model.

Muse Spark Open is also “optimized” to run on Apple’s advanced M5 Ultra chips, Meta said, signaling an unusual partnership between the two tech giants.

Meta boss Mark Zuckerberg wrote on X that the new model “runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work” with Apple and its new CEO John Ternus.

Ternus, who took over as Apple’s chief from Tim Cook in September, responded that it is “amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!”

Muse Spark Open still requires significant computing power, though.

Users can run the model on two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra chips to create a “supercomputer” on their own desktop, Meta said.

The launch comes just days after Meta announced its newest closed model.
