On Monday, the company unveiled two new “frontier” models called Wonder and Wonder Full, which the company claimed rival the most advanced versions of ChatGPT and Claude.

Meta’s AI efforts were initially focused on open models, but more recently Zuckerberg has pushed the company to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.

Meta launched its Spark model in April, marking a departure from its open-source model known as Llama, which lagged behind the rest of the industry.

AFP

World.title: Tompolo to Oyo electorate: Why Tinubu deserves four more years
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has urged the people of Oyo State to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that the President deserves another four-year term to consolidate his reforms.

Tompolo, who described Tinubu as a son of Oyo State, made the call while donating 32 vehicles to the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state to strengthen its grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general election.

He spoke through his representative, the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, at the inauguration of the movement’s Oyo State structure at the Liberty Stadium, Ibadan, on Thursday.

The vehicles, according to him, were donated to support the movement’s campaign for Tinubu’s re-election and the election of other candidates contesting under the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Tompolo urged the people of Oyo State to support the President’s return to office, arguing that his re-election would enable him to complete the South’s two-term presidential tenure.

He also commended Tinubu for what he described as far-reaching reforms across critical sectors of the economy, particularly those that had increased the resources available to state governments to pay salaries and pensions and execute major development projects.

He charged members of the movement to take the message of the President’s re-election to every part of Oyo State, insisting that the state should be among those supporting Tinubu’s bid for another four years.

“We are here today to tell you that we are coming to join you to canvass for votes across the country for your son, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What Tompolo is preaching is that Tinubu is doing very well.“

“Tinubu’s reform policies are fantastic. We want you to support President Tinubu’s re-election for him to continue with the good work he is doing,” he said.

Also speaking at the rally, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, assured the gathering that the party would deploy all available resources to secure victory in the state.

Alli said Oyo State had remained disconnected from the centre for too long, expressing the party’s determination to return to power.

He thanked Tompolo for the donation of the 32 vehicles and his support for Tinubu, urging party members and supporters to ensure that the vehicles were effectively deployed across the state during the campaign.

“We are very grateful. I want to assure you that we are going to make judicious use of all these vehicles and all other items that you may want to give us or from any other support group.“

“As far as we are concerned in Oyo, we have stayed out of government for too long and we are sincerely working assiduously to ensure that we take over the mantle of leadership in Oyo State,” Alli said.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Mr Sunday Asuku, urged the people of Oyo State, particularly the youth, to support Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Asuku described the President’s reforms as necessary for Nigeria’s economic growth and sustained development, citing the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as one of the administration’s people-oriented policies that had made a positive impact.

He urged members of the movement to intensify their grassroots mobilisation efforts and take the campaign for Tinubu’s second term to every nook and cranny of the state.

Calling on the electorate to turn out in large numbers during the election, Asuku said: “Oyo State, come out massively in January 2027 to vote massively for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu for President and vote Senator Sharafadeen Alli for Governor of Oyo State.

“Listen to me, Oyo State, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu has done a lot. He has done a lot in the past three years and a half. We want to give him four more years to consolidate on what he has started.

“Listen to me, a vote for Asiwaju is a vote for progressive Nigeria. A vote for Asiwaju is a vote for development.”

World.title: Two Boko Haram members arrested by DSS bag life imprisonment
World.content:
A Federal High Court in Abuja has sentenced two men arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS) to life imprisonment for their membership of the proscribed Boko Haram terrorist group.

The men, Abba Mustapha and Bukar Ibrahim, both from Borno State, were sentenced after pleading guilty to charges bordering on membership and providing support for the terrorist group and concealing information on their activities.

Consequently, the presiding judge, Justice Salim Ibrahim sentenced both defendants to life imprisonment on the first count and 20 years’ imprisonment on the second count.

The sentences were handed down during the Federal Government’s latest phase of mass trials of suspected terrorists at the trial court.

The exercise, which began on Thursday, is being conducted across several courtrooms.

Among the judges handling the proceedings are Justices Salim Ibrahim, James Omotosho, Binta Nyako, Emeka Nwite, Obiora Egwuatu, Hauwa Yilwa, Joyce Abdulmalik and Peter Lifu.

No fewer than 34 suspects were listed for proceedings before Justice Ibrahim, while 25 were listed before Justice Lifu.

World.title: Terrorism: Court jails 2 for life for assisting Boko Haram members
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced two men to life imprisonment for providing support to members of the proscribed Boko Haram terrorist group.

The convicts, Abba Mustapha and Bukar Ibrahim, both from Borno State, were arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS).

Trial Justice Salim Ibrahim handed down the sentence after the duo pleaded guilty to the charge the Federal Government preferred against them.

The Federal Government alleged that, aside from aiding the operations of insurgents, the convicts also concealed information about their whereabouts.

While they received life imprisonment on the first count of the charge, the court sentenced them to 20 years on the second count.

The judgment followed the resumption of another phase of the mass trial of alleged terrorists and their facilitators by the Federal Government.

No fewer than 59 suspects were listed to appear before various judges of the court.

Some of the judges presiding over the cases include Justices Ibrahim, James Omotosho, Binta Nyako, Emeka Nwite, Obiora Egwuatu, Hauwa Yilwa, Joyce Abdulmalik and Peter Lifu.

It will be recalled that in June, the Federal Government prosecuted over 600 individuals allegedly affiliated with terrorist organisations.

The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, said the exercise was meant to send a clear message that the administration is not treating terrorism with levity.

World.title: TINUBU’S PROXY ELECTIONEERING
World.content:
Time will tell whether the President’s campaign strategy will secure him victory, writes BOLAJI ADEBIYI

At last, the crowds are gathering, signalling that politics is about to heat up. Welcome to the electioneering season. Politicians have been politicking, many of them beginning almost immediately after President Bola Tinubu was inaugurated on 29 May 2023. Something akin to permanent politics has emerged, with all manner of support groups springing up, their battle cry: Tinubu beyond 2027.

Well, 2027 is around the corner. A clearer sign is not merely that it is less than three months away; Wednesday’s inauguration of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu/All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council signals the intense electioneering ahead of the 16 January presidential poll.

The council had interesting features: a deft blend of internal and external interests that, a few weeks ago, threatened to erupt into a conflagration. It turned out to be a presidential nod to Minister Nyesom Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, a political contraption some APC governors loathe, with shaky bases at home. It included opposition governors Ademola Adeleke of Osun State (Accord Party) and Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra State (All Progressives Grand Alliance), as well as Wike (Peoples Democratic Party). They are to take charge of their states as coordinators of the president’s campaign.

The president used the inauguration to outline his electioneering, saying the campaign would operate at the regional, state, local government, and ward levels, with zonal coordinators and governors leading the charge while he remains at his desk, running the affairs of state. This campaign model was proposed by Imo State Governor Hope Uzodinma, who is the secretary of the Council and the director-general of the Renewed Hope Agenda Ambassadors, a pre-campaign mobilisation group. The president will attend a few campaign rallies, while his coordinators take his messages of hope to the 36 states and the FCT, 744 LGAs, and 8,809 wards across the country.

“I hear you. I fully agree with your decision. Nigeria needs more attention now than ever before. The responsibility of this office does not pause,” President Tinubu told the impressive gathering in the expansive Banquet Hall of the State House, Presidential Villa, Abuja.

Opposition elements have, as expected, criticised this electioneering model, dismissing it as a veiled excuse for the President’s inability to face the rigours of an expectedly intense campaign, given public apprehension about his reform policies, which have inflicted pain on the people. They point to the President’s reputation as a fierce campaigner who deploys every resource to achieve his political objectives.

At first glance, the idea of a candidate sitting idle somewhere while others run around town explaining his manifesto and programmes to the electorate may seem unusual. Indeed, it is. The nation’s electoral history is replete with candidates mounting the rostrum at public rallies, telling the multitude what they intend to do for them if elected to office. President Tinubu is a master of this. He was energetic at the podium when APC’s Muhammadu Buhari defeated PDP’s President Goodluck Jonathan in 2015 to take power. He was also at his best in 2019, helping President Buhari retain his seat. His titanic battle to take power in 2023 succeeded because the war effort centred on him.

While this model’s critique is understandable, the historic success of conventional electioneering cannot preclude innovation. After all, electioneering aims to communicate effectively with the electorate. The candidate has the prerogative to determine the most effective strategy to reach and persuade voters. In any case, Tinubu’s approach is not entirely novel. It draws on the thinking of his mentor, the late Shehu Yar’Adua, leader of the defunct Patriotic Front.

Yar’Adua believed in collective leadership, contending that his followership was the aggregation of his associates’ influence. Hence, when an opposing politician challenged him to a popularity walk on the street, he responded that the challenge was not for him but for his associates, who, as leaders in their own right, wielded the influence accorded to him. Although he could not ultimately lead the country, his younger brother, Umaru, did so in 2007, on the same principle.

Elected President in 2007, Umaru Yar’Adua loathed addressing large crowds at rallies. “It is a waste of my time,” he told his strategy team. According to him, a few people decide who gets the vote. Those people are rarely at those large rallies. “The multitude at those large gatherings go back home to take instructions from those influential people they call their leaders. So, why don’t I just go to the decision-makers who will instruct those people at the rally?”

However, his strategists argued that, because politics is about sight and sound, the rallies were good for optics and could have a psychological impact on the electorate. The compromise: Yar’Adua spent at least one night in each state, addressing rallies during the day and meeting stakeholders at night. It worked for him, and he won.

President Tinubu appears to have modified this strategy, opting to attend rallies at a few strategic locations while his associates take charge in their areas of influence. Beyond rallies, the President has access to other electioneering channels, including focus groups, town halls, and door-to-door canvassing.

Those criticising his unusual electioneering model fail to recognise its similarity to US presidential campaign trends over the years. Frontline presidential candidates do not campaign in all 52 states of the federation. In fact, they do not expend much energy in their strongholds, concentrating on swing states regarded as battlegrounds. In 2016, for instance, the candidates campaigned in only 23 states. The record worsened in 2024, as the challenging Republican President Donald Trump and incumbent Vice President Kamala Harris appeared in only 17 states, concentrating their efforts on the seven battleground states, including Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, North Carolina, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, as well as Nebraska and Maine Districts.

Does this mean the US presidential candidates did not run campaigns in the other states? Certainly not. They had offices and campaign staff on the ground who did the canvassing for them. However, 246 of the 262 presidential campaign events in 2024 took place in the seven battleground states. This signals prioritisation. This appears to be President Tinubu’s preference. Time will tell whether he has adopted the right electioneering strategy.

Adebiyi, a Fellow of the Nigerian Guild of Editors, writes from Abuja

World.title: Two Boko Haram Members Bag Life Sentences in Abuja
World.content:
Two men arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS) have been sentenced to life imprisonment by a Federal High Court in Abuja for their membership of the proscribed Boko Haram terrorist group.

The convicts, Abba Mustapha and Bukar Ibrahim, both from Borno State, were handed the sentences after pleading guilty to charges bordering on membership of and providing support for the terrorist group, as well as concealing information on its activities.

Presiding over the case, Justice Salim Ibrahim sentenced the two men to life imprisonment on the first count and 20 years’ imprisonment on the second count.

The judgment was delivered during the Federal Government’s latest phase of mass trials of suspected terrorists, which began on Thursday and is being conducted across several courtrooms.

Other judges handling the proceedings include Justices James Omotosho, Binta Nyako, Emeka Nwite, Obiora Egwuatu, Hauwa Yilwa, Joyce Abdulmalik and Peter Lifu.

No fewer than 34 suspects were listed for proceedings before Justice Ibrahim, while 25 others were listed before Justice Lifu.

The mass trials form part of the Federal Government’s ongoing judicial proceedings involving suspected members and supporters of terrorist groups.

World.title: Cardoso Makes Case for Transparent, Consensus-driven Monetary Policy at IMF Forum
World.content:
Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, has emphasised that credible monetary policy depends on informed committee deliberations, independent perspectives and clear communication of decisions to financial markets and the public.

Speaking at an International Monetary Fund (IMF) seminar in Bangkok on Thursday, Cardoso explained how the CBN has strengthened these practices within its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), drawing on Nigeria’s experience of navigating complex economic reforms and restoring confidence in monetary policymaking.

The seminar, ‘How Central Banks Decide: Committee Decision-Making and Communication in an Era of Uncertainty,’ brought together Cardoso; Chairman of the Swiss National Bank’s Governing Board, Martin Schlegel; and Governor of the Banque de France and member of the European Central Bank’s Governing Council, Emmanuel Moulin. The discussion was moderated by IMF First Deputy Managing Director, Dan Katz.

Addressing the role of committee members in reaching credible decisions, Cardoso explained that the CBN provides external MPC members with dedicated technical support and opportunities to consult independent specialists.

The bank also organises retreats involving experts from other central banks and wider stakeholder engagements, allowing members to consider diverse economic perspectives beyond formal policy meetings.

These arrangements extend to Nigeria’s ongoing transition towards inflation targeting, supported by IMF technical assistance, with external members involved from the outset of the process.

Cardoso said the arrangements were particularly important in establishing the credibility of the MPC following the economic and institutional challenges confronting the CBN when the current leadership assumed office.

He also highlighted the bank’s practice of publishing individual MPC members’ policy statements, which provides greater transparency around the reasoning behind monetary policy decisions.

According to Cardoso, he personally reviews the statements to understand the different assessments informing committee deliberations, including opinions that may differ from the eventual decision.

On the role of leadership, he explained that effective deliberation requires identifying areas of agreement before addressing disagreements and proceeding to a vote.

“What are the things we all agree on? That should be number one. What are the things we don’t really agree on? And then number three, of course, is to vote,” he said.

Cardoso noted that this approach helps prevent committees from becoming absorbed in relatively minor disagreements while losing sight of the broader economic questions requiring decisions.

His remarks reflected a central theme of the IMF discussion: how central banks can encourage rigorous internal debate while maintaining a coherent institutional position.

Schlegel described the Swiss National Bank’s approach, where governing board members examine the merits and disadvantages of competing policy options before reaching consensus. The institution communicates a common position without attributing individual votes, a practice he said also helps protect members from external pressure.

Moulin discussed the European Central Bank’s consensus-building culture under President Christine Lagarde, highlighting inclusive deliberations, equal access to information and a shared monetary policy framework. He stressed that communication must help households understand the implications of policy decisions for prices, employment and borrowing costs.

Cardoso illustrated the application of Nigeria’s approach through the September MPC meeting, when members agreed that weaknesses in the monetary policy transmission mechanism required correction.

That common assessment helped focus deliberations on the appropriate response, resulting in a 350-basis-point reduction in the benchmark interest rate from 26.5 per cent to 23 per cent.

He explained that Nigeria’s distinct inflation cycle, influenced by foreign-exchange harmonisation and subsidy reforms, required the committee to assess domestic economic conditions rather than simply follow monetary policy developments in other countries.

Although the decision surprised markets, Cardoso said earlier reforms, stronger economic fundamentals and carefully considered communication helped investors understand its rationale.

“To do such a thing successfully, you must have an element of credibility with the market,” he said.

Katz observed that financial markets absorbed the unexpected decision without significant disruption, describing the response as a testament to the clarity and credibility of the CBN’s communications.

The discussion also examined the growing role of artificial intelligence in interpreting central bank statements. Schlegel emphasised the importance of precise language, while Katz disclosed that the IMF had developed AI tools to analyse monetary policy communications in near real time.

In closing, Katz noted that although central banks operate under different governance arrangements, effective decision-making depends on candid debate, diverse perspectives, strong leadership and clear communication.

Cardoso’s contribution offered Nigeria’s experience of combining independent participation, transparent policy assessments and structured committee deliberations with the responsibility to communicate collective decisions clearly.

The exchange highlighted how the credibility of monetary policy is shaped not only by the decisions central banks announce, but also by the institutional processes through which those decisions are reached.

World.title: Senate Declares ‘No Vacancy’ As Akpabio, Barau Get Backing for 11th Assembly
World.content:
* Lawmakers endorse return of principal officers

* Dismiss politically motivated attacks on Senate President

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate on Thursday threw its weight behind Senate President Godswill Akpabio’s bid to retain his position in the 11th National Assembly, declaring that there would be “no vacancy” in the offices of the Senate President, Deputy Senate President and other principal officers who secure re-election in the 2027 general election.

The endorsement, which followed a spontaneous motion moved by the Senate Chief Whip, Tahir Monguno, and seconded by Senator Cyril Fasuyi, signalled an early attempt by serving lawmakers to consolidate support for the current leadership ahead of the inauguration of the next National Assembly.

The lawmakers also backed the return of Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin, Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele, Monguno and Deputy Senate Whip Peter Nwaebonyi, alongside Minority Leader Abba Moro, Deputy Minority Leader Olalere Oyewumi and Minority Whip Tony Nwoye, provided they win re-election on January 16, 2027.

Monguno, who represents Borno North, moved the motion during plenary after Akpabio complained that political opponents were allegedly exploiting controversies surrounding recent Senate debates to undermine his reputation and weaken his chances of retaining the Senate presidency.

“Insha Allah, by the grace of God, the majority of us are going to make it back to the Senate, and this seat is hereby declared: there is no vacancy,” Monguno said.

He extended the declaration to the office of the Deputy Senate President and other principal officers, insisting that those who returned to the Senate after the elections should retain their positions.

“There is no vacancy at all, including the seat of the Deputy Senate President and all other principal officers. I hereby declare, there is no vacancy,” he added.

Fasuyi, who represents Ekiti North, immediately endorsed the motion, declaring that Akpabio’s position should not be open to a contest in the next Assembly.

“I hereby support the motion ably moved by Senator Monguno that the seat of the Senate President in the 11th Assembly is not open to any contest. It is already occupied by Senator Godswill Obot Akpabio,” he said.

Akpabio subsequently put the declaration to a voice vote, with senators present responding affirmatively when he called for those in support. No audible opposition was recorded during the exchange.

“I think that settles it,” the Senate President declared.

However, the endorsement does not remove the constitutional requirement for newly elected senators to elect their presiding officers when the 11th National Assembly is inaugurated. The declaration instead reflects the position expressed by the lawmakers who supported the motion.

The development comes amid speculation that other political heavyweights, including Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and Senator Adams Oshiomhole, may be interested in the Senate presidency.

Before the motion, Akpabio had defended himself against what he described as politically motivated attempts to misrepresent his comments during Tuesday’s debate on the Suicide Prevention Bill 2026.

The bill, sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, representing Cross River South, scaled second reading and triggered debate on whether survivors of suicide attempts should face criminal prosecution or receive medical and psychological assistance.

Akpabio cautioned commentators against interpreting individual contributions during legislative debates as the Senate’s final position.

“When we discuss here, we discuss for and against, and in the course of our discussions, whatever we say should not anger anybody outside this chamber, because at the end, what matters is our final decision,” he said.

He argued that lawmakers must be allowed to disagree during deliberations without their remarks being distorted to damage their reputations.

He said: “We want to make the best laws, so we are bound to oppose each other, and we are also bound to support each other,” urging television commentators to avoid politically motivated interpretations of parliamentary proceedings.

“No matter the discussion, please take the final decision of the Senate into consideration. Don’t go and sit down in panels and try to do politically motivated discussions,” Akpabio added.

The Senate President also rejected attempts to associate terrorism with any particular religion, insisting that acts of violence should not be used to stigmatise religious communities.

“Terrorists are not Muslims. Terrorists are not Christians. Terrorists are human beings who believe in taking their lives and the lives of others,” he said.

Akpabio maintained that Islam prohibits suicide and killing, adding that public discussions should distinguish between people experiencing mental health challenges and those who deliberately take their lives or harm others.

He also cited his longstanding relationships with Muslims and Christians, including his support for religious pilgrimages, to reject allegations of religious bias.

Akpabio’s defence and the subsequent endorsement of his leadership highlighted the political sensitivities surrounding the Senate presidency as lawmakers prepare for the 2027 elections.

While Thursday’s declaration demonstrated support for the current leadership among the senators who backed the motion, the final composition of the 11th Senate and its choice of presiding officers will be determined after the elections.

World.title: ODCF Lauds Makinde for Developmental Strides in Oke Ogun
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

President of the Oke Ogun Development Consultative Forum (ODCF), Alhaji Ahmed Raji (SAN), on Thursday, lauded Oyo State Governor, ‘Seyi Makinde, for the administration’s developmental strides in Iseyin and the wider Oke Ogun Zone.

Raji spoke at the inauguration and handover of the Alhaji Kazeem Owonikoko Building at L.A. Primary School, Oke Esa, Iseyin, which he donated to the state government.

He praised Governor Makinde for major infrastructure projects, including the Moniya–Iseyin Road, the Oyo–Iseyin Road, and the Iseyin–Fapote–Ogbomoso Road. The newly donated building, equipped with classrooms, offices, solar power, desks, chairs and modern learning gadgets, was described as a world class educational facility.

The legal icon particularly lauded the establishment of the College of Agricultural Sciences and Renewable Natural Resources, a campus of the Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, in Iseyin.

He said: “When those who call themselves progressives were in government, they didn’t give us this. You came and gave us what they could not.”

Raji appealed to the governor to grant autonomy to the Iseyin campus as a full fledged university, adding that the people of Oke Ogun deeply appreciate the governor’s contributions to infrastructure and education.

In his remarks, Governor Makinde thanked Raji for transforming the 92-year-old school, noting that the gesture demonstrated that government alone cannot meet all societal needs.

He said well-meaning individuals must continue to support education and community development.

Makinde said: “This building can stand anywhere in the world. It shows that no government can do everything alone. Those who are blessed must support the education of our children.”

The governor reiterated his commitment to serving Oyo State without bias for political affiliations, stressing that development, not party labels, guides his administration.

He encouraged Raji to continue his philanthropic efforts, noting that while governments and political parties come and go, Oyo State remains.

Makinde also highlighted ongoing industrial development in Iseyin, including the sugar factory near Fasola Farms, which is currently undergoing test running. He said improved road networks have made the project viable and positioned Iseyin for global recognition.

Responding to Raji’s request for autonomy for the LAUTECH Iseyin Campus, Governor Makinde said: “Regarding your request on the Iseyin Campus of LAUTECH becoming an autonomous university, we will go through the process. We will apply through the NUC, and I will carry out a sustainability study too. So, what you have asked for is done.”

Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Justice and Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF), Prince Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), commended Raji for the project, just as he called on individuals to join hands to support the Makinde administration.

He said: “I am happy to witness a day like this. This is a very good project from my respected colleague. I want to add that all of us need to join hands together to keep supporting Governor Seyi Makinde.”

Speaking on behalf of the Owonikoko family, Mr Abduljelil Owonikoko (SAN) and the Headteacher of L.A. Primary School, Mr. Dauda, thanked Governor Makinde for prioritising education and transforming Iseyin into a hub of opportunities.

Present at the event included the Deputy Governor of Oyo State, Mr ‘Bayo Lawal; a retired Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Abdul Aboki (rtd); Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Hon. Adebo Ogundoyin; Member representing Iseyin/Itesiwaju/Kajola/Iwajowa Federal Constituency, Hon. Shina Oyedeji; Secretary to the State Government, Professor Musibau Babatunde; Chief of Staff to the Governor, Bashorun Akinwale Akinwole; Head of Service, Dr. (Mrs.) Adenike Fashina; Deputy Chief of Staff, Hon. Kazeem Adeniyi; and Senior Executive Assistant to the Governor on General Duties, Chief Bayo Lawal.

Others present included Chief Niyi Akintola (SAN); deputy governorship candidate of the Allied People’s Movement (APM), Mr. Mufutau Open Salawu; Director General of the APM Apex Campaign Council, Oyo State, Dr. Nureni Adeniran; and the House of Assembly candidate for Iseyin/Itesiwaju State Constituency, Mr Dasola Fadiran.

World.title: ASUU Condemns Arrest, Arraignment of ABU Don, Accuses Katsina Govt of Intimidating Academics
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Sokoto Zone, has condemned the arrest and arraignment of Dr. Kurfi of Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, describing it as intimidation of academics by the Katsina State Government.

The Zonal Chairman of the Union, Professor Abubakar Sabo Yabo, who briefed journalists in Sokoto said Dr. Kurfi was arrested by operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) allegedly on the instruction of the Katsina State Government over his comments on the security situation in the state.

Yabo said the development remains an issue of grave concern to the academic community and the general public, as it raises questions about the misplacement of government priorities.

According to him, it is evident that the recent antics of the government showcase a tendency to instil fear in an already traumatised nation, rather than provide solutions to pressing challenges.

He noted that while ASUU accepts the application of the rule of law in every circumstance, where it becomes a tool for intimidation, it becomes a serious matter of concern to the Union.

The Zonal Chairman stressed that deploying instruments of state security to harass an academic for expressing views on insecurity amounts to an assault on freedom of expression and academic freedom.

He therefore called on the Katsina State Government to focus sincerely on addressing the economic, social and security challenges affecting the state, rather than resorting to unnecessary intimidation of academics.

Yabo further called on relevant security agencies and the judiciary to be fair and impartial in treating Dr. Kurfi, insisting that due process must be strictly observed.

He added: “Let it be on record that Nigerians are watching as the legal processes take place. Justice to one is justice to all, while injustice to one is injustice to all.”

The Union warned that it would not stand aloof while its members are harassed under the guise of law enforcement, stressing that an injury to one academic is an injury to all.

Efforts to get the reaction of the Katsina State Government as at press time proved abortive.

World.title: Customs Intercepts Contraband Worth N722m in Sokoto
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Sokoto/Zamfara Area Command, has intercepted assorted contraband goods with a Duty Paid Value of N721.9 million.

The Acting Customs Area Controller of the Command, Deputy Comptroller Haliru Isah Abdullahi, disclosed this on Thursday at a press briefing held at the Command Headquarters in Sokoto.

Abdullahi said the seizures were made in line with the policy thrust of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, which emphasises consolidation, collaboration and innovation.

He said despite insecurity in parts of the two states, operatives of the Command have sustained anti-smuggling operations to secure the borders and protect the nation’s economy.

Giving a breakdown of the seizures, the Controller listed one used DAF truck with registration number JEG 199 XA and Chassis No. XLRAS85WCOE421859 used as means of conveyance, 599 bales of second-hand clothes and seven sacks of second-hand women’s bags.

Other items, according to him, include 43 cartons of cigarettes, seven cartons of Akouna coffee and a large quantity of unregistered pharmaceutical products.

He listed the pharmaceutical products as 100 packages of quinine, 500 packages of amodiaquine, 140 packages of paracetamol, 300 packages of anti-cold tablets, one carton of analgesic injections, two cartons of Dynewell syrup, one carton of Dynewell tablets and one carton of Clear Cold.

Abdullahi put the cumulative Duty Paid Value (DPV) of the seized items at N721,957,021.41.

He said the actions of operatives were in line with the provisions of Sections 245 and 248 of the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023, which empowers the Service to seize and condemn any goods liable to forfeiture.

The Acting Controller appealed to well-meaning Nigerians to provide credible information that would aid the eradication of smuggling, noting that curbing the menace would prevent consumption of unregistered drugs that pose grave danger to citizens’ health.

He also warned smugglers and their collaborators to desist from the nefarious act, stressing that the Command under his watch would not be a safe haven for economic saboteurs.

Abdullahi commended the Comptroller-General of Customs, officers and men of the Command for their resilience, sister security agencies for their collaboration and members of the press for their support in sensitising the public.

He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, collecting revenue for national development and suppressing smuggling to the barest minimum.

World.title: FACC Disburses N2.428tn September Allocations as Federation Revenue Grosses N3.913tn
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) has disbursed a total of N2.428 trillion to the Federal Government, states and local government councils, as Federation Revenue grossed N3.913 trillion for September 2026.

FAAC shared the amount during its October meeting in Abuja, Thursday, the Director of Press and Public Relations, Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation (OAGF), Bawa Mokwa, said in a statement.

The N2.428 trillion September allocations surpassed the sum of N2.338 trillion shared in the preceding month of August by N90 billion.

Citing the communiqué issued at the meeting, Mokwa said from the N2.428 trillion distributable revenue, the Federal Government received N832.242 billion, state governments received N799.872 billion, while local government councils got N560.660 billion.

The sum of N236.049 billion went to oil mineral producing states as 13 per cent derivation revenue.

The N2.428 trillion total distributable revenue for September comprised a distributable statutory revenue of N1.672 trillion and distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N756.587 billion.

Although gross revenue was N3.913 trillion in September, total deductions for cost of collection stood at N131.758 billion, while total transfers, refunds and savings accounted for N1.352 trillion.

According to the communiqué, gross statutory revenue of N3.096 trillion was received for September 2026, an amount higher than the sum of N2.850 trillion received in the preceeding month by N246.384 billion.

Value Added Tax (VAT) also posted a gross revenue of N816.872 billion in September, N17.972 billion, an amount less than the N834.843 billion recorded in August 2026.

However, from the N816.872 billion gross VAT revenue, distributable VAT revenue was N756.587 billion from which the Federal Government received N75.659 billion, state governments got N416.123 billion, and local government councils received N264.805 billion.

According to the figures, state and local government councils received larger shares of distributable VAT revenue, while the Federal Government got a smaller share.

The communiqué also showed that gross statutory revenue rose in September, while VAT revenue declined during the period.

It equally emerged that gross statutory revenue stood at N3.096 trillion in September, up from N2.850 trillion in August, the N246.384 billion rise reflecting higher revenue available from statutory sources.

Overall, FAAC attributed the changes in revenue performance to increases in some tax and petroleum-related revenue sources, alongside declines in others.

Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax, petroleum royalties, import duty, Common External Tariff (CET) levies and excise duty recorded significant increases in September.

But Companies Income Tax (CIT), Capital Gains Tax (CGT), Stamp Duties Tax (SDT), VAT, mineral royalties, gas-flaring penalties, rental gas-flaring fees and miscellaneous oil revenue declined during the period.

World.title: St. Anne’s Diocesan College’s matric learner takes life before exams
World.content:
St Anne's Diocesan College matric student Reneiloe Monkhi took her own life. Images via Facebook/TikTok

St. Anne’s Diocesan College in KwaZulu-Natal is mourning the death of matric learner Reneiloe Monkhi, who tragically took her own life via suicide. This comes as the class of 2026 has officially commenced their final exams.

ST ANNE’S MATRIC LEARNER TAKES HER OWN LIFE

In a statement on their Facebook account, St Anne’s Diocesan College announced the sad passing of one of their Grade 12 learners.

The statement read: “Rest in peace, Reneiloe. 💙🕊️ The St Anne’s community mourns the untimely loss of one of our precious matrics, Reneiloe Monkhi, who, it appears, tragically took her own life.



“Rene was greatly appreciated for her loyalty, care and kindness towards others. Her gentle nature was complemented by her sense of humour and vibrant spark. She was poised, beautifully elegant and dignified.

“Rene will be remembered with much love and will be sorely missed”

No othr details about her death was publicly shared



In the comments section, schools from near and far, including Hilton College, Durban Girls High and St Andrew’s School for Girls, sent their condolences

On Tuesday, 13 October, matric exams commenced for learners around South Africa.

Just days earlier, St. Anne’s had urged its learners ot practise self-care amid Mental Health Awareness Month and the onset of matric exams.



MATRIC DANCE AND MENTAL HEALTH

Earlier this year. Reneiloe Monkhi’s video documenting her St Anne’s Matric Dance went viral on various social media platforms.

The teen wore a sparkly gown and a matching tiara

Reneiloe appeared to be struggling with her mental health, as her final repost hinted at suicide

World.title: IFP’s Asanda Duma captures hearts with his good looks! [video]
World.content:
While Asanda Duma is focused on his political ambitions, it is his good looks that have seemingly captured the hearts of many on social media.

Duma, a young politician representing the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP), is actively campaigning for the coveted Ward 10 councillor position in Estcourt, KwaZulu-Natal.

IFP’S ASANDA DUMA CAPTURES HEARTS WITH HIS FACE CARD

Facebook user Mayor Mduduzi Myeza shared a viral video that drew over 2,000 comments and 51,000 likes.



In the clip, a woman can be heard admiring Asanda’s handsome face while looking at a campaign poster.

She also playfully says that his good looks alone were enough to earn her vote, adding that his contact details should have been included on the poster.

She said: “We will vote for you because you’re handsome, but they should’ve included your number as well. Could we please have your number?”

ELECTION SEASON IS UPON US

The election season is officially upon us, as the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has confirmed that preparations for the 2026 Local Government Elections are underway.

Naturally, political parties have rolled out vigorous campaigns in a bid to garner support and votes.

Among them is the IFP, which launched its manifesto in September 2026, reinforcing its presence as one of KwaZulu-Natal’s leading political parties.



The IFP has thrown several hats in the ring ahead of the elections, including that of Mkhuleko Hlengwa, whom the party is touting as its mayoral candidate in eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality.

Meanwhile, Asanda Duma is also forging his political career, with many seemingly warming up to the young leader.

World.title: Andile Mpisane claps back with ‘AI-statement’
World.content:
Andile Mpisane claps back at claims he is a 'deadbeat dad'. Images via IG

Andile Mpisane has responded to a claim, reportedly by his ex, Sithelo Shozi, accusing him of neglecting his children.

The Royal AM soccer boss and amapiano artists has two daughters, Florence and Coco, with the influencer, and another two, Miaandy and Messiah Shauwn with his wife, Tamia.

In recent months, Tamia has dropped her marital surname, fuelling rumours that the couple have separated.



ANDILE MPISANE RESPONDS TO ‘DEADBEAT DAD’ CLAIMS

On his Instagram, Andile Mpisane denied allegations that he had neglected his children.

The “AI-generated” statement read: “My responsibilities and commitment as a father should not be judged on the basis of speculation, assumptions or one-sided narratives. I have continued to contribute towards my children’s education, including paying their school fees, and I remain committed to their well-being and future.

Andile claimed that his access to his children had been “limited” and that he had recently “reconnected” with them.



He continued: “My decision to remain silent about private family matters should never be mistaken for a lack of responsibility, love or commitment. I will not allow assumptions or speculation to define my role as a father or undermine the efforts I have continued to make for my children.

“My focus remains firmly on rebuilding and maintaining a meaningful relationship with my children, supporting their education, and ensuring their emotional, physical and overall well-being remain a priority”

Andile Mpisane – the son of businesswoman Shauwn Mkhize, or “MaMkhize” – did not specify which of his ex’s children he was referring to.

However, in the comments section, followers suggested his statement was in response to Sithelo Shozi’s TikTok claims that he had not seen their children in “six years and counting”.

Without naming him, Sithelo claimed that Andile was an “absolute deadbeat”.

World.title: Botswana safari: The top places to visit on a 1 week trip
World.content:
Botswana is one of the Southern African countries with wildlife-rich national parks, waterways and vast wilderness areas, which travellers can explore within a single safari holiday.

For visitors planning a seven-day trip, choosing destinations carefully is essential because some camps and reserves require long road transfers or light aircraft flights.

Here are the top places to consider when planning a one-week Botswana safari.



Botswana safari: Exploring the Okavango Delta

The Okavango Delta is one of Botswana’s best-known tourist attractions, offering a combination of wetlands, lagoons and islands that support diverse wildlife.

According to the Botswana Tourism Organisation, the destination offers big-game viewing alongside opportunities to explore its waterways.

Visitors can enjoy guided game drives, birdwatching and traditional mokoro canoe excursions, depending on the location and water conditions.



Travellers should consider spending two or three nights in the Delta to experience its different safari activities.

What to see in Moremi Game Reserve

Located in the eastern and central parts of the Okavango region, Moremi Game Reserve is another destination to consider.

The reserve covers approximately 3 900 square kilometres and includes floodplains, lagoons, grasslands and forests.



Its varied habitats support numerous animal species, including predators and herbivores, making it attractive to wildlife enthusiasts and photographers.

Moremi can be combined with the Okavango Delta as part of a northern Botswana safari.

Travellers should check accommodation locations and transfer arrangements before booking.



Botswana safari: Wildlife encounters in Chobe National Park

Chobe National Park is renowned for its elephants and wildlife along the Chobe River.

The park offers game drives and river cruises, allowing visitors to observe animals from land and water.

Kasane, a town in northeastern Botswana, serves as a convenient base for exploring the park.



A seven-day itinerary combining the Okavango Delta, Moremi and Chobe is offered by safari operators, including Go2Africa.

Travellers could allocate two nights to Chobe before departing from Kasane.

Discovering Savuti

Savuti, within Chobe National Park, offers another option for visitors interested in wildlife viewing.



The region is known for its open landscapes and opportunities to spot predators and other animals during game drives.

However, adding Savuti to a trip that already includes the Delta, Moremi and Chobe’s riverfront may require additional transfers. Travellers should consider whether the extra journey is worthwhile within a seven-day schedule.

What makes the Makgadikgadi Pans special

The Makgadikgadi Pans offer a different experience from Botswana’s wetlands and traditional safari destinations.



The vast salt flats provide striking landscapes, while seasonal conditions influence wildlife activity and opportunities to see flamingos.

Although the pans are worth considering, travellers with only seven days may find it more practical to save them for another visit.

Planning a one-week Botswana safari

For a first visit, prioritising the Okavango Delta, Moremi and Chobe provides a varied safari experience without attempting to cover too much ground.



The final itinerary will depend on the budget, accommodation availability and transport arrangements. Travellers should confirm transfer times and seasonal activity options before booking.

World.title: Two ANC members shot and killed while campaigning in KZN
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal police have opened two murder cases and three counts of attempted murder following a shooting in which two African National Congress (ANC) members, a man and a woman, were allegedly killed in Area 24, Umgababa.

The incident happened on Thursday afternoon while the victims were reportedly taking part in a door-to-door campaign in the KwaZulu-Natal South Coast.

TWO ANC MEMBERS KILLED IN UMGABABA

KZN police spokesperson Colonel Robert Netshiunda said reports indicate that two women and one man affiliated with a political party, accompanied by two bodyguards, were conducting a door-to-door campaign when a white Isuzu bakkie approached them from behind.



“The occupants of the bakkie reportedly opened fire on the five using rifles and pistols. Two people, a man and a woman, were declared dead at the scene and one woman reportedly injured her leg when she was fleeing from the assassins. The two bodyguards fled the scene and are yet to be found.

“The motive of the killing is unknown but political intolerance cannot be ruled out,” Netshiunda said.

ANC convenor in eThekwini Thanduxolo Sabela said their councillors were ambushed and shot at.

“The branch coordinator and a volunteer passed away in today’s shooting on ward 98. The ward candidate was rushed to hospital for a check up and she is fine now,” he said.

“We don’t believe that when conducting a campaign the would be areas where our campaigners would be met with such hostility and be shot at,” he said.

Police are currently on the scene where 2 ANC members were shot and killed with a further 3 more injured in Umgababa, south of Durban.



Eyewitnesses have told EWN the group was shot while conducting door to door campaigns in the area. TCG pic.twitter.com/pNkFenluDv  October 15, 2026

The shooting comes just a few months after another ANC councillor in Klaarwater, Sibusiso “Khekhe” Khwela was gunned down in broad daylight.

World.title: Number Of The Day | 10% | 15 October 2026
World.content:
South Africa's Retirement Crisis Begins Long Before Retirement

South Africa has a retirement problem that begins decades before people reach retirement age. The warning is not simply that workers are saving too little. It is that the economic circumstances shaping their working lives are making long-term financial security increasingly difficult to achieve.

The Alexforbes Member Insights 2026 report illustrates the scale of the challenge. Only 10% of contributing members in the retirement funds administered by Alexforbes are projected to replace at least 75% of their final pensionable salary when they retire. Although this represents an improvement from 6% in 2021, the

findings suggest that the overwhelming majority of contributing members remain financially unprepared for retirement.

The question is no longer simply whether South Africans understand the importance of saving. It is whether the country's economic realities allow enough people to act on that understanding.

The Difference Between Having A Job And Building Wealth

Employment provides an income, but it does not automatically create financial security. Workers must divide their earnings between immediate expenses and obligations that may be decades away. Housing, transport, food, education and family responsibilities all compete with retirement contributions.

This creates a difficult contradiction. Retirement planning rewards consistency, while financial pressure frequently demands flexibility. A worker may understand the value of preserving retirement savings but still need money to manage an immediate household emergency.

The Alexforbes research found that the average member contribution rate was 11.2% of salary, below the 15% benchmark used in its long-term retirement illustrations.

The significance extends beyond the contribution gap. Money not invested today also loses the opportunity to accumulate returns over time. For workers whose financial circumstances delay retirement saving, catching up can become progressively more expensive.

Time Is An Asset That Cannot Be Recovered

Consider two workers contributing the same percentage of their salaries towards retirement. One begins at the start of a career. The other begins 20 years later.

Under the assumptions used by AlexForbes, saving 15% of salary for 40 years could provide retirement income equivalent to 75% of final pensionable salary. Saving the same percentage for only 20 years produces a projected replacement ratio of 27%.

To reach the 75% target within that shorter period, the required contribution rises to 41% of salary.

These are illustrative projections rather than guaranteed outcomes, but their implication is clear. Delaying retirement contributions creates a financial burden that higher earnings later in life may not easily overcome.

It also reveals a structural inequality. Workers who enter stable employment early have more time to accumulate savings than those who experience prolonged unemployment, interrupted careers or irregular income.

When Today's Emergency Becomes Tomorrow's Shortfall

South Africa's two-pot retirement system creates another important tension. Access to a portion of retirement savings can provide financial relief when households face unexpected expenses. However, repeated withdrawals reduce the money available to remain invested for retirement.

The Alexforbes illustration discussed on Number of the Day shows how annual withdrawals could reduce a projected 75% retirement-income replacement ratio to 51%.

That does not mean access to savings is inherently harmful. The deeper problem arises when retirement funds become a substitute for emergency savings or a response to persistent financial insecurity.

A sustainable retirement system must therefore address both sides of the problem: preserving money for the future while acknowledging the financial pressures workers face today.

Retirement Security Cannot Be An Afterthought

Retirement planning needs to become part of financial decision-making from the beginning of working life. Starting early, reviewing contribution levels, preserving investments and seeking appropriate financial advice can all improve retirement prospects.

But individuals cannot carry the entire burden. Employers, financial institutions and policymakers also have roles in making retirement planning accessible, understandable and sustainable.

A country cannot measure financial wellbeing only by how much its people earn while working. It must also consider whether those earnings allow them to live with independence and dignity once work ends.

The real retirement crisis is not simply that South Africans are failing to prepare for the future. It is that too many are struggling to afford that preparation in the present.

References

· Moneyweb: Alexforbes data shows 10% of retirees now on track · BusinessTech: Retirement shock for South Africans · Alexforbes: Financial planning and advice

World.title: 'Only 10% of contributors can retire comfortably' - Alex Forbes
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - More South Africans will be able to fund their retirement according to data released by Alex Forbes.

But many more will face lost income and poverty - when it's too late to save. Retirement savings in focus as only one in ten will live comfortably

Alex Forbes is one of South Africa's biggest financial service providers focusing on retirement with 1.1 million active members.

It says the number of contributors to Alex Forbes-administered funds who are expected to have an income of at least 75% of their final pensionable salary has gone from 6% to 10%.

READ | WATCH | Is your boss paying your pension ?

That's a significant increase but it still means that only one in ten will be able to enjoy a comfortable retirement.

This figure excludes South Africans who aren't saving at all.

The data shows that someone who contributes 15% of their salary towards retirement for 40 years could achieve the required amount.

But less time, less money or withdrawals from the two-pot system can all lead to significantly lower income.

World.title: Afrika Mayibuye probes links to Katlehong alleged gunman
World.content:
KATLEHONG - John Sibeko, the man accused of carrying out a deadly mass shooting in Katlehong, made a brief appearance at the Palm Ridge Magistrate's Court on Thursday.

Sibeko has been in custody since handing himself over to the police on Tuesday night.

He allegedly opened fire on a group of African National Congress (ANC) Youth League members as they returned from a fellow member's memorial service.

Two people died at the scene, while two others later succumbed to their injuries in hospital, bringing the total death toll to four.

READ | ‘He was right in front of us’: Katlehong gunman hands himself over

The accused faces a string of charges, including four counts of murder, four counts of attempted murder, discharging a firearm in a public space and failing to secure a weapon in a safe.

A conviction on just one of the murder charges carries a minimum sentence of 15 years behind bars.

Sibeko is a former Katlehong councillor and reportedly a member of Afrika Mayibuye Movement Party.

The party said they would probe links to him and if it is found that he is a member, his membership will be terminated.

Sibeko is expected back in court on 22 October for a possible bail application.

World.title: Venezuela's Maduro denies US torture charges as 'false accusations'
World.content:
NEW YORK - Ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores pleaded not guilty Thursday to new torture charges brought against the pair held in US custody since their extraordinary capture in January.

They appeared at a New York court after prosecutors alleged they conspired to commit acts including waterboardings, rapes and beatings against victims, including American citizens, in Venezuelan detention.

Maduro, who has previously called himself a "prisoner of war," slammed the latest charges as "false accusations" during a 35-minute hearing.

Asked by the judge how he pleaded to the indictment against him, the 63-year-old responded, "I reject this document in its entirety."

Flores, who wore the same brown prison jumpsuit as Maduro, said: "I am completely innocent, I am not guilty."

According to prosecutors, the couple used torture to "intimidate, harass, and neutralize their opponents, including through kidnappings."

Maduro "presided over" a system of repression and torture, while Flores helped him to develop it, according to a charging document.

In one 2022 instance, Venezuelan authorities allegedly tortured an American who they accused of plotting to assassinate Maduro.

"That torture included electric shock to arms, legs, and genitals; asphyxiation; beatings; deprivation of food and water; and forced injections of a substance that caused (the victim) to experience seizures," a court filing states.

During his 2013-2026 presidency, rights groups widely accused Maduro of using political repression to cling to power.

- Immunity plea -

World.title: Umgababa shooting leaves ANC members fearful
World.content:
DURBAN - ANC volunteers in eThekwini are now afraid to continue campaigning after two party members were shot dead in Umgababa, south of Durban.

Supporters were conducting door-to-door campaigning as part of an ANC Women's League programme when three unknown men opened fire.

The regional convenor, Thabani Nyawose, said the motive for the shooting remains unclear but believes the group’s coordinator may have been targeted.

"Our coordinator was targeted. At this point in time, we don't know what the motive was. But we hope that police will investigate this. Because it looks like now ANC volunteers, they are scared. From today, it will be difficult for them to continue to conduct in this area," he said.

Nyawose said political parties deserve to campaign freely in all wards without any fear or intimidation.

READ | Two ANC members killed while campaigning

"This is very unfortunate incident, and we hope that police will follow up, investigate and arrest these criminals. Because as long as these people are not arrested, it will be difficult for political parties, not only the ANC, to run campaign. But we have lot of questions," he said.

Police in KwaZulu-Natal said they have opened two counts of murder and three counts of attempted murder.

Two people, a man and a woman were declared dead at the scene, and one woman reportedly injured her leg when she was fleeing from the assassins.

The two bodyguards fled the scene and are yet to be found.

The motive for the killing is still unknown however, authorities said they can't rule out a political motive for the shooting.

World.title: The world we live in is bad - Brother of slain ANC member speaks out
World.content:
DURBAN - The brother of one of the ANC members who was shot dead in Umgababa, KwaZulu-Natal on Thursday said the victims were conducting door-to-door campaigning with ANC members when gunmen opened fire.

Sihle Makhathini said according to information from the community, two men got out of a car and started shooting.

He said the loss is devastating.

"It is very devastating losing someone close to you its even sad when you lose a community member. The world we live in now has turned out to be bad," he said.

READ | Two ANC members killed while campaigning

Makhathini said the killings have renewed concerns of safety among residents in the community,

" We have been losing a lot of community members in different ways and it really sad. We need our community to be safe, to be able to walk around in peace. But its clear that life is gone now."

Police in KwaZulu-Natal said they have opened two counts of murder and three counts of attempted murder.

READ | Katlehong mass shooting suspect to appear in court



Two people, a man and a woman were declared dead at the scene, and one woman reportedly injured her leg when she was fleeing from the assassins.

"The two bodyguards fled the scene and are yet to be found," police statement said.

The motive for the killing is still unknown however, authorities said they can't rule out a political motive for the shooting.

World.title: Raila's spirit: Pro-Ruto, Linda Mwananchi leaders contend for Baba's magic
World.content:
Late Raila Odinga Family, friends follow proceedings during the remembrance service at Migwena ground. [Michael Mute, Standard]

It was an event that many had hoped would be the turning point to unite all the political orphans of the late Raila Odinga and breathe new life into a region, a support base and a party in discord.

But if Raila had hoped in his grave that his first anniversary would be the uniting factor, he is probably turning in his grave in disappointment as fissures of division among his former troops deepened in a politically charged anniversary at the historic Migwena grounds in Bondo.

World.title: From 'Chogo' to senator? Winnie Odinga steps into her own political spotlight
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

From Raila Odinga’s shadow to her own political path, Winnie sets her sights on the Nairobi Senate seat in 2027. [Courtesy]

The hat was more than a hat. Literally.

As Raila Odinga’s body made its final journey home from India, his youngest daughter, Winnie, held tightly to his familiar cream-coloured fedora. It was one of the few things she could still protect, a small piece of a man whose presence had filled her life and Kenya’s political imagination for decades.

The image of Winnie carrying her father’s hat was deeply personal. The country was mourning a political giant, but she was mourning her father.

A year later, on the first anniversary of Raila’s death, Winnie has announced her intention to contest the Nairobi Senate seat in the 2027 General Election.

The timing is poignant. On a day devoted to remembering her father, she has declared her own political ambitions, signalling a shift from being one of the most recognisable faces of the Odinga family to a politician seeking a mandate in her own right.

“As Edwin Sifuna seeks a higher office, I see an opportunity in Nairobi, which is why I have decided I will vie for Senator of Nairobi County,” she said.

And just like that, the conversation shifted from the daughter who carried Baba’s hat to the politician who wants a seat of her own.

The last-born girl

To many Kenyans, Winnie is Chogo, the last-born child of Raila and Ida Odinga. The nickname carries the familiarity of family life, a reminder that behind the powerful surname is a daughter who grew up in a household where politics was never far from the conversation.

Her father was no ordinary political figure. His name could summon crowds, ignite debate and divide opinion. His decades-long career placed the Odinga family at the centre of Kenya’s political story.

Growing up as Raila’s youngest daughter meant sharing him with a country that claimed a piece of his time, energy and, eventually, his final goodbye.

Yet Winnie was not simply a spectator in her father’s political world. She worked around his campaigns and communications before stepping into politics herself, eventually winning a seat in the East African Legislative Assembly.

In November 2022, Parliament elected her to represent Kenya in the regional legislature, where she took office in December that year. Based in Arusha, Tanzania, she became part of the East African Community’s legislative institution, serving a five-year term running to 2027.

The EALA offered Winnie a political platform beyond her father’s immediate circle and an opportunity to participate in regional affairs. Her current tenure has also given her experience in legislative politics before her proposed move into elective politics at home.

The Nairobi Senate bid would take her into a different contest, one in which voters will have to decide whether her experience, ideas and political programme merit their support.

The hat she could not let go

For years, Raila’s trademark headgear had been part of his public identity, appearing at political rallies, meetings and public ceremonies. But in Winnie’s hands, it became something else: a personal possession tied to the final journey of a daughter and her father

She explained how protective she had been of it throughout the journey, describing it as one of the few things she could still hold on to.

The image captured a kind of helplessness that public figures’ families rarely get to show. Crowds could mourn Raila, politicians could speak of his legacy, and supporters could debate who would inherit his political movement. Winnie, however, had been left with the painful task of bringing her father home.

The symbolism of the hat has since acquired another layer. At a ceremony in Bondo earlier this month, elders placed a traditional hat on Winnie’s head in a symbolic gesture associated with the possibility of her carrying forward her father’s political mantle.

Winnie’s political journey has not started with this Senate announcement.

Her election to the East African Legislative Assembly placed her among Kenya’s representatives in a regional institution whose work concerns cooperation among East African Community partner states.

The role gave her a platform in regional legislation while her father remained a central figure in national politics.

The Senate is responsible for representing counties, participating in lawmaking on matters concerning counties and exercising oversight over revenue allocated to county governments. A Nairobi senator must therefore make a case on issues that touch residents directly, from public spending and service delivery to the accountability of county leadership.

The capital is also a demanding political terrain. Its electorate is diverse, its concerns immediate and its contests fiercely competitive.

A famous surname may open doors, but it cannot replace a convincing programme on jobs, housing, transport, healthcare and the management of public resources.

Winnie will have to demonstrate that she understands Nairobi beyond its place in her father’s national political story.

Can she translate the loyalty associated with Raila into support for her own agenda? Can she persuade voters that she is more than the daughter of a political icon?

Those questions will follow her into the campaign.

The Odingaism

Political inheritance can be both an advantage and a burden.

Raila’s name carries a formidable history of opposition politics, democratic reform and a loyal support base. It also invites comparisons that few politicians have to contend with.

Winnie’s challenge will be to honour that history without allowing it to become the entirety of her political identity.

Raila’s death left a space in the Orange Democratic Movement and among supporters who had looked to him for direction through decades of political contests. The question of who will carry his legacy has inevitably turned towards his family and the wider political movement he helped build.

Winnie’s Senate bid will require her to turn recognition into a political proposition that voters can interrogate. Her experience at EALA gives her a legislative starting point; the Nairobi contest will demand that she demonstrate how that experience can serve residents of the capital.

She must also navigate the expectations attached to her father’s name while making room for her own ideas, priorities and leadership style.

There is a temptation to see Winnie’s future entirely through the lens of inheritance. She is Raila’s daughter, the last-born known as Chogo, the woman who carried his hat and the politician whom some supporters hope will continue his legacy.

But she is also a woman making a decision about her own future.

The Senate bid offers her an opportunity to define what that future means, beyond the grief surrounding her father’s death and the weight of a name that has shaped Kenyan politics for decades.

The hat remains an unforgettable image from Raila’s final journey home. A daughter attempted to protect the last tangible thing she could hold on to.

The Senate will demand something different: a political vision, a campaign and the votes of Nairobi residents.

Chogo has announced her next move. Will Winnie Odinga turn the memory of Baba into a mandate of her own?

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
