World.title: Liberia: Beijing 12345 Hotline Urges African Countries to Adopt Chinese Public Service Model
World.content:
BEIJING, China — Authorities operating Beijing’s 12345 Citizens Service Hotline are encouraging African countries, including Liberia, Sierra Leone and Nigeria, to adapt China’s public service model to strengthen government accountability, improve service delivery and enhance citizen engagement.

By J.H. Webster Clayeh | [email protected]

The call was made by Feng Yingyi, Deputy Director of the Beijing Municipal Citizens Service Hotline Center, during a visit by participants of the Second Session of the China International Press Communication Center.



Feng said China is willing to share its experience with African countries and other developing nations interested in improving the way governments response to public concerns.

“In the past years we have received guests from abroad most especially from the African countries who are more interesting in our Beijing models. We are very much willing to share our success stories,” Madam Feng told journalists.

“We also hope that all countries can adapt this model to their own conditions and learn properly from these practices because we have the Chinese characteristics model. We hope that these countries can develop their own model, their own characteristics so that we can all be successful,” she stated.

A MODEL FOR AFRICAN GOVERNMENTS

The Beijing 12345 hotline provides a centralized platform through which residents can submit complaints, make inquiries and offer suggestions to government authorities.

With Beijing’s population estimated at 21.8 million, the system enables residents to communicate their concerns to relevant government departments while allowing authorities to coordinate responses and monitor cases.

For African countries such as Liberia, Sierra Leone and Mali, the model could offer lessons in establishing integrated citizen service centers that connect people to ministries, local authorities and public agencies through telephone services, digital platforms and in-person assistance.

Such systems can also help governments establish clear deadlines for resolving complaints, track cases transparently and use public feedback to identify recurring problems and improve policies.

Madam Feng called on developing countries to study Beijing’s experience while adapting the system to their respective national circumstances.

THE CHALLENGES FACING THE HOTLINE

Despite its reported achievements, Beijing’s 12345 hotline continues to face challenges associated with heavy workloads, complicated complaints, interdepartmental coordination, service quality and the long-term resolution of public problems.

According to figures cited in the center’s 2025 annual report, the hotline handled 25.802 million requests from the public and businesses in 2025, representing a 6.6 percent increase from 2024.

The report put the resolution rate at 97.3 percent and the satisfaction rate at 97.7 percent.These figures highlight the scale of the operation and the demands placed on the system as Beijing continues to address the concerns of residents and businesses.

Madam Feng said the city’s size, population and complex urban challenges require authorities to continually improve public service delivery. She acknowledged that the challenges confronting the hotline change as the city develops and public expectations increase.

“We have higher rates and higher standards for future governments. So, for the challenges, we have different stages when it comes to development. But we are trying our best to continue to overcome more challenges back to another and then we set our new higher goals for us,” Madam Feng said.

HOW THE 12345 HOTLINE OPERATES

The Beijing 12345 Citizens Service Hotline originated in 1987 as the Mayor’s Hotline. In January 2019, it was renamed the Beijing Citizen Service Hotline Center and developed into a central platform for handling public complaints and supporting urban governance reforms.

The system operates on a people-centered approach built around rapid response, efficient processing, timely feedback and proactive governance. According to information provided by the center, the hotline has handled approximately 200 million requests from residents and businesses over more than seven years.

The center’s reported resolution and satisfaction rates have remained high, reflecting its central role in Beijing’s approach to public administration. In 2025 alone, the hotline processed 25.802 million requests, averaging more than 70,000 cases daily.

To manage the workload, the center operates 750 workstations staffed by more than 1,700 operators working in shifts to provide round-the-clock services. Its mission is captured in the phrase, “When the people call, we respond,” while its service commitment is expressed through the slogan, “Let You Hear Our Smile.”

The operational framework is designed to ensure that citizens’ concerns are received, assigned to the appropriate departments, addressed and followed up. The hotline consequently serves as a link between residents’ everyday experiences and the broader machinery of municipal administration.

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TRANSFORMS PUBLIC SERVICE

The visit also provided journalists with an opportunity to learn about the digital transformation of Beijing’s 12345 hotline and the growing role of artificial intelligence in public service delivery.

In line with the 2026 Beijing Forum on Swift Response to Public Complaints, whose annual theme is “Digital Intelligence Era and People’s City,” Beijing has upgraded its “Visit 12345” program.

The initiative includes the “12345 Hotline Digital Intelligence Innovation Lab,” which showcases developments in digital technology and artificial intelligence through interactive demonstrations and practical applications. The transformation focuses on four major areas: intelligent customer service, intelligent agent systems, intelligent workplace operations and the intelligent hub.

These innovations are intended to improve efficiency, strengthen coordination among government departments and help authorities respond more accurately to public needs.

Technology has helped transform the hotline from a traditional telephone-based complaint service into an integrated, data-driven public service and governance platform.

Through digital communication systems, big data, artificial intelligence and interconnected government information systems, the hotline can receive complaints, transfer cases to responsible departments, monitor progress, analyze recurring problems and provide feedback to citizens.

The approach supports Beijing’s Swift Response to Public Complaints reform, which emphasizes addressing citizens’ needs and resolving problems more efficiently.

TECHNOLOGY AND THE HUMAN TOUCH

Feng said the growing demands on government made technological innovation increasingly important in improving public service delivery. “Now with Science and Technological advancements, our artificial intelligence with our technological model, it is guaranteed that our services are fast running,” she said.

She added: “By the technology we can use these to analyze, to make judgment in an accurate way to identify potential risks and timely and accurate support to decision makers.”

One major area of development involves using large artificial intelligence models to improve communication between residents and the hotline.

The technology can facilitate dialogue between people and AI, automatically collect information about requests, generate work orders and direct cases to the appropriate government departments.

Through the Jingtong App, residents can access the quick-response public complaints service and use the 12345 intelligent agent. The system allows users to submit requests through an interactive process similar to a telephone conversation. It also supports text-based submissions, multilingual consultations and the uploading of photographs and videos.

These features give residents additional ways to explain their concerns, provide supporting evidence and communicate with government authorities.

MULTILINGUAL SERVICES EXPAND ACCESS

Beijing’s 12345 hotline also provides multilingual services to improve access for foreign residents and users who do not speak Chinese. According to a Beijing municipal government report published on October 11, 2026, the hotline provides services in eight foreign languages in addition to Chinese.

However, the official Beijing government website’s multilingual hotline page lists 10 languages, including Portuguese and Italian, suggesting a discrepancy between the two published sources. The multilingual arrangements reflect the importance of making public services accessible to people from different linguistic backgrounds.

For African countries considering similar systems, Beijing’s experience offers examples of how centralized complaint-handling platforms, digital technologies and multilingual communication can be incorporated into public administration.

While Feng expressed Beijing’s willingness to share its experience, she emphasized that countries should adapt the approach to their own circumstances and develop systems reflecting their national characteristics.

World.title: Liberia: Amelia Queen Cassell Turns Birthday into Hope for Chief Compound School Pupils Gbarnga Struggling to Find Chairs
World.content:
The Bong County Land Administrator also emphasized the importance of individuals taking practical steps to address community challenges instead of relying exclusively on government institutions. She expressed hope that her intervention would encourage other prominent citizens, businesspeople and organizations to identify pressing needs within their communities and contribute toward addressing them

GBARNGA, Bong County — For hundreds of children attending Chief Compound Community Public School in the heart of Gbarnga, the struggle to secure a comfortable place to sit has become an unfortunate part of their daily educational experience. While some pupils manage with broken chairs and damaged benches, others have been forced to sit on bricks or classroom floors, a situation that has recently brought the government institution under public scrutiny.

But amid growing concerns about the deteriorating learning conditions, Bong County Land Administrator Madam Amelia Queen Cassell has offered a measure of relief, donating 40 armchairs to the institution as part of activities commemorating her birthday.

The gesture, which also included the distribution of traditional lappers to elderly women selling vegetables and greens at the Gbarnga Sunday Market, marked a departure from conventional birthday celebrations, as Cassell chose to direct attention toward vulnerable residents and schoolchildren confronting everyday difficulties.



Her intervention comes at a time when Chief Compound Community Public School has been attracting attention over the shortage of classroom furniture, a problem that has continued to undermine efforts by teachers and administrators to provide a conducive learning environment.

Located in Gbarnga, the administrative headquarters of Bong County, the school occupies a position that makes its difficulties particularly troubling. The city is home to county authorities, educational administrators, lawmakers’ local offices and other influential stakeholders whose responsibilities include promoting development and improving public services.

Yet, within this same urban setting, children attending one of the city’s government schools continue to struggle with something as basic as finding a proper chair during classroom instruction.

With an enrollment reportedly exceeding 1,500 pupils, the institution has experienced increasing pressure on its limited furniture, leaving administrators to manage overcrowded classrooms with insufficient desks and chairs.

Recent reports about conditions at the school have drawn attention to pupils sitting on bricks, damaged benches and classroom floors while attempting to follow lessons. Some students reportedly carry chairs from

their homes, while others rely on makeshift seating arrangements that provide little comfort during lengthy instructional periods.

The situation has also raised concerns about educational inequality, particularly for children from low-income households whose parents are unable to purchase chairs for their use.

Although the 40 armchairs cannot accommodate the school’s entire student population, they represent immediate assistance to children who might otherwise continue attending classes without suitable seating

Reports that some pupils have stayed away from school because of the furniture shortage have added urgency to calls for intervention, with residents questioning how such conditions can persist in the heart of a city where many of the county’s decision-makers are based.

It is against this background that Cassell’s birthday donation has taken on significance beyond the number of chairs presented. Although the 40 armchairs cannot accommodate the school’s entire student population, they represent immediate assistance to children who might otherwise continue attending classes without suitable seating.

Cassell said her decision to support the school was motivated by a desire to make her birthday meaningful through service to others. According to her, the occasion presented an opportunity to reflect on the needs of people within her community and provide assistance where it could make a difference.

She explained that children should be encouraged to pursue their education under conditions that promote concentration, dignity and academic achievement.

The Bong County Land Administrator also emphasized the importance of individuals taking practical steps to address community challenges instead of relying exclusively on government institutions. She expressed hope that her intervention would encourage other prominent citizens, businesspeople and organizations to identify pressing needs within their communities and contribute toward addressing them.

For Chief Compound Community Public School Principal Moses Plator, the donation represents a welcome response to an issue that has remained a serious concern for the institution. Plator expressed appreciation to Cassell for recognizing the plight of the students and making their welfare part of her birthday activities.

He noted that the school’s administration has continued to face difficulties providing adequate seating for its growing population, describing the shortage as a challenge that affects both students and teachers.

The principal said the donation demonstrates that meaningful assistance to public schools does not always require large-scale projects, but can begin with individuals identifying specific problems and responding according to their abilities.

Plator said, “We want to sincerely appreciate Madam Amelia Queen Cassell for this important gesture toward our school. The fact that she decided to remember our students while celebrating her birthday means a great deal to us. We have been experiencing serious challenges with classroom furniture, and anyone who understands the situation at Chief Compound Public School will appreciate the importance of these 40 armchairs. They will provide some relief to our children and help create better conditions for learning. We are grateful that she has recognized education as something deserving of her personal attention and support.”

Plator explained that the institution’s furniture shortage has become increasingly difficult to manage because of the number of children seeking education at the school.

He said the challenge extends beyond the physical discomfort experienced by pupils, noting that inadequate seating can interfere with classroom organization and make it difficult for teachers to maintain an effective instructional environment.

According to him, a child who spends several hours sitting on an uncomfortable surface may struggle to concentrate fully on lessons, while teachers must devote additional attention to managing seating arrangements instead of focusing entirely on instruction.

He stressed that the donation should serve as a reminder to county authorities, educational stakeholders and other concerned citizens that improving public education requires consistent attention to the basic needs of students.

The principal further observed that the school’s location in central Gbarnga should make it easier for concerned individuals and institutions to witness its difficulties firsthand.

He expressed hope that the recent public attention surrounding the furniture shortage, together with Cassell’s intervention, would encourage broader efforts to improve conditions at the institution.

“Our school is situated right here in Gbarnga, the capital of Bong County, where government officials, education authorities and many prominent citizens are carrying out their responsibilities every day. Yet, we are still struggling to provide enough chairs for our children. Madam Cassell has taken an important step, and we appreciate her for that. However, the need remains enormous, and we are appealing to other well-meaning individuals to follow her example. We want a situation where every child who comes to Chief Compound Public School can enter the classroom and find a proper place to sit and learn. Education is everybody’s responsibility, and we believe that with collective support, these challenges can be addressed,” Plator said in a second proposed quotation requiring verification.

Beyond the school compound, Cassell extended her birthday outreach to elderly women at the Gbarnga Sunday Market, where she distributed several pieces of traditional lappers.

The beneficiaries included women who depend on selling greens, vegetables and other locally produced agricultural commodities to generate income for their households.

Cassell acknowledged the difficult circumstances under which many elderly market women operate, noting that some spend long hours at the market despite their advanced ages and limited financial resources.

She said their contributions to family welfare and the local economy deserve greater recognition and support. The women welcomed the assistance and expressed appreciation for being included in the birthday activities.

They described the gesture as a demonstration of concern for ordinary people whose daily struggles often receive limited public attention. Meanwhile, the challenges confronting Chief Compound Community Public School remain far from resolved.

World.title: Liberia: Agriculture Minister Unveils US$370 Million Investment Portfolio in Rome, Rallies Global Investors to Boost Food Production
World.content:
Rome, Italy– Agriculture Minister Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah has unveiled a US$370 million agricultural investment portfolio at the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Hand-in-Hand Investment Forum in Rome, rallying international investors, development finance institutions and agribusiness leaders to support Liberia’s drive to boost domestic food production, reduce import dependence and create thousands of jobs.

By Augustus D.R [email protected]

Minister Nuetah, accompanied by a high-level Liberian delegation, is attending the 2026 World Food Forum, being held from October 8–16 at FAO headquarters under the theme, “Innovate Today. Nourish Tomorrow.”



The gathering brings together government leaders, investors and development partners to advance agricultural investment, innovation and global food security.

Presenting Liberia’s investment opportunities on Wednesday, October 14, under the theme, “Liberia: From Import Dependence to Food Self-Sufficiency,” Minister Nuetah outlined four priority investment areas: US$243 million for rice, US$70 million for cocoa, US$32 million for cassava and US$25 million for maize.

“Liberia should not remain a country with abundant agricultural potential that depends heavily on imported food. We must turn our land and natural agricultural endowment into food, wealth, employment and prosperity,” the Minister declared.

Rice accounts for the largest share of the proposed investments, reflecting the Government’s determination to reduce import dependence. Domestic production currently meets only 35 to 40 percent of national demand, while rice imports exceeded US$75 million during the first half of 2026.

With more than 600,000 hectares of potentially irrigable land, Minister Nuetah highlighted opportunities to invest in irrigation, mechanized production, modern milling facilities, and market development.

“Our ambition is not simply to grow more rice. It is to build a competitive domestic industry that serves not just Liberian consumers but continental Africa and the rest of the world,” he emphasized.

The Minister also highlighted opportunities in cassava processing for industrial starch and animal feed, cocoa production and value addition, and maize cultivation to support Liberia’s poultry and livestock industries.

The four investment opportunities are projected to benefit about 23,900 people directly and 119,700 indirectly, creating jobs, expanding markets, and improving livelihoods, particularly for smallholder farmers, women, and young people.

With agriculture contributing approximately 29 to 34 percent of Liberia’s GDP and employing more than 60 percent of the workforce, Minister Nuetah stressed the importance of private investment in unlocking the sector’s largely untapped potential.

He assured prospective investors of the Government’s commitment to facilitating investment through One-Stop-Shop services, investment incentives, agro-industrial processing zones and duty-free provisions for eligible agricultural machinery and inputs.

“Capital does not move on ambition alone. Investors need credible information, sound project preparation, clear implementation arrangements and a supportive policy environment.

The Government of Liberia(GoL) is committed to providing these,” he stated.

Concluding his investment presentation, Minister Nuetah invited international investors, financial institutions and development partners to engage directly with the Liberian delegation and explore opportunities to transform the proposals into concrete investments.

“Let us move from agricultural potential to productive investment. From import dependence to food self-sufficiency. And from underused resources to a prosperous, resilient and inclusive agricultural economy,” he urged.

The Minister thanked FAO for providing a platform to connect Liberia’s agricultural priorities with international financing, expertise, and commercial partnerships.

In a related engagement earlier in the day, Minister Nuetah participated in a high-level panel discussion titled “From Bean to Bar: Ensuring Chocolate’s Value Reaches Cocoa Farmers,” alongside senior representatives of the Democratic Republic of Congo, European Investment Bank, African Development Bank and global chocolate manufacturer Ferrero.

The discussion examined how cocoa-producing countries can secure greater benefits from the global chocolate industry through improved farmer incomes, stronger market access, sustainable production and increased investment in processing and value addition.

For Liberia, the engagement highlighted the country’s growing potential as an emerging cocoa producer in West Africa and the importance of attracting private investment in processing, aggregation, storage, and marketing to strengthen competitiveness in international markets.

The discussion also reinforced Liberia’s US$70 million cocoa investment proposal, which seeks to expand production, promote value addition and improve market opportunities for more than 40,000 smallholder cocoa farmers.

World.title: Government calls for restoration of ecosystems
World.content:
Government has called for community involvement in the protection and restoration of critical ecosystems.

‎Isoka District Administrative Officer, Sarah Sooli says all environmental conservation efforts must take into account the livelihood needs of people who depend on the same natural resources for survival.

‎Ms Sooli notes that local communities should be involved in identifying environmental challenges and developing practical solutions, stating that their participation is essential to the success and sustainability of conservation initiatives.

‎The District Administrative Officer said this during the Global Environment Facility (GEF-9) Scoping Mission for Muchinga Province, held at Isoka Town Council Chamber.

‎The meeting was aimed at developing a funding proposal for the restoration and protection of critical ecosystems within the Upper Luangwa catchment.

‎Ms Sooli said stakeholders need to understand the circumstances that drive communities into activities that contribute to environmental degradation and work together to identify sustainable alternatives.

‎She cited charcoal production as an example of an activity that, despite putting pressure on forests, provided an income for some households.

‎“We need to work closely with our communities and understand the challenges they face. If people depend on activities such as charcoal burning to support their families, we must explore sustainable alternatives that protect the environment while also addressing their livelihood needs,” she said.

‎Ms Sooli said government departments, traditional leaders and other stakeholders should collaborate in promoting environmental awareness and supporting communities to adopt practices that would protect natural resources without undermining their livelihoods.

‎Meanwhile, GEF-9 Scoping Mission Consultant, Royd Vinya, said agricultural expansion, infrastructure development, population growth and the production of charcoal and timber were among the major drivers of environmental degradation in Muchinga Province.

‎Professor Vinya said the increasing demand for agricultural land was contributing to forest loss, soil erosion and habitat destruction, while agricultural chemicals are finding their way into water systems and negatively affecting aquatic life.

‎He said Isoka’s agricultural activities need to be managed sustainably to prevent continued forest clearance and damage to surrounding ecosystems.

‎“People must survive. The charcoal producers have responded by producing charcoal because they must feed their children. We must understand that they are also trying to make a living,” Professor Vinya said.

‎He said the proposed intervention should therefore address the underlying causes of environmental degradation by promoting sustainable land management, restoring degraded areas and conserving biodiversity.

‎Professor Vinya explained that the Upper Luangwa catchment was an important biodiversity area supporting various plant and animal species, wetlands and other critical ecosystems, but continued pressure from human activities threatened its long-term sustainability.

‎He said the proposed project would focus on biodiversity conservation, sustainable land management and restoration, as well as reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

‎Professor Vinya added that the ultimate goal was to ensure communities could continue benefiting from natural resources while maintaining the ecological systems that support agriculture, water resources and other livelihoods.

‎And Ministry of Green Economy and Environment Senior Environmental Management Officer, Mirriam Mbewe, said Zambia is eligible to access funding from the Global Environment Facility because the country was part of several international environmental agreements supported by the facility.

‎Ms Mbewe, who represented the GEFs Operational Focal Point person said the facility provided financial support to developing countries to address global environmental challenges, including biodiversity loss, land degradation and climate change.

‎She said the funding framework also supported initiatives in chemicals and waste management, international waters and integrated programmes that linked environmental protection with sustainable livelihoods.

‎Ms Mbewe said the scoping mission was an important step towards identifying environmental priorities and shaping a funding proposal that aligned local needs with the GEF’s strategic areas of support.

‎She added that Zambia had implemented 30 regional, sub-regional and global projects since the facility was established, demonstrating the country’s engagement with GEF-supported environmental initiatives.

World.title: North-Western holds 16 Days of Activism against GBV preparatory meeting
World.content:
North-Western Province Senior Gender Officer in Charge of Gender Rights Protection, Leah Chivube, has commended the steady increase in the number of boys and men reporting Gender-Based Violence (GBV) cases in the country.

In an interview with ZANIS News today following the first preparatory meeting for the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, Ms Chivube said deliberate activities have been lined up to raise awareness of GBV among men.

Ms Chivube said the activities will be held ahead of the official launch and will include the commemoration of International Men’s Day on November 19.

“We have lined up activities prior to the actual launch, which include the commemoration of International Men’s Day on the 19th of November,” Ms Chivube said.

She said police statistics on the number of men reporting GBV cases showed that more men could come forward if they were provided with the right information and a safe environment in which to report their experiences.

“As a committee, we will have sporting activities such as soccer, chess and a match to commemorate International Men’s Day because we want to honour and appreciate their efforts,” Ms Chivube said.

She said the activities would also encourage men to report any form of GBV they might be experiencing.

Meanwhile, Ms Chivube disclosed that the committee planned to host a fundraising event, with proceeds going towards supporting GBV survivors.

She said the provincial theme for the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence was “Unite to End Gender-Based Violence, Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity,” which had been derived from the international theme.

World.title: Women cooperatives urged to venture in value addition
World.content:
Chilanga Acting District Commissioner, Maureen Chilende, has urged women cooperatives to venture into value addition in order to grow their agricultural enterprise projects.

Ms Chilende says the agricultural sector has huge potential to contribute to the economic development of the country through value addition and access to markets.

She said this when she officiated at the Agape Women’s Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society 25 years Silver Jubilee celebration held in Chilanga today.

Ms Chilende has noted that value addition will enable cooperatives to earn more income, extend shelf life of their products and compete favorably on both local and regional markets.

“I urge the community to support locally produced products. When we buy local merchandise, we support local businesses, create opportunities and contribute to community development,” said Ms Chilende.

She has further encouraged the Women’s Cooperative to practice transparency and accountability and maintain proper records and invest in sustainable income generating activities.

Ms Chilende has observed that good governance within cooperatives is key to attracting partnerships and growing their businesses.

“I therefore encourage Agape Women’s Multi-Purpose Cooperative to continue building partnerships that can strengthen its business operations and expand its impact,” she said.

And Chilanga District Small and Medium Enterprises Development Officer, Eugene Maliwa, has urged cooperatives to generate income from various businesses and run their cooperatives without waiting for government grants.

Mr Maliwa has reaffirmed Government’s commitment to guide and support local cooperatives in growing their businesses.

He has indicated that cooperatives that diversify their income sources and embrace entrepreneurship are more resilient and sustainable in the long term.

World.title: ZRA calls for stronger international cooperation in tax administration
World.content:
Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) Commissioner General, Dingani Banda, has called for stronger international cooperation among tax administrations to address increasingly complex transactions, rising taxpayer expectations and other emerging challenges in revenue collection.

In a speech read on his behalf by Acting ZRA Commissioner General, Ernest Sigande, at a reception hosted by the British High Commission in Zambia, Rebecca Terzeon, for participants in the Commonwealth Association of Tax Administrators (CATA) Senior Leadership Programme, the commissioner said partnerships were essential to strengthening tax administration.

“Addressing these challenges requires not only strong institutions, but also cooperation, trust and a willingness to learn from one another,” Mr Banda said.

The remarks were made as Zambia hosts the first phase of the 2026/2027 Commonwealth Association of Tax Administrators (CATA) Senior Leadership Programme, which has brought together 28 delegates representing 20 tax administrations across 20 countries.

The Commissioner General said the programme provided an opportunity for tax officials from different jurisdictions to exchange experiences and strengthen professional relationships to support improved tax administration.

Mr Banda also highlighted the longstanding cooperation between Zambia, the United Kingdom and CATA, noting that continued support and shared learning in tax administration and capacity development had strengthened institutions and enhanced their ability to deliver on their mandates.

He urged participants to use the programme to build relationships and share experiences that would continue to benefit their respective tax administrations beyond the training period.

The Commissioner General thanked the British High Commissioner for hosting the reception and reaffirmed the importance of sustained collaboration in strengthening tax administration across participating countries.

Speaking earlier, British High Commissioner, Rebecca Terzeon, stressed the importance of a fair and predictable tax system in ensuring businesses contribute to national resources and economic growth benefits communities across Zambia.

The High Commissioner said effective taxation and the equitable distribution of public resources were essential to ensuring that economic growth translated into job creation and support for vulnerable members of society.

“Companies to be paying taxes that are fair and predictable so that they are contributing to the resources of the country,” the High Commissioner said.

Ms Terzeon said effective economic management required not only businesses to meet their tax obligations but also the fair distribution of resources to ensure communities benefited from economic progress.

She said economic growth should create employment opportunities and improve support for vulnerable people.

Ms Terzeon encouraged participants to use the programme to build lasting professional relationships, saying the networks and friendships developed during leadership training could prove valuable long after the course ended.

The High Commissioner said such connections could enable participants to seek advice and support from one another when confronted with professional challenges or new opportunities.

World.title: Lavushimanda Presidential Irrigation Initiative Programme progressing well
World.content:
All the Presidential Irrigation Initiative Programme (PIIP) are progressing well in Lavushimanda district of Muchinga Province as four schools implementing the programme have planted their winter Maize.

District Education Board Secretary (DEBS) Beatus Nshenda says the progress in the four schools implementing the PIIP namely Lukulu Day Secondary, Salamo Day Secondary, Mununga Day Secondary and Mununga Primary school is visible with irrigation facilities working well in the planted fields.

Mr Nshenda said the one hectare piece of land at each of the implementing schools has been well secured with fences.

” As of now, all the four schools implementing the PIIP have planted the maize and are just waiting for the seed to germinate”, he said.

Mr Nshenda said the school was empowered with equipment for drilling boreholes which have been sunk and were given the farming inputs.

And Deputy Headteacher at Mununga Primary School, Mwangala Siyunyi, thanked the Government for the initiative which has also boosted knowledge on agriculture in the leaners.

Ms Siyunyi said the learners, especially those in grade four to seven, have been fully involved from the inception of the programme.

She added that the programme will allow the school to sell fresh maize within three months’ time.

“I thank the Government for this programme because we are also privileged to teach our learners real agriculture skills,” she said.

And one of the Grade Seven learners, from Mununga Primary School, Gift Mukuka said the programme has enabled her and other leaners to acquire skills on irrigation agriculture.

She stated that she will utilise the knowledge acquired in farming especially during calamities such as droughts or dry spells.

“Our teachers have taught us Irrigation agriculture skills through this project and how we can grow winter Maize,” she said.

World.title: Kabuswe’s petition case continues tomorrow
World.content:
Three witnesses have testified how some people allegedly failed to vote in Chililabombwe constituency on August 13 due to alleged violence in some polling stations.

This is in case where former Minister of Mines and Minerals Development, Paul Kabuswe, has petitioned the election of Nsofwa Lupele as Chililabombwe Member of Parliament on account of violence and corruption.

During cross examination before Kitwe High Court Judge-in – Charge, Judge Lastone Mwanaabo, Patricia, Bweupe 38 of G11 Mine Area in Chililabombwe narrated that she was viciously attacked by assailants that trailed her with her colleagues after voting.

Ms Bweupe also narrated that cadres allegedly from Mr Lupele’s camp had put logs and rocks on the road to the polling station and threatened to beat up people going to vote, a situation she alleged instilled fear into the voters who were ready to vote.

“Many people did not vote in my own home because of how badly I was beaten” She narrated.

However, in cross examination by the two respondents’ legal teams, it was established that the medical report stated that the witness had no visible injuries and appeared normal contrary to her statement which stated that she was badly injured, the disparity which she agreed to.

The legal team also established that the witnesses lied that she received medical treatment on August 13 the very day she was attacked when infect she was treated on 18th August according to the doctor’s medical report the inconsistent she admitted before court.

Another witness Peter Musonda 31, of residential area W533, Lubengele in Chililabombwe also narrated that he was attacked by unidentified people after delivering food to the UPND Polling Staff at Chitobaula Polling Station.

Mr Musonda said he would love to see the results nullified as the elections in the constituency were not fair as other people were scared to go and vote after he was beaten.

However, during cross examination, Mr Musonda’s witness statement differed from the doctor’s report where he said he was badly injured and the body parts that were affected and treated as the doctor’s statement showed that he was normal and was not treated for some injuries he stated in his statement.

The respondents’ legal team also wondered why he only went to the hospital for treatment on 18th August after obtaining a police report on August 13, an action which was common among all the four witnesses examined so far.

In this case, Mr Kabuswe sued Mr Lupele as first respondent and the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) as second respondent.

Trial continues tomorrow.

World.title: Government urged to continue upholding the Rule of Law
World.content:
Governance Activist and Political Commentator Sam Zulu has called on the government to continue to uphold the rule of law.

Mr Zulu urged the government to strengthen the rule of law, protect democratic institutions and promote national unity.

Mr Zulu said the government’s commitment to peace, stability and the rule of law is important for economic growth, adding that investors, farmers and small businesses need a safe and fair environment to operate and expand Zambia’s economy.

He stressed that the government’s commitment must be demonstrated through equal application of the law, regardless of political affiliation.

He further said independent institutions such as the Judiciary, Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) and the Human Rights Commission (HRC) should operate without political interference.

Mr Zulu advised that arrests and prosecution must be based on evidence and due process, with citizens’ rights to fair trials, bails and legal representation respected.

He has encouraged the general public to maintain peace and political stability by resolving disputes through dialogue and courts rather than violence, hate speech and misinformation.

“Politicians, traditional leaders, churches and civil society organisations also have a responsibility to promote national unity and condemn violence among their supporters”, he said.

Meanwhile, Mr Zulu has also commended Zambia on its election to the United Nations Human Rights Council for the 2027-2029 term, adding that the development as a significant milestone that will raise the country’s international profile while placing greater responsibility on Zambia to protect human rights.

“Zambia should demonstrate its commitment by protecting freedom of expression, assembly, association and the media as well as strengthening institutions that citizen’s access justice,” he added.

He further said the country should cooperate with the United Nations Human Rights mechanisms and implement recommendations aimed at protecting vulnerable groups including women, children and persons with disabilities.

Mr Zulu has since called for peace, national unity, respect for human rights and rule of law for Zambia’s sustainable development and shared future.

World.title: Chitambo MP calls for increased private sector participation
World.content:
Chitambo Constituency Member of Parliament, Nelson Kabanda, has called for national unity and increased private sector participation in achieving the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Mr Kabanda notes that the government has made progress in restoring macro-economic stability and strengthening economic resilience despite global conflicts and severe droughts.

He says the Grow Zambia Agenda, which seeks to double the size of the economy, create jobs and expand business opportunities, required collective efforts from government, the private sector and citizens.

Speaking to the Motion of Thanks in parliament today, Mr Kabanda submitted that Chitambo is ready to contribute to the national development agenda through agriculture, livestock production and mining.

He however, urged the government to ensure that farmers received agricultural inputs, particularly fertiliser, on time to enable them to increase production to contribute meaningfully to national food security.

On livestock, the lawmaker said Chitambo is poised to contribute to the government’s target of earning 1U$D billion annually from beef exports and expanding the national cattle population.

Mr Kabanda also disclosed that Chitambo had mineral potential, including gold, manganese and copper, which could contribute to economic growth and employment creation.

He urged the government to streamline the issuance of mining licenses and accelerate the formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining activities to enable local people, particularly young people, to participate in the sector.

Meanwhile, Senga Hill constituency legislator Mukwavic Sichula called on the government to prioritise rural development by investing in roads, clean water, health facilities, skills training and other essential services.

Mr Sichula noted that the area still lacked a district administration block, good township roads, piped water and a skills training college to unlock the constituency’s economic potential.

He contributed to the debate on the Motion of Thanks delivered by President Hakainde Hichilema last week to the First Session of the 14th National Assembly, that improved road infrastructure would enable farmers to increase production and contribute to national economic growth, while access to clean water would help children remain in school.

Mr Sichula revealed that out of 2,000 hectares allocated for agriculture in Senga Hill, only 150 hectares were being utilised.

He expressed optimism that the government’s commitment to improving agricultural markets would benefit farmers, who depend on farming for their livelihoods.

Mr Sichula stressed that rural communities deserved an equitable share of national development, adding that improved access to basic services would enhance productivity and living standards.

World.title: Africa: New TB Vaccines Could Save Millions, but Africa Must Prepare Now
World.content:
interview

More than a century after the BCG vaccine was licensed, new tuberculosis vaccines could arrive in 2029. Gavi says the groundwork has to start now.

TB remains one of the world's deadliest infectious diseases, causing around 1.2 million deaths every year - equivalent to roughly one death every 26 seconds. Africa still records the highest rates of cases and deaths of any region. The burden remains substantial despite progress in diagnosis, treatment and prevention.

For more than 100 years, the only licensed defence has been the Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine.

But now, a new generation of vaccines could offer a major breakthrough in the fight against the disease, potentially saving 7.3 million lives between 2030 and 2050, according to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance. The opportunity, however, will depend on more than scientific progress. This will include ensuring that vaccines reach the countries and communities that need them most, which will require early planning, sufficient manufacturing capacity, sustainable financing and equitable access.

The next-generation TB vaccines will potentially become available from 2029. Gavi is urging governments and global health partners to prepare now, before the first products are approved.

Closing the gaps in TB prevention

Africa has made significant progress in expanding access to diagnosis, treatment and prevention. However, significant gaps remain, with many people diagnosed late or not at all, while others struggle to access treatment.

Emily Kobayashi, Director of Vaccine Programmes at Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, said these gaps allow TB to continue spreading within communities, particularly among people living in poverty, overcrowded environments and areas with fragile health systems.

"Too many people with TB are diagnosed too late, or not at all, and others fail to access treatment," she said.

Closing those gaps, Kobayashi said, will take both stronger delivery of proven interventions and new tools. She said that the existing BCG vaccine remains vital in protecting infants and young children against severe forms of TB. However, it has limited impact on pulmonary TB in adolescents and adults, who account for most TB transmission.

"New vaccine candidates are being developed specifically to address this gap," she said. "If successful, they could represent the first major breakthrough in TB prevention in more than a century."

She said that the vaccines could offer a real opportunity to dramatically reduce transmission, save millions of lives and accelerate progress towards ending one of the world's deadliest infectious diseases.

Next-generation vaccines, if proven safe and effective, could complement existing prevention, diagnosis and treatment efforts by reducing the number of people who develop infectious TB.

"Next-generation TB vaccines can help to further bend the curve, meaningfully reducing the number of people getting sick with TB," she said. "In practical terms, it means millions of families being spared the devastating consequences of TB, with fewer parents, teenagers and breadwinners becoming seriously ill or dying from a disease that remains one of the world's leading infectious killers."

GAVI Emily Kobayashi, Director of Vaccine Programmes at Gavi.

For countries with a high TB burden, she said, a successful vaccine could also reduce pressure on health systems, lower treatment costs and boost economic productivity by helping adolescents and adults stay healthy during their most productive years. However, Kobayashi cautioned that the ultimate impact would depend on the characteristics of the vaccines approved and how quickly countries could introduce them.

She said the projected 7.3 million lives saved highlights why new TB vaccines are considered one of the most significant public health opportunities in decades.

Preparing for demand and securing supply

For Africa, where TB continues to cause significant illness and death, the question is not only whether new vaccines will work, but whether they will be accessible and affordable when they become available.

Kobayashi said that figure shows where the new vaccines must be prioritised. "The greatest health impact will come from reaching the communities where the disease continues to cause the most illness and death," she said.

That is why Gavi's focus from the outset has been on readiness. If a vaccine is successfully developed and approved, the countries carrying the heaviest burden need to be able to access and introduce it as quickly as possible. "Working with governments and partners," she said, "we want those most affected by TB to benefit first."

Gavi's Early Market Shaping Roadmap for Novel TB Vaccines suggests demand could average 86 million vaccination courses a year, with high-burden countries needing substantial supplies during the initial rollout.

The roadmap estimates that global demand could average 86 million vaccination courses annually. The vaccines could also generate up to US$135 billion in economic benefits for low- and middle-income countries, according to Gavi analysis.

One of the principal risks, said Kobayashi, is uncertainty over future demand. Manufacturers must be confident that sufficient demand will exist to justify investing in production capacity before a vaccine receives regulatory approval.

Manufacturers need confidence that there will be sufficient demand for the vaccine to justify investments in production capacity before a vaccine is licensed. Without that confidence, there is a risk that supply may not increase quickly enough to roll out the vaccine broadly after the evidence comes from the ongoing trials. That is why early planning is so important, she said. Working with countries, manufacturers and partners to describe future demand and likely introduction timelines, which she said can help reduce uncertainty and encourage investments that then support adequate supply.

Between now and 2029, Kobayashi said, several things must happen in parallel.

First, vaccine candidates must successfully complete clinical trials and demonstrate that they are safe and effective. At the same time, country governments, manufacturers and global health partners need to prepare for widespread access to the vaccine. This includes understanding future demand for the vaccine, planning how it will be delivered to communities, assessing manufacturing needs, developing policy recommendations and ensuring financing is available the moment a vaccine is licensed.

Simi Vijay/WHO Low funding, COVID-19 curtail tuberculosis fight in Africa.

"The key lesson from previous vaccine introductions is that preparation cannot start after approval," she said. "It needs to begin well in advance."

Kobayashi pointed to the malaria vaccine rollout as an example of how early coordination among partners can support rapid scale-up, with preparations taking place while vaccines were still undergoing trials. It resulted in one of the fastest rollouts in Gavi's history.

For African countries, this means considering how potential vaccines would be integrated into existing immunisation and TB programmes, which populations should be prioritised and what resources would be needed to deliver doses effectively.

Beyond preventing illness and death, next-generation TB vaccines could also contribute to efforts to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR), including drug-resistant TB.

Drug-resistant TB is one of the most challenging forms of the disease because it is difficult, lengthy and expensive to treat. It can take a significant toll on individuals and families, often requiring prolonged treatment and time away from work or school. By preventing TB disease in the first place, she said, vaccines can reduce the number of people requiring treatment and help limit opportunities for drug resistance to develop or spread.

Kobayashi said that is why vaccination is increasingly recognised as an important part of the broader response to AMR alongside diagnosis, treatment and infection control. Vaccines can help reduce reliance on antibiotics and contribute to long-term efforts to combat AMR.

Making sure access is equitable

The risk with any new vaccine is that it reaches wealthier or lower-risk populations first. Gavi said its focus is on the countries with the highest TB burden, most of which are low- and middle-income.

Drawing on more than two decades of experience supporting vaccine introductions and shaping vaccine markets, she said the goal is "to help ensure that public health need drives access." If a new vaccine becomes available, she added, the countries hardest hit "should be among the first to benefit."

Why now?

Kobayashi said the urgency of preparing for new TB vaccines was underscored by the continuing toll of the disease, which claims around 1.2 million lives globally each year. Africa bears a disproportionate share of the burden, with the region continuing to face high rates of TB cases and deaths despite progress in prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

At the same time, she said, the world was closer than it had been in decades to developing a new vaccine that could protect the communities most affected by TB and responsible for much of its transmission.

"This combination of urgent need and scientific progress makes now the moment to start preparing," said Kobayashi.

She warned that the decisions made before the vaccines become available, including forecasting demand, planning delivery strategies and ensuring adequate supply, would help determine how rapidly people will benefit from these vaccines and how much impact they can ultimately have on reducing the global burden of TB.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 15, 2026
World.content:
Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case Linked to First Patient

Kenya has confirmed a second Ebola case, 10 days after a 40-year-old man died from the virus following travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) through Uganda. The new patient, a 39-year-old close relative of the first victim, was already in quarantine when he developed symptoms. The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks. Health officials said that both cases are linked, with no evidence of wider community transmission. Authorities have traced 128 contacts of the first patient, 113 of whom are in quarantine. Efforts to find the remaining contacts continue. Kenya has maintained that travel, trade and public gatherings remain unrestricted. More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Mauritius Imposes Curfew After Violent Protests

Mauritius has imposed an overnight curfew following violent protests over water shortages and the rising cost of living, marking the island's worst unrest in decades. Demonstrations escalated after a woman was shot and injured by police at a roadblock. The circumstances of the shooting were not clear, but the officer has since been arrested and remanded in custody. Protesters burned tyres, blocked roads and vandalised police stations and public infrastructure, prompting school and public transport closures. Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam warned that those responsible would face consequences. Police reported some overnight incidents and arrests. Analysts warn that unrest could return if water shortages persist until the rainy season in December.

Sudan's War Deepens Humanitarian and Food Crisis

Fighting between Sudan's Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has intensified in North Kordofan and parts of Blue Nile state. The fighting has forced thousands of civilians to flee amid the planting season. The conflict, which began in April 2023, has displaced more than 12.4 million people and left an estimated 24.6 million facing acute food insecurity. Aid organisations warn that hundreds of thousands of young children are suffering severe malnutrition. Drought, flooding, fuel shortages and declining fertiliser supplies are worsening food production and prices. The UN's 2026 humanitarian response plan, requiring US$2.9 billion, is only 41% funded. Observers also warn that continued arms supplies and drone attacks are prolonging the conflict and increasing civilian casualties.

Amnesty Warns of Continued Abuses in Mali Despite Wagner's Replacement

Amnesty International has warned that serious human rights abuses against civilians in Mali continue despite the Russian-backed Africa Corps replacing the Wagner Group in supporting Malian military operations. The organisation documented seven incidents between 2023 and 2025 in which 34 civilians were allegedly deliberately killed, alongside torture, sexual violence, arbitrary detention, looting and destruction of property. Members of Fulani, Tuareg and Arab communities along the Mauritanian border were among those most affected. Amnesty also cited allegations of abuses by Africa Corps members, including a July 2026 raid in Bombori in which six people were reportedly shot dead and three others executed. It called for independent investigations to hold accountable those suspected of war crimes and for greater protection for civilians.

DR Congo Cholera Cases Surge Amid Ebola Outbreak

The World Health Organisation has said that from January 2025 to the end of September 2026, there were more than 125,000 suspected cases of cholera and 3,644 suspected deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In 2026, there were more than 51,400 suspected cases and 1,487 deaths in 21 provinces. Most of the cases were in South Kivu, North Kivu, and Haut-Katanga, which together made up almost 60% of the cases. Response efforts are being hampered by a lack of clean water and toilets, as well as by safety concerns and problems getting to remote communities. Health authorities are expanding water chlorination, household disinfection and vaccination preparations, including a planned cross-border campaign with the Republic of Congo. The crisis comes as the DR Congo continues to battle Ebola, with neighbouring Kenya recently confirming a second case linked to the outbreak.

Close 

Foot-and-Mouth Restrictions Push Up Meat Prices in Namibia

Foot-and-mouth disease restrictions in Namibia are causing meat shortages and price increases at butcheries and restaurants as limits on livestock sales and slaughtering disrupt supplies. Butchers report rising costs for meat trimmings and cheaper cuts traditionally used to make mince and sausages, forcing some businesses to switch to more expensive cuts and raise prices. Restaurants have also increased prices for selected dishes, including rump, sirloin and T-bone steaks. Others are absorbing higher supplier costs to avoid passing them on to customers. Some small businesses say they cannot obtain livestock at all, threatening their ability to operate. The disease has spread to 17 farms in the ||Kharas region. Positive cases have also been reported in the Zambezi region.

World.title: Jerry Seinfeld turns tables on radical anti-Israel agitators after chaotic Chicago stunt backfires
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Comedian Jerry Seinfeld turned the tables on anti-Israel hecklers who attempted to derail his Chicago performance last Friday, mocking the protesters as security removed them from the venue.

Viral video from the confrontation shows activists shouting at Seinfeld at the Chicago Theatre, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" in Gaza and alleging that American taxpayer dollars are funding the deaths of thousands of civilians.

"Twenty-two thousand Palestinians who are children now are killed with our taxpayer money, and you’re making jokes!" a woman shouted in clips posted online.

JERRY SEINFELD GIVES BLUNT THREE-WORD RESPONSE TO INFLUENCER ASKING FOR A 'FREE PALESTINE'

Seinfeld then dances on stage and mocks the protesters with sarcastic remarks, calling himself "racist" and saying, "It’s a genocide. I’m into it." He also joked that he would find out how much the protesters paid for their tickets and send the money directly to Israel.

As security personnel escorted the demonstrators out of the auditorium, one audience member shouted, "Rough her up!"

The Anti-War Committee Chicago and the Chicago branch of the US Palestinian Community Network have taken credit for organizing the disruption, writing on Instagram, "Friday’s disruption sent a clear message: Those who defend Israel’s genocide and ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in Gaza and throughout Palestine will be met with protest and are not welcome on Chicago’s stages without opposition."

COMEDIAN DECLARES JERRY SEINFELD 'UNCANCELLABLE' DESPITE 'WOKE' ANTI-ISRAEL FESTIVAL BOYCOTT

Fox News Digital reached out to Seinfeld’s team for comment but did not hear back.

The altercation is the latest in a string of protests targeting the 72-year-old Jewish comedian over his staunch defense of Israel.

ANTI-ISRAEL PROTESTERS LABEL MAMDANI A 'TRAITOR,' ACCUSE HIM OF 'GENOCIDE' OUTSIDE OCT 7 VIGIL

Comedian and media analyst Tim Young told Fox News Digital he believes protesters are paying top dollar to hijack comedy shows for viral attention rather than political discourse.

"They know that once they start yelling, everyone will whip their cameras out, and it is a very direct interaction and maybe one of the only direct interactions protesters get to have with celebrities and with the internet," Young said.

"If you are in a very intimate environment where everyone is quiet, listening to one person, you will be heard. And, so, that's what they're taking advantage of here."

Young compared the disruptions at Seinfeld's shows to protests at political rallies, arguing that some activists are willing to pay steep ticket prices to confront the comedian.

"It seems like people are going to Jerry Seinfeld's shows like they're going to a Trump rally to protest," Young said. "They wanted to get Jerry's attention. They want to, for some reason, they're very, very adamant on getting him to react to the Israel-Palestine conflict."

Young also linked the disruptions to Seinfeld's past criticism of performing at universities.

30% OF COLLEGE STUDENTS SAY VIOLENCE ACCEPTABLE WAY TO STOP SPEAKERS ON CAMPUSES, SURVEY FINDS

"It's why Jerry doesn't like to go and perform at college campuses. And he said he hates performing at college campuses specifically for that reason," Young said.

"He doesn't want to get into the political thing. He doesn't want to have protesters yelling back and forth with him. It's a waste of the rest of the audience's time, and he knows that."

In May 2024, dozens of students walked out during Seinfeld's commencement address at Duke University, some holding Palestinian flags.

Seinfeld returned to the university in September 2025 to introduce freed Israeli hostage Omer Shem Tov at a campus event, where he addressed anti-Israel protests, saying, "Free Palestine is, to me, just — you’re free to say you don’t like Jews. Just say you don’t like Jews."

QUIET PART OUT LOUD: ANTI-ISRAEL MOBS WANT ONE STATE CALLED 'PALESTINE,' ERASING ISRAEL

"By saying ‘Free Palestine,’ you’re not admitting what you really think," he said. "So, it’s actually — compared to the Ku Klux Klan, I’m actually thinking the Klan is actually a little better here because they can come right out and say, ‘We don’t like Blacks, we don’t like Jews.’ OK, that’s honest."

Seinfeld also faced controversy overseas last month when several European acts withdrew from the inaugural MEO Commedia a La Carte Fest in Lisbon, Portugal, where he is scheduled to headline later this year.

The acts did not name Seinfeld directly in their withdrawal statements, but some cited concerns about the Israel-Gaza conflict. One performer said someone involved in the festival defended ideas they considered indefensible.

Young, who previously dismissed efforts to cancel Seinfeld over his support for Israel, argued that protesters target the billionaire comedian because of his influence and celebrity status.

"This is all about control. It's all about power. And it's all about the left having power over these very influential and powerful people," Young said. "And they’re not having it."

World.title: Autistic teen lured to fake Snapchat meetup, brutally beaten by group of teens: report
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Three teenage boys have been charged after a 15-year-old boy with autism was beaten and robbed near a train station in Australia, with video capturing the violent attack as other teenagers watched.

The assault happened Oct. 5 in Stawell, a town in the Australian state of Victoria, after the victim was reportedly lured to the area through a Snapchat meetup arranged with two girls, according to Australian news outlet news.com.au.

Video of the attack shows several teenagers punching and kicking the boy, knocking him to the ground and repeatedly striking him as he attempts to get away. One attacker demands the victim hand over his shoes before the group allows him to leave.

TEXAS TEENS ACCUSED OF USING DATING APPS TO LURE YOUNG MEN INTO VIOLENT ROBBERIES THAT LEFT ONE VICTIM SHOT

Victoria Police announced Tuesday that detectives had charged three boys, ages 14, 15 and 15, following an investigation into the assault.

Detectives from the Northern Grampians Crime Investigation Unit executed four search warrants in the region before arresting the teenagers, police said.

All three face charges of affray, robbery, recklessly causing injury and theft. They are expected to appear in a children's court at a later date.

TEEN BURGLARY RING LINKED TO NEARLY 80 BAY AREA BREAK-INS DISMANTLED AFTER MONTHS-LONG INVESTIGATION: PD

Police said a fourth boy who was not present during the search warrants would be interviewed as part of the ongoing investigation.

The victim, who also has epilepsy, suffered soft tissue injuries and possible head injuries, according to news.com.au. His mother told the outlet that doctors were conducting additional scans to determine whether he had bleeding in his brain.

"I’m just lucky to have him alive … he’s having nightmares," she said.

TEEN PUNCHED AND KICKED INTO A COMA AFTER KNICKS-SPURS ALTERCATION NEAR MADISON SQUARE GARDEN: POLICE

The boy has since returned home but is afraid to go outside, his mother told the outlet.

Superintendent Dan Davison acknowledged the concern the attack had caused in the Stawell community and said police had been working to identify those responsible.

"Since last Monday, local uniform police and detectives have been working tirelessly to identify those involved and hold them to account, and this important work will continue," Davison said in a news release.

"There is never any excuse for violence in our community, and we will not accept it in any form."

"Detectives are continuing to investigate the matter and while we are treating it as an isolated incident, additional patrols will take place across Stawell to ensure our community not only is safe but feels safe," he added.

Police said additional patrols would be deployed throughout Stawell as detectives continued investigating the assault.

World.title: TSA warns travelers about seasonal mistake that could trigger airport security delays
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Travelers planning to fly in costume this Halloween could face unexpected hurdles at airport security.

While costumes themselves are generally allowed, certain accessories, masks, special makeup and metal pieces can create problems at TSA checkpoints, according to the agency's website.

Travelers wearing elaborate face coverings or heavy costume makeup may be asked to remove it if their identity cannot be verified during screening.

POPULAR PANTRY STAPLE COULD GET YOU STOPPED AT AIRPORT SECURITY UNDER LITTLE-KNOWN TSA RULE

Keith Jeffries, vice president of K2 Security Screening Group and a former federal security director for TSA at Los Angeles International Airport, told Fox News Digital that facial recognition technology is becoming more common at airports.

"If you're wearing … Halloween costume-style makeup, and it can't recognize you, that's going to create some challenges," he said.

Costume props packed in luggage can also raise security concerns, particularly when they resemble weapons or other prohibited items.

Replica explosives, including fake bombs and grenades, are not allowed in carry-on or checked luggage, according to TSA guidance.

CLICK HERE TO 

Weapon-like props, such as fake knives, swords, guns and pitchforks, should also stay out of carry-on bags, experts say. Some may be permitted in checked luggage, depending on the item.

Jeffries recalled seeing similar issues during his 20 years with the TSA, including travelers trying to bring replicas of "Lucille," the barbed-wire-covered baseball bat featured on "The Walking Dead," through security.

"Of course, that just can't go through the checkpoint," he said, noting that it could be placed in checked luggage.

Metal-heavy costumes could create another headache by triggering screening equipment and potentially leading to additional screening, Jeffries said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"That's going to cause all kinds of challenges and just slow the whole process down," he said.

Travelers packing makeup must also follow standard TSA liquid restrictions.

Liquid makeup in carry-ons generally must be in containers of 3.4 ounces or less, while larger quantities should go into checked luggage, according to the TSA.

For travelers bringing more elaborate costumes or accessories, Jeffries recommended packing these items rather than wearing them through security.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"My biggest recommendation [is] put all of that stuff in your checked luggage, even if you normally don't like to check a bag," he said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Pack your costumes, go to where you're going and enjoy your fun," Jeffries said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the TSA for further details and comment.

CBS News is facing a defamation lawsuit as a Maryland teenager seeks $20 million in damages, claiming he was falsely identified as a person arrested for vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool’s lining.

The lawsuit, filed on Wednesday in U.S. District Court in the District of Columbia, identified the 15-year-old plaintiff simply as "JV."

"He was not arrested for vandalizing it. He was not accused by law enforcement of vandalizing it. Yet CBS News broadcast and published a story to a national audience that placed JV's image alongside the assertion that five people had been arrested for vandalizing and ‘sabotaging’ the Reflecting Pool, thereby falsely portraying JV as one of the perpetrators of a highly publicized federal crime," the lawsuit stated.

NORTH CAROLINA STUDENT WINS $95K AFTER SCHOOL ACCUSED HER OF VANDALIZING SPIRIT ROCK WITH CHARLIE KIRK TRIBUTE

"The accusation was particularly damaging because at all times material to the allegations, the Reflecting Pool renovation and subsequent alleged vandalism of the Reflecting Pool is or has been the subject of intense national attention and political controversy," the complaint continued.

"President Donald Trump frequently discusses the Reflecting Pool renovation and publicly condemned those accused of vandalism in extraordinarily harsh terms, stating that they should be ‘prosecuted to the max,’" it added.

The lawsuit states that CBS "inserted" JV into the controversy and "exposed him to extreme embarrassment, humiliation, and the public condemnation" directed at the actual vandals. The lawsuit claims JV’s presence near the Reflecting Pool "was entirely unrelated to the vandalism" and he was simply briefly detained for riding an e-bike in the area.

NEW YORK TIMES LOSES DEFAMATION SUIT, ORDERED TO PAY $9.25M TO FORMER ALABAMA BASKETBALL PLAYER

JV was released without charges and "his detention had nothing whatsoever to do with vandalism or sabotage of the Reflecting Pool."

"CBS nevertheless used video footage of JV's detention in its report about the Reflecting Pool vandalism. As CBS anchor Jericka Duncan told viewers that ‘five people have been arrested,' the video depicted JV in handcuffs," the lawsuit stated.

"In the version CBS distributed online and through social media, CBS showed JV turning toward the camera with his face fully visible as Duncan made the statement concerning the arrests and then identified one of the alleged perpetrators, David Hearn," it continued.

"The visual and verbal presentation published by Defendants unmistakably conveyed the false message that JV was among the persons arrested for vandalizing the Reflecting Pool and further confused JV with Hearn, an adult who was subsequently indicted on a felony charge arising from the vandalism," the complaint added.

JV’s legal team claimed CBS was aware that the 15-year-old was detained for the e-bike, and not vandalism, because the original video obtained by the network clearly distinguished between the two issues.

"The facts alleged herein demonstrate that CBS either knew its portrayal of JV was false or acted with reckless disregard for whether it was true," the lawsuit alleged.

"CBS compounded the harm through the manner and breadth of its publication," it continued. "Although the national television broadcast did not show JV's face, CBS's online and social-media version did. It showed his face immediately after depicting his distinctive sweatshirt and while reporting that arrests had been made. JV was readily recognized by friends and acquaintances."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The lawsuit pointed out that video of the report accumulated at least 1.8 million views on social media alone. JV’s legal team said he has faced "profound" consequences, including embarrassment, humiliation, anxiety, loss of sleep, emotional distress, friends distancing themselves and a continued "fear that CBS's false accusation will follow him through high school and affect his college admissions, athletic opportunities, employment, and future career."

The lawsuit noted that CBS issued an on-air correction but said the "belated acknowledgment … cannot undo the publication or erase its consequences."

CBS News declined comment on pending litigation.

A judge permanently dismissed the Reflecting Pool vandalism case against former Olympian David Hearn, who was accused of damaging the costly $14 million renovation project in June.
