TANZANIA · TRADE

Key Facts — The country Tanzania is an East African country whose Dar es Salaam Port serves Tanzania and landlocked neighbours such as Zambia and DR Congo.

— What happened On Wednesday 14 October the Transport Ministry’s top civil servant set a target of 1,500 rail containers a day from Dar es Salaam Port.

— The numbers About 500 a day would run on the Tazara line and up to 1,000 on a new 3.8-kilometre standard-gauge link.

— Rail now The Tazara line moves up to 100 containers a day, and two private depot operators are testing a service for about 300 a day.

— The scale The port handled about 1.34 million containers in 2025/26, so the rail target equals roughly a third of the busiest month’s daily flow.

— What it means for you Faster rail clearance could cut delays and costs on copper and cobalt shipments that pass through Dar es Salaam to world markets.

— Still open No start date, rail price list or cost has been published for the full 1,500 a day.

Tanzania has set a target of 1,500 rail containers a day out of Dar es Salaam Port, a sea gateway for East and Central Africa. Prof Godius Kahyarara, the Transport Ministry’s Permanent Secretary, told The Citizen on Wednesday 14 October that the plan uses railway lines that already exist.

For US readers, the target matters because the port serves Zambia and DR Congo, whose copper and cobalt exports feed American industry. Fewer trucks and faster clearance would cut the time and cost of moving those goods.

What the Ministry Said on 14 October

Prof Kahyarara said preparations were complete to use more rail to inland container depots, the yards where boxes are cleared. He said the aim is to cut the cost of congestion, which delays deliveries and ties up trucks.

The plan relies on lines that have been improved rather than newly built, he told The Citizen. The newspaper’s Gadiosa Lamtey reported the story on Thursday 15 October.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Tanzania Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the 1,500 Containers Add Up

Two railways make up the total of rail containers. Tazara, owned jointly by Tanzania and Zambia, could carry about 500 a day, and the state operator TRC (Tanzania Railways Corporation) up to 1,000.

The Tazara line already moves up to 100 containers a day from the port, according to the Permanent Secretary. It runs 40 kilometres to depots along Nyerere Road, in Temeke, at the airport and at Mwakanga.

Private Operators Test the Tazara Line

Bravo Logistics and African Inland Container Depot have begun trial runs using hired locomotives and wagons, with capacity for about 300 containers a day. Other depots expected to join could add another 200 a day, which brings Tazara’s potential to 500.

TRC separately runs 22 kilometres of metre-gauge track serving freight and industrial areas in Ilala, Buguruni, Mandela Road, Mabibo and Ubungo. The Permanent Secretary said the existing lines have been improved and are already operating.

The New Standard-Gauge Link to Gate 14

TRC has extended its standard-gauge railway (SGR) by 3.8 kilometres to Gate 14 of the port. The Permanent Secretary said the link allows up to 1,000 rail containers a day to travel to Kwala, Morogoro, Bahi and Isaka.

To prepare, TRC bought diesel-powered wagons for shunting and is rehabilitating 300 metre-gauge wagons. The earnings of the standard-gauge line were covered in an earlier Rio Times report on US$64 million in revenue.

Why the Port Needs the Relief

Chief Government Spokesperson Gerson Msigwa said the port handled a record 138,000 containers in July 2026, the Daily News reported. At that pace the port moves about 4,450 containers a day, so 1,500 rail containers would be about a third.

Port Director Abed Gallus Abed told The Citizen the port handled about 1.34 million containers in 2025/26. He said moving 300,000 containers to the Kwala depot would still leave more than one million to handle elsewhere.

What Industry Groups Say

Meleck Shange, chairman of the Clearing and Inland Depots Association, said truck jams at the port had fallen after recent improvements. He credited a regional commissioner’s order that no trucks may park along roadsides.

Shange said some inland depots still need upgrades because heavy truck traffic crowds nearby neighbourhoods. He added that the port is adding berths and deepening its channel so larger ships can dock.

What It Means for US Readers

Zambia and DR Congo, major copper and cobalt producers, rely on Dar es Salaam as a sea outlet. Transit cargo rose 17% to 14.61 million tonnes in 2025/26, the Daily News reported on 2 October.

The Tanzania Ports Authority (TPA), the state port owner, is building a container facility with Dubai’s DP World and East Africa Container Terminal. The Daily News reported the plan on 8 September.

The Lobito Corridor, a rail route to Angola’s Atlantic coast backed by Washington, competes for the same minerals. A faster Dar es Salaam route therefore matters for supply chains.

What Is Not Known

No date has been given for when 1,500 containers a day will run, and no rail price list has been published. The Citizen noted that the commercial benefit depends on competitive tariffs, reliable train schedules and efficient handling at the port and depots.

The cost of the Gate 14 link and the new wagons was not stated, nor how many containers TRC carries now. Tazara’s present 100 containers a day is a fifth of the 500 a day it is expected to reach.

More: Tanzania news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Tanzania’s new rail container target?

Tanzania wants 1,500 rail containers a day from Dar es Salaam Port. About 500 would run on the Tazara line and up to 1,000 on the standard-gauge railway.

Who runs the railways involved?

Tanzania Railways Corporation is the state railway operator, and Tazara is the Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority. Both lines connect the port with depots and inland destinations.

How many containers does Dar es Salaam Port handle?

The port director said it handled about 1.34 million containers in 2025/26. The government said July 2026 set a record of 138,000 containers.

Why does the port need rail?

Trucks carry most cargo out of the port and cause jams that delay deliveries and raise costs. Rail containers travel together in one train and take pressure off city roads.

Why should US companies care?

Dar es Salaam is an outlet for copper and cobalt from Zambia and DR Congo, which US industry buys. Smoother rail clearance can shorten delays on those shipments.

When will the 1,500 containers a day start?

No start date has been announced. Tazara carries up to 100 containers a day at present, and the standard-gauge line has been extended 3.8 kilometres to Gate 14 of the port.

Sources: The Citizen (Tanzania), Gadiosa Lamtey, Tanzania targets moving 1,500 containers daily on railway, 15 October 2026; Daily News (Tanzania), Dar Port handles record 138,000 containers, 24 August 2026; Daily News (Tanzania), TPA plans four-line cargo railway, 8 September 2026; Daily News (Tanzania), Dar es Salaam transit cargo rises 17%, 2 October 2026.

World.content:

GHANA · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country Ghana is a West African democracy of more than 30 million people and a major gold producer, led by President John Dramani Mahama.

— What happened On Thursday 15 October, the Ghana Statistical Service said economic activity in July grew 7.4% from July 2025.

— The numbers Services grew 12.2%, industry 5.4% and agriculture 3.7%. The activity index reached 121.6, up from 113.2 a year earlier.

— The trend Monthly growth was 4.7% in April, 6.0% in May and 6.5% in June. The Bank of Ghana put second-quarter growth at 6.0%.

— The drivers Information and communication led services, mining and quarrying led industry, and crops and livestock led agriculture, the statistics office said.

— Still open The figure is an early monthly estimate, and official third-quarter growth data has not yet been released.

The Ghana economy grew 7.4% in July from a year earlier, the Ghana Statistical Service reported on Thursday 15 October. The pace is up from 6.5% in June, driven by a 12.2% surge in services led by telecoms and internet.

For US investors, the figure shows that Ghana’s recovery after its debt default and IMF rescue is still gathering pace. It matters most to holders of the restructured dollar bonds and to US-listed energy firms.

What the Statistics Office Reported for July

The Ghana Statistical Service is the government agency that counts the Ghana economy, headed by Government Statistician Dr Alhassan Iddrisu. It published the July figure in its Monthly Indicator of Economic Growth, an early monthly gauge that arrives before official quarterly figures.

The indicator rose to 121.6 in July from 113.2 in July 2025, a gain of 7.4%. A year earlier, growth in the same month was only 4.9%, so the comparison base was low.

The release was reported on Thursday by Citi Newsroom and by MyJoyOnline, two leading Ghanaian news sites. Both gave the same sector figures and the same 7.4% headline.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Ghana Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Services Drove the Jump

Services grew 12.2% in July, against 6.7% in the same month of 2025. The largest part of the Ghana economy includes telecoms, banking, trade, transport and government, and it supplied 63.8% of the month’s growth.

Within services, information and communication was the biggest contributor, the statistics office said. That covers mobile networks, internet providers and the software and data firms that serve Ghana’s more than 30 million people.

Industry added 20.5% of the growth and agriculture 14.1%, MyJoyOnline reported. Net indirect taxes made up the remaining 1.6%.

Mining Lifts Industry While Farming Slows

Industry grew 5.4% in July, compared with just 0.4% a year earlier. Mining and quarrying provided the main push in the Ghana economy, the statistics office said, in a country that is a major gold exporter.

Agriculture slowed to 3.7% from 8.2% in July 2025, with crops and livestock the main contributors. The cooler farm figure is the weak spot in an otherwise strong month, because farming employs a large share of Ghanaians.

Citi Newsroom reported the statistics office as saying the priority is to sustain services growth while strengthening agriculture. That points to a recovery that leans heavily on one sector.

How July Compares With Earlier Months

Monthly growth was 4.7% in April, 6.0% in May and 6.5% in June, according to Ghanaian outlets reporting each release. February was stronger, at 7.7%, so July marks a return to the early-year pace.

April looked weak against a high base, since April 2025 had grown 7.4%. The central bank, led by Governor Johnson Asiama, put real growth at 6.0% in the second quarter.

The Bank of Ghana held its policy rate at 14% in September, the third straight hold this year. Headline inflation was 5.2% in September, the statistics office said on Wednesday 7 October, up from 5.0% in August.

What It Means for US Readers

Ghana finished a US$3 billion IMF loan programme in July, and the IMF’s Africa director praised that record on Thursday 15 October. Faster growth helps the government raise tax revenue and keep paying the restructured dollar bonds US funds hold.

Inflation of 5.2% sits below the central bank’s target band of 6% to 10%, which leaves room for steady policy. Ghana’s oil and gold also matter to US-listed firms such as Kosmos Energy, a partner in the Jubilee oil field.

Travellers and exporters should see little change, because the Ghana economy figure does not alter US visa, tariff or security policy. It is a signal for investors, not a trigger for new rules.

The cedi trades at about 11.69 per US dollar on 15 October, according to open exchange-rate data. Growth numbers alone rarely move a currency, and Ghana’s inflation and central bank decisions matter more.

What Is Not Known

The statistics office has not said when it will publish third-quarter GDP, the full measure of output. Monthly estimates are provisional and can change when more data arrives.

How much of the services surge came from telecoms and how much from other activities is still open. Whether mining output rose on volumes or on higher gold prices is also unclear.

The Bank of Ghana has not said how the July figure will shape its next rate decision. Its September statement called the balance of risks to inflation and growth broadly balanced.

More: Ghana news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does Ghana’s 7.4% growth figure measure?

It is the year-on-year rise in the Monthly Indicator of Economic Growth for July, compared with July 2025, and it tracks the whole Ghana economy. It is an early estimate that comes before official quarterly GDP.

Which parts of Ghana’s economy grew fastest in July?

Services grew 12.2%, led by information and communication. Industry grew 5.4% on mining, and agriculture grew 3.7%.

Is the Ghana economy growing faster than before?

July’s 7.4% beat June’s 6.5% and May’s 6.0%.

Why did Ghana’s agriculture growth slow?

Farm growth in the Ghana economy fell to 3.7% from 8.2% in July 2025, with crops and livestock still the main contributors. The statistics office did not give a reason for the slowdown.

Does the figure change anything for US investors?

It supports the view that the Ghana economy’s recovery after its debt restructuring is holding. It does not change any US rules on trade, travel or sanctions.

Sources: Citi Newsroom, 15 October 2026; MyJoyOnline, 15 October 2026; MyJoyOnline, 15 October 2026; Ghanaian Times, 10 September 2026; Ghana News Agency, 25 September 2026.

World.title: Somalia Constitution Bill Due in 2 Months
World.content:
SOMALIA · POLITICS

Key Facts — What is happening Somalia’s Council of Ministers, chaired by Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre, approved a plan on Tuesday, 13 October to implement the new constitution and gave a ministerial committee two months to draft a bill on the structure of government.

— Why it matters The bill would set the size and duties of the cabinet under the 2026 constitution, as a row over the government’s mandate continues and a deadline on dual posts has just passed.

— The numbers Two months is the drafting window, six months was the transition on dual posts that ended on 14 October, and the new law is described as the first of its kind since 1968.

— Who is who Hamza Abdi Barre is prime minister, Hassan Moalim Mohamud is the justice and constitutional affairs minister who chairs the committee, and President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s mandate is disputed by opposition figures.

— What to watch The two month drafting deadline, which ends around 13 December if counted from the cabinet meeting, a possible opposition case at the Supreme Court, and the elections set for 15 April and 15 May 2027, which the opposition rejects.

— What it means for you US travellers face no change to the Level 4 Do Not Travel advisory, and Washington’s counterterrorism partner is a government whose mandate the opposition contests, which could complicate security cooperation.

Somalia’s cabinet has given a ministerial committee two months to draft a law on how the federal government is built. The order lands as the opposition disputes the president’s mandate and a deadline on dual posts passes.

The Somalia constitution bill that the cabinet ordered on Tuesday, 13 October must be drafted within two months. It will set out the structure of the federal government, including the size and responsibilities of the cabinet, SONNA reports.

Somalia is a front-line state against the militant group al-Shabaab and a long-time security partner of Washington. How its government is organised, and for how long it governs, therefore matters well beyond Mogadishu.

What the Cabinet Decided on 13 October

SONNA, the Somali National News Agency, reported the resolution on Tuesday, 13 October. It says the Council of Ministers, the federal cabinet, met in extraordinary session that evening under Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre.

The cabinet appointed a ministerial committee, chaired by the Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, to speed up implementation of the constitution. Dawan Africa, a regional news site, adds that the committee includes the interior, finance, endowments, education and information ministers.

Within two months, the committee must draft a bill on the structure of the federal government. The government calls it the first law of its kind since 1968, SONNA says.

Dawan Africa’s account of the resolution adds a directive to all government institutions. They must ensure that administrative measures without a constitutional basis are not carried out through conflicting procedures.

The Justice Ministry and other relevant bodies must also inform the public about how implementation will proceed. A separate technical committee will help schedule and monitor priority work, though its members have not been named.

Prime Minister Hamza said the constitution is in force and is being implemented in stages, SONNA says. He added that the government is working toward federal one person, one vote elections next year.

Dawan Africa also covered a press briefing on Wednesday, 14 October by committee chair Hassan Moalim Mohamud, the justice minister. It says he described implementation as phased work that needs new laws, new institutions and changes in how government operates.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Africa politics Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the 14 October Deadline on Dual Posts Matters

The constitution took effect on 14 April 2026, the commission says, and a six-month transition ended on Wednesday, 14 October. The Independent Constitutional Review and Implementation Commission said on 7 October that it would then enforce the dual post ban.

Under the provisions the commission cited, a minister who also sits in parliament loses the cabinet seat. A lawmaker who accepts another government post loses the parliamentary seat.

The commission oversees the rollout, and chairman Burhan Aden Omar called enforcement a constitutional obligation, Dawan Africa reported. Dawan Africa said the rule could affect dozens of ministers and deputy ministers, but no official count was found.

Garowe Online, a Somali news site, said on Monday, 12 October that parliamentary leaders wanted the provisions enforced from 14 October. It added that some cabinet members from Jubaland and Puntland, two federal member states, had raised concerns.

Garowe also described open questions about how vacated seats would be filled and whether ministers could keep posts after leaving parliament. Much of its account is attributed to unnamed sources, so it is treated here as unconfirmed.

A Mandate Dispute Sits Behind the Plan

In May, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said the amended constitution gives the federal government a five-year term to 15 May 2027. Dawan Africa reported that he also said the executive and parliament would be separated and implementation had already started.

Opposition figures say his term ended on 15 May 2026, Garowe Online reported on Tuesday, 13 October. They accuse him of clinging to power and call for an inclusive electoral agreement.

The federal government is pushing a one person, one vote system, which it says lets citizens choose their own leaders. Critics, who are not named, say any process needs broad consensus to avoid deeper division.

Garowe Online reported on 12 October, citing unnamed sources, that the Supreme Court accepted an opposition lawsuit against the new constitution. The report says a senior Somali Salvation Council member filed it; accepting a case is not a ruling on the merits.

What It Means for US Readers

The US State Department rates Somalia Level 4, Do Not Travel, in an advisory issued on Thursday, 21 May 2026. Nothing in the cabinet’s decision changes that advice.

Washington has long backed Somalia’s government against al-Shabaab, and a contested political calendar can complicate that work. That is an assessment, and none of the sources describes a change in US policy.

Somalia’s finance minister, Bihi Iman Egeh, met World Bank and IMF officials in Bangkok this week, the Ministry of Finance said. The talks covered reforms and financing, and the ministry gave no figures.

Direct market exposure for US investors is minimal, so the practical stakes are security cooperation, aid and travel risk. Background on the wider region is collected in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea hub.

What Is Not Known

It is not confirmed how many officials with dual posts chose one seat on 14 October. No official count of affected officials was found, and Dawan Africa’s own totals differed between April and October.

The full text of the cabinet resolution has not been seen, and the technical committee’s members are not named. The committee chair’s estimate of how long full implementation will take came from one outlet only, so it is not repeated here.

The Supreme Court case rests on unnamed sources, and no court statement or hearing date has been reported. Whether opposition leaders and the federal member states will accept the bill is also unknown.

What Comes Next

The two-month drafting window runs to about 13 December if counted from the cabinet meeting, although no start date was published. The bill is meant to fix the size and duties of the cabinet.

The cabinet plan does not set an election date, and it does not settle the dispute over the government’s mandate. The prime minister has said one person, one vote elections are the goal for next year.

On Thursday, 15 October, the national electoral commission announced parliamentary elections for 15 April 2027 and a presidential vote on 15 May. Dawan Africa and Garowe Online reported that the opposition rejects the timetable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Somalia’s cabinet decide on 13 October?

It approved a resolution on implementing the new constitution and set up a ministerial committee chaired by the justice minister. The committee has two months to prepare a bill on the structure of the federal government.

What is the 14 October deadline for ministers?

The constitution bars ministers from also sitting in parliament, and a six-month transition ended on 14 October. The constitutional commission said it would begin enforcing the rule from that date.

Who disputes the government’s mandate?

Opposition figures say President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s term ended on 15 May 2026. The president says the amended constitution gives the federal government a term to 15 May 2027.

Is it safe for US citizens to travel to Somalia?

The State Department rates Somalia Level 4, Do Not Travel, in an advisory issued on 21 May 2026. The advisory says not to travel to Somalia for any reason.

Does this affect US investors?

Direct exposure for US investors is minimal. The main relevance is security cooperation, aid and regional stability in the Horn of Africa.

SOUTH AFRICA · INVESTMENT

Key Facts — The country South Africa is Africa’s most industrialised economy, and KwaZulu-Natal is its eastern coastal province, home to the port city of Durban.

— What happened Investment pledges of R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) were made at the 2026 KwaZulu-Natal Investment Conference in Durban, IOL reported on Thursday 15 October.

— The target The province had aimed for R95 billion (about US$5.7 billion), so the pledges beat the goal by nearly R30 billion (about US$1.8 billion).

— The pledgers 47 companies and entities made pledges, led by Senzo Esihle Rail at R34.104 billion (about US$2.1 billion).

— The backdrop Soldiers were sent into central Durban on Saturday 10 October after days of anti-immigrant violence.

— Still open A pledge is a promise, not a contract, and the province has not said how much money has been committed in writing.

Investment pledges to KwaZulu-Natal, the South African province around the port city of Durban, reached R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion). IOL, a South African news site, reported the total on Thursday 15 October after the provincial investment conference.

For US readers, the figure matters because soldiers were sent into Durban days earlier over anti-immigrant violence. The investment pledges beat the province’s R95 billion (about US$5.7 billion) target by nearly R30 billion (about US$1.8 billion).

What Was Pledged in Durban

The 2026 KwaZulu-Natal Investment Conference took place at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in Durban, IOL reported. A total of 47 companies and entities made pledges.

The largest single pledge came from Senzo Esihle Rail at R34.104 billion (about US$2.1 billion). Azania MediaWorks followed at R6.5 billion (about US$0.4 billion), and Cedar Falls Properties 205 pledged R4.5 billion (about US$0.3 billion).

Bidvest Freight pledged R2.015 billion (about US$0.1 billion), Afchlor R1.75 billion (about US$0.1 billion) and AJ Property Holdings R1.072 billion (about US$0.06 billion). IOL named only these six amounts, so the other 41 pledges were not itemised.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on South Africa Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Behind the Conference

Premier Thami Ntuli, the head of the provincial government, led the event. Trade, Industry and Competition Minister Parks Tau, the national minister in charge of trade policy, joined him.

Musa Zondi, the provincial minister for economic development, and Cyril Xaba, the mayor of the eThekwini municipality that governs Durban, also took part. Musawenkosi Myeni, chair of Trade and Investment KwaZulu-Natal, the provincial investment agency, joined Tau and Ntuli to launch an investment booklet for 2026 to 2028.

Ntuli told the audience that KwaZulu-Natal is “open for business”. He said the pledges would be spread across all districts, adding that “a province that grows in one place is a province at risk”.

Pledges Beat Last Year’s Result

Last year’s investment pledges came to R100.1 billion (about US$6 billion), The Mercury reported on 23 October 2025. This year’s total is about R24 billion (about US$1.5 billion) higher.

The 2025 investment pledges were expected to create about 260,000 construction jobs and more than 60,000 permanent jobs, The Mercury said. Projects were meant to start within three years, and Zondi said some businesses held back because they could not meet that timeline.

The Unrest Behind the Headline

Soldiers began patrolling central Durban on Saturday 10 October after days of anti-immigrant violence, as Rio Times reported at the time. The protests began at the city’s refugee reception office, where a movement called March and March campaigns against illegal immigration.

Police reported 19 arrests in Durban between Thursday 8 and Saturday 10 October. In September, police whisked the mayor away from a hostile crowd during earlier anti-immigrant protests in the city.

IOL’s headline said the billions were pledged despite the protests. The conference took place in the same city where soldiers had patrolled days earlier.

Why Durban Matters to Investors

Durban is South Africa’s third-largest city and home to one of Africa’s busiest container ports. Bidvest Freight, one of the named pledgers, is a logistics company.

The six pledges IOL named add up to about R50 billion (about US$3 billion), or 40 percent of the total. That leaves about R75 billion (about US$4.5 billion) in pledges from the other 41 companies and entities.

What It Means for US Readers

Investors with exposure to South African ports, rail and property will watch whether these investment pledges turn into signed projects. The rand figures also shift with the exchange rate, which stood near 16.58 rand to the US dollar on 15 October.

Travellers and companies with staff in Durban can weigh the investment message against the unrest of early October. Government travel advice remains the best guide to local security.

What Is Not Known

Nobody has said how much of the R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) is signed and funded. IOL named no US company and did not say how many pledges come from foreign investors.

The province has not published a full list of the 47 pledges or a timetable for the projects. It has also not said how many jobs this year’s investment pledges could create.

More: South Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did investors pledge to KwaZulu-Natal?

Investors pledged R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) at the 2026 KwaZulu-Natal Investment Conference in Durban. The province had set a target of R95 billion (about US$5.7 billion).

Who made the biggest pledge?

Senzo Esihle Rail made the largest pledge at R34.104 billion (about US$2.1 billion). It was one of 47 companies and entities that made pledges, according to IOL.

Are investment pledges the same as investment?

No, a pledge is a stated intention to invest, not a signed contract or money already spent. Projects can be delayed or dropped if funding or approvals fall through.

How does this compare with last year?

The 2025 conference produced R100.1 billion (about US$6 billion) in investment pledges, according to The Mercury. This year’s R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) is higher.

Is it safe to travel to Durban?

Soldiers were sent into central Durban on 10 October after anti-immigrant violence, and police reported 19 arrests. Travellers should check their government’s travel advice and local news before visiting.

Sources: IOL, Billions pledged despite KZN protests (Thulaganyo Sethibe), 15 October 2026; The Mercury, KwaZulu-Natal investment conference pledges exceed expectations, 23 October 2025; The Witness, KZN Investment Conference to focus on industrialisation, local production, 15 October 2026.

World.content:

DR CONGO · HEALTH FUNDING

Key Facts — The country DR Congo is a central African nation where an Ebola outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain has run since May.

— What happened On Wednesday 14 October, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said about US$700 million of Ebola funds paid out by donors has not been traced.

— The numbers Donors say they paid out more than US$900 million, and about US$200 million has been traced, nearly US$100 million of it unspent.

— The reply Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba has threatened to strip the accreditation of aid groups that cannot show how they spent their funds.

— The outbreak Journal de Kinshasa put the toll at 9,144 cases and 4,410 deaths on 15 October, with the east of the country hardest hit.

— US link The US State Department says Washington has provided US$887 million for this Ebola response, and a CDC order still bars travellers from DR Congo.

— Still open Kaseya has not said where the money sits, and no donor or aid group has answered in public.

Ebola funds worth about US$700 million have not been traced, the head of Africa CDC said in Kinshasa on Wednesday 14 October. Actualite.cd, Radio Okapi and Congo Quotidien, three Congolese news outlets, reported his remarks on Thursday 15 October.

Donors say they paid out more than US$900 million to the groups running the response, and about US$200 million has been traced. Washington says it has provided US$887 million to this response, though no report names any donor behind the missing money.

What Jean Kaseya Said in Kinshasa

Kaseya leads Africa CDC, the African Union’s public health agency, and has been in DR Congo since 13 October. He told a news conference that donors had sent him their Ebola funds figures through diplomatic notes.

Of the Ebola funds donors say they paid to implementing partners, the aid groups running the response, only about US$200 million has been traced. Nearly US$100 million of that has not yet been spent, he said.

That leaves about US$700 million still to find, money that in his words “exists”. He promised to press each partner for an account and said, “we will not let go”.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on DR Congo Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Tracing the Money Is Hard

The traced figure comes from a meeting convened by the National Institute of Public Health, known as INSP, with the health ministry’s technical lead. Fewer than 30% of the partners took part, and Radio Okapi reported that only those present declared amounts.

At a press briefing on 2 October, INSP director general Dieudonné Mwamba said only 25 of about 94 accredited partners had sent information, Actualite.cd reported. Those groups reported receiving US$226.3 million and spending US$127.4 million.

How Congo’s Government Is Responding

Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba called the handling of Ebola funds a “flou artistique”, a French phrase for a deliberate-looking blur. He announced coercive measures against groups that cannot justify their funds, following an instruction from President Félix Tshisekedi.

Groups that fail to comply could lose their accreditation and face action by the immigration directorate, known as DGM. The government has written to the partners concerned, Actualite.cd reported.

Kamba said the first three-month response plan raised about US$227 million, of which nearly US$99 million was unused. He added that the state’s own US$50 million was spent transparently, according to a report sent to the prime minister.

Kamba also said the lack of visibility on partner funds complicates talks with the International Monetary Fund on budget support. The IMF lends to governments and often asks for proof that public money is tracked.

The Outbreak Behind the Money

The disease is Ebola of the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine or treatment is approved. The World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May.

Journal de Kinshasa, a Congolese news site, put the toll at 9,144 cases and 4,410 deaths on 15 October. Ituri province in the east is at the centre, and Radio Okapi reported no new case for 21 days in Tchomia, a locality in Ituri.

Radio Okapi also listed a further US$80 million from the World Bank for the response on 15 October. The World Bank is the global development lender that funds public health and infrastructure projects.

A G20 meeting in New York raised about US$2.6 billion in Ebola commitments in September, Kaseya said at the time. He asked that the money reach people in need directly and that its use be tracked.

What It Means for US Readers

The State Department, which took over US emergency aid after USAID closed in 2025, said on 23 September that it had provided US$887 million. Rio Times reported that total when the latest US$267 million was announced.

No report ties the United States to the untraced Ebola funds, and the donors behind them are not named. Taxpayers still have a stake, because a leaky response can let the outbreak run longer.

The CDC says anyone who has been in DR Congo within 21 days cannot board a commercial flight to the United States. US citizens are told to stay outside DR Congo for 21 days before entering, and the page was updated on 13 October.

What Is Not Known

Kaseya has not said which partners hold the missing Ebola funds or where they went. Outlets quote the donor total as US$926.66 million or US$962 million, so the gap of about US$700 million is rounded.

No donor, aid group or health agency has answered in public, and no investigation has been announced. Journal de Kinshasa stressed that the statements point to a tracing problem, not to embezzlement.

More: DR Congo news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Africa CDC?

Africa CDC is the African Union’s public health agency, based in Addis Ababa and led by Jean Kaseya. It coordinates Africa’s response to outbreaks such as Ebola.

How many Ebola funds are untraced in DR Congo?

Kaseya said about US$700 million of the Ebola funds donors say they paid out has not been traced. Donors report more than US$900 million, and about US$200 million has been traced.

Does untraced money mean it was stolen?

No report says so, and Kaseya says the Ebola funds exist. Journal de Kinshasa stressed that the statements show a tracing problem, not embezzlement.

Which outbreak is the money for?

It is for the Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, centred on Ituri province. No vaccine or treatment is approved for this strain.

Can Americans travel to DR Congo?

The CDC bars anyone who has been in DR Congo within 21 days from boarding commercial flights to the United States. US citizens should stay outside DR Congo for 21 days before entering.

Sources: Actualite.cd (French), opaque management of response funds, 15 October 2026; Radio Okapi (French), Africa CDC demands accounts, 15 October 2026; Congo Quotidien (French), 700 million not traced, 15 October 2026; Journal de Kinshasa (French), 700 million missing, 15 October 2026; US CDC, Ebola situation summary and entry restrictions, 13 October 2026.

World.title: DR Congo Ebola Aid Over US$700M Unreported
World.content:
DR CONGO · EBOLA FUNDING

Key Facts — What is happening Africa CDC, the African Union health agency, said on Wednesday, 14 October, that more than US$700 million of Ebola response money paid to partners working in DR Congo is unknown to national authorities.

— Why it matters Donors pay for the Ebola response through international groups, so an accounting gap about three quarters the size of the payments raises oversight questions for every donor government, including Washington.

— The numbers Donors paid nearly US$962 million to international organisations and NGOs; the groups that shared figures declared about US$220 million received, US$120 million spent and US$100 million unspent, leaving more than US$700 million unreported.

— Who is who Africa CDC is the African Union’s continental health agency, led by Director General Jean Kaseya, and the INSP is Congo’s national public health institute, which convened the partners to report their funds.

— What to watch Africa CDC and the government plan to reconcile every payment, and the agency would back suspending the accreditation of organisations that stay silent, though no date or name has been announced.

— What it means for you Americans who fund global health through the government or charities should watch whether donors demand itemised accounts from partners, while the statements announce no change to travel or health advice.

Africa CDC says more than US$700 million of Ebola response money is unknown to national authorities in DR Congo. The agency says donors paid the funds to international partners, not to the Congolese government.

More than US$700 million of DR Congo Ebola aid is unknown to national authorities, Africa CDC said on Wednesday, 14 October. Director General Jean Kaseya spoke in Kinshasa, and the agency repeated the figure in a statement dated Thursday, 15 October.

Donors paid nearly US$962 million directly to the international organisations and NGOs that run the response, not to the Congolese state. The groups that shared figures with officials declared receiving about US$220 million.

The Gap in DR Congo Ebola Aid Reports

Only about 30% of the organisations attended a verification meeting convened by the head of the INSP and shared financial data. The INSP is Congo’s national public health institute, and Dr Hyppolite Kalambay, Africa CDC’s country director in Congo, supported the meeting.

Those groups said they had received about US$220 million, of which US$120 million was spent and US$100 million remains unspent. Subtracting that from nearly US$962 million leaves more than US$700 million that national authorities cannot account for.

The unreported amount is roughly three quarters of everything the donors paid out. Africa CDC is the continental health agency of the African Union, the bloc of 55 African states.

Radio Okapi, a Congolese radio network, gave a similar picture of the Wednesday press conference. It put the traced amount at about US$200 million and the unspent sum at about US$100 million.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on DR Congo Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Africa CDC Says Happens Next

Africa CDC says it will work with the government to reconcile the funding and identify what each organisation received. The exercise is to document spending, remaining balances, activities and results.

The agency calls the partners’ lack of cooperation unacceptable and says sovereignty carries duties to respect national coordination and accountability rules. It would back administrative measures the government judges necessary, up to suspending or withdrawing an organisation’s accreditation.

Africa CDC may also alert authorities in other African countries to the names of organisations that do not comply. Its written statement does not name the organisations that failed to report.

Africa CDC Stops Short of Alleging Theft

In an interview with Actualite.cd, a Kinshasa news site, Kaseya said the money being sought is with the partners, not the government. He called it unclear management and added that he was not yet speaking of embezzlement.

The written statement describes a reporting gap, saying the amounts remain unknown to national authorities. It says the partners have not provided the information, which is a different finding from lost money.

That wording matters because some headlines have called the sum untraceable or missing. The statement itself does not say any money was lost, stolen or misused.

Earlier Calls for Transparency

On 4 October, Africa CDC said it backed the Congolese government’s call for stronger transparency and traceability in Ebola funding. It promised to strengthen its Financial Tracking Mechanism, which gathers partner data and flags funding gaps.

That statement put announced donor commitments at US$2.9 billion, far above the nearly US$962 million now said to have been paid. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka urged rapid disbursement of those pledges at a G20+ meeting in New York on 23 September.

Africa CDC also said it supports administrative action against organisations that miss reporting rules, in line with national law. President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo had led a high-level meeting on Wednesday, 5 August that set priorities on coordination and financial accountability.

What It Means for US Readers

The State Department announced an additional US$267 million for the Ebola response in DR Congo on 23 September. The Africa CDC statements do not say whether any US money sits inside the unreported amount.

For US readers, the question is oversight: will donors demand itemised accounts from the groups that spend their money? US charities and contractors working in Congo could face tougher reporting demands, because Africa CDC backs sanctions on groups that stay silent.

Travellers should note that the finding concerns accounting, not the outbreak, and the statements announce no change to health advice. Nothing in the statements points to a change in entry rules for Congo.

What Is Not Known

The statements do not name the organisations that failed to report or say how much each donor paid. They also do not say whether any US money is in the unreported amount.

The figures differ across statements, with about US$200 million, US$220 million and US$228 million given for the amount already traced. No audit report was linked in any of the statements, and the numbers come from Africa CDC and its Congolese partners.

Kaseya said in the interview that US officials promised a list of every partner that received money. No US statement confirming this was found.

He also said Africa CDC will publish a report on where each amount went. No publication date has been given.

What Comes Next

Africa CDC and the Congolese government now have to reconcile the payments, and no deadline has been announced. The step to watch is whether the government suspends the accreditation of any organisation that stays silent.

Nothing in the statements says the Ebola response has stopped or that any money has been shown to be stolen. The gap concerns reporting, and it will narrow only if the partners publish their figures.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much Ebola money is unaccounted for in DR Congo?

Africa CDC says more than US$700 million is unknown to national authorities. Donors paid nearly US$962 million, and partners have declared receiving about US$220 million.

Does Africa CDC say the money was stolen?

No, its statement describes a reporting gap and does not allege theft or misuse. Director General Jean Kaseya told Actualite.cd he was not yet speaking of embezzlement.

Who received the money?

Donors paid it directly to international organisations and NGOs that run the response, not to the Congolese government. Only about 30% of those groups attended the meeting where they were asked to report.

What happens to organisations that do not report?

Africa CDC says it would support government measures up to suspending or withdrawing their accreditation. It may also alert authorities in other African countries to the names of non-compliant groups.

Does this affect US readers or travellers?

It raises oversight questions for donors such as the United States, but the statements do not say whether US funds are involved. The finding concerns accounting, and the statements announce no change to health advice.

Sources: Africa CDC statement of 15 October 2026; US State Department media note of 23 September 2026; Africa CDC statement of 4 October 2026; Actualite.cd, interview with Jean Kaseya; Radio Okapi; Actualite.cd, report of 15 October (all accessed 15 October 2026).

World.title: What to Do in Cancún in October 2026
World.content:
CANCÚN · Culture

A week-long rock festival at a resort, a symphony in a cenote and free theatre downtown. The rest of the month, day by day.

Beachfront hotels along the Zona Hotelera in Cancún. File photo (dronepicr, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons).

RT Ask Rio Times Latin American culture, food and life. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. CANCÚN — This guide is for people who live here, not weekend tourists. It covers things to do in Cancún in October 2026 from Friday 16 October to Halloween, with venues, dates and practical notes for expats and long-stay visitors.

October in Cancún is hot, humid and often wet, with brief heavy showers and the tail end of hurricane season. The Atlantic season officially runs until 30 November, so keep an eye on weather alerts before planning outdoor events.

The month has a clear shape. Free municipal and cultural events fill the first weekend of this guide, the big rock festival takes over a hotel-zone resort from 20 to 25 October, and Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October before Día de Muertos on 1 and 2 November.

Mexico’s federal mandatory-rest-day list does not include 12 October 2026; after 16 September, the next generally applicable federal mandatory rest day is 16 November 2026, followed by 25 December 2026. That means banks and most shops keep normal hours through the rest of October.

Friday 16 to Sunday 18 October: Free Culture Downtown

Cancún’s municipal programme leans on free events at Teatro de la Ciudad, the city’s main theatre in the centre. Prices below are as listed by the Riviera Lowdown events calendar, with pesos converted at about 18.4 pesos per US dollar (RT spot, 15 October 2026).

Friday 16 October, 8:00 p.m. Rocktubre Teatro de la Ciudad, Cancún · Free A free rock evening at the city’s main municipal theatre. It is an easy first night out for residents who live downtown.

Friday 16 October, 9:00 p.m. Retro Disco Centro Cultural Underground Xtabay, Cancún · Free A free retro dance night at an independent cultural centre. It suits long-stay visitors who want a local crowd rather than a hotel-zone club.

Saturday 17 October, 6:00 p.m. Décadas Parque de Las Palapas, downtown Cancún · Free A free open-air music session in the park that serves as downtown’s social square. Arrive early on a Saturday evening, because the park fills with families.

Saturday 17 October, 8:00 p.m. Art After Dark Marina Puerto Cancún · MXN 350 (about US$19) An evening art event at the marina development on the edge of the hotel zone. It is the more upmarket pick of the weekend.

Saturday 17 October, 8:00 p.m. Multiverso de la Locura Centro Cultural Toltecayotl, Cancún · MXN 250 (about US$14) A paid evening show at a community cultural centre.

Sunday 18 October, 6:00 p.m. Soy Puro Mexicano Teatro de la Ciudad, Cancún · Free A free Sunday-evening show at the municipal theatre. It is a gentle way to end the weekend.

The Sands Rocks at Paradisus: 20 to 25 October

The biggest music event of the month is not a normal concert. SANDS 2026 is an adults-only private event that takes over the Paradisus Cancún resort in the hotel zone from Tuesday 20 to Sunday 25 October 2026, with attendance limited to 1,200 guests.

The announced line-up is Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark, Bobby Brown, Queensrÿche, Cutting Crew, Dishwalla, Winger, Sheila E. and The Smithereens. Tickets are sold as resort packages through the organiser at thesands.rocks, not as single-night entries, and the organiser has not published a day-by-day running order.

During SANDS, 20 to 25 October Cutting Crew at The Sands Paradisus Cancún, hotel zone · Package price on the organiser’s site The British band behind the 1980s hit “(I Just) Died in Your Arms” lists this show on its own tour page. Because the festival is a private package, residents cannot simply buy a ticket for one night at the door.

Late October: A Symphony in a Cenote and Halloween

Friday 30 October Symphony in a Cenote Fairmont Mayakoba, Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen · Hotel booking The hotel announced a one-night orchestral concert inside a cenote, limited to 50 guests, with private transport from the resort. Ask the hotel on +52 984 206 3000 for the current booking terms, because its own event page still says details are coming soon.

Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October. Many bars, hotels and expat groups host parties that night, so book tables early and expect higher prices for taxis late in the evening.

Planning your Cancún in October

Carry an umbrella and expect sudden downpours, especially later in the day. Tropical systems can bring longer rain, so check forecasts before travelling far.

Downtown venues such as Teatro de la Ciudad and Parque de Las Palapas are in the centre of the city. The hotel zone, where Paradisus and the marina sit, is a taxi or bus ride away.

Getting around at night is easiest by taxi or ride-hailing app, though availability can be patchy late in the evening. Agree a fare before you get in, or use an app that shows the price first.

Smaller venues often take cash only, so carry some pesos. For paid events, buy from the venue or organiser, because Mexican listings change dates and prices at short notice.

Día de Muertos is on 1 and 2 November. Altars and decorations begin to appear in public spaces in the last days of October.

Background: Brazil Election Results Put Lula and Flávio in Runoff.

Background: 11 BRICS Members in 2026 and 10 Partner Countries.

Background: Brazil Economy 2026 Grows 2% as Selic Falls to 13.75%.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the biggest music event in Cancún in October 2026?

SANDS 2026 at Paradisus Cancún runs from 20 to 25 October as an adults-only private event limited to 1,200 guests. Queensrÿche, Cutting Crew, Winger and Sheila E. are on the announced line-up.

Can I buy a single-night ticket for The Sands Rocks?

The organiser sells the festival as an all-inclusive resort package at thesands.rocks. It has not published single-night entry or a day-by-day running order.

Is there a public holiday in Cancún in October 2026?

12 October 2026 is not a mandatory rest day under Mexico’s Federal Labor Law; Día de la Raza, now Día de la Nación Pluricultural, is commemorated but is not a federal labor holiday.

What is the weather like in Cancún in October?

Expect hot, humid days with brief heavy showers and a continuing tropical-cyclone risk. The Atlantic hurricane season officially runs until 30 November.

Are there free events in Cancún this month?

Yes. Rocktubre and Soy Puro Mexicano at Teatro de la Ciudad, Décadas at Parque de Las Palapas and Retro Disco at Centro Cultural Underground Xtabay are listed as free on 16, 17 and 18 October.

World.title: Belize participates in U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue hosted by U.S. Deputy Secretary of State
World.content:
Belize participates in U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue hosted by U.S. Deputy Secretary of State

By Zoila Palma: Today, Oscar Arnold, Chief Executive Officer for Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, is participating in the U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue, hosted by U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau.

The Ministry says that the high-level dialogue provides an important platform to strengthen regional partnerships and advance shared priorities in security and defense coordination, strategic economic growth, disaster response, and regional health cooperation.

CEO Arnold is joined by the Ambassador of Belize to the U.S., Nestor Mendez, and Counsellor, Alexya Perez.

“Belize remains committed to constructive engagement and regional collaboration with the Caribbean and its partners,” the Ministry said.

World.title: Belize City man fined $55 for riding bicycle up-stop on his own street
World.content:
Belize City man fined $55 for riding bicycle up-stop on his own street

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 26-year-old Belize City man found himself in trouble with the law after police caught him riding his bicycle against the flow of traffic on the very street where he lives.

Jermaine Lewis, a resident of King Street, was detained on Saturday, October 10, 2026, after police observed him riding his bicycle in the wrong direction along the one-way street.

Lewis was escorted to the nearby Precinct 1 Police Station, also located on King Street, where he was charged with causing a bicycle to proceed up a one-way street.

He appeared before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, October 13, and pleaded guilty to the traffic offence.

The Magistrate imposed a fine of $50 plus $5 court costs, giving Lewis until November 30, 2026, to pay or face one week in prison.

Riding a bicycle against the designated flow of traffic is an offence under Belize’s traffic laws, and similar violations have resulted in fines and, in some cases, imprisonment for unpaid penalties.

World.title: International News: Strong El Niño raises global concerns over wildfires, food security and power shortages
World.content:
International News: Strong El Niño raises global concerns over wildfires, food security and power shortages

By Zoila Palma: An exceptionally strong El Niño weather cycle is contributing to drought, wildfires, power shortages and growing food security concerns in several parts of the world, with scientists warning that its effects could intensify as the phenomenon approaches its expected peak in December.

In Indonesia, prolonged dry conditions have contributed to fires in forests and plantations in Borneo and South Sumatra, triggering a regional haze crisis that has affected neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore.

Authorities and conservation groups have rescued dozens of orangutans from the fires. Meanwhile, Brazil’s Amazon region has also experienced widespread fires, with Amazonas state recording nearly four times as many fire hotspots in September as in the same month last year.

In Myanmar, authorities have warned of possible electricity outages as unusually high temperatures increase power demand, while the Philippines is preparing for higher energy consumption and potential declines in hydropower production. The impacts are also raising concerns about food security, with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva expressing concern about the global consequences and saying the IMF is preparing to support countries that may struggle to cope.

The World Meteorological Organization has warned that El Niño is likely to bring above-average temperatures to much of the world and alter rainfall patterns, increasing the risk of droughts and floods.

World.title: Wrong And Strong: ‘Dads’, 61, fined $110 for riding bicycle up-stop and upstarting police
World.content:
Wrong And Strong: ‘Dads’, 61, fined $110 for riding bicycle up-stop and upstarting police

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 61-year-old Belize City man who was caught riding his bicycle against traffic on a one-way street ended up facing two charges after allegedly refusing to cooperate with a police officer.

Jose Augustine August appeared unrepresented before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday, October 14, where he pleaded guilty to causing a bicycle to proceed against the designated direction of a one-way street and obstructing a police officer.

According to police, the incident occurred on Sunday, October 11, on Cemetery Road, where August was intercepted for riding his bicycle in the wrong direction. He subsequently obstructed a female corporal while she was executing her duties.

August admitted both offences and did not dispute the prosecution’s allegations. When given an opportunity to offer mitigating circumstances, he remained silent.

The Magistrate imposed a fine of $50 for each offence, along with $5 court costs on each charge, bringing his total penalty to $110.

August was given until November 30, 2026, to pay the fines or face one week in prison for each offence.

World.title: Charge dropped against man accused of going equipped to steal but remains behind bars
World.content:
Charge dropped against man accused of going equipped to steal but remains behind bars

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A man who has spent three months behind bars because he could not post bail received some good news in court on Wednesday, October 14, when prosecutors withdrew one of two criminal charges against him.

Wilfred Dixon, 39, was initially charged with going equipped to commit burglary or theft and handling stolen goods after police allegedly found him with a tool kit containing a grinder in Hattieville on July 13, 2026.

During his latest appearance at the Belize City Magistrate’s Court, a police prosecutor informed the court that the prosecution was withdrawing the charge of going equipped and would proceed to trial solely on the handling stolen goods charge.

Dixon, who remains unrepresented, was provided with eight pages of disclosure and three photographs. He disputed part of a witness statement alleging that he was seen throwing an object.

According to previous BBN reporting, police allegedly spotted Dixon carrying the tool kit in a yard near Locario Street in Hattieville around 4:50 a.m. When approached, he reportedly fled and later discarded the kit near Mile 16 on the George Price Highway.

At his initial arraignment, Dixon denied wrongdoing, telling the court, “I nuh guilty because I nuh thief it. I found it dah Sibun.”

Although he was granted bail of $800 plus one surety, Dixon has remained at the Belize Central Prison because he has been unable to secure someone to sign his bail.

His trial for handling stolen goods is scheduled for November 13, 2026.

World.title: PI delayed again for police officer accused of murdering ex-mother-in-law and her twin brother in Hattieville
World.content:
PI delayed again for police officer accused of murdering ex-mother-in-law and her twin brother in Hattieville

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Nearly one year after being remanded to prison for a double murder in Hattieville, interdicted police officer Orvin Justin Williams, 26, is still awaiting his Preliminary Inquiry (PI) after another adjournment in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court.

Williams appeared before a Senior Magistrate in Court #2 on Wednesday, October 14, but his PI could not proceed because the Magistrate assigned to his case was on duty in another jurisdiction.

Represented by attorney Gilroy Usher Jr., Williams was further remanded to the Belize Central Prison until October 21, 2026, when his PI is expected to commence in Court #3.

Williams is charged with the September 15, 2025 murders of 57-year-old twins Paula Belisle, his former mother-in-law, and her brother, Paul Esquilliano, who were shot inside a residence on Ysaguirre Boulevard in Hattieville Village.

Police investigations revealed that a gunman arrived at the property in a vehicle, opened fire on the siblings, and fled. Investigators subsequently recovered five expended 9mm shells and obtained surveillance footage that helped them identify a vehicle of interest.

Williams was formally arraigned on October 15, 2025, and has remained on remand since then.

The case has faced repeated delays. In May, Williams received 201 pages of disclosure and 10 DVDs as part of the prosecution’s evidence. His PI was postponed again in August because the assigned Magistrate was unavailable.

Williams remains on interdiction from the Belize Police Department pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

World.title: Pesticides Control Board hiring Programme Manager for Technical Services
World.content:
Pesticides Control Board hiring Programme Manager for Technical Services

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Pesticides Control Board of Belize (PCB) is looking for a new Programme Manager for Technical Services to join its management team.

The position is based in Central Farm, Cayo District.

The PCB is the statutory body responsible for regulating pesticides in Belize, working to safeguard public health, food security and the environment.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree in agriculture, or a bachelor’s degree with at least seven years of agricultural experience.

Experience in chemicals management, programme management, team leadership and project development is required.

Applications should be emailed to [email protected] or [email protected] by October 23, 2026.

For more information on the work of the Pesticides Control Board, visit pcbbelize.com.

World.title: Fort Hood shooter’s execution reignites death penalty debate, including in Belize
World.content:
Fort Hood shooter’s execution reignites death penalty debate, including in Belize

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan will go ahead on December 3, but the public will not be watching.

President Donald Trump confirmed on Thursday that Hasan will be executed by firing squad at Fort Hood, Texas, as scheduled. He overruled a plan by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to livestream it.

Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, killed 13 people and wounded more than 30 in a 2009 attack at Fort Hood. He was convicted by a military court and sentenced to death in 2013.

The case has once again put the death penalty in the spotlight, a debate that also echoes here in Belize.

The death penalty remains on Belize’s law books, with hanging as the method of execution. But Belize has not carried out an execution since 1985. Court rulings over the years have also ended the mandatory death sentence for murder, giving judges discretion in sentencing.

Every so often, especially after violent crimes that shock the nation, calls resurface for Belize to resume executions. Others argue the death penalty does not deter crime and risks irreversible mistakes.

So we want to hear from you, Belize.

Should Belize bring back executions for the most serious crimes? Or should the death penalty be abolished altogether?

Tell us what you think in the comments.

World.title: Prison officials deny reported fight between P Diddy and Dudus
World.content:
American rapper P Diddy and Jamaican drug lord Christopher 'Dudus' Coke a

Prison officials are reportedly denying a reported physical altercation between American music mogul Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs and convicted Jamaican drug lord Christopher ‘Dudus’ Coke, which resulted in the rapper being rushed to hospital on Wednesday.

A TMZ report on Wednesday said the confrontation reportedly erupted after Combs allegedly caused trouble that resulted in disciplinary action against fellow inmates. The Bad Boy for Life singer reportedly sustained a head injury and was subsequently transported to an outside medical facility for treatment.

But the Federal Bureau of Prisons is denying that the fight took place.

“While, for privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, we can tell you that the story you are referring to is false and did not happen. Sean Combs is in the custody of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and is incarcerated at the Federal Correctional Institution Fort Dix. Beyond this, we have no additional information to provide,” a spokesman for the Federal Bureau of Prisons was quoted as saying in a statement to The Daily Mail.

Combs was sentenced last year to just over four years in federal prison after being convicted on prostitution-related charges involving two of his former girlfriends.
